interpretation_2_zh: 这里实际借“共同语言”转指父母写作文时文风不一致，暗示这篇作文前后分别由爸爸和妈妈代写，因此语调风格完全不同。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the parents do not get along or do not communicate well, and because the essay was written by different parents, their different styles and tones caused the inconsistency.
context: 老师质疑作文前后文风差异，学生用“爸爸和妈妈没有共同语言”作答，借该短语的常义和字面义制造双关。
literal_translation: Teacher: Why is the style and tone of your essay completely different from beginning to end? Student: My dad and my mom simply don't have a common language.
functional_equivalence_translation: Teacher: Why does your essay sound like it was written by two different people? Student: Because my mom and dad don't exactly speak the same language.
explanatory_translation: Teacher: Why is the style of your essay completely inconsistent? Student: Because my dad and mom don't have a common language—normally meaning they can't communicate well, but here implying they write in different styles, so different parts were written by different parents.
interpretation_1: 指两个人在想法或沟通上有共识、能谈得来。
interpretation_2: 字面转为“使用同一种语言风格”，暗指父母分别代写作文不同部分，导致文风不一致。

surface_text: 胖姐在做运动，同事小张、小刘路过，小张说：胖姐减肥呢？胖姐不高兴的瞪了小张一眼转身离去。 小刘说：以后不能说减肥，是瘦身。 小张说：现在的人真疯狂胖的叫兽身，瘦的叫魔鬼身材。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层里把“瘦身”故意说成“兽身”，字面上像是在说胖的人被称作野兽般的身形，带有贬损和荒诞效果。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, '兽身' means 'the body of a beast' or 'an animal-like body,' contrasting with '魔鬼身材' in a joking way.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是对“瘦身”这一委婉说法的调侃，意思是本来只是把“减肥”换成更好听的“瘦身”，却被小张借同音近似转成“兽身”，讽刺这种说法过于讲究包装。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a playful mishearing of '瘦身' ('slimming' or 'getting a slimmer body') as '兽身,' creating a semantic shift from 'becoming slim' to 'beast body' to mock the euphemistic wording.
context: 胖姐做运动减肥，同事先说“减肥”惹其不快，后改说“瘦身”，另一人故意把“瘦身”曲解为“兽身”，并与后文“魔鬼身材”形成戏谑对照。
literal_translation: Nowadays people are really crazy: the fat one is called a beast body, and the thin one is called a devil figure.
functional_equivalence_translation: People are crazy now—if you're fat, they call it a “beast body”; if you're slim, it's a “killer body.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese near-homophones “瘦身” (slimming, getting a slimmer body) and “兽身” (beast body). After someone says one should say “slimming” instead of “losing weight,” the speaker twists “瘦身” into “兽身” to mock the euphemism.
interpretation_1: 表层上承接前文“减肥要说瘦身”，指让身体变瘦、塑形。
interpretation_2: 把“瘦身”故意说成“兽身”，讽刺胖人若叫“瘦身”就像“野兽的身体”。

surface_text: 泥瓦匠出身的部长接受记者采访。 记者问：“你觉得当部长和当泥瓦匠有什么相似之处？” 部长答道：“第一，要有和稀泥的本领：第二，站在高处头不昏！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把部长工作类比为泥瓦匠手艺：泥瓦匠要会和稀泥，也常常需要站在高处施工而不头昏。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the minister compares the two jobs literally: both a mason and a minister need the skill to mix mortar well, and both may work at heights without getting dizzy.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上借泥瓦匠的话说官场处事之道：当部长要善于调和矛盾、做圆通周旋的人；身居高位也要保持清醒，不因职位高而昏头。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, he is making a political pun: 'he xi ni' also means smoothing over conflicts or being evasively conciliatory, and 'standing high' refers to being in a high official position without becoming arrogant, losing balance, or being overwhelmed by power.
context: 泥瓦匠出身的部长被问到当部长和当泥瓦匠的相似之处，他回答要有“和稀泥”的本领。
literal_translation: A minister who used to be a bricklayer was interviewed. The reporter asked, “What similarities do you think there are between being a minister and being a bricklayer?” The minister answered, “First, you need the skill of mixing mud; second, when standing high up, you must not get dizzy!”
functional_equivalence_translation: Asked how being a minister is like being a bricklayer, he said, “First, both require knowing how to smooth things over; second, when you’re up high, you can’t lose your head.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “和稀泥,” which literally means mixing mud for bricklaying, but figuratively means smoothing over conflicts or fudging issues. The minister uses the bricklayer sense on the surface while implying the political sense.
interpretation_1: 指泥瓦匠把水和泥搅拌成可用的泥料。
interpretation_2: 指当部长要会做和事佬，在矛盾中模糊表态、折中调停。

surface_text: 我们寝室在六楼，我寝一位在寝室说：这天天爬五层楼梯，可真累！ 这时，旁边一人说：啥叫爬楼梯呀？！谁不是走上来的？那你要是往上爬，那能不累？！ 众人无语……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本中“爬楼梯”是日常说法，意思是步行上楼、一级一级走到六楼，所以说很累。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "climb the stairs" means going up many flights of stairs to reach the dorm room, which is tiring.
interpretation_2_zh: 旁边的人把“爬”按本义理解为像攀爬一样手脚并用地往上爬，从而故意曲解“爬楼梯”，制造出‘那当然更累’的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning focuses on the literal sense of "crawl/climb" with hands and feet; the speaker deliberately interprets "爬" literally instead of its common figurative sense of "walk up" stairs.
context: 六楼寝室的人抱怨天天上五层楼很累，旁人故意把“爬楼梯”的常用说法理解成字面动作。
negative_example: 这天天走五层楼梯，可真累
literal_translation: Our dorm is on the sixth floor. A roommate said in the dorm: “Climbing five flights of stairs every day is really tiring!” Then someone nearby said: “What do you mean climb stairs?! Who didn’t walk up? If you were really crawling upward, of course it would be tiring!” Everyone was speechless...
functional_equivalence_translation: Our dorm is on the sixth floor. One roommate complained, “Going up five flights every day is exhausting.” Another guy quipped, “Why say ‘climb’ the stairs? Everyone walks up. If you literally climbed, no wonder you’d be tired!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese phrase “爬楼梯,” which normally just means “to go up the stairs,” but one person deliberately interprets “爬” literally as “to crawl/climb on all fours,” creating the pun.
interpretation_1: 按日常说法，指沿楼梯上楼，是对上楼过程的通俗表达。
interpretation_2: 被故意按字面理解为像动物一样手脚并用地向上爬楼。

surface_text: “服务员，快跟我说你们家洗手间在哪？快！” 服务员一愣：“出。。出。。 出门左拐第二个红绿灯右转上58路公交7个站， 下车向前500米第三个小区入口第3栋901进门左边。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，服务员把客人的催促和自己结巴说出的“出”接成了“出门左拐……”，随后报出一长串离得很远的路线，像是在认真指路。
interpretation_1_en: The waiter is stammering on the word 'chu...' and then gives directions to the restroom, starting with 'go out, turn left...'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，“出”原本只是服务员因紧张或发愣而结巴的起始音，本应接成对洗手间位置的正常回答，如“厕所在……”；却被误接成“出门”，形成答非所问的喜剧效果。
interpretation_2_en: The word '出' is shifted from meaning the beginning of 'go out' for restroom directions to sounding like the repeated start of a stammer, which humorously makes the waiter give an absurdly long set of directions as if the restroom were extremely far away.
context: 顾客急问洗手间在哪，服务员先结巴地说“出……出……”，随后报出一长串公交路线，造成“指出位置”与“出门去某处”的意义偏移。
literal_translation: "Waiter, quickly tell me where your restroom is! Quick!" The waiter froze: "Go... go... go out, turn left at the second traffic light, then turn right, take bus 58 for 7 stops, get off, walk 500 meters forward, enter the third residential compound, Building 3, Room 901, left after entering."
functional_equivalence_translation: "Waiter, where's the restroom? Quick!" The waiter stammered, "Go... go... go out, left at the second light, right, take the 58 for seven stops..."
explanatory_translation: The humor hinges on the Chinese word "出". In context, the waiter should "指出" (point out) where the restroom is, but instead shifts to "出去" (go out) and gives an absurdly long route, as if answering how to go somewhere far away.
interpretation_1: 服务员本应回答并指出洗手间的位置。
interpretation_2: 服务员把“在哪”理解成去往很远地点的路线询问，给出一整套“出去”的路线说明。

surface_text: 妻子生了小孩后，丈夫说：我们实行承包制吧。 妻子说：儿子在我肚子十个月，已经到了承包期，现在该你买断了。
拉面店柜台前，女孩正排队等候。 到她时，拉面师傅问：你要粗的还是细的？ 女孩答：你拉什么我就吃什么。
昨天上午，看着同班的女孩喝奶那优雅的姿势不由得神迷。那女孩也发现了我看她很久，不由得柳眉横竖：怎么？想喝我的奶？没门！！
小王急忙阻拦，说：“你看，窗上写着‘请勿往窗外扔东西’！” 老婆想了想，把东风西风挑出来，剩下的哗啦丢了下去……
一天，老板让张斌和吴山各写一篇文章。 第二天，老板问：“小斌啊，你的文章带来了吗？” 张斌说：“哦，我忘带了。” 老板又说：“小山带来了吗？” 这时，老板秘书悄悄对老板说：“小三不能带来。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中把“吴山”简称成“小山”，秘书的话是在说“小山”没有把文章带来。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'Xiao San' is simply the secretary mistakenly or jokingly using a nickname to refer to Xiao Shan, the person the boss is asking about.
interpretation_2_zh: “小山”被说成近音的“小三”，激活了“第三者、情人”的常见含义，所以表面是在汇报文章没带来，实际上形成了“小三不能带来”的歧义效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'xiao san' in Chinese also means a mistress or the other woman in an extramarital affair, so saying 'Xiao San cannot be brought here' carries an extra suggestive meaning.
context: 老板问“小山带来了吗”，秘书故意或误听成“小三不能带来”，利用“小山”与“小三”近音造成歧义。
literal_translation: One day, the boss asked Zhang Bin and Wu Shan to each write an article. The next day, the boss asked, “Xiao Bin, did you bring your article?” Zhang Bin said, “Oh, I forgot to bring it.” The boss then asked, “Did Xiao Shan bring it?” At this moment, the boss’s secretary quietly said to the boss, “The mistress can’t be brought here.”
functional_equivalence_translation: When the boss asked, “Did Xiao Shan bring it?”, the secretary quipped, “A mistress isn’t someone you can just bring along,” playing on the similar sound between “Xiao Shan” and “xiaosan” (mistress).
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the near-homophony between “Xiao Shan” (a nickname for Wu Shan) and “xiaosan,” a common Chinese term meaning “the other woman” or “mistress.” So the secretary twists the boss’s question into a socially awkward meaning.
interpretation_1: 表层上是把“吴山/小山”听成了“小三”，像是在回答老板对“小山是否带来文章”的询问。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“小三”指婚外情对象、第三者，因此“不能带来”带有社会禁忌和身份不当的戏谑意味。

surface_text: 警方询问了送外卖的小哥的邻居。
被一个小孩打了一下， 本人怒道：“你为什么欺负大人？” 小孩说：“你不是大人，你是不良青年！” 本人心里咯噔一下， 难道他还看出本人的不良史了？ 遂心虚道：“我哪儿不良了？” 没想到他一句就把我秒杀了， 他说：“你发育不良！” 熊孩子，你家人在附近吗？ 我保证不打死你！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上小孩说的是“你发育不良”，意思是身体发育得不好，所以不算“大人”。
interpretation_1_en: Here, 'bad youth' is first understood in the usual sense of a delinquent or morally bad young person, so the speaker thinks the child is saying he has a bad past or questionable character.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上先激活了“不良青年”里的“不良”，让人误以为是在说品行不好、有不良经历的人，形成语义转移的双关。
interpretation_2_en: The child actually means 'poorly developed': 'bad' shifts from moral misconduct to physical underdevelopment, so he is mocking the speaker for being undergrown rather than delinquent.
context: 小孩先说“你是不良青年”，说话人误以为是道德评价，追问后小孩用“你发育不良”揭示真实所指。
literal_translation: A kid hit me, and I angrily said, “Why are you bullying an adult?” The kid said, “You’re not an adult, you’re a delinquent youth!” My heart skipped a beat. Could he see my bad history? So I guiltily said, “What’s bad about me?” Unexpectedly, he killed me with one sentence: “You’re underdeveloped!”
functional_equivalence_translation: A kid hit me, so I snapped, “Why pick on a grown-up?” He said, “You’re not grown-up—you’re poorly grown up!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “不良,” which first sounds like “bad/delinquent” in “delinquent youth,” but the child actually means “underdeveloped” in “developmentally poor,” mocking the speaker’s small stature.
interpretation_1: 说话人先把“不良”理解为品行不好、有劣迹的意思。
interpretation_2: 小孩实际指的是“发育不良”，即身体发育不好、长得矮小。

surface_text: 这家饭店真下饭，菜特别下饭，老板聊天也很下饭。
hidden_form: 有意思、能让人配着吃饭
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“下饭”指菜品味道好、咸淡适中，很适合配米饭吃，容易让人多吃几口。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'xiàfàn' means the dishes go well with rice or make you want to eat more, so the restaurant and its food are very appetizing.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“下饭”指老板聊天风趣生动，吃饭时听着很有意思，提升了整体用餐体验。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, 'xiàfàn' is extended to mean highly enjoyable or entertaining; even the owner's conversation is so engaging that it feels as pleasing as something that makes a meal better.
context: 同一句中前两个“下饭”指菜适合配饭，后一个“下饭”转指老板聊天也很有吸引力。
negative_example: 这家饭店真下单，菜特别下单，老板聊天也很下单。
literal_translation: This restaurant is really good with rice; the dishes are especially good with rice, and even the boss's chatting is very good with rice.
functional_equivalence_translation: This restaurant is so appetizing—the dishes are great with rice, and even the owner’s conversation is oddly binge-worthy.
explanatory_translation: This restaurant is really “good with rice”: the dishes are appetizing to eat with rice, and the owner’s chatting is also called “xiafan,” using an extended internet sense meaning engaging enough to accompany a meal.
interpretation_1: 形容菜很适合配饭吃，很开胃。
interpretation_2: 借用网络语义，形容老板聊天内容有趣、吸引人，像能让人边看边吃一样。

surface_text: 这位策划真会铺，现场会铺陈，故事线也被他铺得很顺。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“铺”指策划在活动现场对物料、流程和空间做出完整铺陈与安排，层次清楚。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means this planner is very good at physically laying things out and arranging the on-site setup neatly.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“铺得很顺”指他在叙事设计上也能把故事线展开得自然流畅，不显生硬。
interpretation_2_en: The implied meaning is that he is also good at developing and unfolding the narrative structure smoothly, as in '铺陈' a story line well.
context: 策划人员既负责活动现场布置，也负责故事线或内容结构的展开，因此“铺”同时关联物理布置与叙事铺陈。
negative_example: 这位策划真会摆，现场会摆陈，故事线也被他摆得很顺。
literal_translation: This planner is really good at laying things out: he can lay out the venue, and he also laid out the storyline very smoothly.
functional_equivalence_translation: This planner really knows how to set things up—he set up the venue well, and set up the plot just as smoothly.
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on 铺, which can refer both to physically laying out the venue and to spreading out or developing a narrative, as in 铺陈.
interpretation_1: 指在现场进行布置、摊设和安排。
interpretation_2: 指在叙事中展开、组织和顺畅推进故事线。

surface_text: “大夫，我爹怎么样了？” “拿着这张纸，请遵遗嘱。” “啊，我爹走了？爹！你怎么就走了啊！” “我说的是请遵医嘱啦。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“请遵医嘱”听成了“请遵遗嘱”，意思变成要按照死者留下的遗嘱去办，因此让人误以为病人已经去世。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the doctor seems to say, "Please follow the will," which makes the listener think the father has died and left a last testament.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的真实意思是医生让家属按照医疗建议和处方办事，即“请遵医嘱”，并不表示病人已经死亡。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is actually, "Please follow the doctor's instructions," because "遗嘱" is a mistaken or sound-based shift from "医嘱."
context: 医院里，家属询问父亲病情，医生交给他一张纸并说一句话，家属将“医嘱”误解为“遗嘱”。
literal_translation: "Doctor, how is my dad?" "Take this paper and please follow the will." "Ah, my dad is gone? Dad! How could you leave!" "I said please follow the doctor's advice."
functional_equivalence_translation: "Doctor, how's my father?" "Take this note and follow the orders." "What? His last orders? Dad!" "No, I meant the doctor's orders."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the near-homophony between "医嘱" (doctor's instructions) and "遗嘱" (last will). The doctor means "follow the medical instructions," but the family member mishears it as "follow the will," assumes the father has died, and breaks down.
interpretation_1: 医生本意是让家属按照医嘱行事。
interpretation_2: 家属误听成按照遗嘱行事，以为病人已经去世。

surface_text: 康妮这几天非常繁忙，因为她要帮助丈夫竞选区工会副主席的职务。选举那天，正好遇到康妮出差，她特地在电话留言机中录了几句话：“亲爱的，祝你好运。不论选举结果如何，你永远都是我们家中的副主席。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指丈夫参加竞选的职位——区工会副主席，妻子祝他无论结果如何，家里也总有他这个“副主席”的位置。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she means that no matter whether he wins the election for vice chairman of the district union, he will always be the vice chairman in their family.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“副主席”借转为家庭中处于次要、从属地位的人，暗示妻子才像家里的“主席”，丈夫在家中只是“二把手”。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, she is joking that at home he is not the real boss; she is the actual head of the household, so he is only the 'vice chairman' there.
context: 丈夫正在竞选区工会副主席，妻子在电话留言中把同一称呼转用于家庭内部地位。
literal_translation: You will always be the vice chairman in our family.
functional_equivalence_translation: No matter how the election goes, you'll still be the vice-chair at home.
explanatory_translation: She jokes that even if he fails to win the union vice-chair position, he is still the “vice-chairman” at home, meaning he is only second-in-command in the family.
interpretation_1: 指丈夫竞选的区工会副主席这一正式职务。
interpretation_2: 指在家里并非当家作主的人，而是排在妻子之后的“副手”。

surface_text: 晚上睡觉，夫妻俩聊天。 老婆撒娇地说道：女人结婚前是珍珠， 结婚后就是鱼眼珠了！ 老公说：不对！ 结婚前是珍珠结婚后还是真猪！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层里“真猪”是字面意思，表示丈夫把妻子婚后调侃成真的猪，带有戏谑和贬损意味。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, the husband says that before marriage a woman is like a pearl, and after marriage she is still a real pig.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上是把“真猪”谐拟为“真珠”，承接前文“珍珠”，意思是妻子结婚后依然像珍珠一样珍贵，没有变差。
interpretation_2_en: The pun plays on 'zhen zhu': it sounds like 'pearl' (珍珠) but is shifted to 'real pig' (真猪), humorously insulting the wife by replacing the original compliment with a similar-sounding phrase.
context: 夫妻夜里聊天，妻子说女人婚前是“珍珠”、婚后成“鱼眼珠”，丈夫接着把“珍珠”转成“真猪”形成调侃。
literal_translation: At night before sleep, the couple were chatting. The wife said coquettishly: Before marriage, a woman is a pearl; after marriage, she becomes a fish eye! The husband said: No! Before marriage she is a pearl; after marriage she is still a real pig!
functional_equivalence_translation: The wife said, "Before marriage, a woman is a pearl; after marriage, just fish eyes." The husband replied, "Wrong—before marriage she's a pearl, and after marriage she's still a sow-called 'pearl'."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese near-sound between "珍珠" (pearl) and "真猪" (real pig). The husband twists the wife's flattering metaphor into an insulting one, saying that after marriage she is not a pearl but a "real pig."
interpretation_1: 妻子先用“珍珠”比喻女人婚前珍贵美丽。
interpretation_2: 丈夫把“珍珠”改听成“真猪”，戏称女人婚后像真的猪一样。

surface_text: 这家火锅店真有味道，锅里有味，老板说话也有味。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“有味”指火锅香气浓郁、滋味十足，让人一闻就有食欲，强调食物本身的风味出色。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'you wei' means the hotpot is flavorful: the soup in the pot has a strong and tasty flavor.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“有味”指老板谈吐风趣、个性鲜明，话里带着趣味和态度，强调人的表达也耐人寻味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the boss's way of speaking is also 'you wei,' meaning interesting, expressive, or full of personal charm, not literally about taste.
context: 同一句中前半说锅里食物有滋味，后半说老板说话有趣，形成同词不同义的并列。
literal_translation: This hotpot restaurant really has flavor: the pot has flavor, and even the boss's way of speaking has flavor.
functional_equivalence_translation: This hotpot place is full of flavor—the broth is tasty, and the owner is pretty flavorful too.
explanatory_translation: This hotpot restaurant really has 'flavor': the food is delicious, and the owner's speech is also 'flavorful,' meaning witty and interesting.
interpretation_1: 指火锅食物味道好、滋味足。
interpretation_2: 指老板说话风趣、有意思、有个人风格。

surface_text: 商场的折扣海报写着“省美主义”，买得克制一点，也要穿得好看一点。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是主张既省钱又追求美感的消费理念。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it advocates a consumption style that values both saving money and aesthetics.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义仿拟“审美主义”，把“审”替换为“省”，突出理性消费中的美学追求。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning parodies 'aestheticism' by replacing 'aesthetic' with 'saving', highlighting beauty within budget-conscious consumption.
context: 适用于服饰促销、消费观表达、品牌文案。
literal_translation: The mall's discount poster says 'save-aesthetic-ism': buy a bit more restrained, but still dress a bit better.
functional_equivalence_translation: The mall is selling 'budget chic'—spend smarter, still look better.
explanatory_translation: This coined term parodies 'aestheticism' by replacing the first morpheme with 'save'. The hybrid word simultaneously evokes thrift and taste, making it suitable for retail advertising.
interpretation_1: 省钱也要美
interpretation_2: 理性消费审美

surface_text: 经常听同事讲另一女同事他二姨，他二姨....以为他们是亲戚，后来才知他讲的是：猪八戒他二姨。
一同学被表扬后上台发言：“其实我未必是最好的，我未必是最优秀的，我未必是最聪明的，我未必是最努力的。大家好，我叫魏毕。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是这位同学自我介绍，说自己名字叫“魏毕”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the student is simply introducing himself after saying he may not be the best, the most outstanding, the smartest, or the hardest-working: 'Hello everyone, my name is Wei Bi.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“魏毕”与“未必”近音，前面连续说“我未必是……”是在为名字做铺垫，形成把名字说成“未必”的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'Wei Bi' sounds like '未必' ('not necessarily'), so his self-introduction humorously repeats and reinforces the phrase he has just used several times.
context: 同学被表扬后上台发言，连续重复“我未必是……”，最后补充“大家好，我叫魏毕”揭示姓名谐音。
literal_translation: After being praised, a student went on stage and said: “Actually, I may not be the best, I may not be the most outstanding, I may not be the smartest, and I may not be the most hardworking. Hello everyone, my name is Wei Bi.”
functional_equivalence_translation: After being praised, a student said on stage, “I’m not necessarily the best, not necessarily the brightest, not necessarily the most diligent. Hi everyone—I’m Wei Bi,” making his repeated “not necessarily” sound like his name.
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “未必” (wèibì, meaning “not necessarily”) and the name “魏毕” (also wèibì). The speaker keeps saying “未必,” and the final self-introduction reveals that the repeated phrase sounds exactly like his name.
interpretation_1: 前四句中的“未必”表示“不一定、未必如此”的否定性判断。
interpretation_2: 最后自我介绍“我叫魏毕”使前面的“未必”可被重新听成姓名“魏毕”。

surface_text: 期末周的图书馆简直像“卷命舱”，一进去不是续命，就是继续卷。
hidden_form: 救命舱 / 卷 / 续命
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是形容图书馆像一个让人靠学习硬撑下去的空间。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it describes the library as a place where students keep themselves going through studying.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义仿拟“救命舱”，把“卷”代入，表达期末高压下靠内卷求生的校园状态。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning parodies 'lifeboat' or 'rescue pod' by replacing it with 'grind/compete,' suggesting students survive finals through intense academic competition.
context: 适用于校园吐槽、考试周段子、社交媒体配文。
literal_translation: During finals week, the library is basically a 'grind-life pod': once you enter, you're either saving your life or continuing to grind.
functional_equivalence_translation: In finals week, the library turns into a survival pod—you go in either to stay alive or to keep grinding.
explanatory_translation: The pun is built by parodying a rescue-related expression and replacing one morpheme with '卷' (the Chinese slang for over-competition). It creates a hybrid word that simultaneously suggests survival and academic grinding.
interpretation_1: 学习续命空间
interpretation_2: 内卷求生

surface_text: 一大妈来电器店买东西，赖着讲价，于是店主掏出手机， 打开我查查，扫下条码，指着我查查上的价格对大妈说：“你看， 我给你便宜了的，网上还卖的贵些。”大妈一听， 眉头一紧说一句：“啥？晚上还要卖贵些？那我不买了， 白天来！白天……来…”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中大妈把“网上”听成了“晚上”，理解成到了夜里价格会更贵，所以说白天再来买。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the aunt mishears it as “at night it is sold at a higher price,” so she says she will not buy it now and will come during the daytime instead.
interpretation_2_zh: 原本店主想表达的是“网上”售价更高，即网络平台上的价格比店里更贵，并不是指晚上这个时间段。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is actually “online it is sold at a higher price” (“网上” meaning on the internet), but she mistakes “online” for “at night” (“晚上”), which creates the pun.
context: 店主在电器店用“我查查”扫码后说“网上还卖的贵些”，顾客将“网上”误听为“晚上”。
literal_translation: A middle-aged woman came to an appliance store to buy something and kept bargaining. The shop owner took out his phone, opened a price-checking app, scanned the barcode, and pointed to the price on the app, saying, “Look, I’ve already given you a cheaper price. It’s even sold for more online.” Hearing this, the woman frowned and said, “What? It costs more at night? Then I won’t buy it. I’ll come in the daytime! Daytime...”
functional_equivalence_translation: The owner said, “It’s even pricier online,” but the woman misheard it as, “It’s pricier at night,” and replied, “Then I’ll come during the day!”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the Chinese near-homophones “网上” (online) and “晚上” (at night). The shop owner means the product is more expensive on the internet, but the woman mishears it as being more expensive at night, so she decides to come back in the daytime.
interpretation_1: 店主说的是网络平台上的价格更贵。
interpretation_2: 大妈误听成晚上卖得更贵，以为价格按白天晚上变化。

surface_text: 小名的爸爸拿着一本书，要给小名讲故事，可是小明却理也不理爸爸，只顾自己看电视。 爸爸气极了，说：你快看我呀，你不看我，怎么知道非洲野猪长什么样呀？
在一个村里，有一个妇女生了两个孩子，一个叫地球，一个叫屁股。 一天，地球和屁股出去玩，玩着玩着，屁股不见了，妈妈去报警：“我的儿子不见了。” 警察问：“叫什么名？”“叫屁股。” 警察愣了一下，问：“他有多大？”“跟地球一样大。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是在说孩子名叫“地球”，失踪的孩子名叫“屁股”，所以“他有多大”被回答为“跟地球一样大”，意思是和另一个孩子差不多大。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, this is a story about a woman whose child is literally named 'Butt.' When the police ask how big the missing child is, she says he is 'as big as the Earth,' taking both 'Butt' and 'Earth' as the names of her two children.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上激活了“屁股”和人体部位“屁股”的常见意义，于是“跟地球一样大”就被理解成把屁股夸张地说成像地球那么大，形成荒诞效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from reading 'butt' as an actual buttocks and 'Earth' as the real planet. Then 'the butt is as big as the Earth' becomes an absurd and shocking statement, which creates the joke.
context: 两名孩子分别被取名为“地球”和“屁股”，警察问失踪的“屁股”有多大，母亲回答“跟地球一样大”。
literal_translation: As big as the Earth.
functional_equivalence_translation: He’s as big as Earth.
explanatory_translation: Because one child is named Earth and the missing child is named Butt, the mother’s answer literally means the child named Butt is the same size as the child named Earth, but it also sounds like “a butt as big as the Earth.”
interpretation_1: 按故事设定，失踪孩子名叫屁股，另一个孩子名叫地球，所以意思是屁股的个头和地球一样大。
interpretation_2: 脱离名字语境时，会被理解为字面上的屁股大到和地球一样，形成荒诞效果。

surface_text: 这首歌很洗脑，旋律洗脑，评论区也跟着一起洗脑。
hidden_form: 被歌曲带动而重复同样的话
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“洗脑”指旋律重复性强、记忆点突出，让人听后一直在脑中循环，难以忘记。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "brainwashing" describes the song's melody as so catchy and repetitive that it gets stuck in people's heads, and the comment section also repeats the same reaction.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“洗脑”指评论区大量重复同类说法，持续强化某种印象，使读者容易被带节奏。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "brainwashing" shifts toward its literal sense of influencing people's minds: not only the melody, but also the comments collectively reinforce the song's influence and spread the same impression among listeners.
context: 前半句说歌的旋律很洗脑，后半句把“洗脑”延伸到评论区的跟风重复表现。
negative_example: 这首歌很上头，评论区也很热闹。
literal_translation: This song is very brainwashing; the melody is brainwashing, and the comment section also follows along and gets brainwashed.
functional_equivalence_translation: This song is insanely catchy—the melody is addictive, and even the comment section joins in like they’ve all been brainwashed.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “洗脑,” which first means the melody is so catchy it keeps looping in one’s mind, and then extends to the comment section, where people echo and repeat things as if they too were “brainwashed.”
interpretation_1: 歌曲旋律极强传播性，听后在脑中反复回响。
interpretation_2: 评论区用户也被带动，出现重复、跟风式发言，像一起被“洗脑”。

surface_text: 这家咖啡店主打“醒价比”，一杯下去，人醒了，价格也挺有道理。
interpretation_1_zh: 把咖啡的提神效果和价格评价拼接起来，表示既能让人清醒又划算。
interpretation_1_en: A blended expression meaning the coffee both wakes you up and offers good value for money.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含激活常用词“性价比”，借其评价框架来夸产品值得买。
interpretation_2_en: It invokes the common term 'cost-performance ratio' to suggest the product is worth buying.
context: 适用于咖啡、功能饮料等强调提神与价格优势的广告语。
negative_example: 这家咖啡店性价比很高。
literal_translation: This coffee shop specializes in 'wake-price ratio'; one cup wakes you up, and the price also makes sense.
functional_equivalence_translation: This cafe offers great bang-for-your-buzz.
explanatory_translation: The pun blends '醒' (to wake up) into the familiar expression '性价比' (value for money), creating a new product-evaluation term for coffee.
interpretation_1: 提神又划算
interpretation_2: 借性价比夸值

surface_text: 小张和小明吵架，小明说；“你这个2b，怎么什么都不懂啊。” 小情刚好路过听到了，说了一句：“你是2b人家铅笔还不愿意了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层里“2b”被理解成铅笔的型号，后一句是在说你就算是2B，人家铅笔也不愿意，把人和铅笔并置来调侃。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “2B” is understood literally as the pencil grade 2B, so the reply jokes that even a 2B pencil would not want to be associated with him.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里“小明”原本是用“2b”谐指“二逼”，是在骂对方愚蠢、不开窍。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that “2B” is slang for an idiot or a foolish person, so the sentence is really an insult, and the reply plays on the double meaning to mock him back.
context: 前文中“小明”用“2b”骂人，后文“小情”把“2b”故意按“2B铅笔”来理解并接话。
literal_translation: Zhang and Ming had a quarrel. Ming said, “You 2B, why do you understand nothing?” Xiaoqing happened to pass by and said, “If you are 2B, even the pencil wouldn’t agree.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Zhang and Ming were arguing. Ming snapped, “You idiot!” A passerby quipped, “An idiot? Even the pencil marked 2B wouldn’t want that title.”
explanatory_translation: In Chinese internet slang, “2B” can insult someone as stupid, but it is also the standard label for a 2B pencil. The joke comes from taking the insult literally as the pencil grade.
interpretation_1: 作为骂人的网络用语，指人很蠢、很二。
interpretation_2: 字面上被理解为铅笔的硬度型号“2B”，指2B铅笔。

surface_text: 小明：出个对联，很简单，我说上联你说下联，上联：在上不是南北。下联？？ 小华：…… 在下不是东西吧。 ……
一对夫妇质问一家商店经理说：“上星期，我们在这里买了一个象牙盒，经鉴定，是假象牙制成的。” 经理说：“在当前科技条件下，大象安装假牙，也是非常有可能的。”
interpretation_1_zh: 经理把“假象牙”故意理解成“大象的假牙”，说成在科技条件下大象装假牙也有可能。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the manager says that with current technology, it is quite possible for an elephant to be fitted with false teeth.
interpretation_2_zh: 顾客原本的意思是这个盒子不是用真象牙做的，而是用仿制材料制成的“假象牙”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the complaint about 'fake ivory': instead of admitting the box is made of imitation ivory, the manager twists it into the absurd idea that the ivory could have come from an elephant's dentures.
context: 顾客投诉“象牙盒”经鉴定是“假象牙制成的”，经理故意曲解为“大象安装假牙”。
literal_translation: A couple questioned a shop manager: “Last week, we bought an ivory box here. After appraisal, it turned out to be made of fake ivory.” The manager said: “With current technology, it is very possible for an elephant to have false teeth installed too.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A couple complained, “The ivory box we bought here turned out to be imitation ivory.” The manager replied, “Well, these days, even elephants could probably get dentures.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the manager deliberately reinterpreting “fake ivory” as “an elephant’s false teeth.” The customers mean the box is made from imitation ivory, but he twists the phrase to evade the complaint.
interpretation_1: 经理把“假象牙”故意转成“大象的假牙”来理解。
interpretation_2: 顾客原本说的是“盒子不是象牙制的，而是仿制象牙”。

surface_text: 食人族族长生了一种病，医生说：“是吃肉太多引起的，要多吃植物。” 从此，食人族组长做了个决定：不吃普通人，只吃植物人！！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“植物人”按字面理解为像植物一样的人，因此族长决定不吃普通人，改吃“植物人”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the doctor means he should eat more plant-based foods, so the chief decides to stop eating ordinary people and eat "vegetative people" instead.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上医生原本是劝他多吃植物、少吃肉，“植物人”借用了“植物”的字面成分，造成从“吃植物”偏移到“吃植物人”的荒诞双关。
interpretation_2_en: The pun hinges on "植物人": it normally means a person in a vegetative state, but it is humorously reinterpreted as a "plant-person," as if such a person counted as a plant he was advised to eat.
context: 医生建议食人族族长“要多吃植物”，族长随后把“植物”错误套用到“植物人”上，形成字面与常用义的偏移。
literal_translation: The cannibal chief decided not to eat ordinary people, only vegetative people.
functional_equivalence_translation: The doctor said, “Eat more greens,” so the cannibal chief decided to stop eating normal people and eat only “vegetables” instead—meaning people in a vegetative state.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “植物人,” which normally means “a person in a vegetative state,” but is misread literally as “plant-person,” letting the cannibal twist “eat more plants” into “eat vegetative patients.”
interpretation_1: 指医学上处于持续性无意识状态的病人。
interpretation_2: 被字面拆解为“植物”和“人”，理解成和植物有关、可作为“多吃植物”的对象。

surface_text: 小兔说：“我妈妈叫我小兔兔，好听！” 小猪说：“我妈妈叫我小猪猪，也好听！” 小狗说：“我妈妈叫我小狗狗，也很好听！” 小鸡说：“我妈妈叫我小鸡鸡！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是按照前面“小兔兔、小猪猪、小狗狗”的昵称格式，小鸡说妈妈叫自己“小鸡鸡”，是在重复“鸡”字形成可爱的称呼。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the chick says that its mother calls it “little chicky,” following the same cute repeated naming pattern as the other baby animals.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“鸡鸡”在中文口语里也常指男性生殖器，因此“小鸡鸡”会额外触发带有性意味的联想，形成笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that “小鸡鸡” is also a childish slang term for male genitals, so the phrase suddenly sounds sexually suggestive and creates the joke.
context: 前面连续出现“小兔兔”“小猪猪”“小狗狗”等动物昵称叠词，最后轮到“小鸡鸡”时因“鸡鸡”的口语转义形成双关
literal_translation: The little chick said, “My mom calls me little chick-chick!”
functional_equivalence_translation: The chick said, “My mom calls me chickie-willie!”
explanatory_translation: The joke is that “little chick-chick” follows the cute reduplication pattern, but the second part sounds like a childish slang term for a penis, creating an awkward double meaning.
interpretation_1: 按前文叠词昵称模式，指小鸡被妈妈亲昵地叫作“小鸡鸡”
interpretation_2: “鸡鸡”在口语中可指男性生殖器，因此引发猥亵、尴尬的另一层理解

surface_text: 可不久这个人又谈起了恋爱，而且谈的很起劲。 于是他朋友问他，你不是说女人是毒药吗？怎么又谈起来了？ 这人回答说：自从上次失恋后，老想服毒自杀！
教练拿海绵棒在他头上轻轻敲了一下，队友笑说这可真是当头一棒。
公园里两人正在谈论打麻将怎样才能常赢。 A：孙子说，“知己知彼，百战百胜。” B：你孙子才满月，也懂这个？
H君与朋友进入一家高档商场。 进了店门后才走了两步， 朋友忽见他在光滑的大理石地面上作滑冰状，甚感奇怪。 问他，H君一边继续滑一边指着旁边的牌子， 认真地说：“既然来了，就要遵守这儿的规矩。” 那牌子上写着：“小心地滑“。
interpretation_1_zh: 把“地滑”误解为动词性说法，理解成要小心地滑行，所以H君模仿滑冰动作前进。
interpretation_1_en: Taken literally, the sign says 'carefully slide on the floor,' so H acts as if he should move by sliding like skating.
interpretation_2_zh: 牌子本来的意思是“地面很滑，要小心”，是在提醒顾客注意行走安全。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is 'Caution: the floor is slippery,' warning people to walk carefully because the ground is slick.
context: 商场里有一块写着“小心地滑”的提示牌，正常应理解为“地面湿滑请小心”，人物却把“地滑”理解为动作方式相关表达。
literal_translation: "Be careful, the floor is slippery."
functional_equivalence_translation: "If we’re here, we should follow the rule: slide carefully."
explanatory_translation: The sign normally means “Caution: slippery floor,” but H reads it as if it were telling people to “slide carefully,” which creates the pun.
interpretation_1: 牌子的常规意思是提醒顾客注意地面很滑，不要摔倒。
interpretation_2: H君把它误读成要求人要小心地去滑行，于是做出滑冰动作。

surface_text: 我们全家到朋友家做客，朋友向我们隆重介绍他刚刚得到的名狗，并让我们看了狗食、狗餐具、两室一厅的狗屋、专用的狗浴盆…… 看完之后，儿子不禁羡慕起来：“叔叔，你们家尽是些狗东西啊！”
interpretation_1_zh: 这里的“狗东西”按字面可理解为“与狗有关的各种东西”，指狗食、狗餐具、狗屋、狗浴盆等一整套宠物用品。
interpretation_1_en: Here, "dog things" literally means all the items belonging to or used by the dog, such as dog food, utensils, the dog house, and the bath tub.
interpretation_2_zh: “狗东西”在汉语里也常作为骂人的贬义说法，儿子这句话在称赞狗用品很多的同时，也无意中触发了把对方家说成“尽是些讨厌家伙”的歧义。
interpretation_2_en: It also activates the insulting Chinese expression "gou dongxi," meaning "bastards" or "damn things," so the child’s words sound like a rude insult toward the host’s household.
context: 朋友炫耀自家名狗及其配套用品，儿子总结说家里尽是“狗东西”，既可指狗的物品，也会触发骂人义
literal_translation: Uncle, your home is full of dog things.
functional_equivalence_translation: Uncle, your house is full of dog stuff—what a bunch of "mongrels," huh?
explanatory_translation: The child says “your home is full of dog things,” where “dog things” literally means items for the dog, but in Chinese “狗东西” is also a common insult meaning a nasty person or wretch.
interpretation_1: 与狗有关的各种东西、狗用品
interpretation_2: 骂人的话，指讨厌的家伙或不是东西的人

surface_text: 数学老师写道：”亲爱的，你是正数，我便是负数，我们都是有理数，该是天生的一对啊。” 对方回信：“亲爱的，如果结婚后我做出了无理的事，也还是有理的吧？”
一天，小明和他的爸爸去旅游，小明的爸爸说：“咱们明天坐动车去。” 小明说：“我才不去呢。”爸爸问他为什么，小明说：“那我们还不要冻死。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中小明把“动车”的“动”理解成了“冻”，于是认为要坐的是“冻车”，会被冻死，所以说不去。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child misunderstands '动车' as if it meant 'a freezing vehicle,' so he says he does not want to go because they would be frozen to death.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是爸爸原本说的是“动车”，指高速列车的一种，并没有寒冷、会冻死的意思；笑点来自“动”和“冻”的近音替换。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '动车' actually means a high-speed train unit or bullet train, and the child is making a pun by taking the sound 'dong' as '冻' ('freeze').
context: 父亲说“明天坐动车去”，孩子回应“那我们还不要冻死”，由“冻”触发对“动车”的谐音误解。
literal_translation: One day, Xiaoming and his father were going on a trip. His father said, “We’ll take the EMU train tomorrow.” Xiaoming said, “I’m not going.” His father asked why, and Xiaoming said, “Then wouldn’t we freeze to death?”
functional_equivalence_translation: Dad said, “We’ll take the train tomorrow.” Xiaoming said, “No way.” “Why not?” Dad asked. Xiaoming replied, “Because if it’s a ‘freeze train,’ we’ll freeze to death!”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “动车” (dongche, EMU/high-speed train) and the imagined “冻车” (dongche, literally ‘freezing vehicle’). They sound the same in Chinese, so Xiaoming humorously misunderstands the word and thinks the ride will make them freeze.
interpretation_1: 爸爸说明天要坐动车，即高速列车。
interpretation_2: 小明把“动车”误解成“冻车”，以为是会把人冻着的车。

surface_text: 这家旅行社主打周末短线，口号叫“说走就周”，请假的门槛太高，那就先把周末过成远方。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是到了周末就立刻出发，突出短途旅行的即时性。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means setting off as soon as the weekend comes, highlighting instant short trips.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是仿拟“说走就走”，把原本任性的旅行理想压缩到可执行的周末方案中。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning imitates 'leave whenever you want,' compressing that spontaneous travel ideal into a practical weekend plan.
context: 适用于旅行推广、城市周边游、生活方式营销。
negative_example: 周末说走就走地去旅行。
literal_translation: This travel agency focuses on weekend short trips, with the slogan 'go as soon as it's the week-end'; taking leave is too hard, so turn your weekend into a faraway place first.
functional_equivalence_translation: Their pitch is simple: if you can't take a long trip, make your weekend your getaway.
explanatory_translation: The slogan parodies the fixed phrase 'leave on a whim' by replacing the final morpheme with 'week/weekend,' creating a hybrid expression tied specifically to weekend travel.
interpretation_1: 周末即刻出发
interpretation_2: 仿拟说走就走

surface_text: 这款学习软件号称能帮你进入“稳绩态”，今天背单词，明天看成绩。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指学习状态稳定、成绩也相对稳定提升的状态。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a stable learning condition that also leads to steady grades.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用“稳态”这一术语，把学习成果包装成一种可持续维持的理想模式。
interpretation_2_en: It also borrows the term 'steady state' and adapts it to academic performance as if good grades were a stable system.
context: 适用于教育产品宣传、学习工具广告。
negative_example: 这款软件能帮助你稳定成绩。
literal_translation: This learning app claims it can help you enter a 'stable-grade state': memorize words today, see results tomorrow.
functional_equivalence_translation: This app promises to get you into a steady-study, steady-grades mode.
explanatory_translation: The pun grafts '成绩' (grades) onto the technical-looking word pattern '稳态' (steady state), creating a polished educational buzzword.
interpretation_1: 学习稳定出成绩
interpretation_2: 借稳态概念包装

surface_text: 最要好的朋友对我说想恋爱了，我就带一个漂亮的MM介绍他认识，我向MM介绍我朋友说：“我朋友不仅高帅富，最重要的是他很善解人意。” MM惊叫地说：“善解人衣？可够色的啊。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是夸这个朋友体贴、会理解别人心意，很会照顾他人感受。
interpretation_1_en: It means he is very thoughtful and understanding, someone who knows how to understand other people's feelings and intentions.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“意”谐转为“衣”，理解成很会解开别人的衣服，带有好色、轻佻的玩笑意味。
interpretation_2_en: It is twisted into a similar-sounding phrase meaning 'good at taking off people's clothes,' implying that he is lecherous or sexually forward.
context: 男子向MM夸朋友“很善解人意”，对方将“意”误解为同音的“衣”而产生歧义
literal_translation: I introduced my friend to the girl by saying, “My friend is not only tall, handsome, and rich; most importantly, he is very understanding.” The girl exclaimed, “Understanding people’s clothes? That’s pretty pervy.”
functional_equivalence_translation: I said, “He’s not just tall, handsome, and rich—he’s also very understanding.” She gasped, “Understanding? You mean undressing? What a perv!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese phrase “善解人意” (good at understanding others) being misheard as the homophone “善解人衣” (good at taking off others’ clothes), creating a sexual pun.
interpretation_1: 很会体察并理解别人的心意
interpretation_2: 被误听成很会脱别人的衣服，带有色情调侃意味

surface_text: 一天，小明的奶奶正在家里与邻居李奶奶坐在沙发上聊天。过了一段时间，小明的奶奶痛苦地对李奶奶说：“他李奶，你说这也怪了，我这腰一坐久了就疼，我还是站着和你说会话吧。” 李奶奶不解的说：“怎么回事？” 小明急忙向李奶解释道：“李奶奶，我奶奶的意思是‘她站着说话不腰疼’！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是奶奶因为坐久了腰疼，所以想站起来继续聊天，这样腰会舒服一些。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, Grandma says that when she sits for too long her waist hurts, so she would rather stand while talking because standing does not make her waist hurt as much.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借用了俗语“站着说话不腰疼”，表面说自己站着后腰不疼，实际上激活了这句熟语的固定说法，形成戏谑效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning activates the Chinese saying 'standing and talking without a backache,' which means speaking lightly about someone else's difficulty because you are not the one suffering.
context: 奶奶先说“我这腰一坐久了就疼，我还是站着和你说会话吧”，随后小明将其解释为俗语“她站着说话不腰疼”。
literal_translation: She said she would stand and talk, so her waist would not hurt.
functional_equivalence_translation: Grandma meant, jokingly, that she can be one of those people who “talk standing up and don’t feel the back pain.”
explanatory_translation: The pun comes from turning Grandma’s literal remark “I’ll stand and keep talking because sitting makes my waist hurt” into the Chinese saying “standing and talking without a hurting waist,” which means speaking lightly because one does not share the other person’s discomfort.
interpretation_1: 奶奶表面上是说自己坐久了腰疼，所以想站起来继续聊天。
interpretation_2: 小明把奶奶的话理解并改写成俗语，带出“站着说话的人不体会腰疼者的难处”的调侃意味。

surface_text: 这家火锅店真会烫，菜烫得香，账单也烫得我手一抖。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“烫”指火锅食材在滚汤中煮得恰到好处，热气腾腾且味道鲜香十足。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '烫' means the hotpot food is very hot in temperature, cooked steaming hot and tasting great.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“烫”借夸张指账单金额高得刺手，让人付款时心里一紧，有被“烫到”的感觉。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '烫' also suggests the bill is shockingly expensive, so high that it makes the speaker's hand tremble when paying.
context: 同一句中先说火锅菜品“烫得香”，后说“账单也烫得我手一抖”，将温度义与价格高义并列触发。
negative_example: 这家火锅店真会辣，菜辣得香，账单也辣得我手一抖。
literal_translation: This hotpot restaurant really knows how to be hot: the food is hot and fragrant, and the bill was so hot that my hand shook.
functional_equivalence_translation: This hotpot place is really good at serving heat—the food came out sizzling, and the bill was scorching too.
explanatory_translation: This hotpot restaurant really knows how to be “hot”: the dishes are literally piping hot, while the bill is figuratively “too hot to handle,” meaning shockingly expensive.
interpretation_1: 指火锅和菜品温度高、很烫。
interpretation_2: 指账单金额高得让人吃惊，像烫手一样难以承受。

surface_text: 元世祖至元年间，元人进入南宋都城杭州，南宋朝廷宗庙被洗劫一空。当时有个姓金的，世代为伶官，流离失所，无家可归。一天，金某在路上遇见左丞范文虎。范文虎在宋朝为殿帅时，就与金某熟识。他见了金某说：过几天朝廷举行宴会，你来献技，不愁没有吃穿。 后来金某如期前往，在宴会上表演优戏，插科打诨说：某寺里有座大钟，但一连几天，寺奴都不敢敲这口钟。主僧询问原因，寺奴说：‘近 来钟楼上有位巨神，样子很怪，我不敢上楼。’主僧连忙去看。那巨神见了主僧，立刻倒身下拜。主僧问：‘你是何神？’巨神答道：‘钟神。’主僧反问道：‘你既是钟神（忠臣），为何还下拜？’
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是寺庙钟楼里的神灵，自称掌管大钟的神，所以说自己是“钟神”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '钟神' means the spirit or god of the bell, since the story is about a big bell in a temple and a strange giant appearing on the bell tower.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借“钟神”谐指“忠臣”，主僧反问“既是忠臣，为何还下拜”，是在讥讽所谓忠臣面对新朝却屈身下拜、不守忠节。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is '忠臣' (loyal minister), which has the same pronunciation as '钟神' in Chinese. The joke asks: if you are truly a loyal subject, why are you bowing to the conquerors?
context: 宴会上优人讲笑话：钟楼上有一位自称“钟神”的巨神，主僧追问“你既是钟神，为何还下拜”，由“钟神”联想到“忠臣”
literal_translation: "Bell god."
functional_equivalence_translation: "I am the bell god" / "the loyal minister".
explanatory_translation: “钟神”字面是“bell god”，但在此借与“忠臣”近音形成双关，讽刺所谓忠臣在异族统治下仍然屈身下拜。
interpretation_1: 字面上指钟楼或大钟之神
interpretation_2: 借谐音暗指忠于前朝的臣子

surface_text: 公司招聘打字员。 经理问：小姐你有特长吗？ 小姐说：有。 经理问：什么特长？ 小姐说：头发！
interpretation_1_zh: 经理问“特长”是指有什么擅长的技能或专长，小姐却理解成“特别长的地方”，于是回答自己的头发很长。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the manager asks whether she has any special skills or strengths for the typing job, but she answers that her strong point is her hair, interpreting 'specialty' as a physical feature.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐藏义是把“特长”从“专长、技能”转成“特别长”，形成对词语结构的歧义利用，笑点在于答非所问。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '特长' is supposed to mean a particular skill or expertise, such as typing ability, but the woman deliberately or mistakenly shifts it to mean something literally 'especially long'—her hair.
context: 公司招聘打字员，经理询问应聘者是否有特长，应聘者回答“头发”。
literal_translation: The company was hiring a typist. The manager asked, “Miss, do you have any specialty?” She said, “Yes.” The manager asked, “What specialty?” She said, “Hair!”
functional_equivalence_translation: The company was hiring a typist. The manager asked, “Do you have any strong points?” She replied, “Yes—my hair is very long.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “特长,” which normally means “special skill,” but can be reinterpreted literally as “especially long.” So the manager asks about job skills, while the woman answers that her hair is long.
interpretation_1: 经理问的是应聘者有什么擅长的技能或专长。
interpretation_2: 小姐把“特长”理解成“特别长”，指自己的头发很长。

surface_text: 我最近的消费观是“能省则购”，该克制的时候克制，该下单的时候也绝不含糊。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是购买前会精打细算，争取以省钱方式购物。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means shopping with careful budgeting and trying to save money while buying.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“能省则省”，调侃自己看似节制，实则总能找到下单理由。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it imitates 'save whenever possible,' joking that one always finds a reason to buy anyway.
context: 适用于消费吐槽、网购文案、社交平台自嘲表达。
literal_translation: My recent spending philosophy is 'buy whenever saving is possible': restrain myself when I should, and place orders without hesitation when I should too.
functional_equivalence_translation: My budgeting logic is basically: save smart so I can shop guilt-free.
explanatory_translation: The phrase remodels the common saying 'save whenever possible' by swapping the final word with 'buy,' making it mean both frugal shopping and self-mocking rationalized consumption.
interpretation_1: 省着买
interpretation_2: 找理由购物

surface_text: 我打开小张的作业本，只见上面写着：Yes,it is 爷死，一踢一死。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把英文短语“Yes, it is”用汉字谐音记成“爷死，一踢一死”，呈现出作业本上用中文音译英语的滑稽写法。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the notebook literally writes the Chinese phrases “爷死，一踢一死,” as if they were the content of the sentence.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是学生本来想写或表达标准英文“Yes, it is”，但用近似汉字替代其读音，形成“爷死，一踢一死”的谐音双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the English sentence “Yes, it is,” which these Chinese characters awkwardly imitate by sound, creating a phonetic pun based on miswritten English.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境
literal_translation: I opened Xiao Zhang's workbook and saw written on it: “Yes, it is” — “grandpa dies, one kick one dies.”
functional_equivalence_translation: I opened Xiao Zhang’s homework and saw: “Yes, it is,” humorously written as a Chinese sound-alike phrase with absurd meaning.
explanatory_translation: I opened Xiao Zhang’s workbook and found “Yes, it is” rendered in Chinese characters as “爷死，一踢一死,” a phonetic joke where the Chinese phrase sounds like the English but means something nonsensical.
interpretation_1: 作业本上把英文短语“Yes, it is”写出来。
interpretation_2: 用汉字按读音戏仿英文，形成“爷死，一踢一死”的荒诞中文意思。

surface_text: 弟弟对正在玩电脑的姐姐说：“姐姐，姐姐，妈妈说人的眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴和耳朵是连通的。” 姐姐盯着电脑屏幕头也不回的说：“那什么是电信的？”
interpretation_1_zh: 这里的“连通”表层上是指人的眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴和耳朵彼此相连、相通。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'connected' means that the eyes, nose, mouth, and ears are physically linked as parts of the human face.
interpretation_2_zh: 姐姐把“连通”听成了“联通”，联想到与“电信”并列的通信运营商“联通”，所以才反问“那什么是电信的”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning shifts 'connected' to the telecom sense of having network service or being linked by a communications provider, which is why the sister jokes by asking what would count as 'telecom's'.
context: 弟弟说“人的眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴和耳朵是连通的”，姐姐因正在玩电脑而把“连通”联想到“联通”，再对应提出“电信”。
literal_translation: The younger brother said to his sister who was playing on the computer, “Sis, Mom says that people’s eyes, nose, mouth, and ears are connected.” Without taking her eyes off the screen, the sister replied, “Then which one is China Telecom’s?”
functional_equivalence_translation: “Mom says the eyes, nose, mouth, and ears are all connected.” “Connected? Then which part belongs to China Unicom, and which to China Telecom?”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on 连通 meaning “connected” and 联通, the homophonous name of China Unicom. Because the sister is distracted by the computer, she hears 连通 as 联通 and jokes by bringing up another telecom company, China Telecom.
interpretation_1: 指人的眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴和耳朵彼此相连、相通。
interpretation_2: 被姐姐误听并联想到通信运营商品牌“中国联通”，进而问“那什么是电信的”。

surface_text: 请小王和小李的父母进来。
银行传播很广的一个笑话。经办员：您好，请问您办什么业务？ 客户：哦，我存一个死期(整存整取)！ 经办员：那请问您死多久？ 客户：嗯，死一年！
她真会拿捏，妆容拿捏得准，气氛也总被她拿捏住。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“拿捏”指她对妆容的色彩、浓淡和风格控制精准，效果恰到好处不过分。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '拿捏' means to handle something with precision, as in doing her makeup accurately and skillfully.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“拿捏”指她善于掌控人与人之间的气氛变化，让场面按她期待的方式发展。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that she is also good at controlling or managing people and the atmosphere, as '拿捏' can mean to keep something under control or manipulate it effectively.
context: 同一句中先说“妆容拿捏得准”，再说“气氛也总被她拿捏住”，并置激活“分寸把握”和“局面掌控”两层义。
literal_translation: She really knows how to handle things: she gets the makeup just right, and she always has the atmosphere in her grasp.
functional_equivalence_translation: She really knows how to nail it—her makeup is perfectly on point, and she can also command the whole vibe.
explanatory_translation: She is very good at “na nie,” which in the first part means getting the makeup balance exactly right, and in the second part means controlling or steering the overall atmosphere.
interpretation_1: 指对妆容分寸把握得很准。
interpretation_2: 指对场面气氛有很强的控制和调动能力。

surface_text: 深夜12点，两青年正在热恋当中，忽然有人敲门，两人紧张的松开对方，只见穿着警服的两人站在门口。 “什么事？刚才有人查过了，户口本、身份证、计划生育证……证件齐全。” 来人中其中一人道：不是查证，是收税！ 男：收费？卫生费、水费、电费、管理费都交过了，在银行代扣，你们找银行吧？ 另一人解释：不是收费，是收税的！ 女：收睡的？我们歌唱了，舞也跳了，酒也喝了，亲也亲了，还就是没有睡，你去别处收去吧！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中女子把“收税”误听成“收睡”，理解为有人来管别人是否睡觉、要来“收睡”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the woman mishears it as 'collecting for sleeping' and says they have sung, danced, drunk, and kissed, but have not actually slept together, so the officers should go collect it somewhere else.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是来人真正说的是“收税的”，意思是征收税款，并不是与“睡觉”有关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is 'collecting taxes.' The phrase '收税' sounds similar to '收睡,' which creates the pun and leads to the comic misunderstanding.
context: 深夜一对情侣在屋内，门外来人表明“不是查证，是收税”，女子将“收税”误解为“收睡”。
literal_translation: “Not collecting certificates, but collecting tax.” “Collecting sleep? We sang, danced, drank, and kissed, but we still haven’t slept.”
functional_equivalence_translation: "We’re not here to check papers—we’re here for dues." "For doze? We did everything tonight except actually doze off!"
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the Chinese homophone “收税” (collect tax) and “收睡” (collect sleep). The woman deliberately or comically mishears “tax collection” as something about whether they have slept together.
interpretation_1: 来人说的是征收税款。
interpretation_2: 女子误听成“收睡”，理解为来人是来管他们是否睡觉或索要“睡”。

surface_text: 这家店真会抓人，橱窗能抓人，店员的话也很抓人。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“抓人”指橱窗设计醒目吸睛，能够迅速抓住路人的视线和注意力，促使人停下。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the shop is good at literally 'grabbing' people: the display window attracts passersby, and the clerk's words also pull people in.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“抓人”指店员表达生动、有感染力，说话内容容易打动顾客并引发购买兴趣。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '抓人' also means highly appealing or captivating, so both the window display and the salesperson's speech are very engaging.
context: 橱窗设计和店员话术都很能吸引顾客，因此“抓人”同时激活字面“抓住人”和引申“吸引人”。
negative_example: 这家店真会招人，橱窗能招人，店员的话也很招人。
literal_translation: This shop really knows how to catch people: the display window catches people, and the clerk's words also catch people.
functional_equivalence_translation: This shop really knows how to hook people—the window display hooks you, and so does the sales talk.
explanatory_translation: This shop is very good at attracting people: the window display is eye-catching, and the clerk's words are also very compelling. The pun hinges on “抓人,” which can mean both “to seize/catch someone” literally and “to be highly attractive” figuratively.
interpretation_1: 字面上指把人抓住、攫住。
interpretation_2: 实际指很有吸引力、很能打动顾客。

surface_text: 我请了医生和护士的家属参加说明会。
他真会带节奏，鼓点会带节奏，发言也总能带节奏。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“带节奏”指他在音乐中掌控鼓点和拍子，能把现场气氛和表演步调带动起来。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means keeping or leading the rhythm, as a drumbeat does in music.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“带节奏”指他发言善于影响舆论方向，引导他人情绪和观点朝某个方向发展。
interpretation_2_en: It also means steering the mood or direction of a discussion through one's speech, influencing how others react or think.
context: 同一句中先说鼓点会带节奏，再说发言也总能带节奏，使音乐义与舆论义并列激活。
literal_translation: He really knows how to set the rhythm: drumbeats can set the rhythm, and his speeches always set the rhythm too.
functional_equivalence_translation: He really knows how to drive the beat—on the drums, and in conversation he always knows how to steer the crowd.
explanatory_translation: He is good at “setting the pace”: literally, drumbeats control musical rhythm; figuratively, his speeches always guide the mood or direction of public opinion.
interpretation_1: 指鼓点在音乐中起到掌控和推动节奏的作用。
interpretation_2: 指人在发言中刻意引导他人情绪或舆论走向。

surface_text: 有个男子准备结束十多年的爱情长跑，当个快乐新郎。吉日定好后，他闲来无事，翻看黄历，赫然发现这日竟是只宜入殓，他只好自嘲说：这真的叫做‘婚姻就是爱情的坟墓’！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是套用常见说法，意思是结婚后浪漫爱情似乎走到终点，婚姻像爱情的归宿甚至终结处。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he jokes literally that getting married is like entering a grave for love, especially since the almanac says the chosen day is only suitable for burial.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上是被黄历中的“只宜入殓”激活，把结婚这件喜事临时联想到下葬、坟墓等丧葬语义，因此这句话在此处带有把婚礼说成像进坟墓一样的黑色幽默。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the familiar metaphor that marriage marks the end of romantic freedom and the long love affair, so 'marriage is the tomb of love' becomes a pun that fits both the burial wording and the emotional cliché.
context: 男子准备结婚，翻黄历发现吉日“只宜入殓”，于是借“婚姻就是爱情的坟墓”自嘲。
literal_translation: Marriage is the grave of love.
functional_equivalence_translation: Marriage really is love’s grave—our wedding date was marked for burial.
explanatory_translation: He jokes that “marriage is the grave of love,” a common metaphor, but here it also gains a literal death-related sense because the almanac says the wedding day is only suitable for burial.
interpretation_1: 按常见俗语理解，婚姻被比喻为爱情的终点或束缚。
interpretation_2: 结合黄历“只宜入殓”，婚礼当天仿佛真与死亡、坟墓发生了字面关联。

surface_text: 妈妈：飞飞，昨天叫你送奶奶，你送了没有？ 飞飞：送了。 妈妈：送了？那奶奶咋还跌倒了呢？你是咋送的？ 飞飞：目送。
我最近开始过“省交生活”：不是不社交，是把无效社交省下来，留给真正想见的人。
hidden_form: 社交生活 / 省下社交 / 精简社交
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指一种节省社交成本、减少无效聚会的生活方式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a lifestyle of cutting down on unnecessary socializing and saving social energy.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含激活“社交生活”，通过把“社”替换为“省”，表达从广泛社交转向筛选社交。
interpretation_2_en: It also evokes 'social life'; replacing 'social' with 'saving' suggests moving from frequent socializing to selective socializing.
context: 适用于年轻人关于断舍离、人际边界、情绪节能的日常表达或社媒标题。
literal_translation: I've recently started a 'save-social life': it's not that I don't socialize, I just save unnecessary socializing for the people I really want to meet.
functional_equivalence_translation: Lately I'm living a 'low-social, high-value' life—saving my energy for the people who actually matter.
explanatory_translation: The pun is built by parodying 'social life' with a near-sounding substitution: 'she' (social) becomes 'sheng' (save). The coined phrase highlights both reduced socializing and intentional, selective connection.
interpretation_1: 节省社交精力
interpretation_2: 改造社交生活概念

surface_text: 这位编辑真会改，稿子改得顺，作者脾气也被改顺了。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“改”指编辑把稿件的语言与结构调整得更流畅清晰，使文本质量明显提升。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the editor revised the manuscript so well that the text became smooth and well-organized.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“改顺了”指编辑耐心沟通后，作者原本别扭或坚持的态度也被慢慢安抚下来。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '改顺' also means the editor 'smoothed out' the author's temper, making the author more compliant or easier to deal with.
context: 编辑既修改文章使其通顺，也在沟通中把作者的脾气安抚下来。
literal_translation: This editor is really good at revising: the manuscript was revised into smoothness, and the author's temper was also revised smooth.
functional_equivalence_translation: This editor really knows how to smooth things out—the draft reads smoothly, and even the author was smoothed over.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on "改顺": on the surface it means revising the manuscript so it becomes smooth and fluent, while implicitly it also means smoothing out the author's temper and calming them down.
interpretation_1: 把稿子修改得更通顺、更顺畅。
interpretation_2: 把作者的情绪和脾气安抚得顺了、服帖了。

surface_text: 女：你不是人。男：恩，我不是人，我是狗，我是天狗。女：狗也吃屎。男：恩，我吃屎，我吃的是天使。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是男子顺着前文戏谑地说自己虽然吃屎，但吃的是“天使”，把吃的对象说成了美好的天使形象。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the man says he "eats angels" (天使), taking the woman's insult literally and replying in a bizarre way.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含意思是把“天使”借同音转到“天屎”，与前面的“狗也吃屎”呼应，形成粗俗而搞笑的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a sound-based shift from "angel" (天使, tianshi) to "shit" (天屎, a playful invented form echoing 屎), so he is jokingly responding to "dogs eat shit" while softening it into a pun.
context: 男女互相斗嘴；女方说“狗也吃屎”，男方接着说“我吃的是天使”。
literal_translation: Woman: You are not human. Man: Right, I’m not human, I’m a dog, I’m a heavenly dog. Woman: Dogs eat shit too. Man: Right, I eat shit; what I eat is an angel.
functional_equivalence_translation: Woman: You’re such a dog. Man: Sure, I’m a heavenly hound. Woman: Dogs eat crap. Man: Fine, I do—but mine is heaven-sent.
explanatory_translation: The man says “I eat tianshi,” which on the surface means “angel,” but in Chinese it sounds the same as a made-up phrase meaning “heavenly shit,” so he turns the insult into a pun.
interpretation_1: 男方表面上说自己吃的是天使，字面是“angel”。
interpretation_2: 实际借“天使”谐指“天屎”，延续前文“狗也吃屎”的骂战语境。

surface_text: 老公：“老婆，你用我的牙刷没？” 老婆：“你有病吧？我没用！” 老公：“汗，知道了！” 老婆：“知道什么了?” 老公：“知道你没用，你真没用！”
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“没用”是在回答“你用我的牙刷没”，意思是“没有使用过”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'mei yong' means 'didn't use it': the wife is saying she did not use his toothbrush.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“你真没用”把“没用”转成了“没有用处、没本事”的意思，借同样词形形成讥讽。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning of 'mei yong' is 'useless' or 'good-for-nothing': the husband twists her words into an insult, saying she is really useless.
context: 夫妻对话中，前文“你用我的牙刷没”使“没用”先被理解为“没有用过”，后文又转为评价人“很没用”
literal_translation: Husband: 'Honey, did you use my toothbrush?' Wife: 'Are you sick? I didn't!' Husband: 'Phew, got it.' Wife: 'Got what?' Husband: 'Got that you didn't use it—you really are useless!'
functional_equivalence_translation: Husband: 'Did you use my toothbrush?' Wife: 'What’s wrong with you? I didn’t use it!' Husband: 'Ah, now I know.' Wife: 'Know what?' Husband: 'I know you didn’t use it—and that you’re no use either.'
explanatory_translation: The pun is on '没用', which first means 'didn't use (the toothbrush)' and then shifts to mean 'useless / no good'.
interpretation_1: 没有使用牙刷
interpretation_2: 没有用处、很没用

surface_text: 同桌在填写个人信息时，特长一栏填的是看电视。 我很诧异，问：“看电视也可以成为特长吗？” 他不屑地说：“我每天看电视的时间特长啊！”
南宋著名诗人杨万里做监司时，巡视到一郡。太守设宴讨好，并派歌妓到场酬应，歌妓唱《贺新郎》助酒，当唱到：“万里云帆何时到”处，杨万里触动敏感神经，急忙答道：万里刚到。
interpretation_1_zh: 歌词中的“万里”表层上是数量词，指远行万里、远方而来的船帆何时到达。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “wan li” means a vast distance, as in the lyric “When will sails come from thousands of miles away?”
interpretation_2_zh: “万里”同时触发了杨万里的名字，杨万里将歌词中的“万里”借作对自己的指称，所以接话说“万里刚到”，意思是我杨万里刚刚到这里。
interpretation_2_en: Hiddenly, “Wanli” also refers to Yang Wanli’s personal name, so his reply means: “Wanli has just arrived,” turning the lyric into a reference to himself.
context: 宴席上歌妓唱《贺新郎》，唱到“万里云帆何时到”时，在场的杨万里借“万里”与自己姓名重合来接话。
literal_translation: When the singing girl reached the line “When will the sails from ten thousand miles away arrive?”, Yang Wanli quickly answered, “Wanli has just arrived.”
functional_equivalence_translation: As the singer sang, “When will Wanli arrive?”, Yang Wanli jumped in: “Wanli just got here.”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on “Wanli,” which in the lyric normally means “ten thousand miles” or a great distance, but it is also the given name in the poet’s full name, Yang Wanli. So he jokingly replies as if the lyric were calling for him personally: “Wanli has just arrived.”
interpretation_1: 歌词中的“万里”指极远的路程、遥远距离。
interpretation_2: 杨万里将“万里”听作自己的名字，在场应答“万里刚到”。

surface_text: 于是，小明把蛋给煮熟了，又放回鸡窝里。他的举动，被其他人看见了。有人问他：你想给母鸡吃它自己下的蛋吗？小明回答：母鸡也会吃它自己下的蛋？我是等母鸡直接孵出肯德鸡来吃。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上说“孵出肯德鸡来吃”，把“肯德基”故意说成“肯德鸡”，意思像是想让母鸡直接孵出可以吃的鸡。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, Xiaoming literally hopes the hen will hatch a 'Kentucky chicken' for him to eat, treating KFC-style chicken as if it could be hatched directly from an egg.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“肯德基”这一快餐品牌名称，与“鸡”发生谐趣替换，表达小明异想天开地把母鸡孵蛋和炸鸡、吃鸡联系在一起。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a pun on '肯德鸡', which echoes '肯德基' (KFC). It humorously shifts from a real chicken hatched by a hen to the fast-food brand KFC chicken.
context: 小明把煮熟的蛋放回鸡窝，声称不是给母鸡吃蛋，而是等母鸡直接孵出“肯德鸡”来吃。
literal_translation: KFC chicken
functional_equivalence_translation: I’m waiting for the hen to hatch KFC chicken directly.
explanatory_translation: The joke replaces the last character in “KFC” (肯德基) with the near-homophone “chicken” (鸡), pretending a hen could hatch ready-to-eat KFC-style chicken.
interpretation_1: 表面上指像“肯德基”那样的炸鸡食物
interpretation_2: 借“基/鸡”近音，把品牌名改成“鸡”，理解成母鸡能直接孵出可吃的肯德基式鸡肉

surface_text: 有一天，一个还未成年的小孩，在大家聚会吃饭的时候， 问了他父亲一个问题： “爸爸，你猜一个谜语， 说一个人拿着五毛钱去亲了三个女人，你说这个事件的数学符号是什么？” 大家想了好半天，有的说：“是问号”，也有的说是“感叹号”！ 大家都在苦想的时候，服务员突然冒出一句：“绝对值”嘛！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把这个事件对应成数学符号“绝对值”，即回答的是一个数学术语。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the answer is the mathematical symbol or concept “absolute value.”
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上利用“值”与“直”的近音，指拿着五毛钱去亲三个女人，怎么都不拐弯、非常直接，所以是“绝对直”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a wordplay on “three women kissed for fifty cents,” implying “absolutely cheap” or “a definite low price,” which sounds like “absolute value” in Chinese.
context: 聚餐时有人出谜语：一个人拿五毛钱亲了三个女人，问对应什么数学符号；服务员回答“绝对值”。
literal_translation: "Absolute value."
functional_equivalence_translation: "Absolute rip-off."
explanatory_translation: The waiter answers “absolute value,” referring on the surface to the math symbol, while the joke plays on a near-sound reading like “absolutely a loss/too worth it not,” meaning the man paid too little and got way too much, so the situation is “an absolute bargain” or “absolutely too good a deal.”
interpretation_1: 数学符号里的“绝对值”符号。
interpretation_2: “值”谐指“直”，表示拿着五毛钱去亲三个女人的人非常“直”，即太不划算、太吃亏。

surface_text: 这家甜品店的新品叫“芒着开心”，一口下去，工作群都没那么扎眼了。
hidden_form: 忙着开心 / 芒果带来开心
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指芒果甜品让人吃着就开心，芒果是快乐来源。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the mango dessert makes people happy, with mango as the source of joy.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“忙着开心”，像是在说再忙也要安排一点快乐时刻。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it echoes 'busy being happy,' suggesting that even busy people should schedule small moments of joy.
context: 适用于甜品店命名、饮品宣传或社交媒体营销文案。
literal_translation: This dessert shop's new item is called 'mango-ing happy'; after one bite, even the work group chat looks less irritating.
functional_equivalence_translation: This mango dessert is basically a little dose of happiness for busy people.
explanatory_translation: The pun swaps the character for 'busy' with the same-sounding 'mango,' creating a hybrid phrase that means both 'made happy by mango' and 'busy making happiness happen.'
interpretation_1: 芒果让人开心
interpretation_2: 仿拟忙着开心

surface_text: 小姨子要结婚了，我与妻子商量送点礼给她表示祝贺。我说送点钱，妻说那样很庸俗。我跟妻说：“那我们送一把很贵重的伞给她。” 妻说：“太不吉利了，刚结婚就要散了。” 我说：“那送一床踏花被吧。” 妻说：“那更使不得。” 我不解地问：“结婚的人不用盖被子吗？” 妻说：“她的丈夫会忌讳的，因为你是告诉他要是去寻野花会背运的。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是在讨论给新婚的小姨子送礼物：伞是日常用品，踏花被是结婚时可用的被子。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the gifts are simply a valuable umbrella and a floral quilt for the newlyweds.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上利用谐音触发忌讳：'伞'让人联想到'散'，有婚姻离散之意；'被'又让人联想到'背/被运'，结合'寻野花'可理解为会遭背运、走霉运，因此被认为不吉利。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is based on Chinese word associations: 'umbrella' sounds like 'separate,' implying the couple will break up, and a 'floral quilt' suggests that if the husband goes out chasing other women, he will have bad luck.
context: 新婚送礼语境中，妻子把“踏花被”联想到对新郎“寻野花会背运”的谐音暗示。
literal_translation: A patterned quilt.
functional_equivalence_translation: Let’s give them a quilt whose name sounds like “if he chases other women, he’ll have bad luck.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “踏花被” (a kind of quilt), which is humorously heard as something like “他花背,” suggesting that if the groom goes after wild flowers—meaning other women—he will be unlucky.
interpretation_1: 表层是送一床带花纹、名为“踏花被”的被子作新婚礼物。
interpretation_2: 隐含谐音可被听成“他花背”，意思是丈夫若去寻野花、拈花惹草就会倒霉背运。

surface_text: 科幻片里的角色刚换上新的人造外壳，观众就感叹他简直是脱胎换骨了。
这家面包店把加班人专属套餐命名为“续命包”，饿的时候先吃一口，感觉连周一都没那么难了。
hidden_form: 续命 + 面包/包子 + 加班人的“靠食物续命”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指一种面包店推出的“包”类食品套餐，用来填饱肚子、补充能量。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a bread or bun-based set meal sold by a bakery to satisfy hunger and provide energy.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上借用网络表达“续命”，表示这份食物像是在给疲惫的上班族补回精神和生活意志。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it draws on the internet phrase 'to extend one's life,' suggesting the food revives exhausted office workers both physically and emotionally.
context: 适用于餐饮广告、职场吐槽或社交媒体上形容食物很救急的语境。
negative_example: 这家店推出了加班套餐面包。
literal_translation: This bakery named its overtime workers' special combo 'life-extending bun'; when you're hungry, one bite makes even Monday feel less hard.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bakery calls its overtime special the 'survival bun'—one bite, and even Monday feels a little more manageable.
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the hybrid coinage '续命包,' which blends '续命' (to keep oneself going, often exaggerated online as 'to survive') with '包' (bun/bread item). It simultaneously denotes a bakery product and humorously frames the food as something that keeps worn-out workers alive.
interpretation_1: 充饥的面包套餐
interpretation_2: 给打工人续命的食物

surface_text: 我最近开始练“断舍交”，不是断舍离升级版家务，是把无效社交也一起清仓。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上像是从“断舍离”衍生出的新生活方式词，保留整理和减负的意味。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it looks like a new lifestyle term derived from 'decluttering/minimalism', keeping the sense of clearing and reducing burdens.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“社交”纳入清理对象，表示主动减少消耗性的关系和应酬。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning adds 'socializing' as the object of decluttering, referring to actively cutting draining relationships and unnecessary social events.
context: 适用于情绪表达、社交疲惫吐槽或自我管理分享。
negative_example: 我最近在做断舍离，把房间整理得很干净。
literal_translation: I've recently started practicing 'cut-discard-social'—not a household-upgrade version of decluttering, but clearing out ineffective socializing too.
functional_equivalence_translation: I'm into 'social decluttering' lately—not just cleaning my room, but cutting out draining social ties too.
explanatory_translation: The pun truncates the familiar phrase for decluttering and replaces its final element with 'socializing', producing a new coined term that extends physical minimalism to interpersonal life.
interpretation_1: 新式减负生活法
interpretation_2: 清理无效社交

surface_text: 宿舍群里有人发起“赶DDL操”，说不是健身，是用最后一晚把论文和心率一起拉起来。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义像一种专为赶截止日期设计的“操练”或活动。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it sounds like an exercise routine designed for deadline-chasing.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是仿照“做操”的说法，调侃学生在截止前高强度赶作业的状态。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning imitates the idea of doing drills or exercises, humorously describing students rushing assignments before the deadline.
context: 适用于校园熬夜赶作业、期末周吐槽。
literal_translation: Someone in the dorm group started a 'deadline-chasing workout', saying it's not fitness, but using the last night to raise both the thesis and the heart rate.
functional_equivalence_translation: Someone in the dorm chat invented 'DDL aerobics'—not real exercise, just that last-night assignment panic workout.
explanatory_translation: This pun blends 'gan DDL' (to rush a deadline, with DDL from 'deadline') and 'cao' from exercise drills. The coined phrase turns deadline panic into a mock physical routine.
interpretation_1: 赶截止操练
interpretation_2: 熬夜冲刺状态

surface_text: 班主任请小周和小陈的父亲留下。
在历史课堂上，老师问一个学生：屈原是什么人？ 是医生。 胡说！ 怎么胡说呢，书上明明说他是大夫嘛。
周末跟团出来旅游，大家跟过团的都知道团餐难吃的程度， 旁边一64年的阿姨说：“这青菜，比我还老。。。”秒杀有没有！
一位客人去一家小店吃饭，一阵风吹来，客人叫小二关窗，小二指着门外招牌对客人说：客官，你不知道我们这里是‘风味小吃’吗？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上“风味小吃”是指这家店卖的是有特色风味的小吃。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '风味小吃' means snacks with a special local flavor or distinctive taste, so the waiter is referring to the shop's sign literally.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里把“风味”拆解并转成“有风才有味道”，借门外吹进来的风来调侃不用关窗。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the shop is full of wind, so it jokingly treats '风味' as meaning a place characterized by wind, implying there is no need to close the window.
context: 客人因风吹进店里而让小二关窗，小二借店招“风味小吃”把“风味”从“特色风味”转成“风的味道”来回应。
literal_translation: A customer went to a small restaurant to eat. A gust of wind blew in, and the customer asked the waiter to close the window. Pointing at the sign outside, the waiter said, “Sir, don’t you know ours is ‘flavor snacks’?”
functional_equivalence_translation: When a customer asked the waiter to shut the window because of the wind, the waiter pointed to the sign and said, “Sir, this is a place with real air-and-flavor snacks.”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the Chinese word “风味,” which normally means “special flavor” or “local style,” but the waiter jokingly reinterprets it literally as “the taste of wind,” using the blowing wind as part of the restaurant’s “flavor.”
interpretation_1: 招牌中的“风味”指菜品的风格、特色口味。
interpretation_2: 小二把“风味”拆解成“风的味道”，借外面吹进来的风来打趣。

surface_text: 上次看的一个节目,什么名字不记得了,就记得开头是个记者在火车站问人:你幸福吗?,见人就问,有人说幸福有人说不。后来问到一个农民.....记者:你幸福吗?农民看了记者几眼,无辜的说道 俺姓王。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是记者在询问对方是否感到幸福、生活是否满意。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the reporter is asking the farmer, 'Are you happy?' using 'xingfu' to mean happiness or well-being.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是农民把“幸福吗”误听成“姓福吗”，理解成在问自己是不是姓福，于是回答“俺姓王”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from the farmer mishearing 'xingfu' as 'xing Fu' or 'what is your surname,' so he replies, 'My surname is Wang.'
context: 记者在火车站随机采访路人，反复问“你幸福吗”，问到农民时，对方回答“俺姓王”。
literal_translation: A reporter at the train station asked people, “Are you happy?” When he asked a farmer, the farmer replied innocently, “My surname is Wang.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A reporter kept asking people, “Are you happy?” But the farmer misheard it as a question about his family name and answered, “My last name is Wang.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is that “你幸福吗” normally means “Are you happy?”, but the farmer humorously interprets “幸福” as something sounding like a surname being asked about, so he replies with his own surname, “Wang.”
interpretation_1: 记者在询问对方是否感到幸福。
interpretation_2: 农民把“你幸福吗”误听成了在问姓氏，理解为“你姓福吗/姓傅吗”。

surface_text: 丈夫斥责道：“你烧的这哪里是青菜？蜡黄蜡黄的。” 妻子立刻回答：“你每天回家这么晚，当然不会知道它们在我的锅铲上也曾经‘青春’过。”
丈夫什么家物也不会做，一天家里客厅的灯不亮，妻子在厨房做饭让他换个灯泡，丈夫说这个我会做，不一会丈夫喊：老婆那个灯有一点高，灯泡装不上。 妻子说：你垫一下吗，不一会丈夫发出一声惨叫。 妻子问：又怎么了？ 丈夫痛苦的说：我电了一下还是没装上。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本中的“电了一下”是说丈夫在换灯泡时触电了，被电击了一下，所以发出惨叫。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "电了一下" means he got an electric shock while trying to install the light bulb.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里借“电”和“垫”的近音形成双关，原本妻子说“你垫一下吗”是让他踩个垫子把身体垫高，隐藏恢复为“垫了一下还是没装上”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that he misunderstood his wife's "垫一下吗" as "use electricity / get electrocuted a bit" rather than "stand on something to raise yourself," creating the pun around "电" and the shifted action.
context: 丈夫换客厅灯泡时够不着，妻子说“你垫一下吗”，丈夫随后说“我电了一下还是没装上”。
literal_translation: The wife meant, “Use something to stand on,” but the husband understood it as “get electrocuted a bit.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Wife: “Use a step.” Husband: “I got a shock, but I still couldn’t put it in.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on the Chinese expression “垫一下” (to put something under oneself to stand higher) and “电一下” (to get shocked once), which sound the same in context.
interpretation_1: 妻子本意是让丈夫垫高脚下物品，以便够到灯座。
interpretation_2: 丈夫误解成让自己被电一下，结果说“我电了一下还是没装上”。

surface_text: 我们看望了生病的班长的奶奶。
两个小男孩的对话。其中一个男孩说：我们先恋爱，长大后你就嫁给我吧！可以吗？另一个：你姓什么？张啊？怎么了？没事！我姓韩！我妈妈说了，同姓是不可以在一起的，我们不同姓就可以。哦！两人牵着手跑远了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是孩子把“同姓不可以在一起”理解为姓氏相同的人不能在一起，因此一个姓张、一个姓韩，就觉得可以在一起。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the boy misunderstands 'people with the same surname cannot be together' literally. Since one is surnamed Zhang and the other Han, they think they have different surnames and therefore can be together.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“同姓”谐指“同性”，真正被激活的是“两个男孩是同性别”，形成与婚恋话题相关的另一层双关意味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the original warning is really about close relatives or people from the same family line not being allowed to marry. The joke comes from the child taking 'same surname' as a simple surname match instead of the broader kinship meaning.
context: 两个小男孩讨论长大后结婚，其中一人说妈妈讲过“同姓不可以在一起”，因两人姓氏不同而误以为可以。
literal_translation: Two little boys are talking. One says, “Let’s fall in love first, and when we grow up, you marry me, okay?” The other asks, “What’s your surname?” “Zhang. Why?” “Nothing. My surname is Han. My mom said people with the same surname can’t be together. Since we have different surnames, we can.” “Oh!” Then the two run off hand in hand.
functional_equivalence_translation: Two little boys are talking. One says, “Let’s be in love now, and when we grow up, marry me, okay?” The other asks, “What’s your last name?” “Zhang.” “Good, mine’s Han. My mom said the ‘same kind’ can’t be together—but we’re different, so we can!” Then they run away holding hands.
explanatory_translation: The humor hinges on a Chinese homophone: “同姓” (same surname) and “同性” (same sex) are pronounced the same. The child misunderstands an adult rule about two boys being the same sex as a rule about having the same surname, so he concludes they can be together because their surnames are different.
interpretation_1: 字面上指两个人姓氏相同，按男孩理解为婚配限制条件。
interpretation_2: 隐含激活“同性”，即性别相同的人不能在一起的成人婚恋规则，被孩子误听误解为“同姓”。

surface_text: 爸爸带儿子上街，路边的音响播放一首爱情歌曲，儿子跟着学唱，爸爸制止道：“不要唱，这歌不健康。” 儿子好奇地问：“怎么，唱这个会感冒吗？”
周末我回家晚了，一进门老婆就审问我：“怎么7点才回家？” 我说：“下午参加了一个发布会。” 老婆一边翻我的包一边说：“发的是什么布？我正想做条裤子。”
一位基因研究所的专家正在研究一个课题：如何让发黄的植物快速变绿，可一直没有进展。回家后，老婆看到他愁眉不展的样子，便问他：“你这是怎么了？” 专家叹了口气，说：“我不知道怎样才能让植物快速变绿。” 老婆笑着说：“咳，我还以为什么事呢？要快速变绿还不简单啊？直接扔进股市里去呗，你看我昨天买的股票，今天全变绿了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是专家在研究如何让发黄的植物恢复绿色，即植物叶片重新变绿。
interpretation_1_en: The literal meaning is to make yellowing plants turn green again, restoring their healthy green color.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“绿”转到股市语境中，指股票价格下跌后盘面显示为绿色，妻子借此调侃说扔进股市里就会很快‘变绿’。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that in the stock market, 'green' refers to falling prices or losses, so throwing them into the market would make them all 'turn green.'
context: 前文说专家研究让发黄的植物快速变绿，后文妻子转到自己买的股票今天全变绿了
literal_translation: turn green
functional_equivalence_translation: If you want them to turn green fast, just throw them into the stock market.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “turn green”: literally it means yellow plants becoming green again, but in the stock-market context it means stocks falling and showing green on the screen.
interpretation_1: 植物由发黄转为绿色
interpretation_2: 股票下跌，盘面显示为绿色

surface_text: 老妈说家里买了猪头， 于是我就问老妈猪头在哪呢， 老妈乐了：“你看你这猪脑袋，猪头不是长你脖子上嘛？”
有一位到城里打工的青年给远在农村的父母写信，告知自己在城里度日如年。 老父亲看完信后高兴地说：“这小子在城里混的还挺好，过日子就像过年一样。” 老母亲却不放心地问：“那为什么还要我们寄200块钱给他呢？” “你真老土，天天过年能不要钱吗？”老父亲不耐烦地开导老伴儿说。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“度日如年”误解为“过日子像过年一样”，认为他在城里生活得很好、天天都像过年般热闹体面。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the father misreads 'living like a year in a day' as meaning the son lives every day as if it were New Year, enjoying life and spending money happily.
interpretation_2_zh: “度日如年”的常规意思是日子非常难熬，觉得一天像一年那么漫长，实际暗示他在城里过得艰难，所以才要家里寄钱。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is that the son is having a very hard time in the city; '度日如年' is an idiom meaning each day feels as long and painful as a year.
context: 青年写信说自己在城里“度日如年”，父亲把其中的“如年”按“像过年”理解，从而产生误读。
literal_translation: A young migrant worker wrote to his parents in the countryside, saying that in the city he was living as if a day were a year. His father happily said, “The boy is doing pretty well in the city; living his days is just like celebrating the New Year every day.”
functional_equivalence_translation: He wrote home saying, “Life here feels like New Year every day,” which his father took as good news, though he had actually meant that each day felt unbearably long.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on the Chinese idiom “度日如年,” which normally means “life is hard and each day feels like a year,” but the father misreads “如年” literally as “like New Year,” so he thinks his son is living festively and well.
interpretation_1: 本义是日子难熬，感觉一天像一年那么长，说明生活艰难。
interpretation_2: 被老父亲误解为过日子就像过年一样，天天喜庆、过得很好。

surface_text: 这家咖啡馆主打“醒价比”，一杯下去人先清醒，再看价格也觉得值。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指咖啡带来的提神清醒效果很划算。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the coffee's wake-up effect is well worth the price.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含激活“性价比”，表示商品整体很值。
interpretation_2_en: It also evokes 'cost-performance ratio,' suggesting the product offers great overall value.
context: 适用于咖啡、功能饮料等强调提神与实惠的广告文案。
literal_translation: This café promotes 'wake-price ratio': one cup wakes you up first, then even the price looks worth it.
functional_equivalence_translation: This café sells great bang-for-your-buzz.
explanatory_translation: The pun blends 'xing' from 'to wake up' with the common expression 'cost-performance ratio,' creating a hybrid word that refers both to alertness and value for money.
interpretation_1: 提神很值
interpretation_2: 性价比高

surface_text: 一天，和女朋友在步行街逛街，突然一卖花的小姑娘向我跑了过来。 卖花的小姑娘拉着我：“大哥哥，买花吧，一看就知道你是花心的人”
interpretation_1_zh: 表面上小姑娘把“花心”理解为喜欢花、对花有兴趣的心思，因此劝他买花。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the flower-selling girl means he is a person who likes flowers or has a heart for flowers, so he should buy some flowers.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“花心”也指感情上不专一、容易见异思迁的人，这与他正和女朋友逛街形成调侃效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "花心" commonly means being fickle or unfaithful in love, especially a man who easily falls for many women.
context: 步行街上卖花小姑娘向男子推销花，故意把“花心”的贬义转成与“花”有关的字面义来劝买。
literal_translation: One day, I was shopping on a pedestrian street with my girlfriend when a little flower-selling girl suddenly ran up to me. She pulled me and said, “Big brother, buy some flowers. I can tell at a glance that you are a flower-hearted person.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A little flower girl came up to me and said, “Buy some flowers, big brother. I can tell you’re really into flowers.”
explanatory_translation: A flower-selling girl says, “Buy some flowers—I can tell you’re ‘huaxin.’” In Chinese, huaxin usually means “unfaithful/flirtatious,” but here she twists it to mean someone who likes flowers, creating the pun.
interpretation_1: 通常指感情上不专一、容易见异思迁的人。
interpretation_2: 在卖花语境中被转说成喜欢花、会买花的人。

surface_text: 这家店真会藏，菜里藏惊喜，菜单里也藏着价格惊吓。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“藏”指菜品中暗藏特别配料或创意设计，吃到时会给顾客带来意外惊喜。
interpretation_1_en: The shop is literally good at hiding things: the dishes hide pleasant surprises, and the menu also hides something unexpected.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“藏”指菜单价格并不显眼，等看清或结账时才发现不便宜，形成反差吐槽。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the restaurant is not transparent about its prices—the menu conceals shockingly expensive charges, turning 'hidden surprise' into 'price scare'.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：评论一家餐馆，前半句夸菜品有惊喜，后半句转而吐槽菜单价格过高。
negative_example: 这家店真会藏，菜里藏惊喜，菜单里也藏着价格。
literal_translation: This restaurant really knows how to hide things: there are surprises hidden in the dishes, and price scares hidden in the menu too.
functional_equivalence_translation: This place knows how to hide things—pleasant surprises in the food, and nasty surprises in the prices.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on repeating 'hide': first it means the dishes contain pleasant surprises, then it shifts to the menu secretly containing shockingly high prices.
interpretation_1: 菜里藏着额外的惊喜或小心思。
interpretation_2: 菜单里暗含让人被价格吓到的内容。

surface_text: 新娘：“都怨姓不好，才做新娘就变成陈太太！” 新郎：“唉！要是嫁给杨先生该多好，一结婚不就成了杨太太？永远的洋太太。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是说如果嫁给姓杨的人，结婚后就会被称作“杨太太”，即杨先生的妻子。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, if she married a man surnamed Yang, she would become Mrs. Yang after marriage.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上利用“杨”与“洋”同音，触发“洋太太”的意思，指像外国太太一样，带有时髦、洋气的意味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'Yang taitai' sounds like 'foreign lady' or 'Western madam' (洋太太), suggesting she would seem like a forever fashionable foreign-style wife.
