context: 新郎新娘谈论婚后随夫姓的称呼，新娘抱怨“陈太太”不好听，新郎假设若嫁给姓杨的人，就会被叫作“杨太太”，从而联想到“洋太太”。
literal_translation: Bride: “It’s all because the surname is bad. I’ve only just become a bride and already turned into Mrs. Chen!” Groom: “Sigh! If only you had married Mr. Yang. Once married, wouldn’t you become Mrs. Yang? Forever a foreign-style lady.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Bride: “What a pity about the surname—I’m a bride for one day and already just Mrs. Chen!” Groom: “If you’d married a Mr. Young, you’d be Mrs. Young forever.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese homophone 杨太太 (Mrs. Yang) and 洋太太 (a foreign lady / foreigner’s wife). The groom teases that marrying a man surnamed Yang would make her not only “Mrs. Yang” but also, by sound, a “foreign-style lady” forever.
interpretation_1: 如果嫁给姓杨的人，婚后会被称作杨太太。
interpretation_2: 洋太太指外国人的太太或带有洋派意味的太太，借此形成调侃。

surface_text: 你带5个朋友去饭店。 落座后你说：茶！ 小姐没领会就查：123456。 你感到好笑：倒茶！ 小姐倒着查：654321。 你大怒：你数啥啊？ 小姐害羞：俺属猪！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“你数啥啊”里的“数”被按“数数、报数”理解，所以小姐回答成了自己的生肖信息，形成答非所问的效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "数" is understood as "to count numbers." The speaker angrily asks why she is counting, because she has been saying or doing number sequences like 123456 and 654321.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含中更常规的说法应是“你属啥啊”，“属”表示属相、生肖；这里利用“数”与“属”的近音造成语义转移。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the waitress interprets "数啥" as sounding like "属啥," meaning "what is your zodiac sign?" So she shyly answers, "I was born in the Year of the Pig."
context: 饭店点单场景中，顾客说“茶”，服务员连续按“查”来理解，并把“倒茶”误解为“倒着查”。
literal_translation: You took five friends to a restaurant. After sitting down, you said, “Tea!” The waitress didn’t get it and checked: 123456. You found it funny and said, “Pour tea!” The waitress checked in reverse: 654321. You got angry: “What are you counting?” The waitress shyly said: “I was born in the Year of the Pig!”
functional_equivalence_translation: At a restaurant, you said, “Tea!” But the waitress heard it like “check” and started reciting numbers. When you said, “Pour the tea,” she took it as “check it backwards” and read the numbers in reverse.
explanatory_translation: This joke hinges on the Chinese homophone “茶/查” (chá), where “tea” sounds exactly like “check/search.” So the waitress misinterprets the customer’s request for tea as an instruction to check numbers, and even hears “倒茶” (pour tea) as “倒查” (check in reverse).
interpretation_1: 服务员把“茶”误听成“查”，理解为让她查数字或信息。
interpretation_2: 说话人原意是点茶、让服务员倒茶。

surface_text: 老公：我这几天屁股疼，我得痔疮了！ 老婆：从我认识你，你大病小病的没有断过！ 我看你这一辈子就这样了！ 老公生气：不要看不起我！ 我觉得我的人生很有意义！很完整！ 老婆不屑：说说我听听！ 老公：我是有痔青年，因此我的人生很有意义！ 不得痔的人生就不是完整的人生！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“有志青年”替换成“有痔青年”，意思是他因为得了痔疮，自嘲自己成了“有痔”的青年，并进一步说“不得痔的人生就不是完整的人生”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he means that because he has hemorrhoids, his life is somehow meaningful and complete; a life without hemorrhoids would be incomplete.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义激活的是常规说法“有志青年”，本义是有志向、有抱负的年轻人；借“痔”与“志”同音，把疾病状态戏仿成积极评价，制造反差幽默。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on 痔 sounding like 志 in phrases such as 有志青年 and 人生有意义, so he is really echoing the idea of an ambitious, purposeful young person and a meaningful life.
context: 丈夫先说自己得了痔疮，随后把“有志青年”故意说成“有痔青年”，并进一步说“不得痔的人生就不是完整的人生”来强化痔疮的字面义
literal_translation: Husband: I’ve had a pain in my butt these days; I got hemorrhoids! Wife: Ever since I met you, your illnesses big and small have never stopped! I think this is how your whole life will be! Husband angrily: Don’t look down on me! I think my life is very meaningful, very complete! Wife disdainfully: Tell me then! Husband: I am a “hemorrhoid-possessing” young man, therefore my life is very meaningful! A life without hemorrhoids is not a complete life!
functional_equivalence_translation: Husband: I’ve got hemorrhoids. Wife: You’re always sick. Husband: Don’t underestimate me—I’m a man of piles, so my life has purpose. A life without piles isn’t a whole life!
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese homophone “有痔” and “有志.” “有志青年” means “an ambitious young person,” but the husband replaces 志 (ambition) with 痔 (hemorrhoids), turning it into “a young man with hemorrhoids” while pretending it still carries the positive meaning of being ambitious.
interpretation_1: 字面上指长了痔疮、身患痔病
interpretation_2: 借同音激活“有志”，指有志向、有抱负的青年

surface_text: 她真能扮，舞台上扮什么像什么，生活里也总扮得云淡风轻。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“扮”指她在舞台表演中善于塑造角色，化妆和神态都到位，形象转换能力强。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "扮" means to play or portray roles well: on stage she can act as anything convincingly, and in daily life she also presents herself as calm and untroubled.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“扮”指她在生活中也会把情绪藏起来，表面装得轻松从容，不让人看出压力。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "扮" also suggests putting on a front or disguising one's true feelings: in life, she is not necessarily carefree, but deliberately acts as if everything is light and easy.
context: 同一句中先说舞台表演中的“扮演”，再说生活中的“扮得云淡风轻”，由前后并置激活“表演/伪装”两层理解。
literal_translation: She is really good at acting: on stage, whatever she plays, she looks the part; in life, she also always acts as if everything were light and calm.
functional_equivalence_translation: She’s a great performer—on stage she can become anyone, and off stage she performs calm just as convincingly.
explanatory_translation: She is good at “playing a part”: on stage this means acting different roles convincingly, while in life it implies putting on a calm, carefree front.
interpretation_1: 在舞台上进行角色扮演，模仿什么像什么。
interpretation_2: 在现实生活中装作云淡风轻，掩饰真实情绪。

surface_text: 这位律师真会守，底线守得牢，秘密也守得牢。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“守”指律师在职业行为中严守法律和伦理底线，不轻易越界，原则性很强。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means this lawyer is very good at keeping things: he firmly sticks to his bottom line and also keeps secrets well.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“守”指他也能严格保守委托人的隐私与秘密，体现值得信任的职业素养。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '守' is used in two parallel senses at once: to uphold principles and professional ethics, and to maintain confidentiality, highlighting the lawyer's reliability and integrity.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：同一句中先说“底线守得牢”，后说“秘密也守得牢”，同一词“守”并列激活两种守护对象。
negative_example: 这位律师真会守时，开会从不迟到。
literal_translation: This lawyer is really good at keeping: keeps the bottom line firmly, and keeps secrets firmly too.
functional_equivalence_translation: This lawyer really knows how to keep things—principles intact and secrets sealed.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on the repeated word “守” (“to keep/guard”). It first means upholding professional boundaries, and then means keeping confidential information secret.
interpretation_1: 指律师坚守职业底线和原则。
interpretation_2: 指律师严守秘密，不泄露客户信息。

surface_text: 包装绳卡得很紧，他顺着刀刃一划就开了，大家说问题算是迎刃而解了。
“主持人你好，我正挤在1路公交车上，我想给前面靠窗的那位姑娘点一首歌，就是张学友的那首，你知道的，对对对，1路上有你，挤一点也愿意。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层说的是自己正挤在1路公交车上，想点一首和当前乘车情境相关的歌，于是把歌名理解为“1路上有你”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker is calling from a crowded No. 1 bus and wants to dedicate a song to a girl sitting by the window in front, joking that 'having you on Route 1, I'm willing to endure the crowd.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含指向张学友歌曲《一路上有你》，其中“1路”借同音替换成“一路”，既点出歌名，也借歌词式表达对前面姑娘的好感，意思是只要一路有她，挤一点也愿意。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the song title '一路上有你' ('Having You All the Way') by replacing '一路' with '1路' ('Route 1 bus'), turning a romantic lyric into a bus-related confession.
context: 在1路公交车上，给前面靠窗的姑娘点歌，把歌名《一路上有你》借当前乘车场景改说成“1路上有你”。
literal_translation: "Hello host, I'm squeezed on Bus No. 1, and I want to dedicate a song to the girl by the window in front of me—the Jacky Cheung one, you know, right right right, 'On Bus No. 1 with You,' and I'd gladly endure the crowding.'
functional_equivalence_translation: "Hi, host, I'm packed onto Bus No. 1, and I'd like to dedicate a song to the girl by the window up front—the Jacky Cheung song, you know: 'With You on Route One,' and I don't mind being squashed a little."
explanatory_translation: The pun changes the song title 《一路上有你》 ('Having You All the Way') into 《1路上有你》, because “一路” and “1路” sound the same in Chinese. The hidden meaning ties the love song to the speaker's current situation on Bus No. 1.
interpretation_1: 指张学友歌曲《一路上有你》。
interpretation_2: 把“1路”理解为1路公交车，表示在1路车上有那位姑娘相伴，挤一点也愿意。

surface_text: 消防演练时有人端着一杯水去冲着火的卡车，大家都说这简直是杯水车薪。
她认识卖水果的老板娘的弟弟。
pun_word: 卖水果的老板娘的弟弟

surface_text: 罐罐和梅老师在家一起看《时尚王》 梅老师噙着口水感叹说：“女主角可真漂亮啊，要是能娶到这样的老婆，我就此生无憾了……。” 罐罐顿时内疚了：“哎，都因为你娶了我，所以还要一直上班~” 两人若无其事看了很久 罐罐：“你刚刚说的是“此生无憾”还是“辞职不干”？”
pun_word: 此生无憾 / 辞职不干
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是梅老师感叹如果能娶到像女主角那样漂亮的老婆，这一辈子就没有遗憾了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “此生无憾” means “to have no regrets in this life” — he is saying that if he could marry such a beautiful wife, he would be completely satisfied.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“此生无憾”谐转为“辞职不干”，罐罐借此理解成梅老师是在说因为娶了她还得一直上班，所以想辞职不干。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a playful mishearing as “辞职不干,” which means “to quit the job and stop working,” implying that marrying such a wife would make him feel he would no longer need to work.
context: 丈夫看电视夸女主角漂亮，说“要是能娶到这样的老婆，我就此生无憾了”，妻子结合“上班”话题故意谐听为“辞职不干”。
literal_translation: Did you just say 'have no regrets in this life' or 'quit the job and stop working'?
functional_equivalence_translation: Did you say you'd be fulfilled for life, or that you could finally quit working?
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the similar sound between '此生无憾' (have no regrets in this life) and '辞职不干' (quit the job and stop working). The wife jokingly pretends she heard the second one, linking it to having to keep working after marrying her.
interpretation_1: 梅老师表面上是在说如果能娶到那样漂亮的老婆，这一生就没有遗憾了。
interpretation_2: 罐罐故意把话听成“辞职不干”，理解为因为娶了自己所以还得一直上班，若娶到那样的老婆就可以辞职不上班了。

surface_text: 某日上理化课，老师宣布下节课要小考。小明紧张地立即举手问老师会不会考得很难，老师只说了一句：十分简单。 乐得大家拍手叫好，可是考完后每个人都考得惨不忍睹，怎么会简单呢？于是小明又问了老师，只听老师说：我可没说错哦，十分简单，剩下九十分很难！
interpretation_1_zh: 老师表面上说的是这次小考很容易，意思是题目非常简单。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '十分简单' means 'very easy,' so the teacher seems to be saying that the test will be extremely simple.
interpretation_2_zh: 老师实际利用“十分”既可表示“非常”又可表示“10分”的双关，意思是只有10分的题简单，剩下90分的题很难。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '十分' is taken literally as 'ten points,' so the teacher actually means only ten points of the test are easy, while the remaining ninety points are difficult.
context: 老师预告小考，学生问考试难度，老师回答“十分简单”，考后又解释为“十分很简单，剩下九十分很难”。
literal_translation: The teacher said, 'Ten points is simple.'
functional_equivalence_translation: The teacher said, 'Getting a ten is easy—the other ninety points are the hard part.'
explanatory_translation: In Chinese, “十分简单” normally means “very easy,” but the teacher reinterprets “十分” literally as “ten points,” creating the joke that only scoring ten points is easy.
interpretation_1: 非常简单，整体考试不难。
interpretation_2: 只能拿到十分是简单的，剩下九十分很难拿。

surface_text: 这位裁缝真会收腰，裙子会收腰，说话也懂得收腰。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“收腰”指在服装制作中把腰身裁得更贴合，突出线条，使衣服版型更好看。
interpretation_1_en: On the literal level, the tailor is good at taking in the waist of a skirt so it fits better.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“收腰”借指说话懂得收敛锋芒，不把话说满，表达得体而不过分张扬。
interpretation_2_en: On the implied level, '收腰' also means being restrained in speech—knowing when to hold back and not talk too much.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：谈论一位裁缝，前一句说其做裙子会收腰，后一句转到其说话也很有分寸。
literal_translation: This tailor really knows how to take in the waist: skirts can be taken in at the waist, and even in speaking he knows how to 'take in the waist.'
functional_equivalence_translation: This tailor really knows how to trim things down—he slims dresses at the waist, and he also trims his words.
explanatory_translation: This tailor is good at "taking in the waist": literally, he tailors skirts to make the waist slimmer; figuratively, he also knows how to rein in his speech and speak with restraint.
interpretation_1: 指裁缝把裙子的腰身收紧，做出修身版型。
interpretation_2: 指说话有分寸，懂得克制，不把话说得太满太冲。

surface_text: 社团招新海报写着“社牛养成班”，其实不是教你吵，而是教你把开场白说得像开门键。
hidden_form: 社恐 / 社交牛人 / 养成班
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指一个帮助学生提升社交主动性的训练活动或课程。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a training activity that helps students become more socially proactive.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含调用网络词“社牛”，与“养成班”拼接，形成从社交胆怯到社交放开的标签化表达。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it uses the internet slang 'socially bold person' and combines it with 'training class,' creating a label-like expression for transforming social confidence.
context: 适用于校园社团宣传、新生活动或年轻人网络表达。
literal_translation: The club recruitment poster says 'social-cow cultivation class'; it does not teach you to be loud, but to make your opening line work like a door-open button.
functional_equivalence_translation: The club calls it a 'social butterfly bootcamp'—basically a class on breaking the ice fast.
explanatory_translation: The pun relies on the internet label '社牛' for a highly outgoing person, blending it with the structured term 'training class' to create a playful hybrid expression.
interpretation_1: 培养社交主动性
interpretation_2: 借社牛标签造词

surface_text: 这家面包店新出的低糖系列叫“甜而不腻志”，主打想吃甜又不想有负担的人。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上像一个系列名称，强调产品甜味适中、不容易吃腻。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it sounds like a product line name emphasizing sweetness without being cloying.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上把“志”加入表达，仿佛一本关于低糖甜点生活方式的“杂志”式主张。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, the added 'zhi' evokes 'magazine/manifesto,' making the line sound like a lifestyle statement about low-sugar desserts.
context: 适用于烘焙店新品命名、甜品宣传和品牌文案。
literal_translation: This bakery's new low-sugar line is called 'Sweet-but-not-greasy-zine,' aimed at people who want sweetness without the burden.
functional_equivalence_translation: The bakery's new low-sugar line is basically a 'sweet-not-heavy manifesto' for people who crave dessert without the guilt.
explanatory_translation: The pun extends the fixed phrase 'sweet but not cloying' by adding a morpheme associated with magazines or manifestos, turning a taste description into a stylized brand concept.
interpretation_1: 甜但不腻
interpretation_2: 像系列刊物命名

surface_text: 我们部门最近流行“会心上班”：会上频频点头，心里却在默默下班。
hidden_form: 会上 / 会心 / 上班
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指在会议中继续完成上班状态和工作动作。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means being at work during meetings and continuing one's work mode.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“会上”和“会心”嫁接，表达表面投入、内心游离的职场状态。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it fuses 'at the meeting' with 'knowing inwardly,' describing a workplace state of outward engagement but inward detachment.
context: 适用于职场段子、会议吐槽、办公室社交文案。
negative_example: 我们部门最近总在开会。
literal_translation: Our department has been into 'meeting-hearted working': nodding often in meetings while mentally clocking out.
functional_equivalence_translation: Lately we've mastered the art of looking engaged in meetings while mentally checking out.
explanatory_translation: The pun rebuilds the phrase by merging 'meeting' and 'working' with 'knowing inwardly,' so it can mean both literally working through meetings and secretly disengaging inside.
interpretation_1: 开会办公
interpretation_2: 人上班心下班

surface_text: 与教授恩爱甚笃的老妻不幸病故，教授深为悲痛。 一年后，经朋友撮合，再圆春梦。 婚后，教授再上讲台，学生问续弦之味如何，教授沉思片刻， 答：“和你们补考及格差不多。”
宿舍门口新开了家夜宵店，招牌写着“寝商在线”，懂学生几点饿，也懂几点不想睡。
hidden_form: 情商在线 / 寝室 / 夜宵需求
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指这家店很懂学生在宿舍生活中的夜宵需求。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the shop understands students' late-night food needs in dorm life.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借“情商在线”仿拟，表示这家店很会体察人心、很会做生意。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning imitates 'emotionally intelligent online,' implying the shop is highly considerate and business-savvy.
context: 适用于校园餐饮宣传、校园帖子标题或夜宵店文案。
literal_translation: A late-night snack shop opened near the dorm, with a sign saying 'dorm-IQ online'—it knows when students get hungry and when they don't want to sleep.
functional_equivalence_translation: This dormside snack shop really gets student life.
explanatory_translation: The pun remodels the popular phrase 'EQ online' by replacing the first part with 'dorm/sleep quarters.' It suggests both dorm-related insight and emotional smartness in serving students.
interpretation_1: 懂宿舍夜宵需求
interpretation_2: 像情商高一样会拿捏需求

surface_text: 老板说这次团建主打“社牛充电宝”，去的时候替公司活跃气氛，回来顺便把自己的电也社没了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指能给社交场合提供能量、带动气氛的人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a person who powers up social situations and energizes the atmosphere.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“社交牛人”像产品名一样压缩成前缀，调侃外向者在团建中的角色与消耗。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it compresses 'social superstar' into a product-like prefix, joking about extroverts as both atmosphere-makers and energy spenders.
context: 适用于职场团建、社交人格讨论、网络吐槽。
literal_translation: The boss said this team-building event needs a 'social-bull power bank': you energize the company vibe there, and come back with your own battery socially drained.
functional_equivalence_translation: At team-building, the extrovert becomes the human power bank for the whole room.
explanatory_translation: The hybrid word joins the internet slang 'socially fearless person' with 'power bank.' It works because the extrovert both charges the room's mood and gets personally drained.
interpretation_1: 带气氛的人
interpretation_2: 社交消耗者

surface_text: 这家火锅店推出单人套餐，广告写着：一个人也能吃出“社饱感”。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是一个人吃火锅也能获得饱足和被照顾的满足感。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means even solo diners can feel full and emotionally satisfied.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“社交感”和“饱腹感”拼接，表示不必靠热闹社交也能获得类似聚餐满足。
interpretation_2_en: It blends 'social feeling' and 'sense of fullness,' suggesting you can get the warmth of social dining even when eating alone.
context: 适用于餐饮广告、单人消费场景文案。
literal_translation: This hotpot restaurant launched a solo set meal, with the slogan: even one person can eat up a 'social-fullness feeling.'
functional_equivalence_translation: Their solo hotpot set still gives you that full, cozy group-dining vibe.
explanatory_translation: The pun merges '社交感' (social atmosphere) with '饱腹感' (physical fullness), creating a hybrid consumer phrase for solo dining.
interpretation_1: 一个人也很满足
interpretation_2: 社交感与饱腹感叠加

surface_text: 郭先生找了一个女朋友，女朋友姓缴，郭先生的母亲强烈反对他们的恋爱。母亲说：“一个做生意的朋友姓钱，原本生意做得红红火火，因为娶了一个姓裴的老婆，做什么赔什么，后来日子过得一塌糊涂，两人还总打架。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是说那位姓钱的朋友自从娶了姓裴的老婆后，生意运气很差，干什么都赔本亏钱。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the wife’s surname is Pei, and after marrying her, the businessman started losing money in everything he did.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“赔”和妻子的姓“裴”联系起来，借谐音暗示“娶了姓裴的人就会赔”，以此类推反对郭先生和姓缴的女朋友恋爱。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a pun on the surname "Pei" and the word "pei" meaning "to lose money" or "to赔," implying that marrying a woman with that surname brings bad business luck.
context: 母亲以姓名谐音判断婚配吉凶，前文有“钱”与“裴”组成“钱赔”的类比，支撑“缴”被按谐音联想解读。
literal_translation: Mr. Guo found a girlfriend whose surname was Jiao. Mr. Guo's mother strongly opposed their relationship. She said, “A businessman friend surnamed Qian used to have a thriving business, but after marrying a wife surnamed Pei, whatever he did led to losses. Later their life became a mess, and they fought all the time.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Mr. Guo's mother objected to his girlfriend because she believed the girl's surname sounded unlucky with his. She cited another couple: a man named Qian married a woman named Pei, and together their names sounded like “money lost,” and sure enough, everything went downhill.
explanatory_translation: The joke relies on Chinese surname sound associations. The mother treats surnames as omens: “Qian” plus “Pei” sounds like “qian pei” (“money lost”), so she uses that as evidence that marrying someone with an unfortunate-sounding surname brings bad luck. The surname “Jiao”/“缴” is likewise being rejected because of a sound-based associative reading rather than its literal surname meaning.
interpretation_1: 女朋友的姓氏是“缴”。
interpretation_2: 母亲借“缴”联想到“交”，暗指“郭+交”接近“过交”，并与后文“钱+裴=钱赔”类比，认为名字组合不吉利、会影响婚恋或运势。

surface_text: 在我上大学时的一个早晨，很多的同学共同在一起吃早点，这时来了一个穿着时髦的美眉，她走着走着不时地打喷涕。 这时来了另一个女生，远远地就问她：小丽，感冒了？ 由于距离远，她也就远远地大声的回答道：我不是感冒，我是发烧（骚）！ 我们一群人笑晕了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是说她不是感冒，而是发烧，表示自己在发热、生病了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she is saying that she does not have a cold; instead, she has a fever.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“发烧”与“发骚”的近音制造双关，实际让人联想到“发骚”，即卖弄风情、显得轻佻骚气。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from the near-homophone of "fever" and "flirtatious/sexy" in Chinese, so it sounds like she is joking that she is not sick but rather acting seductive or being sexually attractive.
context: 女生打喷嚏，被远处同学问是不是感冒；她高声回答“我不是感冒，我是发烧（骚）”。
literal_translation: I’m not catching a cold, I’m having a fever.
functional_equivalence_translation: I don’t have a cold—I’m hot, not sick.
explanatory_translation: She says, “I don’t have a cold, I have a fever,” but the joke relies on a near-homophone: “fever” sounds like “flirty/sexy,” implying she is not ill but acting fashionable and seductive.
interpretation_1: 说自己不是感冒而是身体发烧，指生病发热。
interpretation_2: 借“烧”和“骚”的近音，暗含自己打扮时髦、风骚。

surface_text: 这部电影很上头，剧情让人上头，票价也让我有点上头。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“上头”指剧情精彩刺激，让人沉浸其中停不下来，带有明显的着迷和投入意味。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'shangtou' means something is highly engaging or addictive: the movie and its plot are so captivating that they make people excited and immersed.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“上头”指票价高得让人头脑发热、略感心痛，表达对价格刺激过强的无奈情绪。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'shangtou' also suggests feeling dizzy, overwhelmed, or mentally pained; here it shifts to the ticket price being so high that it gives the speaker a headache.
context: 同一句中前两次说电影和剧情“上头”表示好看上瘾，后一次说票价“上头”转为价格带来的心理不适。
literal_translation: This movie is very addictive; the plot gets you hooked, and the ticket price also makes me a bit light-headed.
functional_equivalence_translation: This movie is a real rush—the plot is intoxicating, and the ticket price is a shock too.
explanatory_translation: "Shangtou" first means the movie and plot are so engaging that they get you hooked, but then it shifts to mean the ticket price is so high that it makes the speaker feel dazed or pained.
interpretation_1: 形容电影剧情很有吸引力，让人兴奋、沉迷。
interpretation_2: 形容票价太高让人发懵、心疼，甚至有点恼火。

surface_text: 小时候妹妹问我几点了，我答：三扁担（三点半）！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把时间说成“三扁担”，字面上像是在说三根扁担，是一种故意说岔的趣味表达。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker literally answers the time as 'three carrying poles.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义实际指“三点半”，利用“三扁担”与“三点半”的近音关系来回答时间。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is 'half past three' because 'three carrying poles' sounds like 'three-thirty' in Chinese.
context: 妹妹问时间，回答者用近音说法把“三点半”说成“三扁担”。
literal_translation: When I was little, my younger sister asked me what time it was, and I answered: three carrying poles (three-thirty)!
functional_equivalence_translation: When I was little, my sister asked the time, and I said, “tree-thirty” instead of “three-thirty.”
explanatory_translation: When I was little, my younger sister asked me the time, and I replied with a near-sounding phrase “three carrying poles,” which is used as a joke to mimic “three-thirty.”
interpretation_1: 表层上像是在说“三扁担”，即三根扁担。
interpretation_2: 实际回答的是时间“三点半”。

surface_text: 英语课上，小张上课不专心，老师忽然提问：小张，狗怎么读？小张吓一跳边起立边喊了一声：到。对了，dog，请坐下。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层是在英语课上提问单词“dog”怎么读，要求回答其英文读音。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the teacher is asking how to pronounce or read the English word “dog,” and then confirms that the correct word is “dog.”
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含是小张把老师点名后的课堂应答当成了提问内容，先喊“到”表示自己在，形成把“dog”和“到”联系起来的谐音式误解。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that Xiao Zhang mistakes the question for a classroom roll-call response and answers “Here!” (“到”), as if he were being called on rather than asked to read the word.
context: 英语课上，老师问“狗怎么读”，走神的学生误以为被点名，起立答“到”，随后老师纠正为“dog”
literal_translation: In English class, Xiao Zhang was not paying attention. The teacher suddenly asked, “Xiao Zhang, how do you read ‘dog’?” Startled, Xiao Zhang stood up and shouted, “Present!” “Right, dog. Please sit down.”
functional_equivalence_translation: In English class, the teacher called on a distracted student: “How do you read ‘dog’?” Startled, he jumped up and answered as if to a roll call, “Present!” The teacher smiled: “Yes, ‘dog’. You may sit down.”
explanatory_translation: The joke is that the teacher asks in class, “How do you read ‘dog’?” but the inattentive student mistakes it for being called on by name and reflexively answers “到” (“present”), which fits a classroom roll-call situation rather than the English question.
interpretation_1: 学生把老师的点名式提问误解为需要答“到”
interpretation_2: 老师实际是在英语课上提问单词“dog”怎么读

surface_text: 他真会卡点，视频剪得会卡点，迟到也总卡着点来。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“卡点”指视频剪辑精准贴合节奏和节点，让画面转换与音乐配合得非常到位。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means he is good at timing video edits precisely, hitting beats or key moments in the footage.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“卡着点”指他到达时间总踩在边缘，几乎迟到却又勉强赶上，带点戏谑意味。
interpretation_2_en: It also means he always arrives exactly at the deadline or the last possible moment, especially when being late.
context: 同一句中先说视频剪得会卡点，再说迟到也总卡着点来，形成两个相关义项的并列。
negative_example: 他真会踩点，视频剪得会踩点，迟到也总踩着点来。
literal_translation: He is really good at hitting the point: he edits videos right on the beat, and when he is late, he also always arrives right at the time point.
functional_equivalence_translation: He’s great at timing things—his video cuts hit every beat, and even his late arrivals are perfectly timed.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on "卡点," which can mean editing a video to match precise beats or timing points, and also arriving exactly at a critical time point, such as barely making it or being late by design.
interpretation_1: 指视频剪辑时精准踩在节奏点或关键时间点上。
interpretation_2: 指人做事总是掐着时间点，尤其是迟到时刚好卡在某个界限上出现。

surface_text: 这款收纳箱简直是“房间瘦身搭子”，装进去的是杂物，省出来的是呼吸感。
hidden_form: 瘦身 / 搭子 / 空间整理
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指帮助房间减少杂乱、显得更整洁轻盈的收纳工具。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a storage tool that helps a room look less cluttered and more spacious.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把人的“瘦身”概念转移到房间上，再借“搭子”这种网络构词制造亲切的消费表达。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it transfers the idea of a person's 'slimming down' to a room, then uses the trendy label 'buddy/partner' to create a friendly consumer phrase.
context: 适用于家居收纳广告、生活方式种草、租房整理内容。
literal_translation: This storage box is basically a 'room-slimming buddy'; what goes in is clutter, and what comes out is room to breathe.
functional_equivalence_translation: This storage box is your room's decluttering buddy—it hides the mess and gives the space room to breathe.
explanatory_translation: The phrase hybridizes 'slimming' with 'room' and adds the trendy internet suffix-like word 'buddy'. The pun works through metaphorical word formation, not simple sound similarity.
interpretation_1: 帮房间收纳减负
interpretation_2: 把瘦身概念嫁接到空间

surface_text: 朋友换了新床垫后宣布自己进入“躺赢学”阶段：不是摆烂，是终于把睡眠当成硬实力。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是研究如何通过躺着休息获得更好的状态，突出睡眠的重要性。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a 'study of winning by lying down,' emphasizing the value of rest and sleep.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借用网络词“躺赢”，把被动获益改造成一种生活方法论。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning borrows the internet slang 'win effortlessly' and reframes it as a lifestyle doctrine.
context: 适用于家居营销、睡眠话题、自我调侃。
negative_example: 他最近开始研究睡眠学。
literal_translation: After changing to a new mattress, my friend announced that he had entered the stage of 'lying-down winning studies': not giving up, but finally treating sleep as a hard skill.
functional_equivalence_translation: After getting a new mattress, he claims to major in 'sleep-to-win'—not laziness, just strategic rest.
explanatory_translation: The pun turns the slang 'win by lying down' into a mock academic term by adding 'studies,' making it sound both humorous and systematic.
interpretation_1: 研究睡眠休息
interpretation_2: 借躺赢表达轻松获益

surface_text: 有一天记者采访时传祥： “你是做什么工作的？” “捞翔。” 记者一愣： “捞翔，腻也是河南人？”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，“捞翔”是在回答自己的工作内容，意思是打捞粪便、从事清掏粪便之类的工作。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "lao xiang" is understood as the Henan-dialect way of saying "fellow townsman" or "someone from the same hometown," so the reporter thinks he is also from Henan.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，“捞翔”与“老乡”近音，记者把这句话误听成带河南口音的“老乡”，于是理解成对方在说自己是河南人。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that Shi Chuanxiang actually means "scooping out night soil / cleaning cesspits" as his job, but his reply sounds like "lao xiang," creating the pun.
context: 时传祥回答自己的工作内容时说“捞翔”，记者将其误解为带河南口音的“老乡”，于是追问“你也是河南人？”
literal_translation: One day a reporter interviewed Shi Chuanxiang: “What do you do for work?” “I scoop dung.” The reporter froze for a moment: “Fellow townsman? You’re from Henan too?”
functional_equivalence_translation: “What do you do?” “I haul muck.” “Hull… what? Oh—‘homie’? You’re from Henan too?”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “捞翔,” which literally means scooping dung in context, but sounds similar to “老乡” (“fellow townsman”). The reporter mishears the job answer as a regional form of address and asks whether he is also from Henan.
interpretation_1: 表层上指从事掏粪、捞粪的工作。
interpretation_2: 被记者误听为“老乡”，即同乡、河南人之间的称呼。

surface_text: 这款收纳箱被网友封为“箱想力”神器，东西一进箱，房间和心情都像重新有了想象空间。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是收纳箱很能装、很会整理，帮助释放居住空间。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the storage box is highly practical for organizing and freeing up living space.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义仿拟“想象力”，表示收纳不只是装东西，还能让空间、秩序和生活方式重新被构想。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning remodels 'imagination,' suggesting that storage does more than hold things—it lets people reimagine space, order, and lifestyle.
context: 适用于家居收纳产品宣传、生活方式短视频文案。
literal_translation: This storage box has been dubbed a 'box-agination' miracle by netizens.
functional_equivalence_translation: This storage box doesn't just organize your room—it gives your space a whole new imagination.
explanatory_translation: The expression blends 箱 ('box') into 想象力 ('imagination'), creating a hybrid word that points both to a storage box and to the new possibilities opened up by tidying space.
interpretation_1: 收纳箱提升整理力
interpretation_2: 收纳激发空间想象

surface_text: 父亲：刚开学考试，你怎么就得了个零分？ 儿子：老师说，我们一切都要从零开始。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上儿子把老师的话理解为考试得零分也符合“从零开始”，用“零”直接对应分数。
interpretation_1_en: The son takes the teacher's words literally: since everything should start from zero, getting a zero on the test seems appropriate.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是老师原本想表达新学期学习要从头起步、重新开始，并不是让学生考零分。
interpretation_2_en: The teacher actually meant that at the beginning of a new term, students should begin anew and work from the basics, not that they should score zero points.
context: 父亲责问儿子刚开学考试得了零分，儿子借用老师“ 一切都要从零开始 ”的话为自己辩解。
literal_translation: Father: School has just started, how did you already get a zero on the exam? Son: The teacher said that we should start everything from zero.
functional_equivalence_translation: Father: How did you get a zero so soon after school started? Son: Teacher said everything starts from zero, so I did too.
explanatory_translation: The son plays on “start from zero”: the teacher means starting from the basics, but he twists it to mean literally getting a zero score first.
interpretation_1: 老师的话本义是学习要从基础开始。
interpretation_2: 儿子故意曲解成考试先拿零分也算从零开始。

surface_text: 班主任准备去李明同学家家访，班主任问李明的家庭住址，李明说：“我家在接二连三的地方。” 班主任说：“你是不欢迎我吗？” 李明说：“不是这意思，我是说我家在新市二路与新市三路的结合部。”
hidden_form: 新市二路与新市三路的结合部
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上“接二连三”是成语，意思是一个接一个、连续不断，像是在故意含糊其辞，不直接说家庭住址。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “接二连三” is understood as the idiom meaning “one after another” or “repeatedly,” which makes the teacher feel that Li Ming is being vague or joking instead of giving a real address.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上是把“二”和“三”理解为两条路名中的数字，表示新市二路与新市三路连接相交的地方，也就是他家的具体位置。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that Li Ming is referring literally to a location between New City Second Road and New City Third Road, using “二” and “三” to indicate the junction of those two roads.
context: 班主任询问李明家庭住址，李明用“接二连三”回答，后文说明实际指新市二路与新市三路的结合部。
literal_translation: My home is in the place of 'connecting two and linking three.'
functional_equivalence_translation: My home is right where Two Road meets Three Road.
explanatory_translation: Li Ming uses the idiom '接二连三,' which normally means 'one after another,' but here he twists it to mean the junction where No. 2 Road connects with No. 3 Road.
interpretation_1: 通常表示一个接一个、连续不断。
interpretation_2: 在语境中被解释为“二路连着三路”的地理位置，即两条路交接处。

surface_text: 这家书店把靠窗座位区称为“发呆阅”，牌子上写着：欢迎来这里，读两页，想十页。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是一个适合阅读、放慢节奏的座位区名称。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it names a seating area suited for reading and slowing down.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义把“发呆”和“阅”拼接，表达在书店里阅读与神游并存的松弛感。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning blends 'daydreaming' and 'reading', suggesting the relaxed bookstore experience of reading while letting the mind wander.
context: 适用于书店分区命名、文艺空间文案。
literal_translation: This bookstore calls its window-side seating area 'daydream-read': come here, read two pages, think ten pages.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bookstore labels its window seats 'read-and-drift'—read a little, wander a lot.
explanatory_translation: The pun is a blended form combining 'fadai' (to daydream) and 'yue' (to read). It captures the dual function of a bookstore corner: reading and pleasant mental drifting.
interpretation_1: 适合阅读的区
interpretation_2: 阅读兼发呆

surface_text: 食人族不会吃离婚妇女......他们非常苦涩。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是食人族不吃离婚妇女，因为她们让人感觉非常苦涩，像味道发苦发涩一样。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means cannibals would not eat divorced women because they taste very bitter.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含意思是借“苦涩”谐指“苦色”，即脸色愁苦、神情哀怨，因此食人族嫌她们看起来一脸苦相，不愿意吃。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that divorced women have gone through emotional hardship and are therefore metaphorically 'bitter' or full of bitterness.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：前文说食人族不吃离婚妇女，后句用“她们非常苦涩”解释原因，将人的愁苦状态与食物味道连接。
literal_translation: Cannibals won't eat divorced women... they are very bitter.
functional_equivalence_translation: Cannibals won't eat divorced women—they're too bitter.
explanatory_translation: Cannibals won't eat divorced women, because they are “bitter”: on the surface this means they would taste bitter, but it also hints that divorced women look sorrowful or emotionally bitter.
interpretation_1: 表层义是味道苦、不好吃，说明食人族不吃离婚妇女是因为她们“很苦涩”。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“苦色/苦相”，指离婚妇女面带愁苦神色，把情绪状态借成口味评价形成笑点。

surface_text: 马加爵，枪毙了；药加鑫，判死刑！加爵、加薪都是死路一条，历史的血的经验告诉我们：只有加班才是最安全的．．．
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上说的是“加薪”这件事，但在句中被说成和“加爵”一样危险，形成荒诞反差，最后反衬“只有加班最安全”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it says that 'getting a raise' is a dead end, jokingly grouping 'jia xin' with the names Jiajue and Jiaxin and claiming that only working overtime is safe.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“加薪”借“薪”与“鑫”的近音，实际影射“药家鑫”，与前面的“马加爵”并列，意思是名字里带“加爵”“加鑫”都没好下场。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a phonetic pun: '加薪' (salary increase) sounds like '药家鑫', so the phrase plays on the similarity in sound between an ordinary word and the name of a criminal case to create dark humor.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境
literal_translation: Ma Jiajue was executed by shooting; Yao Jiaxin was sentenced to death! Whether adding rank or adding salary, both lead to a dead end. Bloody lessons from history tell us that only working overtime is the safest.
functional_equivalence_translation: Ma Jiajue was executed, Yao Jiaxin got the death penalty—so "promotion" and "pay raise" both seem deadly; only overtime is safe.
explanatory_translation: This joke plays on the similar-looking/similar-sounding forms of the names Ma Jiajue and Yao Jiaxin with the common words "jia jue" (to confer a title/rank) and "jia xin" (to raise salary), then contrasts them with "jia ban" (to work overtime) for dark humor.
interpretation_1: 表层上把“加爵”“加薪”“加班”并列成三个以“加+X”构成的词语。
interpretation_2: 借“加爵”与案件人物名“马加爵”、“加薪”与案件人物名“药加鑫”的谐近与字形替换，制造“加爵、加薪都危险，只有加班安全”的黑色幽默。

surface_text: 公司招聘。有人说：“我叫刘产。”老板吐血：“ 没人怀孕！没人流产”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把姓名说成“刘产”，听起来像在说“流产”，老板因此按字面理解成与怀孕、流产有关的话题。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the boss hears the word as 'miscarriage,' so he reacts by saying that no one is pregnant and no one has had a miscarriage.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是应聘者本意只是自我介绍姓名，常规表达更可能是“我叫刘畅”等近音名字，但因读音近似触发了“流产”的医疗含义。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the speaker's name 'Liu Chan' sounds like 'miscarriage' in Chinese, creating a pun based on similar pronunciation.
context: 公司招聘时，应聘者报出名字“刘产”，老板将其听成“流产”，于是接着说“没人怀孕！没人流产”。
literal_translation: The company is hiring. Someone said, “My name is Liu Chan.” The boss spat blood: “No one is pregnant! No one is having a miscarriage!”
functional_equivalence_translation: The company was hiring. An applicant said, “My name is Liu Chan,” and the boss freaked out, mishearing it as “miscarriage”: “Nobody’s pregnant here!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese name “Liu Chan” sounding exactly like “liuchan,” meaning “miscarriage.” The boss mistakes the applicant’s name for the word “miscarriage,” so he blurts out that nobody is pregnant and nobody is miscarrying.
interpretation_1: 应聘者自我介绍，姓刘名产，是一个人名。
interpretation_2: 老板误听为“流产”，即怀孕后胎儿意外终止。

surface_text: 这家书店真安静，环境安静，连老板的心也很安静。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“安静”指书店空间里没有喧闹声，阅读环境平和舒适，适合长时间停留与看书。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the bookstore is very quiet: the environment is quiet, and even the owner seems calm and silent.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“安静”指老板性情沉稳、不浮躁，内心平和克制，给人一种从容而宁静的感觉。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the owner is not only in a quiet place but also has an inwardly peaceful, settled state of mind.
context: 前两处“安静”描述书店环境，后一处“老板的心也很安静”把通常用于环境的词并置到心理状态上。
literal_translation: This bookstore is really quiet: the environment is quiet, and even the owner's heart is quiet.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bookstore is so quiet—the room is quiet, and even the owner seems inwardly quiet.
explanatory_translation: This bookstore is very quiet: not only is the place quiet, but the owner is also calm inside. The pun-like effect comes from repeating “quiet” for both the physical environment and a person's inner state.
interpretation_1: 指书店环境没有噪音、很安静。
interpretation_2: 指老板内心平和沉静，情绪很平静。

surface_text: 某日，访问我的一个老同学。来到他的寝室门口，轻扣三下，里面的人冒失的问：外头啥人？ 一怔之下顺口回答：我。 许久，里面的人迟疑的问：我是谁？
有个中国留学生教外国同学中文，那个同学请他吃饭。 饭桌上，中国留学生想考考这个外国学生，问：“吃饭饱了用中文怎么说。” 外国同学答：“我饱了。” 又问：“很饱怎么说。” 外国同学答：“我撑着了。” 留学生继续问：“很饱很撑怎么说。” 外国同学想了下答：“我吃饱了撑的。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是把“饱了”和“撑着了”机械组合，意思是我已经吃得很饱，而且撑得难受。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it literally means: 'I ate so much that I am full and bloated.' The foreign student is simply combining 'full' and 'stuffed' into one sentence.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上激活了固定说法“吃饱了撑的”，是口语里指人闲得无聊、没事找事，并不只是字面上的吃太饱。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the Chinese idiom '吃饱了撑的', which is used sarcastically to mean 'having nothing better to do' or 'doing something unnecessary out of boredom.'
context: 先问“我饱了”“我撑着了”，再追问“很饱很撑怎么说”，诱发把俗语误当作程度加深的字面表达。
literal_translation: I’m full and stuffed from eating.
functional_equivalence_translation: I’m so full it sounds like I’m saying a phrase that also means “I’m just doing pointless stuff.”
explanatory_translation: The punchline uses “吃饱了撑的,” which literally means “so full that one is stuffed,” but in Chinese it is also a fixed expression meaning “having nothing better to do” or “doing something pointless.”
interpretation_1: 字面上表示吃得很饱，已经撑到了。
interpretation_2: 俗语里表示人没事找事、做多余的事。

surface_text: 老师告诫全体同学。 老师：同学们可别贪玩了，要珍惜时间呀！古人说少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲。 某生：老师，我是老二。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“老大”出自俗语“少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲”，意思是年老、长大以后只能空自悲伤。
interpretation_1_en: In the saying 'If you do not work hard when young, you will be sad when old,' 'laoda' means being old or elderly.
interpretation_2_zh: 学生把“老大”故意理解成排行第一的人，并借“我是老二”来调侃，触发了把年龄义转成排行义的双关。
interpretation_2_en: The student deliberately misreads 'laoda' as 'the eldest child' or 'number one,' and jokes that he is 'laoer'—the second child—so the warning does not apply to him.
context: 老师引用“少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲”劝学生珍惜时间，学生将其中“老大”从年龄义故意转成排行称谓义来接话。
literal_translation: Teacher: Students, don't just play around; cherish your time. As the ancients said, 'If one does not work hard when young, one will only grieve when old.' A student said: Teacher, I'm the second one.
functional_equivalence_translation: Teacher: Don't waste your youth, or you'll be sorry when you're older. Student: But sir, I'm not the eldest—I'm number two.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the phrase “老大徒伤悲,” where “老大” means “when one is old,” but the student deliberately misreads it as “the eldest one” and replies, “I'm the second one.”
interpretation_1: 学生把“老大”按排行身份理解为家中或群体中的老大。
interpretation_2: 原句“老大徒伤悲”中的“老大”本义是年老、长大后，并非排行老大；学生故意曲解成排行称呼并说自己是老二。

surface_text: 朋友说他最近进入“省钱静养期”，其实就是把购物车当电子鱼缸，只看不捞。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是为了控制支出，进入一种减少消费、安静生活的阶段。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means entering a quiet, low-spending phase in order to save money.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用“静养期”这一身体恢复说法，把财务状态拟人化，像钱包需要休养生息。
interpretation_2_en: It also borrows the term 'recovery period,' personifying one's finances as if the wallet itself needs rest and healing.
context: 适用于消费克制、月底穷、理性购物等生活表达。
negative_example: 他最近在省钱，不怎么买东西。
literal_translation: My friend said he recently entered a 'money-saving recovery period'; actually it just means treating the shopping cart like a digital fish tank—looking but not scooping.
functional_equivalence_translation: He says he's in a 'financial recovery phase,' which really means window-shopping online and buying nothing.
explanatory_translation: The phrase fuses 'saving money' with 'recovery period,' creating a hybrid label that humorously frames budget control as medical-style recuperation.
interpretation_1: 控制消费阶段
interpretation_2: 钱包需要静养

surface_text: 有人的木拖鞋被偷，骂道：哼，要拿我的木拖鞋去做棺材盖。 别人问道：木拖鞋怎么能做棺材盖？ 答道：我的木拖鞋是板皮料。（棺材盖也是板皮料。）
老婆坐在沙发上看着电视， 老公凑过来问我“宝贝，你说你有多疼我？” 老婆想了想，站起身来，一边啪啪啪的甩耳光一边说道：“这么疼。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“疼”被按字面理解为身体上的疼痛，所以老婆用甩耳光来展示“这么疼”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the husband asks, 'Baby, how much do you love/cherish me?' where '疼' is understood as emotional affection or doting love.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里“疼我”本是口语中“爱我、宠我”的意思，老公原本是在问老婆有多爱他。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the wife interprets '疼' as physical pain, so she slaps him and says, 'This much pain.'
context: 老公问“你有多疼我”，常规理解是“你有多爱我”；老婆随即扇耳光，用动作把“疼”转成“痛”的字面义。
literal_translation: The wife was sitting on the sofa watching TV. The husband came over and asked, “Baby, how much do you hurt for me?” The wife thought for a moment, stood up, and while slapping him repeatedly said, “This much.”
functional_equivalence_translation: “How much do you love me?” he asked. She got up, slapped him a few times, and said, “About this much pain.”
explanatory_translation: In Chinese, “疼” can mean both “to dote on/love” and “to feel pain.” The husband means “How much do you love me?”, but the wife deliberately interprets it as physical pain and answers by slapping him: “This much.”
interpretation_1: 关心、心疼、爱惜对方的程度
interpretation_2: 身体上感到疼痛的程度

surface_text: 今天在看电视的时候看到一群日本鬼子进了城，有了以下对话。 其中一个鬼子说：怎么一个人都没？他们是想关门打狗吗？ 另一个鬼子骂到：什么叫关门打狗？我们是狗吗？这应该叫瓮中捉鳖…… 好强的语文功底。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是鬼子纠正说法，认为不该用“关门打狗”来形容当前局面，而应改成“瓮中捉鳖”，意思是城门一关、对方被困住后再进行围捕。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the dialogue jokes about choosing the more accurate idiom: instead of saying 'shut the door and beat the dog,' the speaker says it should be 'catch a turtle in a jar,' because they do not want to compare themselves to dogs.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上是借“关门打狗”中的“狗”来影射日本鬼子，把他们比作狗；后面改说“瓮中捉鳖”是在回避这个带有辱骂指向的说法，笑点来自成语替换触发的讽刺意味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that both idioms describe being trapped and attacked with no way out, and the humor comes from the enemy absurdly focusing on which animal metaphor fits them better, showing a twisted kind of linguistic precision.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：两名侵略者进城后发现城里没人，一人用“关门打狗”形容局势，另一人因觉得“狗”影射自己而改说“瓮中捉鳖”。
literal_translation: While watching TV today, I saw a group of Japanese invaders enter the city and got this dialogue. One said: Why is there nobody here? Are they trying to shut the door and beat the dog? Another cursed: What do you mean shut the door and beat the dog? Are we dogs? This should be called catching a turtle in a jar... Such strong command of Chinese.
functional_equivalence_translation: One invader said, "Is this a trap to shut us in and finish us off?" The other snapped, "Finish off the dogs? Are we dogs? Say 'fish in a barrel' instead!"
explanatory_translation: The joke comes from replacing one Chinese idiom with another. The first idiom, "关门打狗," literally says "shut the door and beat the dog," meaning to trap and defeat someone. The second speaker objects because that would make them the "dog," so he switches to "瓮中捉鳖" (literally "catch a soft-shelled turtle in a jar"), another idiom about trapping prey. The humor is a semantic substitution, not a sound-based pun.
interpretation_1: 表层是在讨论一个成语用得是否恰当，用来形容把敌人困住后再收拾。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是说话者因不愿把自己对应为“狗”，改用“鳖”替换成语中的被攻击对象，形成自嘲式错位幽默。

surface_text: 刘老汉的儿子初中毕业后，跟本村人去城里打工。 回家过年，刘老汉发现儿子身上有伤疤，忙问：“你在外面干什么？” 儿子说：“我专帮房地产包头搭架。” 刘老汉说：“你去帮人打架，做一棍子买卖，怪不得受伤了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 刘老汉把儿子说的“搭架”误听成了“打架”，理解为在外面替人动手斗殴、干危险的勾当，所以觉得受伤是因为打架所致。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the father understands "da jia" as "to fight," so he thinks his son has been helping people get into brawls, which explains the scars.
interpretation_2_zh: 儿子实际说的是帮房地产包工头搭脚手架、做建筑搭架子的活，是建筑工地上的体力劳动，并不是与人争斗打架。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the son actually means "building scaffolding frames" on construction sites for real-estate contractors; "da jia" here refers to erecting work frames, not fighting.
context: 儿子说自己“专帮房地产包头搭架”，父亲将“搭架”误解为“打架”，并据此联想到“做一棍子买卖”和受伤原因。
literal_translation: Old Liu’s son graduated from junior high school and went to the city with fellow villagers to work. When he came home for the New Year, Old Liu found scars on him and hurriedly asked, “What have you been doing out there?” The son said, “I specifically help real-estate foremen put up scaffolding.” Old Liu said, “So you went to help people fight, making a living with sticks. No wonder you got hurt.”
functional_equivalence_translation: “What do you do in the city?” “I help builders raise frames.” “Raise fists? No wonder you came back covered in scars.”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the son’s “搭架” (to put up frames/scaffolding), which the father mishears as the near-sounding “打架” (to fight). The joke comes from this sound-based misunderstanding.
interpretation_1: 给房地产包工头搭建脚手架或架子，从事建筑劳务。
interpretation_2: 被误听成“打架”，即与人斗殴、靠打斗谋生。

surface_text: 同事把午休散步路线叫“摸鱼步道”，走得不快，但每一步都很有工位逃离感。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指一条适合散步放松的小步道。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a walkway meant for a leisurely stroll.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含“摸鱼”这一职场网络词，表示借散步之名短暂逃离工作。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it uses the workplace slang 'slacking off' to describe taking a walk as a temporary escape from work.
context: 适用于职场闲聊、办公区周边环境描述、社交媒体吐槽。
literal_translation: A colleague calls the lunch-break walking route the 'slacking trail'; it's not a fast walk, but every step feels like escaping the desk.
functional_equivalence_translation: We call our lunch-break route the 'slack-off trail'—a little walk with big escape energy.
explanatory_translation: The coined phrase combines 'walkway' with the Chinese internet slang for 'goofing off at work', turning an ordinary path into a humorous symbol of workplace escape.
interpretation_1: 适合散步的小道
interpretation_2: 借散步名义摸鱼

surface_text: 这款便携咖啡杯主打“醒李箱”概念，出差党说：箱子装衣服，它装清醒。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义指一种适合携带、和行李搭配使用的咖啡杯概念。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a travel-friendly coffee cup concept associated with luggage.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义把“行李箱”改成“醒李箱”，强调出行时它像随身携带的清醒来源。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning alters 'luggage' into 'wakefulness-luggage', stressing that it carries alertness during travel.
context: 适用于咖啡杯、出行用品广告。
literal_translation: This portable coffee cup promotes the concept of a 'wake-suitcase': travelers say a suitcase holds clothes, while this one holds alertness.
functional_equivalence_translation: This travel mug is marketed as your 'carry-on caffeine'—your suitcase carries clothes, this carries consciousness.
explanatory_translation: The pun remodels 'xinglixiang' (suitcase) into 'xing Li xiang', replacing the first character with 'wakefulness'. The hybrid form links travel gear with coffee's energizing effect.
interpretation_1: 旅行咖啡杯
interpretation_2: 随身带清醒

surface_text: 老板看了新来的整理师直点头：这不是会收拾，这是自带“归纳气场”。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指一个人特别擅长归类整理，仿佛自带让物品自动就位的气势。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to someone being so good at sorting and organizing that they seem to radiate an ordering aura.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上借“气场”这个人格化词，把整理能力夸张成一种可感知的个人魅力。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it uses the notion of an 'aura' to personify organizational skill as a kind of charisma.
context: 适用于职场评价、家政整理、社交媒体夸人表达。
literal_translation: The boss nodded at the new organizer: this isn't just being good at tidying up; this is having a built-in 'sorting aura.'
functional_equivalence_translation: The boss was impressed: this isn't mere tidiness—it's a whole 'decluttering aura.'
explanatory_translation: The pun hybridizes the abstract social term 'aura' with the concrete act of sorting and categorizing, creating a playful new expression that elevates organization into charisma.
interpretation_1: 很会归类整理
interpretation_2: 整理变成气场

surface_text: 一流浪汉行夜路，被一强盗拦下，抢匪晃着旨首喝道:要钱还是要命。 流浪汉想，我自己一条命都养不活，再要一条命干嘛，不如要点钱实在，于是对抢匪说道：还是要钱吧。
电视正在播放无绳电话的广告，就在这时，家里的电话响了，原来是找爸爸的。 儿子便用剪刀把电话线剪断，拿给爸爸。 “爸爸电话！无绳的！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是儿子把电话线剪断后，把变成没有电话线的电话拿给爸爸，说这是“无绳的”电话。
interpretation_1_en: "Cordless" literally means a telephone that has no cord attached, so the boy says, "Dad, phone! It's cordless!" after handing over a phone with no wire.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“无绳”借作对“无声”的误解或替代，实际剪断电话线后电话无法正常通话，带有把广告里的“无绳电话”和现实中“不能出声”的电话混淆的幽默效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "cordless" normally refers to a specially designed cordless phone from the advertisement, but the boy misunderstands it and creates a 'cordless' phone by cutting the wire.
context: 先播放“无绳电话”广告，随后家里电话响起，儿子误把“无绳电话”理解为“没有线的电话”，于是剪断电话线交给爸爸。
literal_translation: "Dad, phone! A cordless one!"
functional_equivalence_translation: "Dad, your phone—it's cord-less now!"
explanatory_translation: The son hears an ad for a cordless phone, then literally interprets it as a phone with no cord, so he cuts the phone cord and tells his father, "Dad, your phone—it's cord-less now!"
interpretation_1: 广告中的“无绳电话”指一种电话类型，即听筒与座机之间没有连接线。
interpretation_2: 儿子把电话线剪断后，说“无绳的”是按字面理解为这部电话现在没有绳/线了。

surface_text: 昨天中午和同事聊房价。我说：“现在房价这么贵，如果我有块地，那真是发达了！” 他说：“你要是有块地，我马上认你作干爹！” 刚说完，前台那边小姑娘喊我：“XX，你有快递！” 后来，整个下午我干儿子都不愿意和我说话。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是前台在通知“你有快递”，意思是有你的包裹需要领取。
interpretation_1_en: The receptionist is literally saying that there is a package for me: 'You have express delivery.'
interpretation_2_zh: 由于“有快递”与前文“有块地”近音，引发同事把这句话听成“你有块地”，于是联想到先前说过要认作干爹的话，形成双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: It sounds like 'you have a piece of land,' which echoes the earlier joke that if I owned land, my colleague would call me godfather.
context: 先在谈房价并说“如果我有块地，那真是发达了”，同事接话说“你要是有块地，我马上认你作干爹”，随后前台喊“你有快递”，与“有块地”形成近音误听。
literal_translation: Yesterday at noon I was chatting with a colleague about housing prices. I said, “Prices are so high now. If I had a piece of land, I'd really be set!” He said, “If you had a piece of land, I'd call you godfather right away!” Right after that, the girl at the front desk shouted, “XX, you have a delivery!” Later, my godson refused to talk to me the whole afternoon.
functional_equivalence_translation: At lunch we were talking about real estate. I joked, “If I owned some land, I'd be rich.” My coworker said, “If you own land, I'll call you Dad.” Just then the receptionist yelled, “You've got mail!” He misheard it as “You've got a lot,” and sulked all afternoon as my new “son.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the near-homophone in Chinese between “块地” (a piece of land) and “快递” (delivery/package). After joking that having land would make him rich, the speaker is called by the receptionist for a package, but the coworker hears it like “you have land,” so he thinks the joke has come true and becomes the speaker’s “godson.”
interpretation_1: 前台在喊“你有快递”，意思是有包裹需要领取。
interpretation_2: 同事误听成“你有块地”，以为说话人真的有一块地，因此顺势把前面的玩笑当真，认其作“干爹”。

surface_text: 一个顾客指着刚买的菜叹息道：唉，这熘肉怎么才这么几片肉？ 另一位顾客接茬道：肉要是不会溜，能叫熘肉片吗？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“熘肉片”的“熘”借成“溜走”的“溜”，意思是肉片之所以少，好像是因为肉会自己溜走了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker is jokingly taking the dish name literally: if the meat in 'liu pork slices' did not 'slip away,' how could it be called that?
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“熘肉片”中的“熘”本来是烹调方法，指用旺火快炒并勾芡，不是真的“溜走”，这是借同音制造的玩笑。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a complaint that the dish contains too little meat because the word 'liu' in the dish name is humorously reinterpreted as 'to slip away' or 'run off,' implying the meat seems to have disappeared.
context: 顾客抱怨“熘肉片”里肉太少，另一人把菜名中的“熘”故意理解成“溜走”来回应
literal_translation: A customer pointed at the dish he had just bought and sighed, “Alas, why are there only so few slices of meat in this liu-fried pork?” Another customer chimed in, “If the meat couldn't slip away, how could it be called liu pork slices?”
functional_equivalence_translation: A customer sighed, “Why are there so few pieces of meat in this stir-fried pork?” Another replied, “Well, if the pork didn’t slip away, why would it be called slipping pork slices?”
explanatory_translation: A customer complains that the dish “liu pork slices” has too little meat. Another person makes a pun by reinterpreting “熘” (a cooking term, pronounced liu) as “溜,” meaning “to slip away,” joking that the meat became scarce because it ‘slipped away.’
interpretation_1: 指一种烹饪做法的菜名，表示经过熘制的肉片
interpretation_2: 把“熘”曲解为“溜走”，所以肉片少是因为肉会溜

surface_text: 在家里我和老婆一般都直呼其名，一天老婆当着女儿叫我一声老公，没想到女儿插嘴：爸爸，爸爸，妈妈乱说，爸爸怎么会是老公公，外公才是老公公！
胖刘跟导演商量道：我好赖在这个圈里也混了六七年，您能不能在即将投拍的这部连续剧中，给安排个比较有分量的角色。 导演说：我早思谋好了，这次分配给你的角色，是一个体重二百斤的打手，这分量够重了吧。
interpretation_1_zh: 导演把“有分量”理解成身体分量重，于是安排了一个体重二百斤的打手角色。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'weighty' is taken literally: the director says the role has enough physical weight because it is for a 200-pound fighter.
interpretation_2_zh: 胖刘原本说的“有分量的角色”是指角色重要、戏份足、地位较重，不是真的指体重。
interpretation_2_en: The implied meaning is that Liu originally meant an important or substantial role in the show, not a role with great body weight.
context: 演员请求导演给一个“有分量的角色”，导演故意把“分量”从“重要性”转成“体重重量”来理解
literal_translation: Fat Liu discussed with the director: Anyway, I’ve been hanging around in this circle for six or seven years. Could you arrange a rather weighty role for me in this upcoming TV series? The director said: I had already planned it. The role assigned to you this time is a 200-jin thug. That weight is heavy enough, right?
functional_equivalence_translation: Fat Liu said to the director, “I’ve been in the business six or seven years. Could you give me a role with some weight?” The director replied, “Already did—you’ll play a 200-pound tough guy. That’s plenty of weight.”
explanatory_translation: Fat Liu asks for “a role with weight,” where “weight” normally means importance. The director deliberately twists it to mean literal body weight, so he gives him the role of a very heavy thug.
interpretation_1: 指角色重要、有戏份和地位
interpretation_2: 指人物身体重量大、体重很重

surface_text: 大学有只瘟鸡，叫计算机，咬死了很多人。。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“计算机”替换成“计算鸡”，说大学里有一只带瘟疫的鸡，被戏称为“计算鸡”，还能咬人致死，形成荒诞的字面效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it says there is a vicious chicken at the university called a computer, and it has pecked many people to death.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义指真正想说的是“计算机”，借“机”与“鸡”的近音替换，把学校里的计算机说成像有害、令人头疼的东西，以夸张方式表达对计算机的调侃或畏惧。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the word "ji" shifts from "chicken" to "machine," referring to computers as difficult or harmful things that make many students suffer.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：把“计算机”从通常的机器名词临时转成一只鸡的名字，并利用“鸡”可咬人制造荒诞双关。
negative_example: 大学有只公鸡，叫小黄，咬死了很多人。
literal_translation: There was a plague chicken at the university called “computer,” and it bit many people to death.
functional_equivalence_translation: At the university, there was a vicious chicken named “Computer” that ‘killed’ lots of people.
explanatory_translation: The joke shifts the usual meaning of “computer” into the name of a chicken, so the word simultaneously evokes a literal chicken that can bite people and actual computers that metaphorically make many people suffer.
interpretation_1: 表层上把“计算机”理解为大学里一只名叫“计算机”的鸡。
interpretation_2: 隐含上影射真正的“计算机/电脑”让很多人受害或被折磨。

surface_text: 这款保温杯宣传自己有“热爱续航”，水是热的，人也像被顺手鼓励了一下。
hidden_form: 热爱 / 续航 / 保温
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指杯子的保温能力强，热度持续很久。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the cup keeps drinks hot for a long time.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“热爱”也变成可续航的状态，传达生活热情能被延续。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it turns 'passion' into something with battery life, suggesting one's enthusiasm for life can also be sustained.
context: 适用于保温杯、生活方式品牌、礼品文案。
literal_translation: This thermos claims to have 'passion endurance'; the water stays hot, and the person seems casually encouraged too.
functional_equivalence_translation: A thermos that keeps your drink warm and your spirits going.
explanatory_translation: The pun grafts the tech term 'battery life/endurance' onto 'passion,' so the cup's literal heat retention also evokes emotional warmth and sustained motivation.
interpretation_1: 保温持久
interpretation_2: 热情延续

surface_text: 丈夫新婚没多久，却常常很晚回家。这天深夜，他回到家后，发现桌上的饭菜很不新鲜，就斥责妻子：“你炒的这青菜能吃吗？蜡黄蜡黄的。” 妻子立刻回答：“你经常回家这么晚，当然不会知道，它们在我的锅子里也曾经‘青春’过。”
interpretation_1_zh: 妻子字面上说青菜也曾经“青春”过，借“青春”表示它们也有过鲜嫩、状态好的时候。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "youthful" means the greens were once fresh, bright green, and full of vitality when they had just been cooked in the pot.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里实际激活的是“青葱过”的意思，即这些青菜刚炒好时也曾经青绿鲜嫩，只是因为丈夫回家太晚才变得蜡黄不新鲜。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a reproach to the husband: the dish had its brief "prime" long ago, but because he came home so late, its best moment had already passed.
context: 丈夫嫌青菜蜡黄不能吃，妻子借“青春”把人的年轻状态转用于青菜曾经青绿新鲜的状态。
literal_translation: It had once been “youthful” in my wok too.
functional_equivalence_translation: You came home so late that you missed when these greens were still in their youth—fresh and green.
explanatory_translation: She says the vegetables had also once been “youthful,” using a human word for youth to mean the greens were once freshly cooked and green before they turned yellow from sitting too long.
interpretation_1: 表层上指像人一样曾经年轻、青春过。
interpretation_2: 隐含指青菜刚炒出来时曾经青绿鲜嫩，后来放久了才发黄。

surface_text: 老公跟老婆讲了一个荤段子，老婆说：“请你不要用黄色污染我。” 老公说：“现在，污染重而多样，塑料是白色污染，女人出轨是绿色污染。”
我们找到了会写代码的实习生的师傅。
pun_word: 会写代码的实习生的师傅

surface_text: 这位老师真会押，诗句能押韵，考前也总能押中重点。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“押”指诗句在音韵上安排得协调统一，形成朗朗上口的押韵效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the teacher is good at making lines rhyme in poetry, where "押" means to use matching rhyme sounds.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“押中”指老师考前对重点内容判断准确，辅导时抓住了真正会考的部分。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that before exams the teacher can also accurately predict or hit the key test points, where "押" refers to guessing likely exam content.
context: 同一句中先说老师写诗能押韵，后说考前总能押中重点，利用“押”在不同搭配中的并置形成双关。
literal_translation: This teacher is really good at ya: poems can rhyme, and before exams he can also always hit the key points.
functional_equivalence_translation: This teacher really knows how to land things: he can make verses rhyme and also nail the exam topics.
explanatory_translation: This teacher is good at “ya”: in one sense, he makes lines rhyme; in another, he accurately predicts the key exam points.
interpretation_1: 指诗句在音韵上合辙押韵。
interpretation_2: 指在考前准确猜中或圈定考试重点。

surface_text: 自然常识课老师在黑板上给同学们介绍森林中各种各样的毒蛇，并讲授各种应急措施。 老师继而提问道：“如果你碰到眼镜蛇，该怎么办？” 学生急切他说道：“先把它的眼镜打破！”
今天和朋友聊天，我说了句，“其实我很爱憎分明的，只是你没发现。” 朋友很惊讶地说:“曾分明是谁？以前怎么没听你说过这人？”我一听无语了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中朋友把“爱憎分明”误听成了“曾分明”，理解为一个人名，所以追问“曾分明是谁”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the friend mishears "爱憎分明" as mentioning a person named "Zeng Fenming," and reacts as if the speaker is talking about someone he has never heard of.
interpretation_2_zh: 原本说话人想表达的是自己爱和恨的态度很鲜明，喜欢与厌恶分得很清楚。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is that the speaker is saying they have clear-cut likes and dislikes, distinguishing love and hate very clearly.
context: 说话人提到“我很爱憎分明”，听者把其中“憎分明”误解为人名“曾分明”。
literal_translation: Today I was chatting with a friend and said, “Actually, I’m very clear-cut in what I love and hate; you just haven’t noticed.” My friend said in surprise, “Who is Zeng Fenming? Why haven’t I heard you mention this person before?” I was speechless.
functional_equivalence_translation: I told my friend, “I’m very clear about who I love and hate.” He misheard it as a person’s name and asked, “Who’s that? Why haven’t you mentioned them before?”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese idiom “爱憎分明” (clear in love and hate). The listener mishears “憎分明” as “曾分明,” which sounds like a Chinese personal name, and therefore asks who that person is.
interpretation_1: 成语“爱憎分明”，意思是爱和恨的态度非常鲜明。
interpretation_2: 把“憎”误听成“曾”，把“分明”当作人名的一部分，理解成“曾分明是谁”。

surface_text: 宿舍群里有人提议期末周互不打扰，大家一致同意实行“卷静分离”。
hidden_form: 干湿分离 / 内卷 + 安静
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指学习很拼的人和需要安静休息的人在空间或时间上分开安排。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means separating intense study behavior from quiet rest in dorm life.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿照“干湿分离”的说法，把“卷”和“静”并列，调侃期末宿舍里学习焦虑与休息需求的冲突。
interpretation_2_en: It parodies a familiar compound pattern to frame finals-week dorm life as a conflict between overstudying and silence.
context: 适用于校园、宿舍、期末复习的吐槽或群聊表达。
negative_example: 宿舍最好学习区和休息区分开。
literal_translation: In the dorm group chat, everyone agreed to implement 'cram-quiet separation' during finals week.
functional_equivalence_translation: During finals, the dorm decided on a strict separation between grinders and sleepers.
explanatory_translation: The phrase parodies a common compound like 'dry-wet separation' by substituting 'grinding/studying hard' and 'quietness,' creating a hybrid dorm-life pun.
interpretation_1: 学习休息分开
interpretation_2: 仿干湿分离

surface_text: 室友看着电脑：我喜欢这个人的穿衣风格。 我问：谁？ 室友：王菲的制作人，张亚东 我没听清：李亚鹏？ 室友：是王菲的制作人，不是和王菲一起制作人。
和老婆吵架后，老婆闷声去烧开水了。 过了一会我觉得很渴，想问她水开了没有，随口一句：“还没滚啊？！” 老婆听了，一气之下离家出走。
公司茶水间新放的咖啡豆被大家称为“工醒豆”，一杯下去，先恢复的是打工人的表情管理。
hidden_form: 工薪族 / 清醒豆 / 咖啡豆
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是给打工人准备、能让人清醒的咖啡豆。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means coffee beans for workers that can make people feel alert.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义把“工”与“清醒”嫁接，强化打工场景中的提神救场意味。
interpretation_2_en: It also fuses 'work' with 'wakefulness,' stressing the life-saving boost coffee offers in office life.
context: 适用于办公室梗、咖啡产品文案、职场社媒发帖。
literal_translation: The new coffee beans in the office pantry are called 'work-awake beans'; after one cup, the first thing restored is the facial-expression control of office workers.
functional_equivalence_translation: Office coffee that brings working people back online.
explanatory_translation: The coined phrase mixes 'work' and 'awake' into a product nickname, referring literally to coffee beans and figuratively to the emotional rescue they provide office workers.
interpretation_1: 让打工人清醒的咖啡豆
interpretation_2: 职场续航象征

surface_text: 某日，妻子和丈夫因一点小事吵起来了， 妻子在丈夫的胳膊上恨恨地咬了一口，并咬出了血。 丈夫说：“你这臭婆娘，干吗咬人呀？” 妻子说：“因为我君子，俗话说君子动口不动手。”
今天休息，中午我妈说让我给她捶捶背。 我忘了，一直到了晚上才想起来。 我妈在享受的时候自言自语说：“唉，要求了一天，现在才挨打……”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上说的是我晚上才给妈妈捶背，捶背时会用手敲打背部，所以她戏称自己现在才开始“挨打”。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, the mother says that after asking for it all day, she is only now getting 'hit'—referring to her child finally pounding her back at night.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“捶背”借转成“打人”的说法，形成一种夸张调侃：妈妈白天一直提要求，直到晚上才终于等到被捶背，也就是等到这顿“打”。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '挨打' usually means being beaten or physically punished, so her remark humorously frames the back massage as if she were finally getting beaten after waiting all day.
context: 妈妈中午让“我”给她捶背，“我”拖到晚上才做；捶背动作可被夸张说成“挨打”。
literal_translation: Today was a day off. At noon my mom told me to pound her back. I forgot and only remembered at night. While enjoying it, she muttered, “Sigh, I asked for it all day, and only now am I getting beaten...”
functional_equivalence_translation: My mom asked me for a back rub at noon, but I forgot until nighttime. As she enjoyed it, she said, “Asked for it all day, and I’m only just getting ‘beaten up’ now.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “getting beaten” and “having one’s back pounded/massaged.” The mother humorously describes the delayed back rub as if she were finally being hit.
interpretation_1: 字面上像是在说被人打了一顿。
interpretation_2: 实际指终于被儿女按要求捶背按摩了。

surface_text: 裁缝说这件事得量体裁衣，说完就拿起皮尺给他量尺寸。
某女被问：是处女吗？ 女答：说是吧，我已生了孩子；说不是吧，我还没结婚。就算是个“副处”吧。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“副处”被拆解为“副的处女、半个处女”，意思是她已生过孩子，不能算完整意义上的处女，但又未婚，因此自嘲为介于“是处女”和“不是处女”之间的状态。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "deputy virgin" means she is only partly a virgin: she has given birth, so she cannot fully claim to be a virgin, yet she is unmarried, so she also does not fit the opposite category completely.
interpretation_2_zh: “副处”同时激活了常见职级称呼“副处级”的说法，借官职名词制造谐趣，把两难身份用一个现成词语表达出来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "副处" is a pun on a Chinese official rank meaning "deputy division level" or "deputy director level," borrowing a bureaucratic title to jokingly label her ambiguous sexual/marital status.
context: 被问“是处女吗”后，回答者用“已生孩子但还没结婚”的矛盾条件，自造“副处”来折中表达。
literal_translation: Then just count me as a “deputy virgin.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Let’s say I’m only a “vice-virgin.”
explanatory_translation: She jokes that she is a “vice-virgin”: not a virgin in the literal sense because she has had a child, but not fully “not a virgin” in the social sense she invokes because she is still unmarried. The humor comes from borrowing the official title prefix “vice-/deputy” and attaching it to “virgin.”
interpretation_1: 表面上是把自己的身份戏称为“副处”，像行政级别中的“副处级”。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“不是严格意义上的处女，但又未婚”，即对“处女”状态的折中说法。

surface_text: 小侄女快两岁了，已经到了出语惊人的年龄。一日，我正在涂口红，她妈妈逗她，娘娘（姑姑）在干什么？我正准备教她说涂口红，她已经快言快语地说：写字。全家绝倒。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是在嘴唇上涂抹口红，是化妆动作。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the aunt is putting on lipstick, and the child describes the action as if she were writing characters.
interpretation_2_zh: 小侄女把涂口红看成像用笔在嘴上书写，因此说成“写字”，把化妆动作转成了书写动作。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden humor is that applying lipstick is likened to writing because the lipstick is used like a pen on the lips, so the child shifts the meaning from makeup to handwriting.
context: 姑姑正在涂口红，大人问小孩“娘娘在干什么”，小孩把口红当笔，把涂口红说成“写字”。
literal_translation: My little niece is almost two years old and has reached the age of making surprising remarks. One day, I was putting on lipstick. Her mother teased her and asked, “What is Auntie doing?” I was just about to teach her to say “putting on lipstick,” when she quickly said, “writing.” The whole family burst into laughter.
functional_equivalence_translation: My nearly two-year-old niece saw me putting on lipstick and, when asked what I was doing, blurted out, “Writing!” as if the lipstick were a pen.
explanatory_translation: The humor comes from the child mislabeling the action: she sees the aunt holding lipstick like a pen and moving it on her lips, so she says “writing” instead of “putting on lipstick.”
interpretation_1: 小侄女把姑姑拿着口红在嘴上涂抹的动作理解成了写字。
interpretation_2: 在成人语境中，这个动作实际是在涂口红，只是外形上像拿笔写字，形成错位趣味。

surface_text: mm：以后我们结婚了，我要和你生两个小孩，一男一女。 gg：好啊！ mm：男的名字你取，我取女生的。 gg：也可以呀！生女的叫什么呢？ mm：名字叫好美！ gg：为什么呢？ mm：这样别人都回叫我好美的妈妈啦！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是女孩被取名为“好美”，别人称呼她母亲时会说“好美的妈妈”，即“名叫好美的孩子的妈妈”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the daughter is simply going to be named “Haomei” (“Good/Beautiful”), so people would call the speaker “Haomei’s mother.”
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“好美的妈妈”这句话，让别人听起来像是在说“好美啊，妈妈”，从而把“好美”转移成对母亲美貌的夸赞。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that when people say “Haomei de mama,” it sounds like they are saying “the beautiful mom,” so the speaker can indirectly be praised as beautiful.
context: 情侣讨论将来给女儿起名，女生提议把女儿名字取为“好美”，这样别人会叫她“好美的妈妈”。
literal_translation: MM: After we get married, I want to have two children with you, one boy and one girl. GG: Sure! MM: You name the boy, I’ll name the girl. GG: Okay! What will the girl be called? MM: Her name will be Haomei! GG: Why? MM: So that everyone will call me Haomei's mom!
functional_equivalence_translation: MM: When we have a daughter, I’ll name her Belle. GG: Nice. Why Belle? MM: So people will say, “Belle’s mom” — which sounds like they’re calling me a beautiful mom.
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “好美的妈妈,” which literally means “Haomei’s mother” if “好美” is the daughter’s name, but it can also be heard as “so beautiful, mom” when the phrase is re-parsed with a pause.
interpretation_1: 指名叫“好美”的女孩的妈妈。
interpretation_2: 被人当面称赞为“好美，妈妈”。

surface_text: 语文老师说：“路遥是当代作家。” 学生说：“路遥也是伯乐。” 老师问：“他发现了哪个人才？” 学生说：“他发现了千里马。” 老师莫名其妙了，惊讶地说：“你哪里道听途说来的？” 学生说：“俗话说，路遥知马力。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“路遥”理解为作家路遥这个人，因此学生据此把他当成能识别千里马的“伯乐”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'Lu Yao' refers to the contemporary writer named Lu Yao, so the student jokingly takes him as a person who 'knows horses' and even as a Bole who can identify a fine horse.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义其实激活的是俗语“路遥知马力”中的“路遥”，本义是路途遥远，不是作家姓名；整句意思是路途远了，才能知道马的力量。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from the saying 'Lu yao zhi mali' ('A long road tests a horse's strength'), where 'lu yao' means 'when the road is long,' not the writer's name. The joke deliberately shifts this phrase into a reference to the author Lu Yao.
context: 学生先把“路遥”当作作家姓名，再把俗语“路遥知马力”拆解为主谓结构，误读成“路遥知道马力”。
literal_translation: The Chinese teacher said, “Lu Yao is a contemporary writer.” The student said, “Lu Yao is also a talent scout.” The teacher asked, “What talent did he discover?” The student said, “A thousand-mile horse.” The teacher was baffled and said in surprise, “Where did you hear that?” The student said, “As the saying goes, ‘When the road is long, one knows a horse’s strength.’”
functional_equivalence_translation: The teacher said, “Lu Yao is a modern writer.” The student replied, “He’s also a good judge of talent.” “Whom did he discover?” asked the teacher. “A fine steed,” said the student. The teacher was puzzled. The student explained, “Because the saying says, ‘Lu Yao knows horse power.’”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese saying “路遥知马力,” which normally means “Only on a long journey can you know a horse’s strength.” But “路遥” also happens to be the name of the writer Lu Yao, so the student misreads the idiom as “Lu Yao knows horse strength,” making it sound as if the writer Lu Yao discovered a great horse like a talent scout.
interpretation_1: 表层是俗语“路遥知马力”的原义，意思是路途遥远才能看出马的力气。
interpretation_2: 将“路遥”误解为作家“路遥”的名字，于是理解成“路遥知道/识得马力”，进而引出他像伯乐一样发现千里马。

surface_text: 最近复习周，我已经进入“困学模式”：不是孔学，是一学就困、困了还得学。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是形容人在学习时又困又要继续学的状态。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it describes the state of being sleepy while still having to study.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“苦学”仿拟成“困学”，强调学生复习时的疲惫感。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it remodels the expression 'studying hard' into 'studying sleepy', emphasizing exhaustion during exam review.
context: 适用于校园复习、备考吐槽、社交媒体状态更新。
literal_translation: During review week, I have entered 'sleepy-study mode': not Confucian learning, but getting sleepy as soon as I study and still having to keep studying.
functional_equivalence_translation: It's finals week, and I'm in full-on sleepy-study mode: exhausted, but still cramming.
explanatory_translation: The expression is a hybrid coinage built by reshaping a familiar study-related wording. It merges 'sleepiness' with 'studying hard' to create a humorous student label.
interpretation_1: 犯困学习状态
interpretation_2: 对苦学的仿拟调侃

surface_text: 某厂长招待检察团吃午饭，因时间仓促，来不及准备宴席。厂长吩咐厨房煮了一锅狗肉。开饭时，厂长抱歉地说：各位领导，没什么好东西……几条狗，凑合着吃吧！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是厂长在解释菜很简陋，只临时煮了几条狗做成的狗肉，请大家将就吃一点。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the director is saying that there was nothing special to serve, only a few dogs cooked as food, so the guests should just make do with it.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把在座的检察团领导说成“狗”或“走狗”一类的人，带有借题发挥的贬损意味，因此形成双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is insulting: in Chinese, 'dog' can also be used as a derogatory way to refer to people, so 'a few dogs, make do and eat' can sound like he is calling the leaders dogs and telling them to eat themselves.
context: 厂长因来不及备宴，只让厨房煮了一锅狗肉，在饭桌上向来宾介绍菜肴时说“几条狗，凑合着吃吧”。
literal_translation: Leaders, there is nothing good... just a few dogs, make do and eat.
functional_equivalence_translation: Sorry, nothing special today... just some dog to make do with.
explanatory_translation: He says “just a few dogs” instead of “dog meat,” using the animal to stand for the dish, which makes the line sound blunt and unintentionally comic.
interpretation_1: 表面上像是在说有几条活狗，拿来凑合着吃。
interpretation_2: 实际上是指已经煮好的一锅狗肉，用“几条狗”代指菜品原料，形成粗俗而失礼的说法。

surface_text: 妇：想当年我的身材就是身材，体格就是体格。正面山明水秀，侧面悬崖峭壁，背面则是柳暗花明，你说是吧？ 夫：对！不过，妳的水土保持做得很失败。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把妻子的身体比作山水地貌，丈夫顺着比喻说她的“水土保持”做得失败，字面上像是在说山地环境没有维护好。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'water and soil conservation' refers to protecting land and preventing erosion, matching the wife's metaphor of her body as a landscape with mountains and scenery.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含是在借“水土保持”影射“身材保持”，意思是她没有把体型维持住，身材已经走样、发福了。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that her body figure has not been 'maintained' well over time—especially that her breasts or overall shape have sagged or changed, as if the body's 'terrain' could not hold itself together.
context: 妻子用山水地貌比喻自己年轻时前侧背的身材，丈夫顺势以地理术语评价其现在体态变化。
literal_translation: Wife: Back then, my figure was really a figure, and my build was really a build. From the front, it was like beautiful mountains and clear waters; from the side, steep cliffs; from the back, hidden willows and blooming flowers. Don't you think so? Husband: Right! But your soil and water conservation has been a failure.
functional_equivalence_translation: Wife: I used to be stunning from every angle. Husband: True—but you’ve done a terrible job with upkeep.
explanatory_translation: The wife compares her former body to scenic landscapes. The husband replies with “soil and water conservation,” literally an environmental term, but he means she failed to maintain her figure, creating the pun through metaphorical semantic shift.
interpretation_1: 表层上借用地理环境术语，指防止水土流失、维持地貌稳定。
interpretation_2: 实际影射妻子没能保持年轻时的身材，身形走样了。

surface_text: 职员：经理，你的太太又温柔又漂亮，你真让人羡慕。 经理：什么？那不是我的太太啊！我的太太是个母夜叉啊! 职员：那刚才和你在一起的那位小姐是谁啊？？？ 经理：哦，那是我的二奶啊！怎么样不错吧？ 职员：不会吧？你的奶奶那么年青啊！！！！…… 经理：什么……晕了……哎！！！！！！！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“二奶”指男子在妻子之外包养的女人，也就是情人、婚外伴侣。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the clerk misunderstands "ernai" as literally meaning "second grandma," i.e., the manager's grandmother.
interpretation_2_zh: “二奶”被误听、误解为“二/奶奶”里的“奶奶”，于是职员理解成经理的祖母，才会说“你的奶奶那么年青”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "ernai" is a colloquial term for a mistress or kept woman, which is what the manager actually means.
context: 经理解释刚才身边的年轻女子不是太太，而是“二奶”；职员随后故意或误把“二奶”听成“奶奶”。
literal_translation: Employee: Manager, your wife is gentle and beautiful. I really envy you. Manager: What? That’s not my wife! My wife is a shrew! Employee: Then who was the young lady with you just now? Manager: Oh, that’s my mistress. Nice, right? Employee: No way? Your grandma is so young! Manager: What... I’m dizzy...
functional_equivalence_translation: Employee: So who was that young woman with you? Manager: My side chick. Employee: Seriously? Your granny looks that young? Manager: What?!
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “二奶” (mistress/kept woman), which is misheard as “奶奶” (grandma). The employee intentionally or mistakenly shifts the meaning, creating the joke that the manager’s “grandma” is unexpectedly young.
interpretation_1: 经理说“二奶”时，指婚外情人、包养的女人。
interpretation_2: 职员把“二奶”误解为“奶奶”，即祖母，因此说“你的奶奶那么年青”。

surface_text: 一家山西人在纽约唐人街开了家餐馆，儿子当服务生，老妈管收钱，老爸做大厨。 某一天，店里来了个老外，点了套餐，吃到一半，把汤碗打了。老妈听见声音，过来看，见地上有个破碗，问：谁打的？ 老外想：three dollar……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，老妈在问是谁把汤碗打破了，是对责任人的询问。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the foreign customer thinks the owner is asking about the price of the broken bowl, so he answers, 'three dollars.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，老外把“谁打的”听成了价格询问，误以为是在问破碗多少钱，于是心里想到“three dollar”，即三块钱。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the owner's Shanxi-accented Chinese question '谁打的？' sounds like 'three dollar' to the foreigner, but she actually means 'Who broke it?'
context: 餐馆里老外打破了汤碗，老板娘用中文问“谁打的”，老外按英语语音去理解。
literal_translation: The mother asked, “Who broke it?” The foreigner thought: “three dollar...”
functional_equivalence_translation: The owner asked in Chinese, “Who broke it?” but the foreign customer misheard it as “three dollar.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is that the Chinese phrase “谁打的” (who broke it?) sounds similar to the English phrase “three dollar,” so the foreigner mistakes a question about responsibility for a statement about price.
interpretation_1: 老妈在问是谁把碗打破了。
interpretation_2: 老外误听成英文价格表达，以为在说“三美元”。

surface_text: 儿子问：“爸爸，我到底是从哪里来的？” 爸爸支支吾吾地向他讲解生殖的过程。 儿子听完，一头雾水地说：“怎么会这样？我同桌说他是从山东来的！”
儿子：今天老师问我老子是什么人，爸爸你知道吗？ 爸爸：白养你啦！天天见我，你都想不出来。老子还要问学生，告诉你们老师，老子就是我。
这款便当盒广告说自己专治“午力不足”，吃完下午开会都像电量回到百分之八十。
hidden_form: 无力不足 / 午后精力不足
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指中午吃得好，能缓解午后没精神的问题。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a good lunch can relieve the lack of energy in the afternoon.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“无力”类表达，把“午后疲惫”压缩成标签化新词，突出午餐与战斗力的关系。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it remodels expressions around 'powerlessness,' compressing 'afternoon fatigue' into a catchy new term that links lunch with productivity.
context: 适用于食品广告、上班族午餐文案或生活方式内容。
literal_translation: This lunchbox ad says it cures 'noon-power deficiency'; after eating, afternoon meetings feel like your battery is back to eighty percent.
functional_equivalence_translation: This lunchbox is pitched as the cure for the post-lunch energy slump.
explanatory_translation: The phrase inserts 'noon' into a familiar deficiency-like pattern, creating a hybrid coined term that connects lunchtime eating with recovery from afternoon fatigue.
interpretation_1: 缓解午后乏力
interpretation_2: 把无力改造成午后标签

surface_text: 有一天，我和朋友一起去上超市买东西，因为他喜欢吃方便面的原因。 他一进超市就去了方便面专区，而我因为还要买别的东西，就没有跟着去。 过了一会，我正在看货，突然我的朋友大叫一声；“哈哈哈，小明，快来，我们这一次终于可以长生不老了。” 我一听，感到莫名其妙，于是就走了过去问他怎么回事。 只见他指着货架说到；你自己看。 我一看，立马昏了，只见货架上面摆着一排方便面，名字就叫；“唐僧肉”。 奶奶的，真是太坑爹了！！！！！！！
hidden_form: 吃了唐僧肉可以长生不老
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是货架上一款方便面的名称叫“唐僧肉”，朋友看到的是商品字面名称。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "Tang Monk meat" is simply the brand or product name of a type of instant noodles displayed on the shelf.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上激活了《西游记》中“吃了唐僧肉可以长生不老”的说法，所以朋友才会说这次终于可以长生不老了。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning refers to the Tang Monk from Journey to the West, whose flesh is said to grant immortality if eaten, which is why the friend jokes that they can finally live forever.
context: 朋友在超市方便面专区看到一款名叫“唐僧肉”的食品，由商品名联想到传说中的唐僧肉功效“长生不老”。
literal_translation: Its name was simply “Tang Monk Meat.”
functional_equivalence_translation: It was called “Monk Meat,” so my friend joked that eating it would make us immortal at last.
explanatory_translation: The product was named “Tang Monk Meat.” In the Chinese classic Journey to the West, there is a legend that anyone who eats Tang Monk’s flesh can gain immortality, so the joke comes from treating the snack name as if it were the real magical “Tang Monk meat.”
interpretation_1: 表层是方便面的商品名称，指一种叫“唐僧肉”的零食/食品。
interpretation_2: 隐含激活《西游记》中“吃唐僧肉能长生不老”的传说，因此朋友才说终于可以长生不老了。

surface_text: 这款便携榨汁杯简直是“果断瓶”，想喝就打，三分钟把拖延切成果汁。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指一个装水果、打果汁的瓶子产品。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a bottle used for fruit and juice.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含激活“果断”，强调做决定快、行动快，不再拖延。
interpretation_2_en: It also activates 'decisive,' emphasizing quick action instead of procrastination.
