functional_equivalence_translation: “Why isn’t your pen moving?” “Because it’s an auto-pencil, not a self-moving one.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “动” (move). The teacher means “Why aren’t you writing?” but the student pretends it means “Why doesn’t the pen move by itself?” and replies that it is an “automatic pencil” (mechanical pencil).
interpretation_1: 老师问“笔为什么不动”，意思是为什么不用笔书写、没有开始记笔记。
interpretation_2: 学生故意把“动”理解成笔本身是否会自己运动，并回答“这是自动笔”。

surface_text: 这款云盘会员主打“存在感”，文件不乱丢，人才不心慌。
hidden_form: 存在感 / 存储在云端的安全感
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指云盘具备稳定存储功能，让文件一直‘存在’得很有保障。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the cloud drive ensures files truly 'exist' safely through reliable storage.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用常见词“存在感”，把心理上的被看见感转成了数据被妥善保留的安心感。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it borrows the common phrase 'sense of presence,' shifting it from social visibility to the reassurance that data is safely kept.
context: 适用于云存储、数码产品广告或互联网服务宣传。
literal_translation: This cloud storage membership focuses on 'sense of stored existence': files do not get lost, and people do not panic.
functional_equivalence_translation: This cloud drive gives your files a real sense of security—and gives you peace of mind too.
explanatory_translation: The expression reuses the familiar phrase 'sense of presence' but reanchors 'exist' in the context of digital storage, creating a hybrid meaning between social presence and reliable file preservation.
interpretation_1: 文件稳定存储
interpretation_2: 借存在感转成安全感

surface_text: 这家面包店把加班族套餐取名“摸鱼欧包”，海报写着：工位上没法真摸鱼，嘴里先摸个软的。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是一款适合上班间隙吃的欧式面包。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it is a European-style bread meant for office snack breaks.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“摸鱼”指上班时偷闲放松，吃面包也像短暂逃离工作。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning draws on 'moyu' (slacking off at work), suggesting the bread offers a brief escape from work.
context: 适用于餐饮广告、打工人营销文案。
literal_translation: This bakery named its office-worker combo 'slacking-off European bread': if you can't really slack off at your desk, at least let your mouth do it softly first.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bakery calls its office combo 'Moyu Bread'—if you can't sneak a break at work, at least grab one bite at a time.
explanatory_translation: The pun is built by blending 'moyu' (Chinese internet slang for slacking off at work) with 'European bread'. The new expression refers both to a bread product and to the fantasy of taking a work break.
interpretation_1: 上班零食欧包
interpretation_2: 偷闲放松感

surface_text: 他真会撑场面，婚礼现场撑得住，公司年会也全靠他撑场面。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“撑场面”指他在婚礼上能活跃气氛、招呼来宾，让整个现场不冷场、不失礼。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means he can literally hold up or support the scene, as if keeping the wedding venue and the company annual party from collapsing.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“撑场面”指在公司年会上他同样是关键人物，能维持体面与热闹，提升整体效果。
interpretation_2_en: Its intended meaning is that he is very good at handling social occasions, boosting the atmosphere, and making events look impressive and run smoothly.
context: 同一句中同时出现“撑得住”和“撑场面”，使“撑”的字面支撑义与惯用表达义并置。
literal_translation: He is really good at holding up the scene; he can hold up the wedding scene, and the company annual party also relies on him to hold up the scene.
functional_equivalence_translation: He really knows how to hold the room together—at the wedding he could literally hold things up, and at the company party he could hold the whole scene together.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on the Chinese phrase “撑场面,” which normally means to keep up appearances or command a public occasion. The nearby phrase “撑得住” activates the literal sense of “撑” as physically supporting or holding up, creating a juxtaposition between literal support and social poise.
interpretation_1: 指在社交或公开场合中镇得住、能把气氛和局面维持好。
interpretation_2: 借“撑得住”激活字面上的支撑含义，暗示他在婚礼现场也像在物理上把场面撑起来。

surface_text: “你的头是怎么受伤的？” “唉，昨天我在小红楼下念了一夜的诗，然后我说‘亲爱的，把你的电话给我吧！’她就把她们家的电话给我了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“把你的电话给我吧”被理解成把家里的电话机直接给他，所以他因此受了伤。
interpretation_1_en: He literally asked, "Dear, give me your telephone," and she responded by giving him the actual household telephone set, which led to his injury.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义中他说的本意是想要对方的电话号码，用“电话”代指“电话号码”，结果被对方误解成要电话机。
interpretation_2_en: What he really meant was, "Dear, give me your phone number / contact information," but she deliberately interpreted it as the physical telephone.
context: 男子向女子搭讪说“把你的电话给我吧”，女子故意按“电话机”而非“电话号码”理解并真的把家里的电话给了他。
literal_translation: "How did your head get hurt?" "Alas, last night I recited poetry all night downstairs from Xiaohong's place, and then I said, 'Dear, give me your telephone!' She then gave me their family's telephone."
functional_equivalence_translation: "How did you hurt your head?" "I spent all night wooing a girl with poems, then said, 'Sweetheart, can I have your number?' She took it literally and handed me the house phone."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word "电话," which can mean a telephone number in context, but can also mean the telephone set itself. He intended to ask for her number, but she deliberately interpreted it as asking for the actual phone.
interpretation_1: 索要对方的电话号码或联系方式。
interpretation_2: 被理解为把家里的电话机直接给出去。

surface_text: 前天，和朋友去吃饭，要了一盘红烧猪脚，大家都说猪脚有点变味，其中一位就说：我说这猪也太不讲卫生了，怎么也不洗脚。
有一女士家住外地，家里的房子要装修，她向老板请了一周假。一周后房子没有装修完，她只好续假，发了一封电报。 老板接到电报后大吃一惊！电报上写道：房事未毕，续假一周。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层字面上，“房事未毕”通常会被理解为与夫妻私生活、性事有关的事情还没有结束，因此老板看到后会大吃一惊。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "房事未毕" means the house-related work is not finished yet, so she needs to extend her leave for another week.
interpretation_2_zh: 结合前文装修房子的语境，这里实际想表达的是“房饰未毕”，即房屋装修、装饰工作还没有完成，所以需要续假一周。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "房事" is commonly used as a euphemism for sexual activity, so the telegram can be misread as saying her sexual affairs are not finished and she needs another week off.
context: 女子因家里房子装修请假，装修一周未完，发电报称“房事未毕，续假一周”，老板据常用义产生误解。
literal_translation: The house matter is not finished; I request one more week of leave.
functional_equivalence_translation: Domestic affairs unfinished—requesting another week off.
explanatory_translation: She meant the house renovation was not finished, but “房事” is commonly understood as sexual matters, so the telegram sounded shocking to her boss.
interpretation_1: 指夫妻间的性生活之事。
interpretation_2: 实际想表达的是房屋装修相关事务还没完成。

surface_text: 有一外乡青年，去东北某城市出差，向一位当地人打听这儿的可住宿的宾馆有多少。 东北人回答说：“贼多，贼多！” 这个年青人吓得连连后退，赶紧地离开这里。
这家律师事务所真严谨，文书很严谨，连沉默都显得很严谨。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“严谨”指法律文书结构完整、措辞准确、逻辑清楚，体现专业工作上的规范性。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the law firm is extremely rigorous and meticulous: its documents are rigorous, and even its silence seems disciplined and careful.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“严谨”指连他们不轻易表态的态度都透着慎重，表现出思考和处事的高度克制。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it suggests the firm is so stiff, restrained, and overly serious that even not speaking feels formal and tense, extending 'rigorous' into a personality or atmosphere trait.
context: 律师事务所、文书、沉默并列出现，最后一句使“严谨”从赞美风格转向近音联想“严禁”。
literal_translation: This law firm is really rigorous; its documents are rigorous, and even its silence seems rigorous.
functional_equivalence_translation: This law firm is so strict—its paperwork is precise, and even the silence feels like something is strictly forbidden.
explanatory_translation: The sentence repeats “rigorous” on the surface, but in the last clause it suggests the near-sounding word “forbidden,” implying that the firm's silence feels controlled and restrictive.
interpretation_1: 表面上反复称赞律师事务所及其文书风格非常严谨。
interpretation_2: “连沉默都显得很严谨”激活了近音的“严禁”，暗示这里气氛压抑、很多话被禁止说出。

surface_text: 孔子，孟子，老子三人同时在猪圈睡了一夜之后，发现母猪怀孕了，经DNA检验证明，肯定不是孔子干的，也不是孟子干的，请问那是谁干的？
一编剧对一导演说：您好，我是编剧，我姓杨。导演看了他一眼，说：您好，杨编，编剧不太喜欢，就说：能不能换个称呼？好的，杨剧！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中导演把姓杨的编剧改称为“杨剧”，是把职位称呼从“编”换成了“剧”，形成一种生硬但字面上仍像是在称呼“姓杨的编剧”的说法。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the director simply switches the order of the title and surname, calling him 'Yang Ju' as in 'Mr. Yang the screenwriter.'
interpretation_2_zh: “杨剧”谐音“洋锯”，触发了把人名职称说成工具名称的戏谑效果；更常规的称呼本应是“杨编”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'Yang Ju' sounds like 'yangju' (goat semen), so the form of address becomes an awkward and insulting-sounding pun.
context: 编剧姓杨，导演按职业简称称呼他为“杨编”；编剧因该称呼有不雅谐音而要求更换，导演又改成另一个同样带不雅谐音的称呼。
literal_translation: A screenwriter said to a director, “Hello, I’m a screenwriter, my surname is Yang.” The director looked at him and said, “Hello, Writer Yang.” The screenwriter didn’t like it and said, “Could you use another form of address?” “Okay, Yang Ju.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A writer said, “My last name is Yang.” The director greeted him with a title that sounded dirty, so the writer asked him to change it. The director did—only to switch to another title sounding just as dirty.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the director calling the man “Yang Bian” and then “Yang Ju,” both formed from his surname plus a job title abbreviation. In Chinese, these sound similar to vulgar sexual terms, so the humor comes from changing the title but keeping the indecent pun.
interpretation_1: 导演用“姓+职务简称”称呼对方，先叫“杨编”，后改叫“杨剧”。
interpretation_2: “杨编”谐音“洋鞭”，“杨剧”更接近“阳具”，都带有粗俗性暗示，因此构成调侃。

surface_text: 晚上问老公，你说绿豆摔了一跤变成什么了？ 老公说不知道，我就告诉他变成红豆了，因为流血了。 老公说，为什么不是蚕豆啊. 我问为什么会是蚕豆啊？ 老公说，摔残废了呀。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是把“蚕豆”当作豆类名称来回答，表示绿豆摔了一跤后会变成“蚕豆”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '蚕豆' means the bean called a broad bean/fava bean, as if the fallen green bean simply turned into another kind of bean.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“蚕”借为与“残”近音，实际想说的是“摔残废了呀”，用“蚕豆”谐音化地表达受伤致残的意思。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '蚕' sounds like '残' in '残废' (crippled/disabled), so '蚕豆' jokingly implies a bean that became disabled after the fall.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：夫妻在玩“某种豆摔了一跤会变成什么豆”的脑筋急转弯，先有“绿豆流血变红豆”，随后顺着“摔伤”联想到“摔残废”并借近音说成“蚕豆”。
literal_translation: At night I asked my husband, what do you think a mung bean becomes after falling down? He said he didn't know, so I told him it becomes a red bean, because it bled. He said, why not a broad bean? I asked why it would be a broad bean. He said, because it got crippled from the fall.
functional_equivalence_translation: I asked my husband, “What does a mung bean turn into after it falls?” I said, “A red bean—because it bleeds.” He replied, “Why not a ‘crippled’ bean?” playing on the sound of “broad bean” and “crippled.”
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “蚕豆” (a kind of bean), which sounds similar to “残废” (crippled/disabled). In the joke, after “green bean becomes red bean because it bleeds,” the husband extends the logic: if it falls badly enough to become disabled, then it turns into “蚕豆,” exploiting the near-homophony with “残废.”
interpretation_1: 一种豆类，和绿豆、红豆同属“豆”类话题中的正常词项。
interpretation_2: 借“蚕豆”的读音联想到“残废”，意思是摔了一跤把人摔残了。

surface_text: 一次看球赛，曼联赢了一场比赛，乐得我手舞足蹈，老婆很不理解地说：干吗呀？至于么？我说：我兴奋！老婆毫无表情地看了看我说：什么时候改姓了？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“我兴奋”听成了“我姓粪”，其中“姓”被理解为表示姓氏，老婆因此问什么时候改姓了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he says "I’m excited" after Manchester United wins, expressing that he feels thrilled and emotionally stirred.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是说“我很兴奋”，表达因为曼联赢球而情绪激动、高兴。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the sound of "xingfen" (excited), which the wife humorously mishears as if he were saying his surname had changed to "Xing".
context: 看球赛时因曼联赢球而激动，说“我兴奋”，妻子把“兴奋”误解为近音的“姓粪”，于是问什么时候改姓了。
literal_translation: I’m excited. — When did you change your surname?
functional_equivalence_translation: I’m thrilled. — Since when is your last name Thrill?
explanatory_translation: He says “I’m excited,” but his wife deliberately mishears it as something like “my surname is Fen,” so she jokes, “When did you change your last name?”
interpretation_1: 我很兴奋、很激动。
interpretation_2: 被误听成“我姓粪”，像是在说自己改了姓。

surface_text: 这家餐馆真会端，菜端得快，姿态也端得很足。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“端”指服务员上菜动作利索迅速，出餐和传菜效率都很高，服务流程顺畅。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the restaurant is good at serving: the dishes are brought to the table quickly.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“端”指店里整体风格和服务态度很讲究排场，气质拿捏得比较高调体面。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '端' also refers to putting on an air or striking a pose, meaning the restaurant also has a very affected, pretentious attitude.
context: 同一句中先说“菜端得快”再说“姿态也端得很足”，并置激活“端”的动作义和姿态义。
negative_example: 这家餐馆真会送，菜送得快，服务也很周到。
literal_translation: This restaurant really knows how to serve: the dishes are brought quickly, and its manner is also very poised.
functional_equivalence_translation: This restaurant really knows how to carry itself: it carries dishes fast, and carries an air of style too.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “端,” which can mean both “to bring/serve up” dishes and “to put on an affected or poised manner.”
interpretation_1: 指把菜送上来、端上桌，强调上菜快。
interpretation_2: 指拿姿态、故作讲究，强调姿态摆得很足。

surface_text: 这款防晒霜宣传自己是“阳谋终止器”，太阳再有计划，也别想轻易得逞。
hidden_form: 阴谋 / 阳光 / 终结者
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指这款防晒霜能够阻止阳光晒伤皮肤。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the sunscreen can stop sunlight from damaging the skin.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义把“阳光”的伤害拟人化成“阳谋”，借用“阴谋/阳谋”的表达，形成对太阳蓄意晒黑的夸张调侃。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning personifies sun exposure as an 'open plot,' borrowing from the contrast between 'conspiracy' and 'open strategy' to joke that the sun is intentionally trying to tan or burn you.
context: 适用于防晒产品广告、夏季护肤文案、趣味种草。
literal_translation: This sunscreen calls itself an 'open-sun-plot terminator': no matter how well the sun plans, it won't succeed easily.
functional_equivalence_translation: This sunscreen is a 'sun-plot stopper'—whatever the sun has planned, it's not getting through.
explanatory_translation: The pun fuses 'sun' with the Chinese rhetorical term '阳谋' (an open plot/strategy), then adds a device-like ending. It simultaneously refers to blocking sunlight and jokes that the sun is carrying out a calculated scheme against your skin.
interpretation_1: 阻止晒伤
interpretation_2: 太阳的阳谋被终止

surface_text: 王建军和老米是好朋友，一次两人说自己的父亲。 王建军：我爸爸有一次去打猎一颗子弹打死了两只老虎。 老米：你知道死海吗？ 王建军：知道……？ 老米：那就是我爸爸杀死的……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上“死海”指地理上的死海，老米说那片海是他爸爸杀死的，形成夸张荒诞的字面效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'the Dead Sea' is the famous salt lake; Lao Mi is jokingly saying that his father killed that sea.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含是把“死海”借成“死骇”的效果，意思是他爸爸厉害到能把人或事物吓死，用夸张方式吹嘘父亲本事更大。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a bragging pun: he twists the place name 'Dead Sea' into something literally 'killed dead,' to absurdly exaggerate that his father was even more powerful than killing two tigers.
context: 两人互相吹嘘自己父亲的厉害程度，老米借“死海”把地名临时转成字面义来制造夸张效果
literal_translation: Do you know the Dead Sea? That was killed by my dad.
functional_equivalence_translation: Know the Dead Sea? My dad is the one who made it dead.
explanatory_translation: He puns on “Dead Sea”: normally it is the place name, but here he pretends it literally means “a sea that was killed,” boasting absurdly that his father killed even the sea.
interpretation_1: 指著名地名“死海”
interpretation_2: 把“死海”拆解为“被他爸爸杀死的海”，夸张吹嘘其父亲本领极大

surface_text: 用户：我怎么总是上不去网啊？客服询问了一下情况：可能是你的猫的问题。用户：好，你等一下好啦，我家的猫已经让我关门外头了。客服：！！！！！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“猫”理解成家里养的宠物猫，所以用户说已经把猫关到门外了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the customer understands 'cat' literally as the pet at home and says they have already shut their cat outside the door.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义里“猫”是上网设备“调制解调器”的俗称，客服本意是怀疑网络连接不上可能是网络猫或宽带设备出了问题。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that customer service meant the modem, which is colloquially called a 'cat' in Chinese internet slang, so the network problem might be caused by the modem.
context: 用户咨询无法上网，客服说“可能是你的猫的问题”，其中“猫”既可指宠物，也可在网络语境中指 modem。
literal_translation: User: Why can’t I get online? The customer service asked about the situation: Maybe it’s your cat’s problem. User: Okay, wait a moment. My cat has already shut me outside the door. Customer service: !!!!!
functional_equivalence_translation: User: Why can’t I get online? Support: It might be a problem with your modem. User: Okay, hold on—I’ve just put my cat outside. Support: !!!!!
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “猫” (cat), which can colloquially refer to a modem. The support agent means the modem may be faulty, but the user takes it literally as the household pet.
interpretation_1: 用户按日常意义理解为家里的宠物猫。
interpretation_2: 客服实际指的是网络设备“猫”，即调制解调器。

surface_text: 周末，心血来潮，在家煮皮蛋瘦肉粥。满心欢喜地问男友：咸淡合适吗？他边吃边说：还没有吃到咸蛋。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上男友是在说这碗皮蛋瘦肉粥里还没吃到咸蛋这一食材。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he means he hasn't eaten any salted egg yet, so he cannot judge whether the porridge is salty enough.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上男友借“咸蛋”谐指“嫌淡”，意思是并不觉得味道淡，咸淡基本合适。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '咸蛋' echoes '咸淡' and jokingly dodges the question about taste, using a wordplay on similar sounds rather than giving a direct answer.
context: 在家煮皮蛋瘦肉粥，一方问“咸淡合适吗”，另一方回答“还没有吃到咸蛋”。
literal_translation: On the weekend, on a whim, I made preserved egg and lean pork congee at home. Happily I asked my boyfriend: “Is the saltiness right?” While eating, he said: “I still haven’t eaten any salted egg.”
functional_equivalence_translation: I asked, “Is the seasoning okay?” He replied, “Haven’t found the salted egg yet.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the boyfriend playfully mishearing “xiándàn” in “xiándàn héshì ma” (“Is the salt level okay?”) as “xiándàn”/near-sounding “salted egg,” pretending the question was about whether there was salted egg in the congee.
interpretation_1: 女方问粥的味道是否咸淡适中。
interpretation_2: 男友故意把“咸淡”岔听成“咸蛋”，理解为粥里是否吃到了咸鸭蛋。

surface_text: 老婆和几个朋友逛街， 过斑马线没看红灯，交警咆哮：“喂，你们几个！” 天然呆老婆怯怯地说：“我们六个…六个。”
2001年7月的某一天，逛超市，有位富婆对着她满身金器的老公说：老公，你看我们买一袋价格高一点的米吧。 大肚子老公说：好的。 富婆说你看这一袋绿色大米怎么样？ 大肚子老公看了一下包装袋说：不行。 富婆说：怎么不行？ 老公说：这米做出来的米饭是绿色的。 富婆说：这明明是大白米，怎么会做出绿色米饭呢？ 老公指着米袋回答：你看上面写着绿色大米
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“绿色大米”是商品标签，意思是绿色食品类别的大米，即环保、无公害、较健康的大米，并不是说米粒本身是绿色的。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'green rice' is taken literally to mean rice that is green in color, so the husband thinks it would cook into green-colored rice.
interpretation_2_zh: 老公把“绿色”误解为颜色义，理解成这种米煮出来会是绿色的米饭，因此产生了字面错解式的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'green' refers to an eco-friendly or natural label on the package, meaning ordinary white rice marketed as 'green' food, not rice that is actually green.
context: 超市买米场景中，妻子把“绿色大米”理解为绿色食品标签，丈夫把“绿色”按字面颜色义理解。
literal_translation: Green rice.
functional_equivalence_translation: Let’s buy this “green rice.” — No, the cooked rice will turn green.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the phrase “green rice”: the wife means rice certified as “green food” (eco-friendly/healthy), while the husband interprets it literally as rice that is green in color, so he thinks the cooked rice will come out green.
interpretation_1: 表层义是“绿色食品意义上的大米”，指天然、健康、无污染的米。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“颜色是绿色的大米”或“煮出来会是绿色的米饭”。

surface_text: 公司一员工拾获一本书，由于公司人数众多不易寻问，于是在大门口张贴纸条：“失物招领，遗书一本。” 翌日，纸条已改：“书我已领走,谢谢你的遗言。”
某日，小吴到小陈家拜访，碰巧遇到小陈因为儿子在习字簿上写错字大发雷霆。于是小吴就赶紧去劝小陈说：小孩子写错字总是难免，你又何必这么生气呢？小陈告诉小吴说：他老是把列祖列宗写成劣祖劣宗，你说我气不气？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是说孩子把“列祖列宗”错写成了“劣祖劣宗”，字面意思变成了“恶劣的祖先、恶劣的宗族”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child literally wrote the phrase as "inferior ancestors and inferior forefathers" instead of the correct "ancestors and forefathers," which is simply a wrong character substitution in handwriting.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是原本应写的常规表达“列祖列宗”，指历代祖先。错写后因“列”与“劣”替换，褒敬意味被扭成贬义，等于是在辱及祖先，所以小陈才格外生气。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that by replacing "列" with the similar-sounding "劣," the phrase turns into an insult, implying that the family ancestors are bad or inferior, which is why the father is so angry.
context: 孩子在习字簿上把“列祖列宗”写成“劣祖劣宗”，引发父亲愤怒。
literal_translation: He always writes “liezu-liezong” as “liezu-liezong” with the character for “inferior” instead of “listed/ancestral line.”
functional_equivalence_translation: He keeps writing “honored ancestors” as “inferior ancestors” — how could I not be angry?
explanatory_translation: The joke comes from a wrong character: “列祖列宗” means “one’s honored forefathers,” but “列” is replaced with the homophonous “劣,” meaning “inferior,” turning it into an insulting phrase about the ancestors.
interpretation_1: “列祖列宗”指祖先、历代先人，是固定敬称。
interpretation_2: 把“列”误写成“劣”后，意思变成“恶劣、低劣的祖宗”，带有贬损祖先的意味。

surface_text: 家里卫生间的门是塑钢材料做成的。有一天，门有些坏了，卡在那里，于是，我爸就打电话给卖门的师傅。 我爸：“师傅呀，我的钢门（肛门）坏了。” 师傅：“呃~~~那个，要不我给你打个120？”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指家里卫生间的塑钢门坏了、卡住了，需要请卖门的师傅来维修。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he means that the steel bathroom door at home is broken and stuck, so he is calling the door seller to get it repaired.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“钢门”与“肛门”谐音，听起来像是在说自己的肛门出了问题，所以师傅才会误以为是身体急症，提出打120。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from the similar sound of 'steel door' and 'anus' in Chinese, making it sound like he is saying his anus is broken, which is why the repairman jokes about calling an ambulance.
context: 父亲给卖门的师傅打电话报修厕所塑钢门，却把“钢门”说成可被听成“肛门”，引发对方误解。
literal_translation: My home's bathroom steel door is broken.
functional_equivalence_translation: Dad said, “Sir, my toilet door is broken,” but it sounded like, “My back door is broken.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on Chinese “gangmen”: “钢门” means a steel door, while the identical-sounding “肛门” means anus, so the repairman misunderstands it as a medical emergency.
interpretation_1: 家里坏掉的塑钢门、厕所门。
interpretation_2: 人体器官“肛门”坏了，需要急救。

surface_text: 这档节目真会爆，话题一播就爆，嘉宾脾气也差点爆。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“爆”指节目播出后话题迅速走红，热度激增，在传播层面引发大规模关注。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '爆' describes things bursting out dramatically: the show becomes explosive in topic impact once it airs, and the guest's temper almost erupts.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“爆”指嘉宾情绪接近爆发边缘，说明现场气氛紧张，冲突感也被放大出来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '爆' is used in parallel with different senses at once: it means both 'to become hugely popular or trending' for the show and 'to lose control / explode emotionally' for the guest's temper.
context: 节目、话题、嘉宾脾气三个对象连续共用“爆”字，分别激活“爆红”和“爆发”两层含义
literal_translation: This show is really explosive: once a topic airs, it explodes, and the guest's temper almost explodes too.
functional_equivalence_translation: This show really blows up—its topics blow up as soon as they air, and one guest almost blew up too.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on the Chinese word “爆,” which first means “to become hugely popular” for the show/topic, and then shifts to “to erupt/lose one's temper” for the guest.
interpretation_1: 节目和话题迅速走红、引发热议
interpretation_2: 嘉宾情绪失控、脾气要爆发

surface_text: 大刘失业后，家里的生活开始拮据起来，可他仍然很乐观。日子久了，老婆不禁抱怨起来：“大刘，去年你去求签，那解签的说你命里将有贵人相助，现在都快揭不开锅了，怎么贵人还不出现呢？” 大刘哈哈一笑，说：“快了，是贵人暂时把咱给忘了。” “为什么？” “不是有句话，叫‘贵人多忘事’吗？”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指会有身份高、能帮忙的重要人物出现并给予帮助，所以大刘说贵人只是暂时还没来。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '贵人' means a noble or influential benefactor who is supposed to appear and help Da Liu out of hardship.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“贵人多忘事”这句常见说法，把“贵人”解释成健忘、记不起别人的人，因此把贵人迟迟不出现说成是因为对方把自己忘了。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the phrase '贵人多忘事': instead of meaning important people are busy and forgetful, Da Liu twists it literally to say that the benefactor has simply forgotten about them for now.
context: 妻子提到求签说命里有贵人相助，但家里仍很贫困；大刘借“贵人多忘事”解释贵人还没来帮忙。
literal_translation: After being unemployed, Da Liu's family life became strained, but he stayed optimistic. After a long time, his wife complained: “Last year you went to get a fortune, and the interpreter said you'd have a benefactor helping you. Now we can hardly keep the pot uncovered—why hasn't the benefactor shown up?” Da Liu laughed and said, “Soon. The benefactor has just forgotten us for the time being.” “Why?” “Isn't there a saying: ‘Important people tend to forget things’?”
functional_equivalence_translation: “Why hasn't our lucky helper shown up yet?” “Give it time,” Da Liu said. “Big shots are forgetful—ours just forgot about us.”
explanatory_translation: The pun relies on the Chinese saying “贵人多忘事,” which normally means important people are busy and tend to forget things. Da Liu twists it literally to mean their promised “benefactor” has actually forgotten about helping them.
interpretation_1: 成语式说法，指地位高或重要的人事务繁多，容易忘记小事。
interpretation_2: 字面化理解为那个会帮助他们的贵人真的把大刘一家忘了，所以迟迟没有出现。

surface_text: 一女人来到一家名气很大的美容院。 美容师：“您好！有什么我能帮您的吗？” 女人：“我想做隆胸手术！” 美容师：“我们使用最新技术，2边都做的话是1000块钱！” 女人：“难道你们还可以只做一边？” 美容师：“是的！” 女人：“那只做一边是多少钱啊？” 美容师：“300块！” 女人：“为什么做一边300块，两边都做却要1000块啊？” 美容师语重心长的解释道：“一波三折！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上借用成语“一波三折”，字面可理解为做一边隆胸后，胸部轮廓起伏变成一次波动却有三处转折，因此收费更低却更怪异。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "一波三折" keeps its idiomatic meaning: something goes through many twists and turns, so the beautician is jokingly explaining the pricing with a phrase meaning "full of ups and downs."
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是只做一边会导致两侧胸部极不对称，一边隆起一边保持原状，外形会显得别扭曲折；这里把成语“一波三折”转移来形容胸部线条的不协调。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning splits the idiom literally: "一波" sounds like one breast, and "三折" means a 30% discount. So doing only one side costs 300, while doing both sides costs 1000 because the one-side operation is treated as "one boob at 30% off."
context: 美容院报价：两边隆胸1000元，只做一边300元；顾客追问为何一边反而更便宜，美容师回答“一波三折”。
literal_translation: "One wave, three turns."
functional_equivalence_translation: "One boob, one-third price."
explanatory_translation: The beautician twists the idiom "一波三折" (literally "one wave, three twists") by making "波" sound like a joking reference to one breast/one side, implying that doing only one side is charged at a 70% discount, i.e. 30% of the full price.
interpretation_1: 按成语本义，事情过程曲折反复。
interpretation_2: 借“波”谐指胸部的一边，意思是做一边按三折收费。

surface_text: 有一位漂亮的美女，想通过电脑查查自己的未来伴侣！ 美女根据要求填入了交友的两个条件：1，要帅。2，要有车。过了一会，答案出来了：“象棋”。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是美女在择偶，条件是男方长得帅，并且有汽车。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the woman wants a future partner who is handsome and owns a car, and the computer strangely returns the answer 'Chinese chess.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“帅”和“车”转移为象棋里的棋子名称，因此符合这两个条件的答案变成了“象棋”。
interpretation_2_en: The joke hinges on the words 'shuai' and 'che': in Chinese chess, '帅' is the general piece and '车' is the rook piece, so the entered conditions accidentally describe chess pieces rather than an ideal boyfriend.
context: 美女输入择偶条件“要帅、要有车”后，电脑给出的结果是“象棋”。
literal_translation: A beautiful woman wanted to use a computer to check her future partner. She entered two conditions: 1. handsome. 2. has a vehicle. After a while, the answer came out: “Chinese chess.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A woman entered two dating requirements into a computer: 1. good-looking, 2. has wheels. The result came back: “a handsome rider.”
explanatory_translation: The joke is that “象棋” (Chinese chess, xiangqi) sounds like “像骑” (xiang qi), meaning roughly “looks good and rides/has a vehicle,” which humorously matches her two requirements.
interpretation_1: 答案表面上是棋类运动“象棋”。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“像骑”，即长得帅又有车可骑，借谐音拼出对伴侣条件的概括。

surface_text: 这家健身房推出“卡路理”，办卡的时候讲道理，练起来的时候全靠消耗卡路里。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上像是品牌自造词，可理解为与健身和卡路里相关的理念口号。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it appears to be a brand-coined term, understandable as a slogan about fitness and calories.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义将“卡路里”和“道理”拼接，表示健身这件事说到底还是得靠实际消耗热量，不只是听理论。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning blends 'calorie' and 'reason', suggesting that fitness ultimately depends on burning calories rather than just talking theory.
context: 适用于健身房广告、运动品牌宣传或减肥段子。
negative_example: 这家健身房很讲道理，教练解释得很清楚。
literal_translation: This gym launched 'calo-reason': when signing up they talk reason, but when training it all depends on burning calories.
functional_equivalence_translation: This gym sells more than motivation—when it comes to results, calories are the real argument.
explanatory_translation: The coined form blends the sound of 'calorie' with the morpheme for 'reason/principle', creating a slogan that links fitness talk with actual calorie burning.
interpretation_1: 健身理念口号
interpretation_2: 减肥终究靠消耗热量

surface_text: 我妈妈有颈椎病，天天往脖子上抹药，有天我问她：“你药抹脖子了吗？” 妈妈瞪着眼睛看着不解的我说：“我还没有打算自杀！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“药抹脖子”表示把药涂在脖子上治疗颈椎病，是在问是否已经往脖子上抹药。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the question means: 'Have you applied the medicine to your neck yet?' Here, '抹药' is understood as putting ointment or medicine on the neck.
interpretation_2_zh: “药”与“要”同音，容易被听成“你要抹脖子了吗”，其中“抹脖子”常指自杀，所以妈妈才会理解成“你要自杀吗”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from mishearing '药抹脖子' as something like 'using medicine on the neck to kill oneself,' activating the expression '抹脖子' meaning 'to slit one's throat' or commit suicide.
context: 妈妈因颈椎病天天在脖子上抹药，孩子问“你药抹脖子了吗”，触发“抹脖子”既可理解为给脖子抹药，也可理解为自杀俗语。
literal_translation: My mom has cervical spondylosis and applies medicine to her neck every day. One day I asked, “Have you wiped your neck with medicine yet?” Mom stared at me and said, “I’m not planning to kill myself yet!”
functional_equivalence_translation: My mom rubs medicine on her neck every day. I asked, “Did you do your neck yet?” She glared at me: “I’m not planning to slit my throat!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese phrase “mo bozi,” which literally can mean “apply something to the neck,” but idiomatically can also mean “cut one’s throat,” i.e. commit suicide.
interpretation_1: 把药膏涂抹在脖子上。
interpretation_2: 用刀割脖子，指自杀。

surface_text: 同事把每天下班后的散步叫作“续命步”，说这不是运动，是给灵魂缓冲加载。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指下班后通过散步恢复体力和精神状态。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means restoring physical and mental energy through an after-work walk.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用网络表达“续命”，把普通散步升级成维持生活运转的必需仪式。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it borrows the internet expression 'to keep oneself alive,' upgrading an ordinary walk into a ritual essential for surviving daily life.
context: 适用于职场生活分享、情绪表达或都市日常吐槽。
literal_translation: My coworker calls the walk after work a 'life-extending walk,' saying it is not exercise but buffer loading for the soul.
functional_equivalence_translation: My coworker calls the post-work walk a 'survival stroll'—less fitness, more emotional reboot.
explanatory_translation: The pun fuses the internet slang 'extend one's life' with 'walk,' creating a hybrid expression that frames a simple stroll as emotional and existential maintenance.
interpretation_1: 散步恢复状态
interpretation_2: 借续命强调精神补给

surface_text: 高三英语复习课上老师又发下一套试题，限80分钟完成。却听得有人高喊打假、打假，再看试卷赫然几个大字在目，高考英语仿真试题，原来如此。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上“打假”指打击假冒伪劣、揭露造假行为，所以听起来像是在喊要查处假的试题。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, someone is shouting 'fight counterfeits,' as if calling for action against fake goods or fraud.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“打假”是把“打仿”借成了常见说法，因为试卷上写着“高考英语仿真试题”，学生是在调侃这是一套“仿”的试题。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that they are actually complaining about the exam paper being a 'mock' or 'simulated' Gaokao English test; '打假' humorously shifts to reacting to the word '仿真' ('imitation/simulation').
context: 高三英语复习课，老师发下一套写有“高考英语仿真试题”的试卷，学生因此喊“打假”。
literal_translation: On the senior-year English review class, the teacher handed out another set of test papers and required it to be finished in 80 minutes. Then someone was heard shouting, “Fight fakes! Fight fakes!” Looking again at the paper, several big words came into view: “Simulated Gaokao English Test.” So that was why.
functional_equivalence_translation: In a senior English review class, the teacher handed out yet another paper to finish in 80 minutes. Someone suddenly shouted, “Down with the fake stuff!” Then we noticed the title: “Mock Gaokao English Test.” That explained the joke.
explanatory_translation: In a senior-year English review class, the teacher handed out a new test to be completed in 80 minutes. A student shouted, “Crack down on fakes!” The joke comes from the test being labeled “mock/simulated Gaokao English test”: “打假” normally means fighting counterfeit or fake things, but here it is humorously redirected to complain that the paper is a “mock,” i.e. not the real exam.
interpretation_1: 学生高喊“打假”，表面意思是要打击假冒伪劣、揭穿虚假。
interpretation_2: 实际上是抱怨老师发的是“仿真试题”，抓住“仿真≈假的”来喊着反对这份带“假”意味的试卷。

surface_text: 主任把一份材料递给局长看，局长问：“这内容是真的吗？” 主任拍着胸膛大声说：“肯定是真的！” “你怎么知道？” 主任斩钉截铁地说：“因为是传真机传过来的呀！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是说这份材料是通过传真机发送过来的，所以主任据此回答“是真的”。
interpretation_1_en: The director literally means the material must be genuine because it was sent by a fax machine.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“传真机”借成“传真的机器”来理解，激活“真传过来”的意思，仿佛只要经它传送内容就一定真实，形成偷换概念的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The joke plays on treating 'fax' as if it guaranteed 'facts' or truth, confusing the method of transmission with the authenticity of the content.
context: 局长质疑材料内容是否真实，主任用“因为是传真机传过来的”来证明其真实性。
literal_translation: The director handed a document to the bureau chief. The bureau chief asked, “Is this content true?” The director patted his chest and said loudly, “It must be true!” “How do you know?” The director said firmly, “Because it was sent by a fax machine!”
functional_equivalence_translation: “Is this information reliable?” “Of course—it came by fax, so it’s facts.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “传真” (fax), which literally means “transmit truth” in its characters. The director wrongly treats “sent by fax” as if it guaranteed that the content is true.
interpretation_1: “传真机传过来的”指通过传真设备发送来的材料。
interpretation_2: 把“传真”误解为“传来的是真的”，即“真传/传真”被当作真实性的依据。

surface_text: 这位司机真会稳，方向盘打得稳，乘客情绪也安得稳。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“稳”指司机操控方向盘和车速平顺，没有明显颠簸，让乘车过程很舒服。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the driver handles the steering wheel steadily and drives smoothly, so everything feels stable.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“安得稳”指他的服务态度让乘客放心，连焦躁不安的情绪都被安抚下来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the driver's steady driving also calms the passengers emotionally, extending 'steady' from physical control to emotional reassurance.
context: 司机驾驶技术平稳，因此不仅车辆行驶稳定，也让乘客情绪安稳。
negative_example: 这位司机真会稳，方向盘打得稳，车速控制得稳。
literal_translation: This driver is really good at being steady: he turns the steering wheel steadily, and the passengers' emotions are also settled steadily.
functional_equivalence_translation: This driver is really smooth—steady hands on the wheel, and he keeps the passengers calm as well.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on '稳' ('steady/calm'): it first describes the driver's stable driving, then extends to mean that the passengers feel emotionally settled and at ease.
interpretation_1: 指司机开车平稳，操作方向盘很稳当。
interpretation_2: 指乘客情绪被安抚下来，处于安稳状态。

surface_text: 老师在黑板上写上扑朔迷离，然后问一位学生：请你说一下这个成语是什么意思？学生站起来，推了一下深度近视眼镜，仔细看了一下黑板上的四个字，看了半天也不明白，最后他无可奈何地说：老师，看不清楚。老师说：你说对了，请坐！
interpretation_1_zh: 学生因为近视，看黑板上的字时物理上看不清楚，所以回答“看不清楚”。
interpretation_1_en: The student literally means that, because of his poor eyesight, he cannot clearly see the four characters written on the blackboard.
interpretation_2_zh: “看不清楚”也正好对应成语“扑朔迷离”的常规意思，即事情或情况错综复杂，让人难以看清、难以分辨。
interpretation_2_en: At the same time, "看不清楚" also correctly explains the idiom "扑朔迷离," meaning something is confusing, hard to distinguish, or difficult to figure out clearly.
context: 老师让学生解释成语“扑朔迷离”，学生因近视先按自身视觉状态回答“看不清楚”，恰好又对应了该成语的含义。
literal_translation: The teacher wrote “pū shuò mí lí” on the blackboard and asked a student what this idiom meant. The student looked for a long time and said, “Teacher, I can’t see it clearly.” The teacher said, “That’s right. Sit down.”
functional_equivalence_translation: The teacher wrote “confusing and hard to make out” on the board and asked what it meant. A nearsighted student squinted and finally said, “I can’t make it out clearly.” “Correct,” said the teacher.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “看不清楚 / can’t see clearly.” The student literally means he cannot read the words on the board because of poor eyesight, but this also accidentally gives the meaning of the idiom “扑朔迷离,” which describes something as confusing and impossible to see clearly.
interpretation_1: 学生从字面上回答自己因为近视而看不清黑板上的字。
interpretation_2: 老师期待的答案是成语“扑朔迷离”的释义，即事情错综复杂、难以看清真相。

surface_text: 男青年抚摸着女友穿着迷你裙的大腿：亲爱的，我爱你！ 女友被爱抚得神魂颠倒：再，再高一点儿！ 男青年提高嗓门：亲爱的，我爱你！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“再高一点儿”被男青年理解成把声音提高一些，所以他提高嗓门再次说“亲爱的，我爱你”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "higher" means moving his hand further up her thigh while caressing her.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里女友说的“高一点儿”是指抚摸的位置再往大腿更上方移动一些，带有亲昵挑逗意味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that he interprets "higher" as speaking in a louder, higher voice, so he raises his voice and repeats "Darling, I love you!"
context: 男青年一边抚摸女友大腿一边表白，女友说“再高一点儿”，语义可同时指手的位置和说话音量；男青年故意按后者理解。
literal_translation: The young man stroked the thigh of his girlfriend in a miniskirt: Darling, I love you! The girlfriend, overwhelmed by the caress, said: H-higher, a little higher! The young man raised his voice: Darling, I love you!
functional_equivalence_translation: As he caressed his girlfriend’s thigh, the young man said, “Darling, I love you!” Dizzy with pleasure, she whispered, “A little higher...” He took it the other way and spoke louder: “Darling, I love you!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “higher,” which can mean either moving his hand further up her leg or raising the pitch/volume of his voice. He deliberately interprets it as the latter.
interpretation_1: 把声音提高一点，再大声一点说。
interpretation_2: 把手的位置再往上移一点，继续爱抚更高部位。

surface_text: 寝室里有人说：“我搁的洗衣粉儿太多了。” 一个哥们问：“你哥的媳妇儿太多了?有几个？”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中第一人说的是自己放的洗衣粉太多了，表示洗衣粉用量过量。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the roommate mishears the sentence as 'Your brother's wives are too many,' and asks how many there are.
interpretation_2_zh: 第二人把“搁的洗衣粉儿”误听成“哥的媳妇儿”，于是理解成“你哥哥的媳妇太多了”，形成谐音错听的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the original sentence actually said 'I put in too much laundry detergent,' but the sound was shifted and jokingly reinterpreted as 'my brother's wives.'
context: 一人说“我搁的洗衣粉儿太多了”，另一人把“洗衣粉儿”听成“媳妇儿”，并把“我搁的”联想到“我哥的”。
literal_translation: In the dorm, someone said, “I put in too much laundry detergent.” A guy asked, “Your brother’s wife is too many? How many are there?”
functional_equivalence_translation: In the dorm, someone said, “I used too much detergent.” Another guy joked, “Your brother’s got too many wives? How many?”
explanatory_translation: The joke comes from mishearing the Chinese phrase for “laundry detergent” as “brother’s wife,” creating a comic shift from talking about washing powder to talking about how many sisters-in-law there are.
interpretation_1: 原话是在说洗衣粉放多了。
interpretation_2: 被故意听岔成在说哥哥的媳妇太多了。

surface_text: 我把月底状态总结为“余额自闭期”，钱包不想社交，我也不敢路过奶茶店。
hidden_form: 自闭期 / 余额不足 / 消费收缩
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指临近月底时，因为账户余额变少而主动减少消费和出门诱惑。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to the end-of-month state of reducing spending and avoiding temptations because one's account balance is low.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用“自闭期”这种情绪化说法，把钱包拟人化为不愿社交，形成生活化吐槽。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it borrows the emotional phrase 'withdrawn period' and personifies the wallet as unwilling to socialize, creating a relatable complaint.
context: 适用于月末消费吐槽、社交平台段子、年轻人财务自嘲。
literal_translation: I sum up my end-of-month condition as a 'balance-withdrawal period': my wallet doesn't want to socialize, and I don't dare walk past milk tea shops.
functional_equivalence_translation: I call the end of every month my 'wallet hibernation phase'—low balance, low courage, and no detours past bubble tea shops.
explanatory_translation: This hybrid phrase combines 'account balance' with an emotional-state expression, personifying financial shortage as social withdrawal. The humor comes from morphological blending and semantic transfer.
interpretation_1: 月底因钱少而收缩消费
interpretation_2: 把余额不足说成情绪退缩

surface_text: 某电厂老板看到联想公司的一句广告：人类没有联想，世界将会怎样。 老板灵机一动，为自己厂子想出一个标语：世界失去电力，人类只能联想！
发生地震，厨房被震得一塌糊涂，厨房老大冰箱率先站起来：大家都快醒醒，看看自己有没有受伤。 香蕉：我下半身不能动了。 苹果：我成苹果酱了。 菠菜：我成刷墙的涂料了。 …… 大家纷纷讲过自己的伤势以后，冰箱发现只有鸡蛋一个人没有讲话，于是它忙问：鸡蛋，你怎么了，是不是受了很严重的伤？ 鸡蛋：伤倒是没感觉，就是觉得蛋疼。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是鸡蛋在地震后说自己没有明显外伤，只是觉得自己的蛋很疼，符合鸡蛋这一角色的字面身份。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the egg is saying that its egg body hurts after the earthquake.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借用口语“蛋疼”这一说法，表示让人无语、难受或尴尬，并非单纯描述鸡蛋本体疼痛。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the Chinese slang expression '蛋疼,' which means feeling awkward, annoyed, speechless, or troubled, not literally having pain in an egg.
context: 地震后厨房里的食物被拟人化，大家都在汇报自己受伤情况，鸡蛋最后说“蛋疼”。
literal_translation: Egg: I don’t really feel injured, I just feel egg-hurt.
functional_equivalence_translation: Egg: I’m not exactly injured—I just feel kind of "nutsore."
explanatory_translation: Egg: I don’t really feel wounded; it’s just that I feel “dan teng,” a Chinese slang phrase meaning a vague, annoying discomfort, which literally also reads as “egg pain” and fits the egg character.
interpretation_1: 字面上指鸡蛋感到疼痛，符合鸡蛋这一角色身份。
interpretation_2: 借用口语“蛋疼”表示无聊、纠结或说不清的不适感，这里形成拟人化幽默。

surface_text: 朋友把新买的收纳柜夸成“柜在会分层”，袜子、数据线和情绪都终于各归各位。
hidden_form: 贵在会分类 / 柜子会分层
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指这个收纳柜的分层设计合理，便于整理物品。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the cabinet has a well-designed layered structure for organizing items.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“贵在……”句式，把“分类能力”转嫁到“柜子分层”上，突出产品价值。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it imitates the phrase pattern 'the value lies in...,' transferring the idea of classification skill onto the cabinet's layered design.
context: 适用于家居收纳产品文案、种草笔记或生活类短视频标题。
literal_translation: My friend praised the new storage cabinet as 'the cabinet's value lies in layering'; socks, charging cables, and even emotions finally go to their own places.
functional_equivalence_translation: My friend says this cabinet is genius because its tiers do all the sorting for you.
explanatory_translation: The expression parodies the structure 'the key value lies in...' while replacing it with 'cabinet' and 'layering,' creating a hybrid phrase that sounds evaluative and literal at once.
interpretation_1: 柜子擅长分层收纳
interpretation_2: 仿拟贵在会分类

surface_text: 一对男女朋友一起去逛街。 女朋友：哎哟，脚好酸哦。 男朋友很紧张：怎么了？是不是踩到柠檬了？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是女朋友说自己脚部发酸、疲劳，男朋友便按字面理解，紧张地问是不是踩到了柠檬，才会“酸”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the girlfriend says her feet feel sore from walking, and the boyfriend jokingly asks whether she stepped on a lemon, since lemons are literally sour.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“酸”从身体酸痛转移到食物味道的“酸”，利用柠檬典型的酸味制造语义错位与幽默。
interpretation_2_en: The pun is triggered by the word '酸' in Chinese, which can mean physically sore and also sour in taste. The boyfriend intentionally shifts from the 'sore' meaning to the 'sour' meaning, linking it to a lemon.
context: 一对男女逛街时，女方说“脚好酸”，男方将身体感觉的“酸”误解为食物味觉上的“酸”，于是问是不是踩到柠檬了
negative_example: 脚好麻，是不是踩到花椒了？
literal_translation: A couple were shopping together. Girlfriend: Oh, my feet are so sore. Boyfriend, very nervous: What happened? Did you step on a lemon?
functional_equivalence_translation: A couple were out shopping. Girlfriend: Ouch, my feet are really aching. Boyfriend: What happened? Did you step on a lemon or something?
explanatory_translation: A couple were shopping. The girlfriend says her feet feel “suan,” which in Chinese commonly means sore/aching, but the boyfriend humorously interprets it as the “sour” taste associated with lemons, so he asks whether she stepped on a lemon.
interpretation_1: 女朋友说脚很酸，表示脚部疲劳、发酸
interpretation_2: 男朋友把“酸”误解成柠檬带来的酸味，联想到踩到柠檬

surface_text: 学校周围新开了一家沂蒙山羊肉馆， 这天，我作为一个二货陪女同学路过这里， 我当时第一眼看到，然后就读了出来沂蒙山羊肉馆…………山羊？ 山羊！擦，当时我那同学笑的直不起腰来…………
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把店名直接读成“沂蒙山羊肉馆”，容易理解成“沂蒙山羊”的肉，也就是把“沂蒙山羊”当成一种山羊名称。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the sign is read as 'Yimeng Mountain goat meat restaurant,' meaning a restaurant that sells mutton/goat meat from the Yimeng Mountain area.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上更自然的店名结构应是“沂蒙山”加“羊肉馆”，意思是主打沂蒙山风味或与沂蒙山有关的羊肉馆，而不是“山羊”这个动物类别本身。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden joke comes from misparsing the phrase as 'Yimeng Mountain goat'—as if 'Yimeng Mountain' is modifying 'goat' directly—so it sounds like they are specifically talking about a mountain goat, which makes the reading funny and awkward.
context: 读招牌“沂蒙山羊肉馆”时，将“沂蒙山羊肉馆”误切分为“沂蒙+山羊+肉馆”，从而把“山羊”读成独立词。
literal_translation: A Yimeng Mountain mutton restaurant... goat? Goat!
functional_equivalence_translation: I saw the sign “Yimeng Mountain Mutton Restaurant” and misread it as “Yimeng goat restaurant” — “goat?!”
explanatory_translation: The joke comes from mis-segmenting the Chinese shop sign “沂蒙山羊肉馆”. It should mean “a mutton restaurant from/in Yimeng Mountain,” but the speaker reads “山羊” as the separate word “goat,” which creates the comic misunderstanding.
interpretation_1: 店名中的“山羊”被连读理解为一种动物，即goat。
interpretation_2: 实际更自然的店名切分应是“沂蒙山 羊肉馆”，其中“沂蒙山”是地名修饰“羊肉馆”，不是在说“山羊肉馆”。

surface_text: 又到毕业季，食堂门口有学姐卖书，标语写到：“一元一本，买书送学姐啦！” 果断上去围观，一新生装模作样的挑了一本书， 指着标语说：“送的学姐呢？” 姑娘豪迈的答到：“我们后天的火车，到时候记得来送我们啊。” 围观的人爆笑，该男面红耳赤低头而去。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“送”理解为商家促销中的“赠送”，意思是买一本书就附送一位学姐。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the slogan means: for one yuan per book, if you buy a book, you also get a senior girl as a free giveaway.
interpretation_2_zh: 实际把“送”转成“送行、送别”，意思是学姐们后天坐火车离校，到时候记得来送别她们。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the Chinese word '送': it actually means 'to see someone off'. The girl replies that they are leaving by train the day after tomorrow, so he should come to send them off then, not that a senior girl is included as a gift.
context: 毕业季，学姐在食堂门口卖书，标语写“一元一本，买书送学姐啦”，新生误将“送”理解为赠送，学姐则解释为送别她们上火车。
literal_translation: It’s graduation season again. At the cafeteria gate, a senior girl was selling books, with a sign saying: “One yuan per book, buy a book and get a senior girl for free!” A freshman pretended to choose a book and pointed at the sign: “Where’s the senior girl that comes with it?” The girl answered boldly: “Our train is the day after tomorrow. Remember to come see us off then.”
functional_equivalence_translation: At graduation time, a senior was selling books with a sign: “One yuan each—buy a book and I’ll send a senior with it!” A freshman asked, “So where’s the free senior?” She replied, “Our train leaves the day after tomorrow—come send us off then.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “送,” which can mean “to give as a bonus” or “to see someone off.” The freshman reads the sign as “buy a book and get a senior girl for free,” but the seller flips it to mean “come see us off when we leave by train.”
interpretation_1: 标语中的“买书送学姐”被理解为购买书后附赠一个学姐。
interpretation_2: 学姐回答中的“送我们”实际是指到火车站为毕业离校的学姐送行。

surface_text: 昨天带孩子去公园看动物。见孔雀园里有只公鸡，很诧异，正在想是什么情况，边上一对情侣，女说：“有只鸡，怎么回事？” 男说：“不懂了吧，那是怕孔雀近亲结婚。”
六月酷暑，一个月没下过雨，地干田裂，眼看今年将颗粒无收。 “奶奶，奶奶，今晚有流星雨！”兴奋的小孙女想许个公主的愿望。 奶奶一脸期盼:“谢天谢地，终于有雨了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“小孙女说今晚有流星雨”，这里的“雨”指流星成群出现，像下雨一样划过天空的天文现象。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'rain' refers to actual rainfall. The grandmother hears there will finally be rain tonight and feels relieved because the drought may end.
interpretation_2_zh: 奶奶把“流星雨”里的“雨”理解成真正的降雨，联想到久旱之后终于要下雨了，表达的是对雨水的盼望。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the granddaughter is talking about a 'meteor shower,' where 'rain' is part of the fixed expression 'shooting-star rain' rather than real precipitation.
context: 久旱无雨、庄稼将绝收，孙女说“今晚有流星雨”，奶奶因盼雨心切把“流星雨”中的“雨”理解成真正的下雨。
literal_translation: In the scorching heat of June, it hadn’t rained for a month. The land was dry and the fields were cracking, and it looked like there would be no harvest this year. “Grandma, Grandma, there will be a meteor shower tonight!” the excited little granddaughter wanted to make a princess wish. Grandma said expectantly, “Thank heavens, finally, rain is coming.”
functional_equivalence_translation: After a month of drought, Grandma heard “meteor shower” and only caught the “shower,” thinking rain had finally arrived.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “流星雨” (meteor shower). The granddaughter means an astronomical event, but the rain-starved grandmother interprets the word “雨” literally as actual rainfall, creating the humorous semantic shift.
interpretation_1: 指天文现象，大量流星在夜空中划过。
interpretation_2: 被奶奶误听误解为能缓解旱情的降雨。

surface_text: 小兔说：“我是兔娘养的！” 小猪说：“我是猪娘养的！” 小鸡说：“我是鸡娘养的” 小狗说：“我是狗娘养的！”
interpretation_1_zh: 按字面看，小狗在沿着前文句式说自己是被狗妈妈养大的。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the little dog is simply saying, like the other animals, that it was raised by its mother dog.
interpretation_2_zh: “狗娘养的”在汉语里也是一句固定骂人的话，因此这里触发了粗口义，形成表面自我介绍与隐含骂人表达的双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '狗娘养的' is also a common Chinese insult, roughly meaning 'a son of a bitch' or 'bastard.'
context: 前文依次出现“兔娘养的”“猪娘养的”“鸡娘养的”，形成“X娘养的”并列结构，最后“狗娘养的”触发从字面亲属表达到惯用骂语的语义切换。
literal_translation: The little dog said, “I was raised by a dog mother!”
functional_equivalence_translation: The puppy said, “I’m a son of a bitch!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “狗娘养的”: in the list pattern it literally sounds like “raised by a dog mother,” but in Chinese it is also a conventional insult meaning roughly “son of a bitch.”
interpretation_1: 按前文并列句式理解为“由狗妈妈养大的”。
interpretation_2: 在汉语中也是固定骂人话，带强烈侮辱意味。

surface_text: 女儿和妈妈到家后，妈妈急着找东西…… 女儿：妈妈我洗完脸就上网了……行不 妈妈：……（找东西） 女儿：我一会上网了行不？ 妈妈：……（东西哪去了呢） 女儿：妈妈我上网啦！ 妈妈飘出一句话：你上墙都没人管……
interpretation_1_zh: 女儿反复说“上网”，字面意思是去联网、使用网络。
interpretation_1_en: The surface meaning is that the daughter wants to go online and use the internet, asking her mother for permission several times.
interpretation_2_zh: 妈妈把“上网”误听成近音的“上炕”，意思是去炕上、上床一类的动作，所以才说“你上墙都没人管”，表示她根本不在意女儿说的这个事。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the mother is annoyed and uses "go up the wall" to mean even if the daughter climbed the wall, she still would not care; it sarcastically echoes the daughter's repeated "go online."
context: 妈妈忙着找东西，无暇回应女儿反复请求上网；最后用“你上墙都没人管”回话，借把“网”替换成“墙”形成突兀幽默。
literal_translation: Daughter: Mom, can I go online? Mom: No one would care even if you climbed the wall.
functional_equivalence_translation: Daughter: Mom, can I get online? Mom: For all I care, you could go climb the walls.
explanatory_translation: The humor comes from the mother twisting the daughter’s repeated “go online” into “go up the wall.” It is not a sound-based pun, but a semantic substitution that shows the mother is too busy and annoyed to respond properly.
interpretation_1: 女儿说的“上网”是指连接网络、去网上活动。
interpretation_2: 妈妈回“你上墙都没人管”是故意把“上网”夸张替换成“上墙”，表示根本没人限制你，带有不耐烦和调侃。

surface_text: 某日上生物课，生物老师问猫又：“袁隆平取得了什么巨大成就？” 小刚小声道：“杂交水稻。” 小明随即脱口而出：“杂种！”
新出的低糖面包打出“轻碳主义”口号，吃的人像是在跟热量谈判，又没完全和快乐决裂。
hidden_form: 轻断食/低碳 + 极简主义/某某主义
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指减少碳水、追求更轻负担饮食的一种吃法。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a low-carb, lighter style of eating.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿照“某某主义”的说法，把控碳饮食包装成一种生活态度或价值选择。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it imitates ideological labels ending in '-ism', turning low-carb eating into a lifestyle stance.
context: 适用于食品广告、减脂品牌宣传或健康生活话题。
literal_translation: The new low-sugar bread promotes 'light-carb-ism'.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bread sells a low-carb lifestyle, not just a recipe.
explanatory_translation: The pun hybridizes 'low-carb/light carb' with the productive suffix-like pattern of '-ism', making a dietary feature sound like a social philosophy.
interpretation_1: 轻负担低碳饮食
interpretation_2: 把控碳变成生活主义

surface_text: 一天我在上网，他突然跑过来问我：路由是送的还是圆的？ 我白了一眼：方的，自己买的。 舍友大叫：笨蛋，我问的是写诗的那个陆游。 尼玛，遇到这种货实在伤不起。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“陆游”听成了“路由”，于是把问题理解成在问网络路由器的形状或是否附送，所以回答“方的，自己买的”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker mishears 'Lu You' as 'router' and answers the question as if it were about the shape of a router, saying it is square and bought separately.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义其实是在问南宋诗人“陆游”，利用“陆游”与“路由”同音造成误解，形成双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the roommate was actually asking about Lu You, the famous poet, not a network router; the humor comes from the similar pronunciation causing a semantic shift.
context: 一人在上网，舍友问“路由是送的还是圆的”，对方按网络路由器理解并回答“方的，自己买的”，随后舍友说明其实问的是诗人陆游。
literal_translation: One day I was surfing the Internet when he suddenly ran over and asked me: “Is the router given for free or round?” I rolled my eyes: “Square, bought it myself.” My roommate shouted: “Idiot, I meant Lu You, the one who writes poetry.” Damn, meeting this kind of guy is really unbearable.
functional_equivalence_translation: One day while I was online, he asked, “Is Lu You free or square?” I said, “Square, and I bought it myself.” He yelled, “Idiot, I meant Lu You the poet, not the router!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese homophone “luyou”: “路由” means router, while “陆游” is the poet Lu You. The speaker hears it as “router” and answers about the device’s shape and whether it was purchased, while the roommate actually meant the poet.
interpretation_1: 把“路由”理解为网络设备，所以问它是送的还是自己买的、是方的。
interpretation_2: 实际想问的是南宋诗人“陆游”，与“写诗的那个”相关。

surface_text: 室友把宿舍公共冰箱叫“冷静共享体”，每次找不到酸奶，大家都先被迫冷静一下。
hidden_form: 冷净/冷藏 + 共享体 / 冷静
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指一个大家共同使用的冷藏空间或共享冰箱。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a shared refrigerated space used by everyone.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借“冷静”一词，调侃冰箱不仅让食物变冷，也让找不到东西的人情绪降温。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it plays on 'calm down', joking that the fridge cools both food and people's emotions.
context: 适用于宿舍生活、合租吐槽或校园段子。
literal_translation: My roommate calls the shared dorm fridge a 'calm-cold shared unit'.
functional_equivalence_translation: Our shared fridge cools the food—and forces everyone to cool down too.
explanatory_translation: The pun merges the physical coldness of a shared fridge with the emotional sense of 'calming down', producing a humorous hybrid label for communal living.
interpretation_1: 共享冷藏空间
interpretation_2: 让人情绪冷静

surface_text: 一个男青年在饭店，他的菜上了有半个小时他还没动筷子， 服务员很疑惑，就上前询问：“你盯着这菜很久了，为什么不吃？” 男青年回答：“这道菜太咸了，我把它看淡些……看淡些……”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是男青年一直盯着这道菜，希望通过“看”让菜显得淡一点，好像看久了就不那么咸了，形成字面上的荒诞效果。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, he says the dish is too salty, so he is trying to 'look at it until it becomes blander,' as if staring at it could make the flavor lighter.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“看淡”借成了“变淡、没那么咸”，实际激活了“淡”作为味道变淡的含义，把通常表示心态上的“看淡些”转移到了菜的咸淡上。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the common expression '看淡些,' meaning to take something less seriously or be more detached. He jokingly applies this emotional phrase to an overly salty dish.
context: 男青年面对一盘太咸的菜，长时间不吃，被服务员询问原因后回答“我把它看淡些”。
literal_translation: A young man was in a restaurant. His dish had been served for half an hour, but he still had not started eating. The waiter was puzzled and went over to ask, “You’ve been staring at this dish for a long time. Why aren’t you eating?” The young man replied, “This dish is too salty. I’m trying to look at it as lighter... look at it as lighter...”
functional_equivalence_translation: “Why aren’t you eating?” “It’s too salty—I’m trying to see it as less of a big dill.”
explanatory_translation: The joke centers on “看淡,” which normally means “to take something lightly / not care so much,” but here it is reinterpreted literally as if merely looking at the dish could make its flavor “淡” (bland, less salty).
interpretation_1: 把事情看轻、看开，不太在意。
interpretation_2: 字面上希望通过“看”让菜变得更淡一些、不那么咸。

surface_text: 这款香薰被网友称为“情绪灭火器”，一点上，先灭的是焦虑，后灭的是屋里那股加班味。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指像灭火器一样快速压住情绪上头和烦躁。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means something that quickly suppresses emotional flare-ups like a fire extinguisher.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把家居香薰的除味、舒缓功能并置成“灭火”，既灭气味也灭情绪火气。
interpretation_2_en: It also frames the diffuser's deodorizing and calming functions as 'putting out a fire'—both odor and temper.
context: 适用于香薰、助眠、情绪疗愈产品描述。
literal_translation: This aroma diffuser is called an 'emotion fire extinguisher': once lit, it first puts out anxiety, then the overtime smell in the room.
functional_equivalence_translation: This diffuser works like a fire extinguisher for stress.
explanatory_translation: The phrase extends 'fire extinguisher' into the emotional domain. By hybridizing a physical safety object with mood relief, it creates a double reading about calming feelings and clearing unpleasant atmosphere.
interpretation_1: 平复情绪
interpretation_2: 去味降火

surface_text: 这位主播真会挂链接，商品会挂链接，情绪价值也被他挂满了。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“挂链接”指主播在直播间展示商品购买入口，方便观众直接下单消费。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the streamer is very good at posting or attaching product links during a live broadcast.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“挂满了”借指他直播时不断提供陪伴和安慰感，情绪价值输出非常充足。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it suggests he is not only adding shopping links but also constantly delivering emotional value, as if even feelings are being 'hung up' or fully loaded onto the stream.
context: 直播带货语境中，前文说主播会挂商品链接，后文把“情绪价值”也说成被他“挂满了”。
negative_example: 这位主播真会放链接，商品会放链接，情绪价值也被他放满了。
literal_translation: This streamer is really good at posting links: products get linked, and even emotional value is hung all over by him.
functional_equivalence_translation: This streamer really knows how to drop links—he posts product links, and somehow he’s also serving emotional support nonstop.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “挂” in Chinese. It first means “to post/add a link” in livestream sales, then is extended in parallel so that “emotional value” is also said to be “hung up/full,” treating emotional support like merchandise being listed.
interpretation_1: 主播把商品购买链接添加到页面或直播间里。
interpretation_2: 主播把情绪价值也像商品一样不断提供、铺满给观众。

surface_text: 有个人读古文，念道：临清流而赋诗。旁边一人急忙问道：哪里来的临清刘副使？为什么不早给我说，好让我奉承奉承结交他。那人说：我念的是《归去来辞》。旁边那人慢慢地说道：我还以为他是个现任的官儿呢，若是这个归去来辞的官儿，我就不理他了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本把“临清流”误听成“临清刘副使”，理解为一位来自临清的刘姓副使，是个可以巴结结交的现任官员。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the listener mistakes the recited phrase as referring to an actual official named Deputy Commissioner Liu of Linqing, and thinks he is a current officeholder worth currying favor with.
interpretation_2_zh: 原句实际出自《归去来辞》，“临清流而赋诗”是面对清澈水流作诗的意思，并不是在说某个名叫刘副使的官员。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the original line is actually 'facing a clear stream and composing poetry' from the prose piece Returning Home; it is not a person's name at all, and 'guiqu laici' is the title of a literary work, not an official post.
context: 有人诵读古文“临清流而赋诗”，旁人把文言短语误解析成人名加官职，并继续把“归去来辞”理解成官员去职。
literal_translation: A person was reading classical prose and recited, “Facing the clear stream, he composed poetry.” Someone beside him hurriedly asked, “Where did this Vice Envoy Liu from Linqing come from? Why didn’t you tell me earlier, so I could flatter him and get acquainted with him?” The reader said, “I was reading ‘The Return.’” The other man slowly said, “I thought he was a current official. If he is an official of this ‘return-and-resign’ sort, then I won’t bother with him.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Someone read, “By the clear stream he wrote a poem,” but the listener heard it as, “Vice Envoy Liu from Linqing has arrived,” and even took “The Return” to mean the man was already out of office.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on mishearing the classical phrase “临清流而赋诗” (“to face a clear stream and compose poetry”) as if it were “临清刘副使,” meaning “Vice Envoy Liu from Linqing.” The listener then extends the misunderstanding by treating “归去来辞” as if it indicated that the official had already resigned, so he loses interest in currying favor.
interpretation_1: 原句本义是“面对清澈溪流而作诗”。
interpretation_2: 被误听为“临清来的刘副使”这一官员称谓与身份介绍。

surface_text: 老公总是喜欢和老婆唱反调，不论做事说话都如此。 一次老婆大怒：我是你的女人，你怎么老是对着干？ 老公为缓解局面说：正因为你是我的女人，所以我才对着你干，难道你希望我对着别的女人干吗？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“对着你干”承接前文“对着干”，意思是总跟你唱反调、故意作对。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "gan" means to act against someone or confront them directly, as in always opposing his wife and doing things against her.
interpretation_2_zh: “干”同时激活其粗俗的隐含义，指与女人发生性行为，老公借此把“对着你干”歪解成只对自己的女人做这种事，而不是对别的女人。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, "gan" shifts to a vulgar sexual meaning, suggesting having sex with her, creating a crude double entendre from the same word.
context: 夫妻争吵中，妻子先用“对着干”指丈夫总跟自己作对；丈夫随后把成语式表达改按字面拆解理解，并与“别的女人”对比。
literal_translation: My husband always likes to go against his wife in everything he does and says. Once the wife got furious: I am your woman, why are you always opposing me? The husband tried to ease the situation and said: Precisely because you are my woman, I do it facing you; would you rather I do it facing another woman?
functional_equivalence_translation: You’re my woman, so of course I do it with you—not some other woman.
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the Chinese phrase “对着干,” which normally means “to act in opposition / deliberately go against someone.” The husband twists it into a literal reading, “do it facing you,” creating a suggestive sexual implication and defusing the quarrel with wordplay.
interpretation_1: 按固定表达理解，指故意作对、唱反调。
interpretation_2: 拆解为字面义，指“对着你来做”，带有暧昧的性暗示。

surface_text: 这门选修课被我们叫作“学术散步”，内容不水，但每次上完都像脑子去公园透了口气。
hidden_form: 散步 / 学术讨论 / 轻量学习
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是形容课程节奏轻松、启发式强，像边走边学一样自然。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it describes a course with a relaxed pace and strong inspiration, as if one were learning while taking a walk.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把严肃的“学术”与日常的“散步”拼接，弱化学术压迫感，突出轻盈思考。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it blends the serious word 'academic' with the casual activity 'walking', softening the pressure of academia and highlighting light, open thinking.
context: 适用于校园课程评价、讲座宣传、知识分享内容。
literal_translation: We call this elective 'academic walking'; the content isn't shallow, but every class feels like giving the brain a walk in the park.
functional_equivalence_translation: We call this elective an academic stroll—thoughtful, but refreshingly easy to absorb.
explanatory_translation: The pun is built by blending 'academic' with 'walking'. The hybrid expression reframes intellectual activity as something relaxed and breathable rather than burdensome.
interpretation_1: 轻松启发式课程
interpretation_2: 把学术写成散步般体验

surface_text: 大家都夸会做饭的阿姨的女儿。
一个小学语文老师上课时讲到孔子学生很多时，一个学生问老师说：老师，请问孔子的老师是谁？ 老师答不出来，问谁知道。一位学生说：我知道，孔子的老师是钻子，没有钻子那有孔子呀！
有一男滴，暗恋一女滴，没事就喜欢送女滴东西。 某日，男滴欢天喜地的回来，手里还拿了一个芒果。 室友问，怎么今天心情这么好。 男滴说，你看，这是那个女滴送我的。 室友看了一眼，深表同情的拍着男滴肩膀说： 哥们儿，节哀吧，没戏了。 男滴问：为什么啊？ 室友指着芒果说：人家已经告诉你了，芒果，就盲目是没有结果滴。 男滴大哭。。。。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是女生送了男生一个芒果，这只是一个水果礼物。
interpretation_1_en: The literal meaning is that the woman gave him a mango as a gift, and the story treats it simply as a fruit she handed to him.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“芒果”借成“盲果/盲目没有结果”的谐转说法，表示这段暗恋是盲目的，最终不会有结果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'mango' (芒果) is humorously reinterpreted as sounding like 'blindly, there will be no result' (盲目没有结果), implying his crush is hopeless and will not lead to a relationship.
context: 男子暗恋女子，女子送他一个芒果，室友据此解读为对方在委婉表达“盲目没有结果”。
literal_translation: Mango means that blind love bears no fruit.
functional_equivalence_translation: She gave him a mango to say his blind love would bear no fruit.
explanatory_translation: In Chinese, “mango” (芒果) is reinterpreted as the homophone-like phrase “blind fruit” (盲果), implying that a blind or one-sided crush will have no result.
interpretation_1: 女生送的是一种水果芒果。
interpretation_2: 把“芒果”谐解为“盲果”，即盲目的感情不会有结果，暗示拒绝。

surface_text: 老婆对老公说：你负责赚钱养家，我负责貌美如花。 老公深思两秒后说：你确实很像如花。
interpretation_1_zh: 妻子说“貌美如花”，意思是自己负责保持像花一样的美貌。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'ru hua' is understood literally from the phrase 'beautiful as a flower,' so the husband seems to be saying that she really is as pretty as a flower.
interpretation_2_zh: 丈夫把“如花”从比喻美貌转成专名联想，暗指周星驰电影中的丑角人物“如花”，讽刺妻子并不美。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'Ruhua' also refers to the famously ugly comedic female character from Stephen Chow films, so the husband is actually teasing that she looks like that character, not that she is flower-like beautiful.
context: 妻子说“我负责貌美如花”，丈夫接话“你确实很像如花”。
literal_translation: The wife said to the husband: You are responsible for earning money to support the family, and I am responsible for being as beautiful as a flower. After thinking deeply for two seconds, the husband said: You really are a lot like Ruhua.
functional_equivalence_translation: The wife said, “You make the money, I’ll stay pretty.” The husband paused and replied, “Pretty? You do look like ‘Pretty’—and not in the way you mean.”
explanatory_translation: The wife uses “beautiful as a flower” to mean she will remain attractive. The husband twists “ruhua” from “like a flower” into a reference to the comic ugly character Ruhua, turning the compliment into an insult.
interpretation_1: 妻子用成语表示自己会负责保持美貌，像花一样好看。
interpretation_2: 丈夫把“如花”从比喻义转成专名联想，暗指她像名为“如花”的丑角人物。

surface_text: 在一家小镇暂住，问旅店的服务员，“你们这里有什么特色？” 服务员呆了一下，哼哼唧唧地说：“我们老板特色…”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，服务员像是在回答旅店的“特色”，却说成了“我们老板特色……”，把“特色”直接安到老板身上，显得答非所问。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the guest is asking what special features or distinctive services the hotel has, and the waiter seems to answer by saying their boss is a special characteristic of the place.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是服务员想说的其实不是旅店有什么特色，而是老板这个人“特抠、特别刻薄之类”，借“特色”含混带过，形成对老板的暗中吐槽。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '特色' shifts from meaning 'special feature' to implying that the boss himself is odd, eccentric, or otherwise 'quite something,' turning the answer into a joke about the boss rather than the hotel.
context: 顾客问旅店有什么特色，服务员回答“我们老板特色…”，借“特色”引出对老板性格的评价。
literal_translation: Staying in a small town inn, I asked the clerk, “What specialties do you have here?” The clerk froze for a moment and muttered, “Our boss is te-se...”
functional_equivalence_translation: At a small-town inn, I asked, “What’s your special feature here?” The clerk hesitated and said, “Our boss’s special feature? He’s especially stingy.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “特色” (special feature), which is twisted into a near-sounding expression meaning the boss is “especially stingy,” so the answer pretends to describe the inn’s feature but actually insults the boss.
interpretation_1: 询问旅店有什么特色、特点或卖点。
interpretation_2: 服务员把“特色”转说成老板“特抠”，即老板非常吝啬。

surface_text: 这支笔真顺手，写字顺手，拿它签合同也顺手。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“顺手”指这支笔握感舒适、出墨流畅，写字时动作自然，不费力，使用体验很好。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '顺手' means the pen is easy and comfortable to use, both for writing and for holding when signing a contract.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“顺手”指签合同、办事情都特别顺利，借笔的便利延伸出事务推进顺畅的意味。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '顺手' also suggests that using this pen makes the contract-signing process go smoothly and favorably, extending from physical ease to things proceeding without obstacles.
context: 前一句说笔写字顺手，后一句转到“签合同也顺手”，把“顺手”从手感好并置到办事顺利。
literal_translation: This pen is really handy: writing with it is handy, and using it to sign contracts is handy too.
functional_equivalence_translation: This pen really works smoothly—smooth for writing, and smooth for closing a deal too.
explanatory_translation: This pen feels very easy to use for writing, and the speaker jokingly extends that to mean it also helps make signing a contract go smoothly.
interpretation_1: 笔用起来很顺畅、趁手，写字方便。
interpretation_2: 用这支笔签合同也会很顺利，事情容易办成。

surface_text: 张三和李四都是门卫，中午张三来值班，换李四吃饭。 张三突然说：你先等等，我要拉肚子！ 李四答：那你快去拉，拉完了我好去吃。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，李四的意思是等张三上完厕所后，自己就可以去吃饭了，其中“吃”按通常意义理解为进食。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'eat' simply means that Li Si is going to have his meal after the shift change, and he says Zhang San should hurry up so he can go eat.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，“拉完了我好去吃”把“吃”与前文“拉肚子”形成荒诞联想，像是在说去吃屎，借由语境触发了对“吃”的非常规理解。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'eat' shifts to colloquial slang meaning 'to suffer a beating' or 'take a hit,' creating a pun that suggests 'after you finish pooping, it'll be my turn to get beaten.'
context: 两人都是门卫，正在交接吃饭与值班；张三说“我要拉肚子”，李四故意把固定说法拆开，抓住“拉”的字面义来接话。
literal_translation: Zhang San and Li Si are both gatekeepers. At noon, Zhang San came to take the shift, so Li Si could go eat. Zhang San suddenly said, “Wait a moment, I’ve got diarrhea!” Li Si replied, “Then go do it quickly, and after you’re done I can go eat.”
functional_equivalence_translation: “Hold on, I’ve got the runs.” “Then go run and get it over with so I can eat.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese verb “拉.” In “拉肚子,” it means “to have diarrhea,” but Li Si intentionally isolates “拉” and interprets it literally as “to poop,” creating the pun.
interpretation_1: “拉肚子”表示腹泻、要上厕所。
interpretation_2: 李四把“拉肚子”中的“拉”单独按“排便”来理解，并顺着这个义项回应。

surface_text: 陪女友去商场买衣服，女友喜欢上了一件外套， 翻开标签一看要6888元。 女友也特别懂事，知道我赚钱不容易， 转身对我说：“既然这么跪，我就不买了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层字面上说的是“这么跪”，其中“跪”本义是下跪、跪下。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she says, "Since it's so worth kneeling for, I won't buy it," using "kneeling" literally as if the item is so impressive or overwhelming that one would kneel.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里实际借“跪”与“贵”同音形成双关，想表达的是衣服价格太贵了，所以决定不买。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "跪" is a playful substitution for "贵" (expensive). She really means, "Since it's so expensive, I won't buy it."
context: 女友看上一件外套，看到标签价6888元后，对男友说“既然这么跪，我就不买了”。
negative_example: 既然这么鬼，我就不买了
literal_translation: I accompanied my girlfriend to the mall to buy clothes. She liked a coat, but when she checked the tag, it was 6,888 yuan. She was very considerate and knew it wasn’t easy for me to make money, so she turned to me and said, “Since it’s so kneeling, I won’t buy it.”
functional_equivalence_translation: My girlfriend saw a coat she liked, but when she checked the price tag—6,888 yuan—she said, “If it’s that steep, forget it.”
explanatory_translation: My girlfriend saw a coat she liked, but the price tag said 6,888 yuan. She then joked, “Since it’s so ‘gui/kneeling,’ I won’t buy it,” where “跪” (kneel) is used as a same-sounding substitute for “贵” (expensive) to mean “so expensive it makes you want to kneel.”
interpretation_1: 她表面上是在说这件衣服价格太贵了，所以不买。
interpretation_2: 她隐含地说价格高到让人要“跪”，即贵得夸张、令人崩溃。

surface_text: 朋友买了新耳机后说自己进入“勿听模式”，消息可以不回，情绪必须先降噪。
hidden_form: 勿扰模式 / 听歌降噪
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上像是一个“不去听外界声音”的设备模式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it sounds like a device mode for not listening to outside sounds.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“勿扰模式”，把社交隔离与耳机降噪、情绪自护联系起来。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it parodies 'Do Not Disturb' mode, linking social withdrawal with headphone noise cancellation and emotional self-protection.
context: 适用于耳机产品文案、年轻人情绪表达、社交媒体状态更新。
negative_example: 我开了勿扰模式，不想被打扰。
literal_translation: After buying new earphones, my friend said they had entered 'do-not-listen mode': messages can wait, but emotions need noise reduction first.
functional_equivalence_translation: With the new earbuds on, I'm in 'do-not-listen mode'—texts can wait, my mood needs noise-canceling first.
explanatory_translation: The pun modifies the familiar digital phrase 'Do Not Disturb mode' by replacing 'disturb' with 'listen', creating a hybrid expression about both noise cancellation and emotional retreat.
interpretation_1: 不听外界声音的状态
interpretation_2: 仿拟勿扰模式表达自我隔离

surface_text: 父子俩在森林里迷了路，爸爸带着儿子四处摸索，可是没找到一丝能出林的痕迹。突然儿子大叫:要是妈妈在就好了，她一定认识路！为什么？书上说了，老马识途！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上引用成语“老马识途”，意思是年老、有经验的马认识道路，能带人走出困境。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the son is citing the idiom 'an old horse knows the way' and literally thinks that if his mother were there, she would recognize the الطريق and help them out of the forest.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上把“马”借转为“妈妈”的“妈”，儿子因此认为如果妈妈在场就会认路，把成语中的“马”误解并替换成了“妈妈”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the son treats 'ma' in 'old horse' as sounding like 'Mom,' so he jokingly implies that Mom would know the way because 'ma knows the route.'
context: 父子在森林迷路，儿子提到妈妈会认路，并引用“老马识途”形成“老妈识途”的联想。
literal_translation: The father and son got lost in the forest. The father groped around with his son but could not find any trace of a way out. Suddenly the son shouted: It would be great if Mom were here; she would definitely know the way! Why? Because the book says: an old horse knows the road!
functional_equivalence_translation: A father and son got lost in the woods. The boy cried, “If only Mom were here—she’d know the way!” Why? “Because, you know, old mares know the way!”
explanatory_translation: A father and son are lost in the forest. The boy says Mom would know the way because of the idiom “老马识途” (“an old horse knows the road”), but he jokingly reinterprets “老马” (old horse) as “老妈” (mom), which is pronounced the same in Chinese.
interpretation_1: 表层意思是成语“老马识途”，指老马认得道路。
interpretation_2: 隐含意思是把“老马”谐想成“老妈”，儿子认为妈妈会认路带他们出去。

surface_text: 这位记者真敢问，问题敢问，真相也快被他问出来了。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“敢问”指记者提问直接、不回避敏感问题，具有专业勇气和追问意识。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the reporter dares to ask bold and direct questions, and by asking them he may soon uncover the truth.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“问出来”指通过连续发问逼近事实真相，暗示提问本身具有揭示真相的力量。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '敢问' echoes both 'daring to ask' and the formulaic polite phrase meaning 'may I ask,' creating a contrast between politeness and fearless, probing questioning.
context: 记者连续追问、问题尖锐，提问强度大到像审讯，因而“敢问”与“拷问”被并置激活。
literal_translation: This reporter really dares to ask. He dares to ask tough questions, and the truth is about to be asked out by him.
functional_equivalence_translation: This reporter really knows how to press for answers—his questions are so bold they’re practically an interrogation, and the truth is close to coming out.
explanatory_translation: The line plays on the force of 敢问, literally 'dare to ask,' suggesting not only bold questioning but also questioning so intense that it resembles an interrogation, which helps bring out the truth.
interpretation_1: 表层是指记者提问大胆，什么问题都敢问。
interpretation_2: 隐含是指他的追问力度很强，几乎像在拷问，从而逼近真相。

surface_text: 女儿问我：“爸爸，为什么叫公路，不叫母路啊？” 我想了半天回答说：“修公路是体力活，都是男人干的，所以只能叫公路！” 妻不悦，教育女儿说：“公路就是公共的意思，大家都能用的路。” 女儿若有所思，继续问她妈妈：“那老公就是大家都能公用的男人了吗？” 妻无语，我愕然！
interpretation_1_zh: 在“公路”里，“公”表示公共，指大家都可以使用的道路。
interpretation_1_en: In the surface reading, the child takes "公" in "公路" to mean "public," so a road is called that because it is for everyone to use, and then she extends that logic to ask whether "husband" would mean a man shared by everyone.
interpretation_2_zh: 女儿把“公”进一步理解成“公用”的意思，并套用到“老公”里，误解为大家都能共同使用的男人，从而形成双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from switching the sense of "公": in "老公" it is not the "public" meaning from "公路," but part of a fixed colloquial word meaning "husband." The joke is that the child wrongly transfers the meaning of the same character across different words, creating the absurd implication of a "public husband."
context: 围绕“公路”中“公”的含义进行解释后，孩子把同一个“公”机械套用到“老公”中，造成语义错配。
negative_example: 老公就是年纪大的公的男人吗
literal_translation: My daughter asked me, “Dad, why is it called a ‘gong road’ and not a ‘mu road’?” I thought for a long time and answered, “Building roads is physical work done by men, so it can only be called ‘gong road’!” My wife, displeased, corrected her: “‘Gong road’ means a public road, a road everyone can use.” My daughter thought for a moment and then asked her mother, “Then does ‘laogong’ mean a man that everyone can use publicly?” My wife was speechless, and I was stunned.
functional_equivalence_translation: My daughter asked, “Why is it called a public road?” After my wife explained that “public” means everyone can use it, my daughter asked, “Then does ‘husband’ mean a public man everyone can share?”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese character “公.” In “公路” it means “public,” but in “老公” it is simply part of the fixed word meaning “husband.” The child wrongly extends the “public” meaning from “public road” to “husband,” creating the absurd reading “a man for public use.”
interpretation_1: 在“公路”里，“公”表示公共、大家都可使用。
interpretation_2: 在“老公”里，孩子把“公”误解并套用为“公共的”，从而推出“大家都能公用的男人”。

surface_text: 早上起床，打开手机一看：大雪。 于是就把自己包的严严实实的去上班了。 一路上发现艳阳高照的，不太对劲啊。 再打开手机仔细一看：擦，原来是24节气的大雪。
两岁的锐锐兴冲冲地跑到爸爸面前，抬起脚奶声奶气地说：“爸爸你看，妈妈给我买的新皮鞋。” 爸爸说：“真漂亮，还是羊皮的呢！” 锐锐不高兴了：“不是羊皮的，是锐锐的。”
公孙策：“我刚认识包大人时，他还是一位白皙男子。”。 展昭吃惊：“何以变成现在这样？” 公孙策：“因为包大人为官清廉， 得罪了不少朝中奸臣，他们齐心协力在万岁面前搬弄是非。” “原来如此。”展昭若有所悟，“包大人之所以不复白嫩， 就是因为黑他的人太多了。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“黑”理解为颜色变黑，意思是包大人不再白嫩，好像是因为“黑他的人太多了”，于是变得越来越黑。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "too many people blackened him" means Bao Zheng became dark-skinned, so he was no longer fair and pale.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义中“黑”是指诬陷、抹黑、说坏话，意思是朝中奸臣不断在皇上面前搬弄是非、污蔑包大人。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that many people maliciously smeared and slandered Bao Zheng behind his back, since "black" also means to vilify or frame someone.
context: 包大人原本白皙，后来因清廉得罪奸臣，许多人在皇帝面前搬弄是非，因此引出“黑他的人太多了”的双关。
negative_example: 包大人之所以不复白嫩，就是因为晒太阳太多了。
literal_translation: The reason Lord Bao is no longer fair and tender is that there are too many people blackening him.
functional_equivalence_translation: Lord Bao isn’t fair anymore because too many people have been blackening his name.
explanatory_translation: Lord Bao is no longer fair-skinned because too many people have been “blackening” him: on the surface this suggests making him black, but it really means smearing his reputation.
interpretation_1: 表层义是肤色变黑、不再白皙。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是被很多人诬陷、中伤，即“被黑”。

surface_text: 我去医院看病，来到妇科，悄悄地大夫跟说：“我问一个难以启齿的问题。” 医生马上说：“你问错了医生，应该去牙科。”
interpretation_1_zh: “难以启齿”在表层义上是指问题过于私密或尴尬，不好意思说出口。
interpretation_1_en: The phrase means 'hard to say' or 'too embarrassing to speak out loud,' so the patient is saying they have a very awkward question to ask the gynecologist.
interpretation_2_zh: 医生把“启齿”按字面理解成“张嘴露齿、和牙齿有关”，因此故意曲解为牙科范围，形成笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The doctor deliberately interprets the phrase literally as 'difficult to open one's mouth / involving the teeth,' and jokes that such a question should be asked in the dentistry department instead.
context: 在妇科就诊时，病人说自己要问一个“难以启齿的问题”，医生故意把成语按字面拆解理解，因此说应该去牙科。
literal_translation: I went to the hospital and came to gynecology. Quietly I said to the doctor, “I want to ask a question that is hard to mention.” The doctor immediately said, “You asked the wrong doctor. You should go to dentistry.”
functional_equivalence_translation: At the gynecology clinic, I whispered, “I have an embarrassing question.” The doctor replied, “Wrong department—you want dentistry, since you can’t open your mouth.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese idiom “难以启齿,” which normally means “too embarrassing to say,” but the doctor deliberately interprets “启齿” literally as “open/show one’s teeth,” so he jokingly redirects the speaker to the dental department.
interpretation_1: 本义是某个问题羞于开口，说不出来。
interpretation_2: 被医生按字面理解为“张开牙齿/开口露齿”的动作，因而联想到牙科。

surface_text: 话说现在很多人都把“子”说成“纸”， 一女同学经常这样卖萌，于是有一天， 该女感冒后在图书馆看书，纸巾用完了，发短信给室友， 说：“过来的时候带两包纸。” 不一会儿室友过来了，手里拿着两个包子。。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上她想让室友带两包纸，用来擦鼻涕，实际所指是两包纸巾。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she meant: 'Bring two packs of tissues' when you come over.
interpretation_2_zh: 由于她平时把“子”说成“纸”，“两包纸”会被误听成“两包子”，于是室友理解成带两个包子过来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from pronouncing 'zi' like 'zhi': her message sounded like 'bring two bao-zi,' so her roommate misunderstood it as two steamed buns.
context: 女生平时爱把“子”发成“纸”；感冒后在图书馆发短信说“带两包纸”，室友按其习惯把“纸”还原为“子”，理解成“带两个包子”
literal_translation: Nowadays many people pronounce “zi” as “zhi.” A girl often acted cute like this. One day, after catching a cold, she was reading in the library and ran out of tissues, so she texted her roommate: “Bring two packs of paper when you come.” Soon the roommate arrived holding two steamed buns.
functional_equivalence_translation: She often pronounced “tissue” in a cutesy, unclear way. So when she texted, “Bring me two packs,” her roommate showed up with two buns instead of tissues.
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the girl’s habitual mispronunciation: she says the sound for “zi” like “zhi.” So when she texts “bring two packs of zhi,” she means “paper tissues,” but her roommate interprets it as “baozi” (steamed buns) instead of “paper.”
interpretation_1: 指纸巾、卫生纸一类的“纸”
interpretation_2: 因说话者常把“子”说成“纸”，被室友误听为量词结构里的“子”，从而理解成“包子”

surface_text: 我问上六年级的女儿有什么打算，她说目标是考上重点中学市一中。当时恰巧两岁半的小外甥也在，我便问：“城城，长大了考什么？” “我要烤鸡腿。”他毫不犹豫地回答。
