interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，小外甥把“考什么”理解成了“烤什么”，所以回答自己要烤鸡腿，表现出儿童按熟悉词义作答的效果。
interpretation_1_en: The child literally says that when he grows up, he wants to roast chicken legs.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，原本语境中的“考什么”是问长大后想考哪类学校或取得什么升学目标，与姐姐说的“考上市一中”相呼应。
interpretation_2_en: The joke is that he mishears the question about what school/exam to aim for as asking what he wants to 'kao' (roast), shifting from 考 'to take/aim for an exam' to 烤 'to roast'.
context: 先谈论姐姐长大后“考”重点中学，再问年幼外甥“长大了考什么”，儿童将“考”听解为“烤”，回答“烤鸡腿”
literal_translation: I asked my sixth-grade daughter about her plans, and she said her goal was to test into the key middle school No. 1 Middle School. My two-and-a-half-year-old nephew happened to be there, so I asked, “Chengcheng, what will you take when you grow up?” “I want to roast chicken legs,” he answered without hesitation.
functional_equivalence_translation: After my daughter said she wanted to pass the exam for a top middle school, I asked my little nephew, “What will you aim for when you grow up?” He replied, “Grilled drumsticks.”
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on the Chinese syllable “kao”: the adult means 考, “to take an exam,” but the child interprets it as the homophone 烤, “to roast,” so “what will you kao?” becomes “I want roasted chicken legs.”
interpretation_1: 指参加考试、考取学校
interpretation_2: 指把食物烤熟，构成“烤鸡腿”

surface_text: 前台请王总和李总的秘书先进去。
老师：同学们谁知道世界上最冷的国家？ 小强：我知道！ 老师：哪国？ 小强：韩国！ 老师：……怎么会是韩国呢？ 小强：啊……不是这个“寒”呀。
interpretation_1_zh: 老师问的是气候意义上最冷、最寒冷的国家，小强先按字面把“寒”理解成了“韩国”的“韩”，于是回答“韩国”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the student misunderstands the question about the coldest country in the world and answers South Korea because its Chinese name contains the character "Han," which he takes as meaning "cold."
interpretation_2_zh: 双关点在“寒”与“韩”同音，实际隐藏激活的是“韩”这个字，因此“小强”的回答来自谐音联想，而不是对“寒冷”含义的正常理解。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the country name "Korea" uses the character "韩," which is pronounced the same as "寒" meaning "cold," so the joke relies on a sound-based semantic shift between the two characters.
context: 老师提问“世界上最冷的国家是哪国”，学生把专名“韩国”与“寒国”同音替换来作答。
literal_translation: Teacher: Students, who knows the coldest country in the world? Xiaoqiang: I know! Teacher: Which country? Xiaoqiang: Korea! Teacher: ...How could it be Korea? Xiaoqiang: Ah... so it’s not this ‘han (cold)’.
functional_equivalence_translation: Teacher: What’s the coldest country in the world? Student: I know—Brr-tain! Teacher: ...What? Student: Oh, you didn’t mean a country with a cold-sounding name.
explanatory_translation: Teacher: Which is the coldest country in the world? Student: Korea. The joke is that in Chinese, “Han” in “South Korea” sounds the same as “han,” meaning “cold,” so the student misinterprets the question as asking for a country whose name sounds like “cold country.”
interpretation_1: 国家名“韩国”。
interpretation_2: 把“韩”听成“寒”，理解为“很寒冷的国家”。

surface_text: 这位摄影师真会定格，风景能定格，人的青春也像被他定格了。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“定格”指摄影师通过拍摄把风景瞬间固定成画面，保存特定时刻的景象。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the photographer is good at freezing images, capturing scenery and people in a still frame.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“定格”指他拍出的照片让人物青春状态仿佛被永远留住，充满纪念意味。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it also means he seems able to preserve people's youth, as if making their youthful state stay unchanged.
context: 摄影师拍风景，也拍人物；前一句是摄影技术意义上的“定格”，后一句转为对人物青春状态被留住的赞美。
literal_translation: This photographer is really good at freezing frames: scenery can be frozen in frame, and people’s youth also seems to have been frozen by him.
functional_equivalence_translation: This photographer really knows how to capture a moment—he can freeze the scenery, and even make a person’s youth seem frozen in time.
explanatory_translation: This photographer is great at “freezing” moments: literally he freezes scenes in photos, and figuratively he seems to preserve people’s youth as if time had stopped.
interpretation_1: 摄影中把画面瞬间固定下来。
interpretation_2: 比喻摄影师把人的青春之感留住了，仿佛时间停止。

surface_text: 高中的时候，第一次上劳动课， 老师是个老头，自我介绍说：“我叫吴树山。” 我突然来了灵感，马上接道：“西北望长安，可怜无数山。” 全班爆笑，老师面色铁青，随后我被干重活。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层直接引用诗句“西北望长安，可怜无数山”，意思是向西北遥望长安，只见许多山峰，令人感慨。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "无数山" means "countless mountains," quoting a classical poetic line about looking northwest toward Chang'an and seeing many mountains.
interpretation_2_zh: “无数山”与老师名字“吴树山”近音，接这句实际上是在借诗句影射、调侃老师的姓名，所以引发全班发笑。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a sound-based pun: "无数山" echoes the teacher's name "吴树山," so the speaker is jokingly turning the teacher's self-introduction into a poetic line.
context: 老师自我介绍姓名为“吴树山”后，学生立即接出“可怜无数山”。
literal_translation: In high school, during my first labor class, the teacher was an old man. He introduced himself: “My name is Wu Shushan.” I suddenly got inspired and immediately replied, “Looking northwest toward Chang’an, alas, countless mountains.” The whole class burst into laughter, the teacher’s face turned livid, and then I was assigned heavy work.
functional_equivalence_translation: When I was in high school, on the first labor-skills class, the old teacher said, “My name is Wu Shushan.” I instantly quipped with a line sounding like his name: “Alas, countless mountains!” The class cracked up, the teacher went stone-faced, and I got stuck with the heavy chores.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on a near-homophonic pun in Chinese: the quoted phrase “无数山” (wú shù shān, “countless mountains”) sounds close to the teacher’s name “吴树山” (Wú Shùshān). By echoing a poetic line right after the introduction, the speaker turns the teacher’s name into a teasing literary pun.
interpretation_1: 引用诗句中“可怜无数山”，字面意思是有许多山。
interpretation_2: 借“无数山”的读音影射老师名字“吴树山”，形成当面拿名字开玩笑的效果。

surface_text: 两男生出校看病，他们俩是同桌，关系较好，一起回来时。 进校门的时候守门的大爷就亲切的问了句：“你们搞基的啊？” 学生甲小脸儿憋屈，说了句：“大爷，我喜欢的是女的。” 学生乙说：“人家是问我们是高几的。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“大爷”实际想问的是他们读高中几年级，也就是“你们是高几的”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the gatekeeper is asking what grade they are in at school—specifically, which senior high year they belong to.
interpretation_2_zh: 由于“高几的”与“搞基的”近音，先被误听成在问他们是不是男同性恋关系，因此引发了歧义和笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that his words sound like he is asking whether they are gay or in a romantic relationship with each other.
context: 两名男生一起回学校，门卫问“你们搞基的啊”，语音上可被听成“你们高几的啊”。
literal_translation: The guard asked, “Are you guys gay?”
functional_equivalence_translation: The guard asked, “You two together? I meant what grade you’re in.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the similar sound between “搞基” (a slang term suggesting a gay relationship between men) and “高几” (which asks what grade in high school someone is in). The guard meant the latter, but the student misunderstood it as the former.
interpretation_1: 门卫是在问他们读高中几年级。
interpretation_2: 学生甲误以为门卫在问他们是不是男同性恋。

surface_text: 甲同学：“你知道雨果吗？” 乙同学：“不知道。” 甲同学：“你连雨果都不知道，白读一回书了！” 乙同学：“对不起，我从来没吃过，是哪里出产的？”
阿婆：每次车子靠站时，在司机上方的显示板就会显示车停站一下，所以我在每次车子靠站时就要站一下啊！小明：拜托！阿婆是下一站停车，不是车停站一下。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“车停站一下”理解为车子每次靠站都会停一下，因此阿婆认为自己每到一站就要跟着站起来一下。
interpretation_1_en: The old woman takes the sign literally as saying 'the car stops at the station for a moment,' so she thinks she should stand up for a moment every time the bus pulls in.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的原意是“下一站停车”，意思是车辆将在下一站停靠，并不是要求乘客每次车停时都站一下。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is 'Next stop: parking/stopping at the station,' referring to the upcoming stop announcement, not an instruction that the vehicle is stopping only briefly or that she should stand up.
context: 公交车到站前，显示板提示“下一站停车”，阿婆把其中的“站”从站点误解为站立动作。
literal_translation: Grandma: Every time the bus approaches a stop, the display above the driver shows that the bus stops and I should stand for a moment, so I have to stand up every time the bus approaches a stop! Xiaoming: Come on! It means the bus will stop at the next stop, not that you should stand for a moment when the bus stops.
functional_equivalence_translation: Grandma: Whenever the bus nears a stop, the sign seems to say, "next stop, stand up," so I stand up every time! Xiaoming: No, it means "the bus stops at the next stop," not "you stand up at the next stop."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese character "站". In "下一站停车," it means "stop/station" in "next stop," but Grandma misreads it as the verb "to stand," so she thinks the message tells passengers to stand up when the bus stops.
interpretation_1: 提示广播的正常意思是下一站将停车。
interpretation_2: 阿婆误解为车一停站，乘客就要站起来一下。

surface_text: 这杯奶茶的甜度很会做人，喝完只剩“情绪糖定”，没有负罪感。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是奶茶里的糖分让人情绪被安抚下来，获得甜食带来的安定感。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the sugar in the milk tea soothes your mood and gives emotional comfort.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含改造“情绪稳定”，把“稳”换成与甜饮相关的“糖”，形成消费化表达。
interpretation_2_en: It remodels the phrase 'emotionally stable' by replacing part of it with 'sugar,' turning mood regulation into a drink-related pun.
context: 适用于奶茶文案、甜品推荐和情绪消费场景。
negative_example: 这杯奶茶让我情绪稳定了。
literal_translation: The sweetness of this milk tea is socially skilled; after drinking it, only 'emotion sugar-stability' remains, with no guilt.
functional_equivalence_translation: This milk tea delivers sugar-powered emotional stability without the guilt.
explanatory_translation: The pun alters the common phrase '情绪稳定' by inserting '糖' (sugar), linking emotional comfort directly to the sweetness of milk tea.
interpretation_1: 糖分安抚情绪
interpretation_2: 仿情绪稳定

surface_text: 小丽上班时间在吃八宝粥， 经理看见后生气地批评说：“太闲了是不是？” 小丽回答说“：不，一点儿也不咸，这是甜的。”
interpretation_1_zh: 小丽把经理说的“闲”听成了食物味道上的“咸”，回答八宝粥一点也不咸，是甜的。
interpretation_1_en: Lili takes the manager’s words as if he were asking whether the porridge is salty, so she replies that it is not salty at all but sweet.
interpretation_2_zh: 经理原本是在批评她上班时偷懒太闲，并不是在评价八宝粥的味道。
interpretation_2_en: What the manager actually means is that she seems too idle or free during work hours, not that the porridge tastes salty.
context: 上班时间吃八宝粥，经理说“太闲了是不是”，小丽利用“闲/咸”同音故意曲解批评。
literal_translation: Xiaoli was eating eight-treasure porridge during work hours. The manager saw it and angrily criticized her: “Are you too idle?” Xiaoli replied: “No, not salty at all. This is sweet.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Xiaoli was eating porridge at work. Her manager snapped, “Got nothing better to do?” She replied, “Nope, nothing bitter about it—it’s sweet.”
explanatory_translation: Xiaoli was eating sweet porridge during work. When the manager said, “Are you too idle?”, she deliberately interpreted “idle” as the homophone “salty,” joking that the porridge was not salty but sweet.
interpretation_1: 经理批评她上班吃东西，意思是太清闲、没事干了。
interpretation_2: 小丽故意把“闲”听成“咸”，理解为粥的味道是否太咸。

surface_text: 家有小屁孩，特皮，特烦。 我忍无可忍，大喝一声：“滚！” “我又不是轮胎，你叫我怎么滚呀。”
interpretation_1_zh: 大人说“滚”，表层是在呵斥孩子离开，意思是让他赶紧走开、别在眼前烦人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "roll" is taken literally: the child says he is not a tire, so he cannot physically roll.
interpretation_2_zh: 孩子把“滚”理解成物体在地上翻转前进的“滚动”，于是说自己不是轮胎，没法那样滚。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "滚" is actually a colloquial command meaning "go away" or "get lost," not a real instruction to roll like a wheel.
context: 家长被调皮孩子惹烦后呵斥“滚”，孩子故意按“滚动”的字面义理解，并提到轮胎。
literal_translation: There is a naughty little kid at home, very mischievous and very annoying. I couldn't bear it anymore and shouted, "Get lost!" "I'm not a tire. How do you expect me to roll?"
functional_equivalence_translation: My naughty kid was driving me crazy, so I yelled, "Beat it!" He replied, "I'm not a drum—how am I supposed to beat it?"
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “滚,” which usually means “go away/get lost” in this context, but the child deliberately interprets it literally as “to roll,” then jokes that he is not a tire so he cannot roll.
interpretation_1: 说话人用“滚”表示叫对方赶紧离开。
interpretation_2: 小孩把“滚”理解成物体在地上翻滚、滚动。

surface_text: 一四岁男孩和一三岁女孩接吻，女孩问男孩：你会对我负责吗？ 男孩严肃地说，别开玩笑，我们都不是一两岁的人了。
这家奶茶店推出“续命冰”，海报上写着：不是药，但下午三点喝了像把电量接回来。
hidden_form: 续命 / 冰饮 / 续命水
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是冰饮产品名，强调冰爽提神。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it is the name of an iced drink, emphasizing coolness and refreshment.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义沿用网络里“靠某物续命”的夸张说法，表示它像恢复体力和精神。
interpretation_2_en: It also follows the internet expression of 'surviving thanks to something,' exaggerating its restorative effect.
context: 适用于饮品命名、外卖平台文案、下午茶推广。
literal_translation: This milk tea shop launched 'life-extending ice'; the poster says: it is not medicine, but at 3 p.m. it feels like plugging your battery back in.
functional_equivalence_translation: An iced drink that basically brings you back to life.
explanatory_translation: The pun turns the slang 'life-saving' into a product name for an iced drink, combining literal cold refreshment with the figurative idea of restoring energy.
interpretation_1: 提神冰饮
interpretation_2: 靠饮品续命

surface_text: 你的猫眼很漂亮。
刚看到新闻，说郭美美家暴富是由于炒股，说几个月内从几万炒到几百万。网民开始研究，郭家炒的是那只股呢？结果一致认为是最牛B的股：屁股。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是在讨论郭家靠炒股暴富，追问炒的是哪只股，字面义中的“股”指股票。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the joke talks about stock trading: people are wondering which stock Guo's family bought that let them turn tens of thousands into millions.
interpretation_2_zh: 双关把“最牛B的股”转到“屁股”上，暗指并非靠正常炒股票赚钱，而是借“屁股”影射通过出卖色相、性交易等方式获利。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'gu' shifts from 'stock' in the word for shares to 'butt' in 'pigu' (buttocks), implying they got rich through selling sex or exploiting the body rather than through real stock speculation.
context: 先出现“炒股”“那只股”，把“股”引向股票语境，随后用“最牛B的股：屁股”改写其所指。
literal_translation: I just saw news saying Guo Meimei’s family got rich because of stock trading, going from tens of thousands to millions within months. Netizens began to study which stock the Guo family traded. The conclusion was unanimous: the most awesome gu was butt.
functional_equivalence_translation: People wondered what stock made Guo Meimei’s family rich. The answer, jokingly, wasn’t a stock pick at all—it was her backside.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “gu.” In context it first means “stock/share” in “trading stocks,” but the punchline shifts it to “pi gu” (“buttocks”), creating a crude sexual insinuation.
interpretation_1: 表层先按“股票”的“股”理解，指在问炒的是哪只股票。
interpretation_2: 后文把“最牛B的股”转到“屁股”，暗指所谓暴富并非靠炒股而是靠身体/性暗示获利。

surface_text: MIKE开了家起名公司，据说由他起名的公司都发达了，一时间名声大噪，生意到也兴隆。有家皮蛋厂皮蛋销路不好，厂长就找上门。要MIKE为他们的皮蛋起个好名字。 MIKE想了想，说道：现在市面上流行的无非是王字和霸字，比如画王，花王，视王，彩坝还有什么面霸的，对了！MIKE一拍大腿叫到：不如你们的皮蛋就叫王霸蛋吧！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把皮蛋取名为“王霸蛋”，借“王”“霸”这类流行字眼包装产品，想表达这是很厉害、很有派头的招牌皮蛋。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "王霸蛋" is presented as a trendy brand name for preserved eggs, using popular naming elements like "king" and "boss/champion" to make the product sound powerful and marketable.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“王霸蛋”近似“王八蛋”，会让人联想到骂人的俗语，形成不雅、贬义的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "王霸蛋" sounds very close to "王八蛋," a common Chinese insult meaning "bastard" or "jerk," so the proposed brand name is actually offensive and ridiculous.
context: 起名公司老板给皮蛋厂起名，前文强调市场上流行带“王”“霸”字样的强势品牌名，因此提出“王霸蛋”。
literal_translation: Mike opened a naming company. He suggested calling the preserved eggs “King-Dominance Eggs.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Mike named the preserved eggs “Badass Eggs,” making it sound powerful while hinting at an insult.
explanatory_translation: Mike suggests naming the preserved eggs “王霸蛋,” which sounds close to “王八蛋,” a common Chinese insult, while also using the trendy branding words “king” and “dominate” to make the product sound powerful.
interpretation_1: 作为产品名，可理解为带“王”“霸”风格、显得强势畅销的皮蛋名称。
interpretation_2: 谐指“王八蛋”，是汉语中常见的骂人话，也可字面联想到“王八的蛋”。

surface_text: 他真把琴搬到牛棚里练，大家笑他这是在对牛弹琴。
搬家那天我彻底进入“箱由人生”，每打开一个纸箱，都像在抽取前任生活副本。
hidden_form: 享有人生 / 箱子构成的生活
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是搬家时整个人被纸箱包围，生活仿佛被箱子接管。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means moving day is completely dominated by boxes.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义仿照“享有人生”一类表达，反讽搬家并不享受，而是被杂物和回忆占满。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it parodies expressions like 'enjoying life,' ironically suggesting that moving is not enjoyment but being overwhelmed by stuff and memories.
context: 适用于搬家日记、生活记录、社交媒体吐槽。
negative_example: 搬家那天到处都是纸箱。
literal_translation: On moving day I fully entered 'box-ruled life'; every time I opened a carton, it felt like drawing a side copy of a former life.
functional_equivalence_translation: Moving day turned my life into an all-box edition.
explanatory_translation: The pun parodies a positive life-expression by replacing the key morpheme with 'box,' creating a hybrid phrase that literally fits moving day while ironically commenting on life being taken over by packed belongings.
interpretation_1: 生活被纸箱占满
interpretation_2: 反讽所谓享受生活

surface_text: 老师：菲利，你们班上有一些同学有一句口头禅，你知道是什么吗？ 菲利：不知道。 老师：说得对！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，老师问班上同学的口头禅是什么，菲利回答“不知道”，老师接着评价“说得对”，意思是他回答正确，因为那句口头禅正是“不知道”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "I don't know" is Fili's literal answer to the teacher's question, saying he does not know what the classmates' catchphrase is.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，“说得对”既是在肯定菲利的回答，也是在揭示班上一些同学常挂在嘴边的话就是“不知道”，形成把回答内容和答案本身重合的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "I don't know" itself is the classmates' habitual catchphrase, so the teacher says Fili is correct because he accidentally said the very phrase in question.
context: 老师问班上同学常说的口头禅是什么，学生回答“不知道”，老师回应“说得对”，既像评价答案，也揭示口头禅内容是“对”。
literal_translation: Teacher: Phil, some students in your class have a catchphrase. Do you know what it is? Phil: I don't know. Teacher: That's right!
functional_equivalence_translation: Teacher: Phil, some classmates have a favorite phrase. Do you know what it is? Phil: I don't know. Teacher: Exactly.
explanatory_translation: The teacher’s reply “That’s right/Exactly” works as a pun: it sounds like praise for Phil’s answer, but it also reveals that the classmates’ catchphrase is “right/exactly.”
interpretation_1: 老师表面上是在评价菲利的回答是正确的。
interpretation_2: 老师实际上借“说得对”点出口头禅是“对”。

surface_text: 小朋友：比小溪大的是什么？小朋友：河小朋友：比河大的是什么？小朋友：海小朋友：比海大的是什么？小朋友：洋小朋友：那比洋大的呢？小朋友：牛
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上前面按水域大小依次回答“小溪—河—海—洋”，问到“比洋大的呢”时，小朋友答“牛”，形成超出常识的跳转笑点。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child is answering a size-ranking question: stream < river < sea < ocean, and then gives 'cow' as the answer to something bigger than 'ocean.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上把“洋”谐转为“羊”，于是问题被理解成“比羊大的是什么”，回答“牛”就顺着动物体型比较成立。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a sound-based pun: '洋' (ocean) shifts to the common phrase '牛' (awesome, impressive), so the last answer is funny because it jumps from geographic scale to slang praise.
context: 按“小溪→河→海→洋”的递进问答，最后一句突然从水域名词切换到同音动物词理解。
literal_translation: Child: What is bigger than a brook? Child: A river. Child: What is bigger than a river? Child: The sea. Child: What is bigger than the sea? Child: The ocean. Child: Then what is bigger than the ocean? Child: A cow.
functional_equivalence_translation: Kid: What's bigger than a stream? A river. Bigger than a river? The sea. Bigger than the sea? The ocean. Bigger than the ocean? A sheep—no, a cow!
explanatory_translation: The pun is on Chinese “yang”: 洋 means “ocean,” but it sounds the same as 羊, “sheep.” So the last question is misheard from “What is bigger than the ocean?” to “What is bigger than a sheep?”, leading to the answer “a cow.”
interpretation_1: 按水域大小序列，“洋”指海洋，比海更大的水域单位。
interpretation_2: 在“比洋大的呢”中把“洋”转听为“羊”，于是回答“牛”，利用生肖/动物体型联想造成跳转。

surface_text: 有几个人在谈论苏东坡。 小王说：“我喜爱东坡的诗。” 老李说：“我喜爱东坡的赋。” 这时来了老李的媳妇，说：“我也喜爱。” 老李听了说：“她最爱东坡肉！”
interpretation_1_zh: 前文中“东坡”都指苏东坡这个人，大家分别说喜欢他的诗和赋，老李媳妇说“我也喜爱”表面上也像是在说喜欢苏东坡。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'Dongpo' refers to Su Dongpo, and the speakers are saying they like his literary works such as his poems and prose.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里借“东坡”的名称发生语义转移，老李说她“最爱东坡肉”，实际是把“东坡”从诗人苏东坡转到以他命名的菜肴“东坡肉”，形成幽默双关。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, when Lao Li says his wife likes 'Dongpo' most, he means not Su Dongpo the writer, but Dongpo pork, the famous dish associated with Su Dongpo.
context: 多人谈论苏东坡及其诗赋，老李媳妇说“我也喜爱”，被老李解释为“她最爱东坡肉”。
literal_translation: Several people were talking about Su Dongpo. Xiao Wang said, “I love Dongpo’s poems.” Old Li said, “I love Dongpo’s fu.” Then Old Li’s wife came and said, “I like him too.” Old Li said, “She likes Dongpo pork the most!”
functional_equivalence_translation: They were discussing Su Dongpo. One said he loved Dongpo’s poetry, another his prose. Then Li’s wife chimed in, “I like Dongpo too.” Li laughed, “Sure—you mean Dongpo pork!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “Dongpo”: at first it refers to Su Dongpo, the famous writer, but in the wife’s case it is reinterpreted as “Dongpo pork,” a dish associated with his name.
interpretation_1: 前文中“东坡”指苏东坡，其诗和赋。
interpretation_2: 后文中“爱东坡”被转成“爱吃东坡肉”。

surface_text: 大学选修JAVA，老师普通话带口音，说：“我们的内裤，是不用自己洗的，要用的时候，就用别人洗好的。”（我们的类库，是不用自己写的，要用的时候，就用别人写好的）
interpretation_1_zh: 表层字面上把“类库”说成了“内裤”，意思变成“内裤不用自己洗，要用时拿别人洗好的”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the teacher seems to say, "Our underwear doesn't need to be washed by ourselves; when we need it, we can just use underwear that others have already washed."
interpretation_2_zh: 实际想表达的是编程中的“类库”不必自己编写，需要时可以直接使用别人已经写好的代码库。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is actually, "Our class library/code library doesn't need to be written by ourselves; when we need it, we can use code that others have already written."
context: 大学 JAVA 选修课上，老师讲解编程中的类库，但因普通话口音把“类库”说成了“内裤”。
literal_translation: In a university JAVA elective, the teacher spoke Mandarin with an accent and said: “Our underwear doesn’t need to be washed by ourselves; when we need it, we just use the ones others have washed.”
functional_equivalence_translation: In a university Java class, the teacher’s accent made him say, “Our underwear doesn’t need to be washed by ourselves,” when he actually meant, “Our class libraries don’t need to be written by ourselves.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the teacher’s accent: he says “underwear” (neiku), but means “class library” (leiku). In the programming context, he is explaining that programmers can reuse libraries written by others rather than writing everything from scratch.
interpretation_1: 老师表面上说的是贴身衣物内裤，不用自己洗，可以用别人洗好的。
interpretation_2: 实际想说的是编程中的类库，不用自己写，需要时直接使用别人写好的库。

surface_text: 儿子在邻居赵伯伯家玩，正巧赵伯伯的收音机坏了，赵伯伯对儿子说：你不是总说你妈是高级修理师吗，干脆你拿回去让你妈给修修。儿子笑道：这东西太小了，我妈只修大件。那就是修洗衣机电冰箱啦？也不是，我妈只修理我爸，或者我。赵伯伯听了笑道：这么个修理师呀。儿子点点头说：我妈修理得特好，技术很高，一般修理完都不会让人看出来。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指像修收音机、洗衣机、电冰箱那样，把坏掉的器物修好。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "repair" means fixing broken appliances or machines, such as a radio, washing machine, or refrigerator.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是指母亲对父亲或孩子进行责骂、管教、收拾，并不是维修电器，而是拿人开玩笑地说成“修理”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "repair" refers humorously to disciplining or dealing with her husband or child, meaning she gives them a hard time or sets them straight rather than fixing objects.
context: 母亲被说成“高级修理师”，但她“只修理我爸，或者我”，说明“修理”从修东西转为修人，即管教人。
literal_translation: My son said: this thing is too small; my mom only repairs big items. Not washing machines or refrigerators either—she only repairs my dad, or me.
functional_equivalence_translation: My mom isn’t that kind of repair expert—she only 'works on' my dad and me.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word 'xiuli' ('repair'). On the surface it means fixing appliances, but here it shifts to mean disciplining or 'sorting out' family members, so the mother is jokingly called a 'senior repair technician.'
interpretation_1: 按通常意思指维修机器、电器等物品。
interpretation_2: 在家庭语境中指母亲对父亲或孩子进行管教、收拾。

surface_text: 小外甥女和姥姥去吃Kfc，姥姥问：想吃啥？ 外甥女答：奥尔良鸡腿堡。 姥姥大声对服务员说：来二两鸡腿堡…
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，姥姥把点汉堡说成了按重量计量的说法，像是在买熟食或肉类一样，要“二两鸡腿堡”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the grandma mishears or reuses the phrase 'er liang' as a quantity expression meaning 'two liang' (a traditional unit of weight), so she loudly orders 'two liang of chicken-leg burger' as if it were food sold by weight.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是姥姥本来想表达“两个鸡腿堡”，但把表示数量的“两个”误说成了表示重量的“二两”，形成了语义错位的双关效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that in a fast-food restaurant like KFC, the intended item is simply an 'Orleans chicken-leg burger,' not something measured in liang. The joke comes from shifting the sound into the familiar marketplace expression 'er liang' used when buying food by weight.
context: 在KFC点餐时，老人因听觉或认知偏差把商品名“奥尔良鸡腿堡”误解为“二两鸡腿堡”。
literal_translation: My little niece and her grandma went to KFC. Grandma asked, “What do you want to eat?” The niece answered, “an Orleans chicken burger.” Grandma loudly said to the clerk, “Two liang of chicken burger...”
functional_equivalence_translation: My little niece and her grandma went to KFC. “What do you want?” Grandma asked. “An Orleans chicken burger,” said the niece. Grandma then shouted to the cashier, “One two-pound chicken burger...”
explanatory_translation: A girl asks for an “Orleans chicken burger,” but her grandma mishears “Orleans” as “two liang,” a traditional Chinese weight unit, and orders it that way. The joke comes from the similar sounds and the mismatch between a menu item name and a weight-based order.
interpretation_1: 外甥女想点的是“奥尔良鸡腿堡”，即肯德基的一种汉堡口味。
interpretation_2: 姥姥把“奥尔良”听成了“二两”，用传统称重说法来点餐，造成误解和笑点。

surface_text: 健身房最近流行一句话：不是我自律，是我在参加“体面改造计划”，先改体，再改面。
hidden_form: 体面 / 身体 + 面子
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是通过健身改造身体状态，让身形和精神面貌都变好。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means improving one's physical condition through fitness so that both body shape and overall appearance get better.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义激活“体面”一词，把“体”和“面”拆开重组，既指身体变化，也指更有体面、更有自信。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning activates the Chinese word for 'decent/respectable' by splitting it into 'body' and 'face,' suggesting both bodily improvement and greater dignity or confidence.
phonological_relation: 同形拆解，无明显语音关系
context: 适用于健身宣传、身材管理内容、励志式社媒文案。
literal_translation: A phrase is trending at the gym lately: it's not that I'm disciplined; I'm joining a 'body-face makeover plan'—first the body, then the face.
functional_equivalence_translation: The gym's new slogan is basically: this isn't self-discipline, it's a full-body dignity upgrade.
explanatory_translation: The pun works by splitting the fixed Chinese word '体面' (decent, respectable) into its literal components 'body' and 'face.' The hybrid phrase therefore means both physical transformation and becoming more socially presentable or confident.
interpretation_1: 健身改造身体
interpretation_2: 变得更体面自信

surface_text: 一天下午，单位同事带来一榴莲和女同胞分享。榴莲味道很臭，整层楼都弥漫着它的味道。 办公室一女同事分到一点，边吃边走出来，迎面碰到一男同事。 女：我吃过的，我想你不会要吧？ 男：我要啊！我就喜欢吃别人吃过的东西！我就好这一口！ 女：你喜欢？我还不愿意呢！ 男：你就不想给我一点留恋（榴莲）？ 女：滚！有多远滚多远！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本中“给我一点留恋”字面上是在说给他留下一点眷恋、不舍之情，表达带有暧昧意味。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the man is asking whether she can leave him a piece of the durian to eat, using a word that sounds like 'durian.'
interpretation_2_zh: 这里实际借“留恋”与“榴莲”同音，隐含意思是“给我一点榴莲”，表面讨要食物，同时双关出调情意味。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is 'leave me some attachment/reluctance to part,' since the word he uses normally means emotional attachment or lingering affection, creating a flirtatious double meaning.
context: 同事分吃榴莲，女同事手里有吃过的榴莲，男同事想要一些，借“留恋/榴莲”同音制造暧昧歧义。
literal_translation: Won’t you leave me a little longing (durian)?
functional_equivalence_translation: Can’t you leave me a little durian—or at least something to long for?
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese homophone between “liulian” meaning “to feel attached/reluctant to part” and “liulian” meaning “durian.” The man pretends to say “leave me some attachment,” but really means “leave me some durian.”
interpretation_1: 男同事表面上说“给我一点留恋”，像是在说让对方对自己有些不舍或眷恋。
interpretation_2: 实际隐含的是“给我一点榴莲”，即想分到一些对方吃过的榴莲。

surface_text: 老板说这次团建主打轻松随意，结果大家到了现场才发现是“社交步入式”安排：想躲都没门。
hidden_form: 步入式空间 / 被迫步入社交
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指一种开放、可自由走动进入的团建社交形式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to an open, walk-in style of social interaction at a team-building event.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借“步入式衣帽间”等说法，把“步入式”挪到社交场景，调侃人一进去就被社交包围，难以退出。
interpretation_2_en: It suggests a social setting that is literally open to enter but figuratively impossible to avoid once inside.
context: 适用于职场团建吐槽、社恐表达、网络段子。
negative_example: 这次团建是开放式社交活动。
literal_translation: The boss said this team-building event would be relaxed, but it turned out to be a 'walk-in social' setup: there was no way to hide.
functional_equivalence_translation: It was basically a walk-in social trap—once you entered, there was no escape.
explanatory_translation: The phrase parodies 'walk-in' as used for physical spaces and applies it to socializing, creating a hybrid expression that means both accessible and inescapably immersive.
interpretation_1: 开放式社交
interpretation_2: 一进去就得社交

surface_text: 一女问男朋友说：“你爱我吗?” 男朋友说：“爱。” 女问：也爱别人吗? 男朋友说：“也爱。” 女又问：“你不老说我是你的一切么?” 男说：“对啊，你就是我的一妾。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“你是我的一切”说成了“你是我的一妾”，字面意思变成你只是我的一个小妾、众多女人中的一个。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the man says, 'You are my one concubine,' literally calling her his single concubine.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“一妾”谐音替换“一切”，反讽男方并非把她当作全部，而是暗示他还爱别人，她只是其中之一。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a sound-based twist on '一切' ('everything'): he pretends to affirm that she is his 'everything,' but replaces it with the similar-sounding '一妾' ('one concubine') to imply she is just one among others, not his whole world.
context: 女生追问男友是否只爱自己，并引用“你是我的一切”这句话；男友借“一切/一妾”近音作答形成反转。
literal_translation: A woman asked her boyfriend, “Do you love me?” He said, “Yes.” She asked, “Do you love others too?” He said, “Yes, also.” She then asked, “Don’t you always say I am your everything?” The man said, “Right, you are one of my concubines.”
functional_equivalence_translation: “You said I’m your everything.” “Of course—you’re my every-thing… just one among the women.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the near-homophony between Chinese “一切” (everything) and “一妾” (one concubine). The boyfriend twists “You are my everything” into “You are one concubine of mine,” implying he loves other women too.
interpretation_1: 表层上像是在回应“你是我的一切”，即你是我的全部。
interpretation_2: 实际把“一切”偷换成“一妾”，意思是你只是我的一个妾，暗示还有别人。

surface_text: 教师：太的意思就是至高无上，像太上皇呀，太空呀等等，明白了吗？ 学生：明白了，怪不得我爸爸管妈妈叫太太呢！
县官太太同学官、营官太太一起吃饭，席间闲谈起来，互相询问诰封的是什么称呼。县官太太说：我们老爷称文林郎。学官太太说：我们老爷称修职郎。二人问营官太太是什么称呼，营官太太说：我们老爷是黄鼠狼。另两位太太忙问：哪有这样的称谓？营官太太说：我常见我们老爷下乡查场回来，总带回不少鸡，自然是个黄鼠狼了。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“我们老爷”的称呼说成了“黄鼠狼”，字面上是那种常偷鸡的动物，并用老爷下乡查场总带回鸡来作解释。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the wife literally says her husband is a 'weasel,' because he often comes back from inspecting the countryside with many chickens, just like a weasel that steals chickens.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含是在把官员封赠称谓中的“郎”字借动物名“狼”来替换调笑，实际应落在某种带“郎”的官衔称呼上，借“狼”讽刺其像黄鼠狼一样弄来鸡。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that she has mistaken her husband's formal official title ending in 'lang' for the animal word 'lang' in 'huangshulang' (weasel), creating a comic semantic shift between an honorific title and the animal name.
context: 三位官太太饭间互问丈夫的诰封称呼，前两人都回答正式官称，营官太太却按字面和行为联想作答。
literal_translation: My husband is a weasel.
functional_equivalence_translation: They asked my husband’s official title, and she answered, “A chicken thief, basically a weasel.”
explanatory_translation: When the other wives asked for her husband’s formal honorific title ending in “-lang,” she misunderstood it as asking what kind of “lang” he was and jokingly said “a weasel,” because he often came back with many chickens.
interpretation_1: 营官太太把“老爷是什么称呼”理解成对人品或行为的描述，说丈夫像黄鼠狼一样总叼鸡回来。
interpretation_2: 原问题本意是询问丈夫受封的正式称谓，应回答带“郎”的官衔称号。

surface_text: 我们联系了照顾流浪猫的志愿者。
一人问曰：相公尊姓？曰：姓杨。其人曰：既是 羊，为甚无角？士怒曰：呆狗入出的！那人错会其意，曰： 嗄！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“杨”错听成“羊”，于是按动物“羊”来理解，追问既然是羊，为什么没有角。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the man hears the surname Yang as the animal 'sheep' and jokes, 'If you are a sheep, why don't you have horns?'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“杨”本是姓氏，并非动物之羊；这里利用“杨”与“羊”同音造成误会和戏谑。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'Yang' is actually the person's surname, only sounding like 'sheep'; the humor comes from deliberately misinterpreting the surname as the animal.
context: 一人询问对方姓氏，对方答“姓杨”，问者将“杨”理解成“羊”，据此戏谑“既是羊，为甚无角”。
literal_translation: One man asked, “What is your honorable surname?” He said, “Yang.” The man said, “If it is a sheep, why does it have no horns?” The scholar angrily said, “You stupid dog-spawn!” That man misunderstood again and said, “Ah!”
functional_equivalence_translation: A man asked, “Your surname?” “Yang,” came the reply. “If you’re a ram, where are your horns?” the other joked, taking “Yang” as “sheep.”
explanatory_translation: A man asks someone’s surname, and the reply is “Yang” (a common Chinese surname). The questioner intentionally or mistakenly interprets “Yang,” which sounds the same as “sheep” in Chinese, and jokes: “If you’re a sheep, why don’t you have horns?” The pun relies on the homophone between the surname 杨 and the word 羊.
interpretation_1: “姓杨”中的“杨”是正常的姓氏回答。
interpretation_2: 问话者把“杨”错听或故意曲解为“羊”，于是追问“为何无角”。

surface_text: 期末周的图书馆像大型“卷面现场”，大家一边刷题，一边把自己卷进答案里。
hidden_form: 见面现场 / 试卷 / 内卷
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指到处都是试卷和刷题场景的现场。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a scene full of exam papers and people doing exercises.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借“见面现场”的格式，同时激活“内卷”，表示竞争氛围很强。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it imitates the pattern of 'meeting scene' while activating the idea of 'involution,' highlighting intense competition.
context: 适用于校园、备考、期末周相关吐槽或社交平台配文。
negative_example: 期末周的图书馆到处都是卷子。
literal_translation: The library during finals week is like a giant 'paper-roll scene'; everyone solves problems while rolling themselves into the answers.
functional_equivalence_translation: During finals, the library turns into a full-on cram-and-compete arena.
explanatory_translation: The phrase blends 'exam paper' (juan) and 'involution/over-competition' (juan) into a remodeled expression based on 'scene,' making the space both literally full of papers and metaphorically full of academic pressure.
interpretation_1: 满场试卷
interpretation_2: 学习内卷

surface_text: 一日，在家里洗澡，妈妈热情地帮我放水，先热水，后冷水，再热，再冷，直到水温不烫手亦不凉。然后退出浴室。 脱衣之前突想小解一下，而妈妈在外听到水声，嚷到：“你还在放水？水温已合适啦！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“放水”指往浴缸或洗澡用水中继续放自来水、调节水温。妈妈以为还在往澡盆里加水。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “放水” means letting water into the bathtub to adjust the temperature, so the mother thinks he is still running the bath water.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里“放水”又被借指撒尿、解小便。实际上发出水声的是准备小解，而不是继续放洗澡水。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that he is actually urinating before taking the bath; the sound of flowing water makes the mother mistakenly think he is still filling the tub.
context: 母亲先前一直在浴室给孩子往浴缸里放水调温；孩子准备洗澡前突然小便，外面的人听见水声，误以为还在继续给浴缸放水。
literal_translation: "You’re still running water? The water temperature is already fine!"
functional_equivalence_translation: "Are you still letting water out? The bath’s ready already!"
explanatory_translation: The pun is on "放水," which on the surface means "to run/fill bath water," but here it is also understood as "to pee" because the mother hears the sound of water and mistakes urination for continuing to fill the tub.
interpretation_1: 往浴缸里放洗澡用水、调节水温
interpretation_2: 小便，放出体内的水

surface_text: 昨天大学同学聚会，很多同学好几年都没见了。 一个同学见我比原来胖了，脑袋大脖子粗像个暴发户，上了就问：老同学，发了吧你？ 我笑了笑：你以为我是海参啊！
骗子：您好，我是xx市中级人民法院，这里有一张您的传票。 同学转过头疑惑地对寝室同学说：船票？我们没订船票啊……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本把“传票”误听成“船票”，理解为乘船出行所需的票据，所以寝室同学才会说没有订船票。
interpretation_1_en: The listener literally hears 'boat ticket' and thinks someone is talking about a ticket for a ship or ferry that they did not book.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的原意是法院所说的“传票”，指司法机关通知当事人到案的法律文书，并不是乘船票据。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is 'court summons,' because 'boat ticket' is a mishearing of 'summons' in the scam call, creating the pun through similar pronunciation.
context: 电话诈骗冒充法院通知有“传票”，旁人将其误听为“船票”。
literal_translation: Scammer: Hello, I’m from the Intermediate People’s Court of xx City. There is a subpoena for you. The student turned around and asked the roommate in confusion: A boat ticket? We didn’t book any boat tickets...
functional_equivalence_translation: Scammer: Hello, this is the xx City Court. There’s a summons for you. The student turned and asked his roommate, puzzled: A ship ticket? We didn’t book a ship ticket...
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the near-homophony between “传票” (court summons/subpoena) and “船票” (boat ticket). The scammer means the legal document, but the student mishears it as a travel ticket.
interpretation_1: 骗子冒充法院，说的是法律语境中的“传票”，即法院传唤文书。
interpretation_2: 同学误听成“船票”，理解为乘船用的票据。

surface_text: 期末周的图书馆里全是“续命水文学”，人手一杯咖啡，边背书边抢救清醒。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是围绕咖啡、茶等“续命水”形成了一套校园日常话题和行为模式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a campus lifestyle and discourse built around coffee and other 'life-saving drinks.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用“文学”这一抽象分类，把喝提神饮料包装成一种可讨论、可共鸣的精神现象。
interpretation_2_en: It also borrows the category of 'literature' to elevate energy drinks into a shared emotional and cultural phenomenon.
context: 适用于校园吐槽、期末周社交平台配文。
negative_example: 期末周大家都爱喝咖啡。
literal_translation: In the library during finals week, there is only 'life-extending-drink-ology'; everyone holds a coffee and tries to rescue their alertness while studying.
functional_equivalence_translation: Finals week turns the library into a full-on survival-drink culture, with everyone clutching coffee just to stay conscious.
explanatory_translation: The pun creates a hybrid expression by attaching the abstract suffix-like category 'literature/ology' to the slang term 'life-saving drink,' making an everyday habit sound like a school of thought.
interpretation_1: 提神饮料文化
interpretation_2: 把熬夜日常文学化

surface_text: 这款通勤鞋宣传自己能带来“脚踏适地”的幸福感，地铁站台走成了自家客厅。
hidden_form: 脚踏实地 / 脚感舒适落地
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指鞋子穿着舒适，脚一落地就有被支撑和放松的感觉。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the shoes feel comfortable and supportive the moment your feet touch the ground.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟成语“脚踏实地”，把做人做事的稳妥感转换成穿鞋时的踏实与舒适。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it parodies the idiom 'to be grounded and practical,' converting that sense of steadiness into physical comfort while wearing shoes.
context: 适用于鞋类广告、电商详情页或通勤生活方式内容。
literal_translation: These commuting shoes advertise a happiness of 'feet stepping on comfort-ground'; the subway platform feels like my living room.
functional_equivalence_translation: These commuter shoes make every step feel grounded and ridiculously comfortable.
explanatory_translation: The phrase modifies the idiom 'to stand firmly on the ground' by replacing 'solid' with 'comfortable,' producing a hybrid expression that links moral steadiness with physical comfort.
interpretation_1: 鞋子脚感舒适
interpretation_2: 仿拟脚踏实地

surface_text: 裴子羽做下邳县令时，张晴任县丞，两人都很有声望，且喜谈时事。有个小吏私下里开玩笑说：县官之间很不和睦。 有人问他缘故，小吏答：长官称雨（羽），赞府道晴，终日如此，哪里会和？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中把裴子羽的“羽”说成“雨”，与张晴的“晴”并提，形成“雨”和“晴”终日并存、彼此不和的字面意思。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, one superior keeps talking about rain while the deputy keeps talking about clear weather all day, so of course they cannot be in harmony.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上是借“羽”与“雨”同音，拿两人的名字开玩笑，说县官之间所谓“不和睦”，其实是把“子羽”的“羽”转成“雨”，与“晴”构成语义上的对立。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the words 'rain' and 'clear' pun on the officials' names, Yu and Qing, implying that these two officials are said to be at odds with each other.
context: 两位县官名字分别关联“羽/雨”和“晴”，又都喜欢谈时事，小吏借“雨”与“晴”难并存来戏称二人“不和”。
literal_translation: A petty clerk joked in private: the county officials are very disharmonious. When asked why, he said: the chief speaks of rain, the assistant speaks of clear weather; they are like this all day long, so how could they be in harmony?
functional_equivalence_translation: A clerk quipped, “Those two county officials just can’t get along—one is all rain, the other all sunshine. How could that ever match?”
explanatory_translation: A clerk made a pun by saying the two officials were “not in harmony.” On the surface, this means they did not get along. But the joke relies on one official’s name sounding like “rain” and the other’s meaning “clear weather,” implying rain and sunshine do not readily go together.
interpretation_1: 表面说县官之间不和睦、不和谐。
interpretation_2: 暗指一个称雨、一个道晴，雨晴难以相合，因而说“哪里会和”。

surface_text: 朋友是个比较贤惠，知性的女士。 她男朋友是个网络部门的员工，有次在室外需要在一个高杆上牵网线，他男朋友就那样徒手爬上去，旁边的几个同事提醒他要穿戴好安全装备才行。 然后朋友很着急的说：“对啊！这样多不安全啊！你还是先带好安全套吧！” 她没意识到这点，，他男朋友差点就摔了。全场人都笑喷了……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层字面上，她说的是让男朋友先带好“安全套”，即通常指避孕套，因此与爬高作业场景明显不搭配，造成笑点。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she meant he should put on safety gear or protective equipment before climbing the pole, so it would be safer.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，她本来想表达的是让对方先穿戴好高空作业所需的安全装备，尤其是安全带之类的防护用具，只是误把“安全装备”说成了“安全套”。
interpretation_2_en: The phrase she actually used, "安全套," commonly means a condom in Chinese, which is why everyone laughed at the unintended sexual meaning.
context: 高杆上牵网线的高空作业场景中，同事提醒要穿戴安全装备，女方情急之下误说成“安全套”。
literal_translation: Yes! That's so unsafe! You'd better put on a condom first!
functional_equivalence_translation: Yeah, that's dangerous! You'd better put on your protection first!
explanatory_translation: She meant to say “safety gear” for climbing, but accidentally said “condom,” because both are associated with “safety/protection,” which creates the joke.
interpretation_1: 表层上说的是避孕套，即日常语义中的“安全套”。
interpretation_2: 实际想表达的是高空作业时应佩戴的安全防护装备，如安全带、安全绳等。

surface_text: 有个秀才向路旁一户人家借宿，那人家只有一个女人，倚靠着大门说道：我家里没有人。 秀才说：你不是人吗？ 女人说：我家里没有男人。 秀才说：我不是男人吗？
一家人吃桃。妈妈问：桃的英文怎么说？女儿答：peach.妈妈对爸爸说：给你个屁吃
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，妈妈把女儿说的英文“peach”听成了“屁吃”，于是对爸爸说“给你个屁吃”，形成粗俗的字面效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the daughter answers that the English word for 桃 is “peach,” and the mother then echoes the sound as if she is saying something to the father.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“peach”对应回“桃子”，更常规的意思其实是“给你个桃子吃”，双关来自英文发音与中文“屁吃”的近音错听。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that “peach” sounds like “屁吃” in Chinese, which means “eat屁,” so the mother’s line becomes a joking insult meaning “Here, have a fart to eat.”
context: 一家人在吃桃，妈妈先问“桃的英文怎么说”，女儿回答“peach”，随后妈妈利用其与“屁吃”近音来接话。
literal_translation: A family is eating peaches. Mom asks: How do you say 桃 in English? The daughter answers: peach. Mom says to Dad: I'll give you a fart to eat.
functional_equivalence_translation: A family is eating peaches. Mom asks, “What’s ‘peach’ in English?” The daughter says, “Peach.” Mom then jokes to Dad, “Here, have some ‘pee-ch’ to eat.”
explanatory_translation: A family is eating peaches. Mom asks for the English word for 桃, and the daughter says “peach.” Mom then makes a pun because “peach” sounds somewhat like the Chinese phrase “屁吃” (literally “eat a fart”), so she jokingly says to Dad, “I’ll give you a fart to eat.”
interpretation_1: 女儿回答“桃”的英文是 peach，即水果“桃子”。
interpretation_2: 妈妈把 peach 谐听成“屁吃”，借机对爸爸说“给你个屁吃”。

surface_text: 猴子对黑猩猩说：人家都买房了，你怎么也不跟潮流？黑猩猩：（双手拍胸脯）哥啥房都没有，只有两个乳房。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是黑猩猩回应自己没有买任何房子，却有两个乳房，利用身体部位来接话。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the monkey says everyone is buying a house and asks why the chimpanzee is not following the trend. The chimpanzee replies that he has no house at all, only two breasts/chests.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“房”从“房子”转移到与胸部相关的说法上，借拍胸脯动作把话题从买房转成自己的胸前两块，形成谐趣。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden joke is triggered by the word “房” (house), which is shifted to the similar-sounding “乳房” (breasts). So instead of talking about buying property, the chimpanzee deliberately twists the meaning to body parts for comic effect.
context: 一方谈论“买房”“跟潮流”，另一方回应“啥房都没有，只有两个乳房”，使“房”从房产义转到身体部位构词成分义。
negative_example: 哥啥房都没有，只有两间平房。
literal_translation: The monkey said to the chimpanzee: "Everyone is buying houses. Why don't you follow the trend?" Chimpanzee: "I don't have any house at all, only two breasts."
functional_equivalence_translation: The monkey said, "Everyone's buying property—why not keep up?" The chimp thumped his chest: "Property? I’ve got none—just these two mammaries."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word "房". In context it first means "house/property," but the chimp shifts it to the "房" in "乳房" (breast), creating a semantic pun.
interpretation_1: 表层是在说买房、拥有房子，指住宅房产。
interpretation_2: 黑猩猩把“房”转成“乳房”的“房”，借此说自己没有房产，只有胸前的两个乳房。

surface_text: 小花的妈妈是医院妇科医生，当小花问妈妈：妈妈你天天在医院里干什么？ 小花的妈妈总是回答：生孩子呗！ 小花又问：妈妈，你一共生了多少个婴儿？
interpretation_1_zh: 按字面理解，妈妈回答“生孩子呗”会被理解成她自己在医院里把孩子生出来。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the mother says she 'gives birth to babies' every day at the hospital, so the child understands it literally and asks how many babies her mother has given birth to.
interpretation_2_zh: 实际隐含义是她作为妇科医生在医院里为产妇接生婴儿，并不是她自己生了很多孩子。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that as a gynecologist/obstetric doctor, she helps deliver babies or assists women in childbirth at the hospital, rather than personally giving birth to them.
context: 妈妈是医院妇科医生，回答“在医院里干什么”时说“生孩子呗”，引发孩子将职业行为误解为自己分娩
literal_translation: Xiaohua's mother is a gynecologist at a hospital. When Xiaohua asks, “Mom, what do you do in the hospital every day?” her mother always answers, “Deliver babies!” Xiaohua then asks, “Mom, how many babies have you given birth to in total?”
functional_equivalence_translation: Xiaohua's mom is an OB-GYN. When Xiaohua asks what she does at the hospital, Mom says, “I help bring babies into the world.” So Xiaohua asks, “Then how many babies have you had?”
explanatory_translation: The humor hinges on the Chinese phrase “sheng haizi,” which can be understood as “give birth to a child” or, in this hospital context, “deliver babies.” The child mistakes the doctor's professional role for the literal act of bearing children herself.
interpretation_1: 字面上指妈妈自己把孩子生出来
interpretation_2: 实际指妇科医生在医院里为产妇接生婴儿

surface_text: 丈夫对妻子说：“你别小看我，在家里我可是个呼风唤雨的人。” 妻子说：“我掌管了财政，你还能有什么能耐？” 丈夫说：“我开空调就有风，开电热水器就有雨。”
hidden_form: 开空调有风，开电热水器有雨
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“呼风唤雨”按字面拆开理解成制造出风和水，丈夫说自己开空调就有风，开电热水器就有雨。
interpretation_1_en: Literally, he says he can 'summon wind and rain' at home: turning on the air conditioner creates wind, and turning on the electric water heater produces water like rain.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的常规意思是“呼风唤雨”本指人很有本事、很有权势，能够左右局面；这里妻子质疑他的能耐，丈夫故意把成语转成字面义来制造笑点。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, 'summon wind and rain' is an idiom meaning to wield great power and influence, but the joke is that he twists it into a mundane household meaning to mock his lack of real authority at home.
context: 丈夫在妻子质疑自己本事时，说自己在家里是个“呼风唤雨的人”，随后把成语的比喻义转成家电带来风和水的字面义。
literal_translation: The husband said to his wife, “Don’t underestimate me. At home, I’m someone who can summon wind and rain.” The wife said, “I control the finances. What ability could you possibly have?” The husband said, “When I turn on the air conditioner, there is wind; when I turn on the electric water heater, there is rain.”
functional_equivalence_translation: The husband said, “Don’t underestimate me—I can make things happen at home.” His wife said, “I control the money. What can you do?” He said, “Easy. I switch on the AC for wind and the shower for rain.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese idiom “呼风唤雨,” which normally means “to wield great power or influence,” but the husband humorously reinterprets it literally as producing wind with the air conditioner and “rain” with hot water from the heater.
interpretation_1: 表面上指人很有权势、很有本事，能够左右局面。
interpretation_2: 实际被解释成字面义：打开家电就能制造风和像雨一样的水流。

surface_text: 小侃随老侃去城里玩，小侃深感城里比乡下好。老侃说：那，我们搬家到城里住好不好？小侃说：好是好，就是妈妈来了不好办。为什么？因为城里只有公厕，没有母厕。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“公厕”中的“公”理解为与“母”相对，认为城里只有‘公的厕所’，没有‘母的厕所’，所以妈妈来了不方便。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child understands '公厕' literally by taking '公' as the opposite of '母', so he thinks the city has only 'male/father toilets' and no 'mother toilets'.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义中“公厕”的“公”本义是‘公共’、供公众使用，并不是‘公母’中的‘公’；小侃是故意把“公共厕所”曲解成与‘母厕’对应来制造笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '公厕' actually means 'public toilet', where '公' means 'public', not the opposite of 'mother'. The humor comes from misunderstanding the word by shifting its meaning.
context: 小侃听到“城里只有公厕”，把“公”从“公共”误解为“公母”的“公”，于是推出不存在“母厕”，担心妈妈不方便。
literal_translation: Xiaokan said: "Good is good, but it would be inconvenient when Mom comes." "Why?" "Because in the city there are only public toilets, no mother toilets."
functional_equivalence_translation: "Moving to the city sounds good," said the child, "but what about Mom? Cities only have 'male' toilets, not 'female' ones."
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on Chinese "gongce" (public toilet). The child misparses "gong" as "male" rather than "public," so he imagines there should also be a matching "mother/female toilet," which creates the pun.
interpretation_1: 孩子把“公厕”理解成“公、母”性别对立中的“公厕所”。
interpretation_2: 实际“公厕”是“公共厕所”的简称，不与“母厕”构成对应。

surface_text: 这是一通宠物食品的电话市场调查，接电话的是一个小孩。 市调员：小朋友，你家里有没有养小狗，小猫，小兔子，或是小鸟？ 小孩：没有，我妈就生了我一个！
德友人魏特茂，娶了中国太太。某日遇一老翁，两人寒暄起来。老翁：您贵姓？德佬：我姓魏。老翁：魏什么？德佬：为什么？姓魏也要为什么？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是老翁追问对方姓魏，想问“姓魏，名字叫什么”或“魏字后面是什么”，因此说出“魏什么”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the old man is asking for the man's full surname or what follows after 'Wei,' saying 'Wei what?'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“为什么”，被德国人听成日常疑问句，以为对方在问原因，所以回答成“姓魏也要为什么”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '魏什么' sounds like '为什么' ('why'), so the German man misunderstands it as 'Why?' and replies, 'Why? Do I need a reason to have the surname Wei?'
context: 初次见面寒暄，老翁问“您贵姓”，对方答“我姓魏”，老翁追问“魏什么”以确认是哪个“魏”，对方却理解成“为什么”
literal_translation: An old man asked, “What Wei?” The German heard it as “Why?”
functional_equivalence_translation: Old man: “Wei what?” German: “Why what? Is there a reason I can’t be surnamed Wei?”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese phrase “魏什么,” which in context means “which Wei character?” but sounds exactly like “为什么” (“why”), so the man mistakenly answers it as a question asking for a reason.
interpretation_1: 询问姓氏的具体字样，意思是“姓魏，哪个魏”
interpretation_2: 被误听成“为什么”，即询问原因

surface_text: 一位萌妹纸感冒了在图书馆纸用完了，于是发短信给室友，说：过来的时候带两包纸。 不一会儿，室友过来了，手里拿着两包子……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文字里，室友把信息理解成了要带两包子，于是拿来了两袋包子。
interpretation_1_en: The roommate literally understood the message as asking for two buns, so she came holding two buns.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的原意是感冒时在图书馆纸用完了，需要的是两包纸巾或卫生纸，而不是食物。
interpretation_2_en: What was actually meant was two packs of tissues or toilet paper; '两包纸' was misheard or shifted into '两包子,' creating the pun.
context: 女生感冒，在图书馆纸用完了，发短信让室友带“两包纸”，室友到来时却拿着两包子
literal_translation: A cute girl caught a cold and ran out of paper in the library, so she texted her roommate: Bring two packs of paper when you come. Soon the roommate arrived, holding two buns.
functional_equivalence_translation: A girl with a cold texted her roommate, “Bring me two packs of tissues,” but the roommate showed up with two buns instead.
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the near-sound between Chinese “zhi” (paper/tissue) and “zi” (a noun ending in “baozi,” steamed buns). So “two packs of paper” is misheard or reinterpreted as “two buns.”
interpretation_1: 让室友带两包卫生纸或纸巾来
interpretation_2: 被室友误解为带两个包子来

surface_text: 这款清洁机器人号称“躺赢家务”，人不用勤快，地板自己上进。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层意思是不必亲自动手做家务，也能获得整洁效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means you can get a clean home without personally doing the chores.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用网络词“躺赢”，把竞技或收益语境搬到家务场景里，制造轻松反差。
interpretation_2_en: It borrows the internet slang 'win while lying down' and relocates it from competition or gain to housework, creating a playful contrast.
context: 适用于家电广告、电商标题或种草文案。
negative_example: 这款机器人可以帮你做家务。
literal_translation: This cleaning robot claims to let you 'lie down and win at housework'; people don't need to work hard, the floor becomes ambitious by itself.
functional_equivalence_translation: This robot vacuum lets you beat housework without lifting a finger.
explanatory_translation: The expression is a hybrid blend of the slang 'lying down and winning' with 'housework,' turning domestic cleaning into a game-like effortless victory.
interpretation_1: 轻松做家务
interpretation_2: 套用躺赢梗

surface_text: 一天跟我老婆去逛街，她指着一家餐厅门口“请不要带宠物入内”的牌对我说：“我进去，你在门口等着。”
那天中午我做饭，他在机前玩兴正酣。菜在热锅里吱、吱乱叫，急得我大叫一声：快把盘子拿来！ 半天，只见他懵懵懂懂地从机旁站起身来：什么盘？光盘，还是软盘！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义中的“盘子”指盛菜用的餐具，说话人是在做饭时急着让对方把装菜的盘子拿来。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "panzi" means a plate or dish needed for serving the cooked food, so the speaker is urgently asking him to bring a plate from the kitchen.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义中，对方因正在电脑前玩，把“盘”理解成了电脑相关的“光盘、软盘”，因此把日常餐具义误听成了计算机存储介质义。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from shifting "pan" to a computer-related sense: he misunderstands it as a disk, such as a CD-ROM or a floppy disk, because he is sitting at the computer.
context: 一人在厨房炒菜，急忙喊“快把盘子拿来”；另一人正在电脑前玩，把“盘子”中的“盘”误解为电脑磁盘。
literal_translation: At noon that day I was cooking while he was having fun in front of the computer. The dishes were sizzling in the hot wok, and in a hurry I shouted: “Quick, bring me a plate!” After quite a while, he stood up from beside the computer in confusion: “What plate? A CD, or a floppy disk?”
functional_equivalence_translation: I yelled, “Bring me a dish!” But from the computer he asked, “What kind of disk—a CD or a floppy?”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the Chinese word “盘/盘子”: “盘子” means a plate for food, but “盘” can also mean a disk, so the listener mistakes a kitchen request for a computer-related one.
interpretation_1: 说话人要对方拿来盛菜用的盘子。
interpretation_2: 听话人把“盘”理解为电脑相关的磁盘，如光盘或软盘。

surface_text: 小明是一个非常宅的宅男，都23岁了还没有成功的谈过一场恋爱，最近和一美女在网上聊了十多天，最终两人约好在公园里见个面。可是两人谈了没一会儿，美女便起身告辞。 小伙子很喜欢那个美女，见她要走，心里特别着急，连忙追问原因。 美女说：“我觉得你虽然相貌堂堂，可是腹中空空。” 小伙说：“谁说我腹中空空？来公园之前还吃了两包方便面。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是肚子里空空的，指没有吃饱、胃里没东西。小伙子把这句话理解成了自己是否吃过饭的问题。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '腹中空空' means his stomach is empty, as if he has not eaten anything.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是说他缺乏内涵和学识，谈吐空洞，没有什么文化修养。美女借“腹中空空”委婉表达他人虽长得不错，但内在贫乏。
interpretation_2_en: Its implied meaning is that he is empty-headed or lacks knowledge, depth, and substance despite looking handsome.
context: 相亲式见面中，美女评价男子“腹中空空”，男子却从是否吃过东西来回应。
literal_translation: The beauty said, “Although you look quite dignified, your belly is empty.” The young man said, “Who says my belly is empty? I ate two packs of instant noodles before coming to the park.”
functional_equivalence_translation: The woman said, “You may look good, but there’s nothing in your head.” He replied, “Nothing? I ate two packs of noodles before I came.”
explanatory_translation: Here “腹中空空” normally means “empty-headed / lacking knowledge or substance,” but the man deliberately or mistakenly interprets it literally as “having an empty stomach,” so he answers by saying he had eaten instant noodles.
interpretation_1: 美女表面上说他没有学识、没有内涵。
interpretation_2: 小伙把这话理解成肚子里没有食物、没吃饱。

surface_text: 正在生气时，他儿子拿着书本走过来问到：“爸爸，成语明珠暗投怎么解释。” 老张一听大怒，打了他儿子一巴掌骂到：“亏老子辛辛苦苦供你上学，连个成语都不会解。‘明猪暗偷’的意思不是很简单吗？白天买的猪，在夜里被人偷了，还用老子教吗？
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把成语误解为“明猪暗偷”，意思成了白天买来的猪，到了夜里被人偷走。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “明猪暗偷” is taken literally as “a pig bought in broad daylight was secretly stolen at night.”
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是常规成语“明珠暗投”，比喻有才能的人或珍贵的东西落到不识货、不合适的人或地方。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the actual idiom “明珠暗投,” which means a bright pearl is cast into the dark, referring to something valuable being given to the wrong person or not being appreciated.
context: 父亲正在生气，儿子来问成语“明珠暗投”的意思，父亲把成语按近音误解成“明猪暗偷”并据此解释。
literal_translation: While angry, his son came over with a book and asked, “Dad, how do you explain the idiom ‘casting pearls before darkness’?” Lao Zhang got furious and slapped him, scolding, “I worked so hard to support your schooling, and you still can’t explain an idiom. Isn’t ‘bright pig, secret steal’ very simple? A pig bought in the daytime was stolen at night. Do I still need to teach you that?”
functional_equivalence_translation: While angry, his son asked, “Dad, what does ‘ming zhu an tou’ mean?” The father snapped, “Isn’t that obvious? It means a pig bought by day gets stolen by night!”
explanatory_translation: The pun hinges on the idiom “明珠暗投” (to cast pearls before one who does not appreciate them) being misheard as the near-homophonous non-idiom “明猪暗偷,” literally “a pig bought in daylight is stolen at night.”
interpretation_1: 成语本义是把明珠暗中投给不识货的人，比喻好东西给了不懂的人。
interpretation_2: 被故意曲解为“明猪暗偷”，即白天买来的猪，夜里被人偷走了。

surface_text: 邻居家婶婶要生宝宝了。 一家人商量是顺产还是剖腹产，婶婶说剖腹产吧！省的受罪。结果他家老爷子不同意， 说：“顺产，一定要顺产，不能让孩子一出生就不走正道。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层说法把“剖腹产”理解成孩子出生时不是从正常产道出来，因此被老爷子说成“一出生就不走正道”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "not walking the right path" literally refers to the baby not coming out through the normal birth canal, but instead being delivered by cesarean section.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借用成语里“走正道”的道德含义，指做人应当走正路、不误入歧途，把分娩方式和做人是否正派幽默地联系起来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is the common expression "not taking the right path," which means going astray morally or behaving improperly; the old man humorously treats cesarean birth as if the child would start life by deviating from the proper way.
context: 一家人讨论婶婶生产方式，老爷子把“顺产”的医学含义误转为“走正道”的道德/路径含义。
literal_translation: The neighbor's auntie was about to have a baby. The family was discussing whether to have a natural birth or a C-section. She said, “Let's do a C-section, to avoid suffering.” But the old man in the family disagreed and said, “Natural birth, it must be natural birth. We can't let the child be off the right path the moment it is born.”
functional_equivalence_translation: They were debating natural birth or C-section. The grandpa insisted on natural birth: “It has to be natural—we can’t have the kid taking the wrong way from day one.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “顺产,” which normally means “natural birth,” but the old man interprets “顺” as “following the proper/right path,” joking that a baby born by C-section would be “not taking the right path” from birth.
interpretation_1: 指自然分娩，与剖腹产相对。
interpretation_2: 被曲解为孩子出生时要“顺着正道出来”，否则就是“不走正道”。

surface_text: 我做水下换能器时要用到防水密封胶，问之于师兄，他说最好问问昆腾或者希捷。我大奇，它们和密封胶有什么关系？ 师兄慢条斯理地说：BBS上天天有人灌水，可没见硬盘漏过。我晕。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“灌水”理解为真的把水灌进去，因此联想到硬盘如果防水密封做得好，就不会漏水。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '灌水' means literally pouring water in, so the joke says people 'pour water' into BBS forums every day, yet hard disks from Quantum or Seagate never leak, as if they had excellent waterproof sealing.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“灌水”理解为在BBS上大量发表无实质内容的帖子，师兄借论坛常用语故意转到硬盘品牌上，形成双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '灌水' on BBS means posting empty, meaningless, or filler messages. Mentioning hard-disk brands is a punning detour: they are not related to sealant at all, but are brought up because 'water-filling' is reinterpreted through computer-related slang.
context: 询问防水密封胶品牌时，师兄提到昆腾和希捷这类硬盘品牌，并用“BBS上天天有人灌水，可没见硬盘漏过”制造语义转折。
literal_translation: When I was making an underwater transducer, I needed waterproof sealant. I asked a senior fellow student, and he said I'd better ask Quantum or Seagate. I was puzzled—what do they have to do with sealant? He said slowly: People flood BBS forums every day, but I've never seen a hard drive leak. I was speechless.
functional_equivalence_translation: I asked what sealant to use for an underwater device, and my senior said, “Ask Quantum or Seagate.” I was baffled. He explained, “People are always ‘watering down’ BBS boards, yet hard drives never leak.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese internet slang “灌水,” which normally means posting lots of trivial messages on a BBS/forum. The speaker deliberately shifts it back to its literal sense of “pouring in water,” then jokes that since forums are full of such “water,” hard drives from brands like Quantum or Seagate must have good waterproof sealing because they never “leak.”
interpretation_1: 在BBS论坛里大量发无实质内容的帖子，即网络义的“灌水”。
interpretation_2: 把真实的水灌进去，因此联想到存储了很多“水”的硬盘也不漏水，可拿来类比防水密封。

surface_text: 表侄很挑食，表哥想改掉他的坏毛病。夹着一把猪心放到他碗里：你必须得吃掉它！表侄不愿意。这时表嫂劝导他：你爸也是为了你好，这可是你爸的一片心啊！
这款收纳柜简直是“断舍柜”本柜，装进去的不只是杂物，还有我对混乱生活的执念。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指一个帮助整理、归纳物品的收纳柜。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a storage cabinet that helps organize and sort belongings.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借“断舍离”观念，把收纳柜塑造成帮助人减少杂乱、整理生活方式的工具。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning draws on the concept of decluttering, turning the cabinet into a symbol of simplifying and reorganizing one's life.
context: 适用于家居收纳广告、生活方式分享、居家整理内容。
literal_translation: This storage cabinet is the very model of a 'declutter cabinet'; what goes into it is not just clutter, but my obsession with a chaotic life.
functional_equivalence_translation: This cabinet is basically decluttering in furniture form—it stores not only stuff, but my attachment to chaos.
explanatory_translation: The phrase modifies the well-known expression for minimalist decluttering by replacing its ending with 'cabinet.' The result is a hybrid word that names a real object while evoking the broader lifestyle ideal of letting go and tidying up.
interpretation_1: 收纳整理的柜子
interpretation_2: 断舍离生活方式

surface_text: 这家面包店的新品海报写着“碳愁无忧”，先吃饱，再考虑卡路里和人生规划。
hidden_form: 弹愁无忧 / 碳水 / 无忧
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是吃到碳水后烦恼会暂时减轻，强调面包带来的安慰感。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means carbs can temporarily ease worries and bring comfort.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“碳水”与“无忧”组合成广告式口号，调侃人们对食物治愈感的依赖。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it turns 'carbs' and 'carefree' into an advertising-style slogan, joking about people's reliance on food for emotional comfort.
context: 适用于烘焙店宣传、甜品营销或治愈系饮食内容。
negative_example: 这家面包店的新品很好吃，让人很开心。
literal_translation: The poster for this bakery's new item reads 'carb-worry no-worry': eat first, then think about calories and life plans.
functional_equivalence_translation: Their bakery slogan is basically: carbs first, worries later.
explanatory_translation: The pun creates a hybrid slogan by blending 'carbs' with a carefree idiom-like structure, making food both the literal subject and the emotional solution.
interpretation_1: 碳水治愈烦恼
interpretation_2: 广告化表达无忧感

surface_text: 蝴蝶对朋友蚂蚁说：你这么闷是永远找不到女朋友的，有没有考虑过以后啊？蚂蚁说：考虑过，但是蚁后看不上我。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层里“蚁后”指蚂蚁群体中的蚁后，蚂蚁说自己考虑过找对象的事，但连蚁后都看不上自己。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '蚁后' means the queen ant. The ant says he has thought about his future, but the queen ant does not like him.
interpretation_2_zh: “蚁后”与“以后”同音，隐藏意思是“考虑过，但是以后也看不上我”，借谐音把对未来找不到女朋友的担忧说出来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '蚁后' sounds like '以后' ('later' or 'the future'). This echoes the butterfly's question about whether he has considered his future.
context: 蝴蝶劝蚂蚁别太闷，要考虑找女朋友；“以后”与“蚁后”同音，触发蚂蚁将时间义误解为对象义。
literal_translation: A butterfly said to his friend Ant: “If you’re this dull, you’ll never find a girlfriend. Have you thought about the future?” Ant said: “I have, but the ant queen doesn’t like me.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A butterfly told the ant, “If you stay this boring, you’ll never get a girlfriend. Have you thought about your future?” The ant replied, “I have, but the queen ant isn’t into me.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese homophone “以后” (yǐhòu, ‘the future/later’) and “蚁后” (yǐhòu, ‘ant queen’). So when asked whether he has thought about the future, the ant pretends he heard “ant queen” and answers that the ant queen is not interested in him.
interpretation_1: 表层义是“将来、未来”，即蝴蝶在问蚂蚁有没有考虑过今后的事。
interpretation_2: 隐含义是“蚁后”，即蚂蚁把“以后”听成了“蚁后”，回答说蚁后看不上自己。

surface_text: “爸爸，是男的跑得快，还是女的跑得快？” “当然是男的快。” “那为什么总是男孩子追女孩子呢。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层把“追”理解为跑步时在后面追赶、试图赶上的意思，因此孩子用谁跑得快来类比谁去追谁。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'chase' means physically running after someone, so the child is asking why boys are not faster in that literal sense if men supposedly run faster.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含把“追”恢复为恋爱语境中的“追求”，即男孩子通常主动追求女孩子，这里的“追”不是比拼跑步速度。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'chase' refers to pursuing someone romantically, as in boys courting girls, rather than actually running after them.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：前文讨论男女谁跑得快，后句转入“男孩子追女孩子”的恋爱表达，使“追”从物理追赶转为感情追求。
literal_translation: "Dad, who runs faster, men or women?" "Of course men run faster." "Then why is it always boys chasing girls?"
functional_equivalence_translation: "Dad, who’s faster, boys or girls?" "Boys, of course." "Then why are boys always the ones who 'chase' girls?"
explanatory_translation: The pun is on "追": first it suggests physically catching up in running, then it shifts to the common expression "追女孩子," meaning to court or pursue a girl romantically.
interpretation_1: 在跑步或行动速度上从后面赶上
interpretation_2: 在恋爱语境中主动追求异性

surface_text: 一天，我正给一顾客介绍上网的好处，我告诉他上网的一大好处是能下载新软件。 这时有人拉我的衣角，回头看去是一妇女，满眼对高科技的崇拜，对上网的憧憬！敬佩万分地指着电脑问到：它？它？？它？？？？它能下崽！！！ 我：O
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中的“它能下崽”被理解为电脑像动物一样能够生崽、繁殖后代。
interpretation_1_en: The woman takes 'xia zai' literally as 'giving birth' or 'producing offspring,' so she thinks the computer can somehow have babies.
interpretation_2_zh: 实际隐含的是把“下载”听成了“下崽”，原意是上网可以把新软件下载到电脑里。
interpretation_2_en: What was actually meant is 'download': the Internet allows a computer to download new software.
context: 介绍上网好处时说“能下载新软件”，听者将“下载”误听并联想到“下崽”
literal_translation: One day, I was explaining to a customer the benefits of going online. I told him that one big benefit was being able to download new software. At that moment, someone tugged at my sleeve. I turned around and saw a woman, her eyes full of admiration for high technology and longing for the Internet. She pointed at the computer and asked with great awe: “It? It?? It???? It can give birth?!” Me: O
functional_equivalence_translation: I told a customer that one advantage of the Internet is that you can download new software. A woman nearby, dazzled by technology, pointed at the computer and gasped, “It can... have babies?!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “下载” (download), which the woman mishears as “下崽,” a colloquial phrase meaning “to give birth to young,” so she absurdly thinks the computer can reproduce.
interpretation_1: 指从网上把软件传输到电脑里
interpretation_2: 被误解为像动物一样生育幼崽

surface_text: 5岁的女儿芳芳随我去朋友的公司，上了二楼，女儿指着一办公室门上的标牌问我上面写的什么字。我告诉她是“董事长”，女儿随即问我：“妈妈，在你们公司，就数他最懂事吗？”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“董事长”是公司的职务名称，指公司董事会的负责人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child interprets '董事长' by linking it to '懂事', so she asks whether he is the most well-behaved and sensible person in the company.
interpretation_2_zh: 女儿把“董事长”听成了“懂事长”，理解为“最懂事的人”，所以才会问他是不是公司里最懂事的人。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '董事长' actually means the chairman of the board, a corporate title, and has nothing to do with being '懂事' in the sense of being obedient or sensible.
context: 孩子看到办公室门牌“董事长”，因“董事”与“懂事”同音而按儿童常识重新解读。
literal_translation: I told her it said “chairman of the board,” and she immediately asked, “Mom, in your company, is he the most sensible one?”
functional_equivalence_translation: I said the sign read “chairman,” and my daughter asked, “So he’s the one who behaves the best in your company?”
explanatory_translation: The joke is that “董事长” (chairman) sounds the same as “懂事长,” a nonstandard phrase that can be understood as “the one who is most sensible/well-behaved,” so the child misinterprets the job title.
interpretation_1: 门牌上的职位名称，指公司里的董事长。
interpretation_2: 被孩子误解为“最懂事、很会懂事的人”。

surface_text: 儿子问老公：张飞他妈姓什么？老公：不知道。儿子：笨，姓吴，无事生非都不知道。儿子再问：张飞他爸姓什么？老公思索半天，猛拍脑门：不知道！儿子狂笑：笨死了！姓张！你不跟你爸姓呀。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上儿子借成语“无事生非”来提问，说的是“没事找事、凭空惹麻烦”的常见意思。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child says Zhang Fei's mother is surnamed Wu because of the phrase 'wu shi sheng fei' ('making trouble out of nothing'), treating 'Wu' as if it directly reveals her surname.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上把“无事生非”谐化为“吴氏生飞”，意思是张飞的妈妈姓吴，由吴氏生下张飞。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a wordplay on the first syllable 'wu' in the idiom 'wu shi sheng fei,' which sounds like the surname Wu, creating a joke by extracting a family name from an unrelated expression.
context: 父子/母子间用“张飞他妈姓什么、他爸姓什么”做脑筋急转弯，前一个答案靠成语“无事生非”引出“吴”，后一个答案靠“子随父姓”的常识引出“张”。
literal_translation: The son asked his dad: What is Zhang Fei's mother's surname? Dad: Don't know. Son: Stupid, it's Wu; don't you even know 'making trouble out of nothing'? Then the son asked again: What is Zhang Fei's father's surname? Dad thought for a long time and suddenly slapped his forehead: Don't know! The son burst out laughing: So stupid! It's Zhang! Don't you take your father's surname?
functional_equivalence_translation: Kid: What's Zhang Fei's mom's surname? Dad: No idea. Kid: Wu—haven't you heard the pun in 'making trouble out of nothing'? Then: What's Zhang Fei's dad's surname? Dad thinks hard. Kid laughs: Zhang, of course—you take your father's surname, don't you?
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges less on sound and more on a semantic twist: the second question sounds like a riddle, but the answer is just the ordinary rule that a child usually shares the father's surname, so Zhang Fei's father is also surnamed Zhang.
interpretation_1: 问答层面上，张飞的爸爸当然也姓张。
interpretation_2: 借“你不跟你爸姓吗”这一日常认知反过来嘲笑回答者，把常识题伪装成脑筋急转弯。

surface_text: “对付庞太师不能掉以轻心。本府需要上策！上策！”包拯自言自语。 一旁的公孙策闻言，默默的躺在了床上。
男：“我们相处这么长时间了，在感情上不但没有发展，而似乎越来越淡漠了。” 女：“你知道吗，感情是有媒介的！”
丈夫斥责妻子道：这就是你烧得菜吗？蜡蜡黄的！还叫‘青’菜吗？ 哪里，叶绿素还是有一点的。谁叫你每天回家这么晚，当然不知道它们在我的锅铲上曾经也‘青春’过。
小明：“爸爸，为什么皇帝要自称是天子？” 爸爸：“因为皇帝自认为是天的儿子嘛！” 小明：“那你是奶奶的儿子，为什么你不叫自己奶子？” 爸爸：“%￥”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中，小明按“天子=天的儿子”的构词方式类推出“奶奶的儿子=奶子”，把“奶子”当成“奶奶的儿子”的简称来理解。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child reasons literally: since an emperor calls himself the 'Son of Heaven' because he is Heaven's son, then a man who is his mother's son should call himself 'milk son' in the same pattern.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含中，“奶子”在汉语里是固定俗称，通常指女性乳房，因此与正常称呼“儿子”形成语义错位，造成笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '奶子' is also a vulgar colloquial term for breasts, so the child's wordplay accidentally turns a kinship-based title into an embarrassing body-related expression.
context: 皇帝自称“天子”被解释为“天的儿子”，小明据此把“奶奶的儿子”机械类推出“奶子”。
literal_translation: Xiaoming: “Dad, why does the emperor call himself the Son of Heaven?” Dad: “Because the emperor thinks he is Heaven’s son!” Xiaoming: “Then you are grandma’s son, so why don’t you call yourself ‘milk-son’?” Dad: “%￥”
functional_equivalence_translation: Xiaoming: “Why did emperors call themselves the Son of Heaven?” Dad: “Because they saw themselves as Heaven’s sons.” Xiaoming: “Then since you’re Grandma’s son, why not call yourself the Son of Granny?” Dad: “...”
explanatory_translation: The joke comes from treating “Son of Heaven” as a literal word-building pattern: “X’s son = X-son.” Xiaoming then wrongly applies it to “grandma’s son,” producing “奶子 (naizi),” which in Chinese commonly means “breasts,” creating the pun.
interpretation_1: 按类推把“天子”的构词方式套用到“奶奶的儿子”上，得到“奶子”。
interpretation_2: “奶子”在汉语中通常指女性乳房，因而产生歧义和笑点。

surface_text: 牛妈妈对鸡妈妈说：生小牛是累死疼死，你生小鸡时为什么笑的咯咯的啊？鸡妈妈说：因为生蛋快乐嘛！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层说的是鸡妈妈生蛋，所以说“生蛋快乐”，把下蛋这件事说成快乐的原因。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the chicken mother says she laughs while laying eggs because laying eggs is a happy thing.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用了“圣诞快乐”的谐音表达，把“圣诞”替换成“生蛋”，形成与鸡会下蛋相关的双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a play on the phrase 'Shengdan kuaile,' which sounds like 'Merry Christmas,' so '生蛋快乐' humorously replaces '圣诞快乐.'
context: 牛妈妈问鸡妈妈为什么生小鸡时笑得咯咯叫，鸡妈妈回答“因为生蛋快乐嘛”。
literal_translation: "Giving eggs is happiness," said the hen mother.
functional_equivalence_translation: Because laying eggs is egg-citing!
explanatory_translation: The joke replaces the usual greeting “Merry Christmas” with a similar-sounding phrase meaning “laying eggs happily,” because the speaker is a hen.
interpretation_1: 鸡妈妈说自己生蛋时很快乐，字面上是“生蛋很快乐”。
interpretation_2: 借“生蛋快乐”谐音“圣诞快乐”，制造幽默效果。

surface_text: 明朝礼部右侍郎程敏政十岁时，以神童被推荐到京城。宰相李贤打算招他为婿，便设宴招待他。席间，李贤指着桌上的果品出个对子让他对：因荷（何）而得藕（偶）。 李贤这样做，一是为了考考程敏政的学问和智力，二是为了探探他对婚事的意见。程敏政当即猜测到了李贤的意思，随口答道：有杏（幸）不须梅（媒）。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上借席间果品作对，说的是因为荷花而得到莲藕，又有杏子就不需要梅子，字面都在说桌上的水果草木之物。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the line talks about fruits and plants on the table: 'How did one get lotus root because of the lotus?' and the reply says, 'If there are apricots, there is no need for plums.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上利用同音转义，实际是“因何而得偶，有幸不须媒”，意思是问为何能得到佳偶、是否愿结亲；回答则表示若有幸成就婚事，便不必再靠媒人撮合。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from sound-based substitution: '荷' sounds like '何' and '藕' like '偶', so it means 'For what reason did I get a spouse?' The reply '杏' sounds like '幸' and '梅' like '媒', meaning 'If I am fortunate, I do not need a matchmaker,' implying acceptance of the marriage proposal.
context: 相府设宴，席上以果品“荷、藕、杏、梅”出对，暗探婚事态度；程敏政借果名谐音回应婚配之意。
literal_translation: If there are apricots, there is no need for plums.
functional_equivalence_translation: If I’m fortunate, I need no matchmaker.
explanatory_translation: On the surface, he says that if there are apricots on the table, plums are unnecessary; underneath, “杏” sounds like “幸” and “梅” like “媒”, meaning that if he is lucky enough to get the marriage, there is no need for a matchmaker.
interpretation_1: 表面上说席间有杏子，就不需要梅子了。
interpretation_2: 实际上借“杏/幸”“梅/媒”表示若有幸成婚，就不必再请媒人撮合。

surface_text: 她很会保养，车保养得新，自己也保养得像刚毕业。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“保养”指她对汽车定期维护、清洁和检查，使车辆状态良好、外观看起来很新。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means she is good at maintenance: she keeps her car well maintained so it looks new, and she also takes good care of herself so she looks like a fresh graduate.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“保养”指她注重护肤和生活管理，因此外貌显年轻，整体状态保持得非常好。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '保养' shifts from mechanical maintenance for a car to beauty and anti-aging care for a person, highlighting the same word being used in two different semantic domains.
context: 同一句中先说“车保养得新”，再说“自己也保养得像刚毕业”，同一词分别作用于车和人。
negative_example: 她很会保修，车保修得新，自己也保修得像刚毕业。
literal_translation: She is very good at maintenance: she keeps her car well maintained and new, and she also keeps herself looking like she just graduated.
functional_equivalence_translation: She really knows how to keep things up—her car looks brand-new, and so does she, like she just graduated.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “保养,” which can mean maintaining a car and also taking care of one’s appearance/body. The sentence juxtaposes these two senses: her car is well maintained, and she herself is so well cared for that she looks freshly graduated.
interpretation_1: 指对汽车进行维护和养护，使车况保持很新。
interpretation_2: 指对人进行美容、护肤和身体调理，使人显得年轻。

surface_text: 这位销售真会聊，客户能聊下来，订单也能聊下来。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“聊下来”指他通过交流把客户留住，使对方愿意继续听、继续谈，不轻易离开。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the salesperson is very good at talking, and through conversation both the client and the order can be 'talked down' or brought along by chatting.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“聊下来”指他最终能把合作谈成，把订单通过沟通真正促成并落实下来。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '聊下来' shifts from literally chatting someone into staying engaged to successfully negotiating and securing the deal.
context: 销售与客户沟通的语境中，前一个“聊下来”对应客户态度缓和，后一个“聊下来”对应订单达成
literal_translation: This salesperson is really good at chatting: customers can be chatted down, and orders can also be chatted down.
functional_equivalence_translation: This salesperson can talk customers over—and talk deals through.
explanatory_translation: This salesperson is very good at talking: he can win customers over through conversation, and he can also talk an order into being, using the repeated phrase “聊下来” with two related meanings.
interpretation_1: 把客户通过聊天安抚或说服下来，愿意继续沟通
interpretation_2: 把订单谈成、拿下来

surface_text: 自从用了这个收纳柜，我终于过上“有盒生活”，找数据线不用考古，找药也不用开奖。
hidden_form: 有何生活 / 盒装收纳生活
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指物品都被装进盒子、分类明确的收纳生活。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a neatly organized life in which things are stored in boxes by category.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义仿拟“有何”或“有序生活”式表达，强调收纳之后生活品质明显提升。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it imitates expressions like 'what kind of life' or 'orderly life', suggesting that boxed organization upgrades one's quality of life.
context: 适用于家居收纳产品、生活博主分享和居家整理文案。
literal_translation: Ever since I started using this storage cabinet, I have finally lived a 'boxed life': I no longer need archaeology to find a charging cable, nor a lottery draw to find medicine.
functional_equivalence_translation: Since I got this organizer, I'm living the 'boxed-up life'—no more excavating for cables or gambling to find medicine.
explanatory_translation: The expression plays with a near-sounding phrase while foregrounding 'box' as the key morpheme, making storage boxes stand for an upgraded and more orderly lifestyle.
interpretation_1: 盒装分类的生活
interpretation_2: 收纳提升生活质量

surface_text: 背景：我姐刚生完宝宝。 昨晚在饭桌上，我当着全家人的面，对我姐说：“你现在比你生前瘦多了。” 于是，整个世界安静了…
interpretation_1_zh: 表层字面上把“生前”理解为“去世之前”，像是在说她现在比活着的时候还瘦，因而造成强烈失言效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker meant: now you are much thinner than before you gave birth.
interpretation_2_zh: 实际想表达的是“生产前、怀孕前”的意思，即她刚生完宝宝后比生孩子之前更瘦了。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning triggered by the wording is: you are much thinner than before you died, because “生前” is usually understood as “during one’s lifetime,” implying the sister is dead.
context: 姐姐刚生完宝宝，饭桌上谈论产后身材变化，说话人本意是比较她现在和生孩子前的体型。
literal_translation: You are much thinner now than you were before your death.
functional_equivalence_translation: You’re much thinner now than you were before the delivery—though I accidentally said “before your death.”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “生前,” which normally means “before death,” but the speaker intended it as a shortened form of “生产前” (“before childbirth”), creating an awkward and darkly comic misunderstanding.
interpretation_1: 按常规理解是“去世之前”，让人误以为在说姐姐已死。
interpretation_2: 实际想表达的是“生产前、生孩子前”，即姐姐现在比生宝宝前更瘦。

surface_text: 大一时，我们教官特逗，两个门牙全掉了，一次我们歌唱比赛，上面报幕，下一首：哭沙。 过一会又报幕：同一首歌。 教官不解：还唱一遍？
interpretation_1_zh: 报幕中的“同一首歌”是歌曲名，表示接下来要演唱这首叫《同一首歌》的作品。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, “同一首歌” means “the same song,” so the instructor thinks they are going to sing the same song once again.
interpretation_2_zh: 教官因门牙掉了、发音受影响，把“同一首歌”误听成“同一首歌再唱一次”，理解为前一首歌还要重唱一遍，所以才会问“还唱一遍？”
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that “同一首歌” is actually the title of a specific song/program, not an instruction to repeat the previous song.
context: 报幕先说“下一首：哭沙”，随后又说“同一首歌”；教官因掉了门牙，对“首”的听辨或发音联想到别的说法，误解为重复演唱。
literal_translation: In freshman year, our drill instructor was very funny. He had lost both front teeth. Once at our singing contest, the announcer said: Next one: Crying Sand. After a while the announcer said again: The same song. The instructor was puzzled: Sing it again?
functional_equivalence_translation: Back in freshman year, our drill instructor had lost his front teeth. At a singing contest, the host announced one song, then later said, “the same number.” He got confused and thought, “What, we’re performing it again?”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese classifier “首” for songs in “同一首歌” (“the same song”). Because the instructor had lost his front teeth, speech or hearing around that sound is humorously distorted, so he misparses it and thinks they mean repeating the song, leading to “Sing it again?”
interpretation_1: “同一首歌”中的“首”是歌曲的量词，表示同一支歌。
interpretation_2: 教官因缺门牙发音受影响，把“首”听成“口”，理解成“同一口歌”，进而误会为还要再唱一遍。

surface_text: 这家理发店推出学生套餐，宣传语是：开学别慌，先把发型整出“新学风”。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指新学期换个新发型、新风格，给人焕然一新的感觉。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means getting a fresh hairstyle and look for the new semester.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含借用“学风”这一校园词，把它转成外形风格表达，形成校园气质与发型更新的双重联想。
interpretation_2_en: It blends a hairstyle makeover with the campus notion of 'study ethos,' making personal style sound like a school-season refresh.
context: 适用于校园周边商家、开学季广告、学生消费场景。
literal_translation: This barber shop launched a student package: don't panic about school starting, first style yourself into a 'new study-style wind.'
