functional_equivalence_translation: New semester, new cut, new campus vibe.
explanatory_translation: The hybrid expression reuses 'study ethos' from campus discourse and blends it with 'new semester style,' so it points to both academic atmosphere and personal appearance.
interpretation_1: 新学期新造型
interpretation_2: 借校园学风

surface_text: 这家面包店新出的低糖吐司被叫作“轻碳主食”，吃起来负担轻，发朋友圈也显得很自律。
hidden_form: 低碳 / 轻负担 / 主食
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指一种吃起来更轻负担、强调低糖低负担的主食产品。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a staple food marketed as light and low-burden.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义激活“低碳”概念，把“碳水”与“轻”嫁接，暗示少碳水、少负罪感的健康饮食。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning evokes the idea of low-carb eating by blending 'light' with 'carb,' implying less guilt and a healthier diet.
phonological_relation: 近形近义联想，无明显语音关系
context: 适用于烘焙店、轻食品牌或健身饮食相关文案。
literal_translation: The bakery's new low-sugar toast is called a 'light-carb staple'; it feels light to eat and disciplined to post online.
functional_equivalence_translation: This bakery brands its low-sugar toast as a 'light-carb staple'—easy on your body and good for your image.
explanatory_translation: The pun works by blending the adjective 'light' with 'carb/staple food' language, creating a coined phrase that literally sounds like a product category while implicitly pointing to low-carb, low-guilt eating.
interpretation_1: 轻负担主食
interpretation_2: 低碳饮食暗示

surface_text: 我的姐夫是一位计算机迷。 有一天，我的姐姐从商店转了一圈后回到家里，把她新买的那件睡衣举了起来，要姐夫评价。我的姐夫回答道：好漂亮的软件！
开车路过一个加油站，老公看看车也快没有油了， 对老婆说：“亲爱的，我去上个厕所，你来加油好不好？” 老婆妩媚一笑：“亲爱的，没问题！” 老公走进了厕所，5秒钟后， 听见老婆在门外大喊：“老公加油！老公加油！老公加油！……”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中“加油”是指在加油站给汽车添加燃油，老公让老婆替车加油。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '加油' means to refuel the car at the gas station while the husband goes to the restroom.
interpretation_2_zh: 老婆在厕所门外喊“老公加油”时，把“加油”转成了给人打气、鼓劲的意思，形成对老公上厕所的戏谑催促。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '加油' also means 'come on' or 'go for it,' so the wife shouts it outside the restroom as if cheering her husband on while he is using the toilet.
context: 在加油站，丈夫说自己去上厕所，让妻子来“加油”；妻子随后在厕所门外对丈夫大喊“老公加油”
literal_translation: While driving past a gas station, the husband saw the car was almost out of gas and said to his wife, “Honey, I’m going to the restroom. Can you do the refueling?” The wife smiled charmingly and said, “No problem, honey!” The husband went into the restroom, and five seconds later he heard his wife shouting outside, “Honey, go! Honey, go! Honey, go!...”
functional_equivalence_translation: At a gas station, the husband said, “Honey, I’m off to the bathroom. You take care of the gas, okay?” A moment later, from outside the restroom came his wife’s voice: “Go, honey, go! Go, honey, go!”
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “加油,” which in Chinese can mean both “to pump gas” and “to cheer someone on.” The husband meant “refuel the car,” but the wife interprets it as “encourage you,” so she stands outside the restroom shouting “Come on, honey!”
interpretation_1: 给汽车添加燃油
interpretation_2: 为人鼓劲、喊加油

surface_text: 老鼠心里不平衡去找黑猫警长理论：“我说你这警察也太不公道了吧？为什么黄鼠狼偷鸡你不管，偏管我们小偷小摸，还死守我家门口不放？ 黑猫答：“我是国内行警不是国际刑警，他是日本人我管不了。” 老鼠：“你怎么知道他是日本人？” 黑猫：“听名字不就知道了，‘皇叔郎’，只有日本人名字才这个君，那个郎的，这点常识你就不懂？还在江湖混啥！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中把“黄鼠狼”说成了一个像日本人姓名的“皇叔郎”，黑猫据此解释为对方是日本人，所以自己这个国内警察管不了。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '皇叔郎' is treated as a Japanese-style personal name, because names ending with things like 'jun' or 'lang' sound stereotypically Japanese.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“皇叔郎”与“黄鼠狼”的近音关系，把偷鸡者“黄鼠狼”伪装成日式名字，制造“因为像外国人所以不归我管”的荒诞效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '皇叔郎' is actually a playful sound-based reshaping of '黄鼠狼' (weasel). The joke shifts the animal's name into something that sounds like a Japanese name to justify the claim that he is 'Japanese.'
context: 黑猫警长解释自己不是国际刑警，管不了“黄鼠狼”；随后用“黄鼠狼”可谐听成“皇叔郎”来证明对方像日本人名。
literal_translation: The mouse complained that the Black Cat Sheriff ignored the weasel stealing chickens but kept watching their door. The black cat said: I’m a domestic police officer, not Interpol; he’s Japanese, so I can’t handle him. The mouse asked how he knew. The black cat said: Can’t you tell from the name? ‘Huangshulang’ sounds like ‘Huang Shu-lang’; only Japanese names are all this -kun and that -lang.
functional_equivalence_translation: The mouse protested: Why do you ignore the chicken-thieving weasel but keep picking on us petty thieves? Black Cat said: I’m local police, not international police—he’s Japanese, out of my jurisdiction. The mouse asked how he knew. Black Cat replied: From the name, of course—“weasel” sounds like a Japanese-style guy’s name ending in “-ro” or “-lang.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “黄鼠狼” (weasel), which is reanalyzed as the name-like “皇叔郎.” Because “郎” is stereotypically associated with Japanese male names in Chinese comedic speech, Black Cat pretends the weasel is Japanese and therefore beyond his authority.
interpretation_1: 指会偷鸡的动物黄鼠狼。
interpretation_2: 把“黄鼠狼”谐听成像日本男性姓名的“皇叔郎”，借此说成“日本人”。

surface_text: 朋友搬进新房后天天研究收纳，整个人都进入了“柜族生活”：不是贵族，是每面墙都想配个柜子。
hidden_form: 贵族生活 / 柜子一族
interpretation_1_zh: 表层指以柜子、收纳系统为中心的居家生活方式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means a home lifestyle centered around cabinets and storage.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿照“贵族生活”，把爱收纳、爱添置柜子的状态说得像高配人生。
interpretation_2_en: It also echoes 'aristocratic life,' humorously elevating a cabinet-obsessed life into something luxurious.
context: 适用于家居消费、租房装修、收纳博主文案。
literal_translation: After moving into the new apartment, my friend entered 'cabinet-class life': not noble life, but wanting a cabinet on every wall.
functional_equivalence_translation: Since moving in, my friend has been living a full-on cabinet-core lifestyle.
explanatory_translation: The pun replaces the near-sounding 'noble' in 'noble life' with 'cabinet,' creating a hybrid phrase that refers both to organized storage living and a mock-upgraded lifestyle.
interpretation_1: 收纳生活
interpretation_2: 仿贵族感

surface_text: 英文课，湖湖又坐在老师面前第一位。 师曰：suspect，嫌犯。 湖湖于是随手在笔记上写：咸饭。 老师不忍使湖湖难堪，于是老师又抬高音量：suspect，嫌疑犯。 只见湖湖若有所悟，提笔将咸饭改成咸鱼饭。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，湖湖把老师读的英文单词按近似读音记成了“咸饭”，后来又根据“嫌疑犯”进一步改写成“咸鱼饭”，都成了食物名称。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, Huhu mishears the English word “suspect” as similar-sounding Chinese food words, first writing “salty rice” and then changing it to “salted fish rice.”
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是老师实际在讲英文单词“suspect”，对应中文义项应为“嫌犯、嫌疑犯”；“咸饭”“咸鱼饭”是把英文发音误听并转成了食物相关词语的谐音替代。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the teacher is actually teaching the English vocabulary item “suspect,” meaning a criminal suspect or a person under suspicion, but Huhu humorously interprets it through Chinese near-homophones instead.
context: 英语课上老师读单词 suspect 并解释为“嫌犯、嫌疑犯”，学生根据读音进行汉字谐音记录。
literal_translation: In English class, Huhu again sat in the first seat in front of the teacher. The teacher said, “suspect, criminal suspect.” Huhu then casually wrote in the notebook: “salty rice.” The teacher, not wanting to embarrass Huhu, raised the volume and said again: “suspect, suspect.” Huhu seemed to realize something and changed “salty rice” into “salted fish rice.”
functional_equivalence_translation: In English class, the teacher said “suspect,” but the student misheard it as something sounding like “salty rice,” then after hearing “suspect” again, changed it to “salted-fish rice.”
explanatory_translation: The joke is that the English word “suspect” is misheard by the student as Chinese food phrases with similar sounds: first “咸饭” (salty rice), then “咸鱼饭” (salted-fish rice), especially after the teacher says “嫌疑犯” to clarify the meaning.
interpretation_1: 老师在教英文单词 suspect，意思是嫌犯、嫌疑犯。
interpretation_2: 学生把 suspect 按汉语近音误记成“咸饭”，后来又根据“嫌疑犯”扩写成“咸鱼饭”。

surface_text: 这位经理真会盯，数据盯得紧，项目细节也盯得人不敢松。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“盯”指经理会持续关注数据变化，不放过关键指标，管理上非常严密。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the manager keeps a very close watch on the data and the project details.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“盯”指他对项目细节要求严格、持续追踪，让团队成员不敢轻忽懈怠。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it also suggests the manager is so strict and pressuring that people feel intimidated and do not dare relax.
context: 经理管理严格，一方面持续盯数据，另一方面对项目细节抓得很死，让人精神紧绷。
literal_translation: This manager is really good at staring: he stares at the data tightly, and the project details also make people not dare relax.
functional_equivalence_translation: This manager really knows how to keep things nailed down—he watches the data closely, and his grip on project details keeps everyone on edge.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on 盯, meaning to watch closely, while also evoking 钉, “a nail,” because both are pronounced the same in Chinese. It suggests not only close monitoring but also a nail-like pressure that pins people down and keeps them from relaxing.
interpretation_1: 指经理紧紧盯着数据和项目细节，监督很严。
interpretation_2: 借“钉”引出像钉子一样把人钉住、压得人不敢放松的感觉。

surface_text: 数学课快下了，只剩两道题了。老师说：我做一道，另一道留给你们。你们挑吧！有同学道：老师，你做难的。老师说：我做男的，你们做女的啊？
interpretation_1_zh: 学生本意是让老师做较难的那道题，"难的"指难度更高的题目。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the student means: 'Teacher, please do the difficult one.' Here, '难的' means the harder math problem.
interpretation_2_zh: 老师故意把"难的"听成近音的"男的"，把做题对象歪解成性别分类，于是说成"我做男的，你们做女的"，形成双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning comes from a sound-based shift: '难的' is jokingly misheard as '男的' ('male one'). So the teacher pretends the student said, 'I’ll do the male one, and you do the female one,' creating the pun.
context: 数学课快下课，还剩两道题；学生说“老师，你做难的”，老师故意误解为“男的”，并对应说“你们做女的”。
literal_translation: Math class is almost over, and there are only two problems left. The teacher said: I'll do one, and leave the other to you. You choose. A student said: Teacher, do the hard one. The teacher said: I'll do the male one, and you do the female one?
functional_equivalence_translation: With only two math problems left, a student says, “Teacher, you take the tough one.” The teacher jokes, “The guy one? Then you take the girl one?”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese near-homophone between “难的” (the difficult one) and “男的” (the male one). The teacher deliberately mishears the student's request and extends it with “女的” (the female one).
interpretation_1: 学生本意是让老师做较难的那道题。
interpretation_2: 老师故意把“难的”听成“男的”，并顺势把另一道说成“女的”，把题目难易转成性别分类来制造笑点。

surface_text: 楼下早餐摊把豆浆套餐叫“醒福配方”，上班路上喝一口，嘴里是热的，人生也像刚开机。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指能让人清醒提神的一份早餐组合。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a breakfast combo that wakes you up and energizes you.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含仿拟“幸福配方”，表示简单热早餐就是普通人早晨的小幸福来源。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it parodies 'the formula for happiness', suggesting that a warm breakfast is a small but real happiness for everyday people.
context: 适用于早餐店广告、城市生活文案或通勤情绪表达。
negative_example: 这份早餐很幸福，也很提神。
literal_translation: The breakfast stall downstairs calls its soy milk combo the 'wake-happiness formula'.
functional_equivalence_translation: For commuters, this breakfast is both a wake-up fix and a little dose of happiness.
explanatory_translation: The pun modifies the familiar phrase 'formula for happiness' by replacing the first syllable with a near-homophone meaning 'to wake up', making breakfast about both alertness and comfort.
interpretation_1: 提神早餐组合
interpretation_2: 早餐是小幸福

surface_text: 他不是在旅游，是在进行“特种兵式省钱游”：白天暴走打卡，晚上在预算里打持久战。
hidden_form: 特种兵式旅游 / 省钱游
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是指一种高强度、压缩时间且强调节省预算的旅游方式。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a high-intensity, time-compressed, budget-conscious way of traveling.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借用“特种兵式旅游”的网络说法，再嫁接“省钱游”，强调既拼体力也拼省钱能力。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning borrows the internet phrase 'special-forces-style travel' and grafts it onto 'budget travel', stressing both physical endurance and money-saving skill.
context: 适用于旅游分享、社交媒体段子或消费观讨论。
negative_example: 他这次出去旅游很省钱，住得比较简单。
literal_translation: He isn't just traveling; he's doing 'special-forces-style budget travel': walking everywhere by day and fighting a prolonged battle with the budget at night.
functional_equivalence_translation: He's not just traveling—he's doing a boot-camp version of budget travel: max mileage, minimum spending.
explanatory_translation: This pun-like construction imitates the popular internet template 'special-forces-style X' and inserts 'budget travel', creating a hybrid phrase that combines intensity and frugality.
interpretation_1: 高强度穷游方式
interpretation_2: 套用网络模板强调又拼又省

surface_text: 一对恋人在公路上散步，迎面跑来一条疯狗，男的扔下女的撒腿就跑。 女：亲爱的，你以前不是经常对我发誓吗？为了我，你是不怕死的呀！ 男：可是，那条狗是活的呀！
爸爸打电话告诉儿子，说今晚有应酬，不能回来吃饭了。 儿子问：什么叫应酬？ 爸爸说：不想去，又不得不去的叫应酬。 第二天早上儿子上学时，说道：爸爸，我要去应酬了。
同事给自动回复取名“已读薪安”，消息虽然回得慢，但工资到账时心里还能保持平安。
hidden_form: 一路心安 / 已读 / 薪水
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是消息显示已读，借工资让人心安，带有职场自动回复的幽默感。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to a read-receipt style auto-reply that brings peace of mind through salary talk.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“薪”嵌入“心安”式表达，调侃上班人的核心安慰其实来自发薪。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it inserts 'salary' into a phrase of peace of mind, joking that workers' real emotional security comes from payday.
context: 适用于职场社交媒体段子、聊天状态文案、办公室幽默。
negative_example: 消息已读，请安心等待回复。
literal_translation: A colleague named the auto-reply 'read-and-salary-peace'; although messages are replied to slowly, the heart can still stay at peace when salary arrives.
functional_equivalence_translation: The auto-reply is basically: seen your message, surviving on payday peace.
explanatory_translation: The pun combines 'read' with a near-sounding reformulation of 'peace of mind,' replacing the emotional core with 'salary' to express a workplace truth through hybrid wording.
interpretation_1: 已读后的职场回复
interpretation_2: 工资才让人心安

surface_text: 上班了第一次看见老板心里很紧张，同事介绍说这个就是老板。 我上前握手说道；老表好！ ……汗死
interpretation_1_zh: 说话者把“老板”误说成了“老表”，字面上是在向对方称呼为表亲、熟人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker mistakenly greets the boss by saying “laobiao,” treating it as a normal form of address like “cousin” or a colloquial greeting.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的原本想表达的是“老板好”，是在初次见面时向老板打招呼，只是因近音误替换造成尴尬效果。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the speaker confuses “laoban” (boss) with the similar-sounding “laobiao,” creating an embarrassing pun caused by a pronunciation slip.
context: 初次上班见到上司，同事介绍“这个就是老板”，说话人因谐音误听，上前说成“老表好”。
literal_translation: It was my first time at work and I was very nervous when I saw the boss. A colleague introduced him, saying, “This is the boss.” I stepped forward to shake hands and said, “Hello, cousin!” ... So embarrassing.
functional_equivalence_translation: On my first day at work, a coworker said, “This is the boss,” and I nervously went up to shake his hand and said, “Nice to meet you, cuz!” ... Mortifying.
explanatory_translation: The joke is that “laoban” (boss) is misheard as “laobiao/laobiao”-like “laobiao/laobiao” here written as “laobiao/老表,” a familiar way to address a cousin or fellow, so the speaker accidentally greets the boss with the wrong, overly casual title.
interpretation_1: 同事介绍的是公司的老板，即上司。
interpretation_2: 说话人误把“老板”听成了“老表”，把对方当成可随便称呼的熟人或亲戚式称呼。

surface_text: 物理课上老师问阿摩尔：你知道什么是电阻，什么是电源吗？ 阿摩尔回答道：店主（电阻）就是商店的老板，店员（电源）就是商店的伙计。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本把“电阻”“电源”分别听解成“店主”“店员”，于是回答成商店里老板和伙计的意思。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, Amor misunderstands the physics terms as ordinary shop-related words: a shop owner is the boss of a store, and a shop assistant is the clerk working there.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的原始表达其实是物理概念“电阻”和“电源”，老师问的是电学术语，而不是商店中的人物身份。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the words are actually puns on the physics terms 'electrical resistance' and 'power source,' which sound similar to 'shop owner' and 'shop assistant' in Chinese.
context: 物理课上老师提问电学术语，学生故意或误将术语按同音词改解为商店相关词语。
literal_translation: In physics class, the teacher asked Amor: Do you know what resistance and a power source are? Amor answered: The shop owner is the boss of the store, and the shop assistant is the clerk of the store.
functional_equivalence_translation: In physics class, the teacher asked, “What are resistance and power supply?” Amor replied, “You mean the shop boss and the shop clerk?”
explanatory_translation: The pun relies on Chinese homophones: “电阻” (electrical resistance) sounds the same as “店主” (shop owner), and “电源” (power source) sounds the same as “店员” (shop assistant), so the student humorously misinterprets physics terms as store-related words.
interpretation_1: 在物理课语境中，“电阻”和“电源”分别指电学概念中的 resistance 和 power source。
interpretation_2: 阿摩尔把“电阻”听成“店主”，把“电源”听成“店员”，理解成商店里的人物角色。

surface_text: 清醒，就是庆幸。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“清醒”说成一种值得庆幸的状态，意思是人保持清醒本身就是可喜、可感到庆幸的事。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the sentence means that being clear-headed and awake is something fortunate and worth feeling grateful for.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上借“清醒”与“庆幸”的近音关系，把“清醒”引向“庆幸”这一情感评价，表达清醒之后会觉得自己很幸运、很值得庆幸。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning plays on the near sound and conceptual link between 'clear-minded' and 'fortunate,' suggesting that staying sober, rational, or mentally awake is itself a blessing.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境：说话者经历或见证某事后，强调头脑清楚本身就是一种值得庆幸的状态。
literal_translation: To be sober is to be fortunate.
functional_equivalence_translation: Staying clear-headed is a blessing.
explanatory_translation: The line plays on the near sound between "qingxing" (clear-headed, sober) and "qingxing"/"qingxing-like" "庆幸" (to feel fortunate), suggesting that being mentally clear is itself something to be grateful for.
interpretation_1: 保持头脑清楚、不糊涂。
interpretation_2: 因看清现实而感到庆幸、幸运。

surface_text: 下课点名，如果没来期末成绩将被扣掉50分！念到一兄弟时不知怎么就跳了过去，于是他大喊一声：老师，你漏点了！ 年逾花甲的老教师低头看看了说：没有啊！
interpretation_1_zh: 学生的意思是老师点名时把自己漏掉了，没有点到自己的名字。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the student means, 'Teacher, you missed calling my name during roll call,' where '漏点' is understood as 'left someone out when checking attendance.'
interpretation_2_zh: “漏点”谐音激活了“露点”，老教师低头查看身体，以为是在说自己是否有身体敏感部位外露。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is a sexual one: '漏点' can also mean 'a nipple/body part accidentally exposed,' so the old teacher misunderstands it as the student saying he has had a wardrobe slip.
context: 课堂下课前老师点名，学生因自己被跳过而喊“老师，你漏点了”，老师将其听成“露点了”。
literal_translation: At roll call after class, if absent, 50 points will be deducted from the final grade. When the teacher somehow skipped one student, he shouted: Teacher, you missed a spot! The elderly teacher looked down and said: No, I didn't!
functional_equivalence_translation: During roll call, a student who got skipped yelled, “Teacher, you missed me!” But it sounded like “You’re showing something,” so the old teacher looked down and said, “No, I’m not!”
explanatory_translation: The pun is on “漏点” (to miss someone during roll call, short for “漏点名”) and “露点” (to expose a private body part). The student means he was skipped in attendance, but the teacher mishears it as an embarrassing remark.
interpretation_1: 学生说老师点名时把自己漏掉了。
interpretation_2: 老教师误听为“露点”，理解成身体敏感部位露出来了。

surface_text: 这家面馆真讲究，面条讲究，连收银台摆得都很讲究。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“讲究”指面条从选料、火候到口感都做得精细，体现出制作上的认真与品质。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '讲究' means carefully made or well-arranged: the noodles are particular about quality, and even the cashier counter is neatly and tastefully set up.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“讲究”指店内陈设、细节布置都有审美与用心，说明整体经营风格也很精致。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '讲究' also suggests this noodle shop is refined, fastidious, and pays attention to details overall, praising the shop's style and standards beyond the literal arrangement.
context: 同一句中先说面条讲究，再说收银台也讲究，使同一词在食物制作和空间布置两个对象上并列生效。
literal_translation: This noodle shop is really particular: the noodles are particular, and even the cashier counter is arranged in a very particular way.
functional_equivalence_translation: This noodle shop really has taste: the noodles are carefully made, and even the checkout counter is stylishly arranged.
explanatory_translation: This noodle shop is really 'particular': the word first means the noodles are carefully made, and then it shifts to mean the cashier area is tastefully arranged.
interpretation_1: 指面条制作讲究，做工和用料都较为精细。
interpretation_2: 指收银台摆设讲究，装修布置有品位、很精致。

surface_text: 中午食堂吃饭，打了一份回锅肉， 小明一看里面都是土豆片子， 小明就问给自己打菜的人：“师傅。。肉呢？” 他还没说话呢，小明后面的一个二货接着说：“回锅里去了。” 小明：就你话多！！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层里“回锅肉”是菜名，指一种炒制的猪肉菜，小明点的是这道菜，但看到菜里几乎只有土豆片，才会追问肉在哪里。
interpretation_1_en: The dish is called 'twice-cooked pork,' and the joke takes 'hui guo' literally as 'returned to the wok,' as if the missing meat has gone back into the pot.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里把“回锅”从菜名成分转成字面意思“回到锅里”，于是“回锅肉”被戏谑地理解成肉又回锅里去了，所以眼前只剩配菜。
interpretation_2_en: In the dish name 'twice-cooked pork,' 'hui guo' is just the fixed culinary term meaning the pork is cooked again in a wok, not that the meat literally 'went back to the pot' after being served.
context: 食堂里打了一份名为“回锅肉”的菜，但盘里几乎只有土豆片，没有肉；有人把菜名“回锅肉”中的“回锅”按字面理解为“回到锅里”。
literal_translation: At noon in the cafeteria, Xiaoming got a serving of twice-cooked pork. Seeing that it was full of potato slices, he asked the server, “Master... where’s the meat?” Before the server could answer, a fool behind him said, “It went back into the pot.” Xiaoming: You talk too much!
functional_equivalence_translation: At lunch Xiaoming ordered twice-cooked pork, but it was basically all potatoes. He asked, “Where’s the pork?” Someone behind him joked, “Well, it’s called twice-cooked—it went back for another round in the wok.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the dish name “回锅肉” (twice-cooked pork). Normally “回锅” is just part of the fixed name of the dish, but the heckler interprets it literally as “went back into the pot,” implying the missing meat has returned to the wok.
interpretation_1: 表层上是在说这道菜名叫“回锅肉”。
interpretation_2: 隐含上把“回锅”按字面拆解为“又回到锅里去了”，用来戏谑肉不见了。

surface_text: 一老中医向一寡妇求爱，未料那寡妇另有所爱，拒绝了他炽烈的追求。老中医非常失望。 一天，老中医的朋友问他：你和那中年寡妇处得怎么样了？ 老中医叹口气道：唉！别提了！这块陈皮，我却挨不得半下！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把那位中年寡妇比作中药“陈皮”，说自己连这味药都碰不得一下，带有老中医说话的行业色彩。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "chenpi" means dried tangerine peel, a common ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine. The old doctor is joking that this piece of chenpi is something he cannot even touch.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含里是把“陈皮”谐转为“人皮”，意思是这个女人他连碰都碰不得，表达求爱被拒、无法亲近对方的失意。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that "chenpi" also points to the older widowed woman he was courting. He means that this "mature woman" is someone he could not get close to or win over at all.
context: 老中医追求一位寡妇失败，朋友问进展时，他用中药名来比喻这位女人，说“这块陈皮，我却挨不得半下”。
literal_translation: An old Chinese doctor courted a widow but was rejected. Later he sighed, “Alas, forget it! This piece of dried tangerine peel, I can’t even touch it for a moment!”
functional_equivalence_translation: An old doctor sighed, “Forget it—she’s a tough nut to crack, and I can’t get anywhere with her.”
explanatory_translation: The doctor uses “陈皮” (dried tangerine peel, a Chinese medicinal ingredient) as a punning label for the widow. On the surface it is a herb name; underneath it suggests a woman he cannot get close to or “handle,” conveying romantic frustration.
interpretation_1: 表层指中药材“陈皮”，老中医把寡妇比作一味药材。
interpretation_2: 隐含借“陈皮”谐指难以下手、令人郁闷的对象，表达自己碰不得、追不到她的失意。

surface_text: 一个女人对一个男人说：你知道世上什么最坚强？ 男的说：不知道。 那女人说：你的胡子。 男人说：为什么？ 因为你的脸皮这么厚它还能破皮而出。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上说男人脸上的皮肤很厚，所以胡子还能从厚厚的脸皮里长出来，显得“胡子最坚强”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'face skin' refers literally to the man's skin being so thick that his beard can still grow out through it.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借“脸皮厚”转指男人厚颜无耻、不知羞耻，即“厚脸皮”，是在用双关讽刺他。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that 'thick-skinned' means shameless or insensitive, so she is really mocking him for having a lot of nerve.
context: 女人先问“世上什么最坚强”，再回答“你的胡子”，并用“你的脸皮这么厚它还能破皮而出”同时激活“脸皮”的字面义和“厚脸皮”的贬义。
literal_translation: A woman said to a man: Do you know what is the toughest thing in the world? The man said: I don't know. The woman said: Your beard. The man asked: Why? Because your face skin is so thick that it can still break through it and grow out.
functional_equivalence_translation: A woman asked a man, “Know what’s toughest in the world?” He said, “No.” She said, “Your beard.” “Why?” “Because it can still push through your incredibly thick skin—literally and figuratively.”
explanatory_translation: A woman mocks a man by saying his beard is the toughest thing in the world, because it can grow through his very thick “face skin.” In Chinese, “thick face skin” also implies someone is shameless or thick-skinned, so the line insults him while pretending to talk literally about skin.
interpretation_1: 表层是在说男人脸上的皮肤很厚，所以胡子还能长出来。
interpretation_2: 隐含是在骂男人厚脸皮、不要脸。

surface_text: 吃饭时我玩手机，妈抒情的说：把你的小鸡鸡收起来
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是母亲在吃饭时让说话对象把正在玩的手机收起来，其中“小机机”是对“小手机”的戏谑说法。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, she is saying, 'Put away your little penis,' using a vulgar body-part expression.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“小机机”谐转并激活了“小鸡鸡”的说法，使这句话在让人收起手机之外，又带出带有性器官意味的暧昧玩笑效果。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is, 'Put away your phone,' because '小鸡鸡' is a joking phonetic/semantic shift from '小机机,' where '机' refers to a mobile device.
context: 母亲看到说话人吃饭时玩手机，要求把手机收起来；“小鸡鸡”被故意用来代指“手机机/手机”。
literal_translation: While eating I was playing with my phone, and my mom said sentimentally: Put away your little dick.
functional_equivalence_translation: I was on my phone at the dinner table, and Mom joked, “Put that little ‘pecker’ away” — meaning my phone.
explanatory_translation: I was using my phone while eating, and my mom jokingly said, “Put away your little dick.” The humor comes from using “小鸡鸡,” normally a childish/slang term for penis, to jokingly refer to the phone because of similar sound and teasing intent.
interpretation_1: 表层上指男性生殖器的戏谑说法。
interpretation_2: 实际在语境中指说话人吃饭时拿在手里的手机。

surface_text: 有一次上语文课，老师问小百事通：你能解释一下‘特长’的意思吗？ 能！小百事通十分神气他说：特长就是特别的长处。 老师说：对，你现在能用它造个句子吗？ 能！小百事通又十二分神气他说：我叔叔的头发和指甲都特长！
interpretation_1_zh: 句中把“特长”按字面理解为“特别长”，所以说叔叔的头发和指甲都很长。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '特长' is understood literally as 'especially long,' so the sentence means the uncle's hair and nails are very long.
interpretation_2_zh: “特长”原本更常见的意思是“特殊的长处、擅长的技能”，前文老师提问时指的是这个义项。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning of '特长' is 'special skill' or 'particular strength,' referring to someone's area of expertise rather than physical length.
context: 老师先要求解释“特长”的词义，再要求造句；学生把“特长”从名词“长处”误解为偏正短语“特别长”来造句
literal_translation: Once in Chinese class, the teacher asked the know-it-all: Can you explain the meaning of ‘specialty’? Yes! He proudly said: ‘specialty’ means a special strong point. The teacher said: Right, now can you make a sentence with it? Yes! He said even more proudly: My uncle’s hair and fingernails are especially long!
functional_equivalence_translation: In Chinese class, the teacher asked, “What does ‘specialty’ mean?” The boy answered, “A special strong point.” “Good. Now use it in a sentence.” He said, “My uncle’s hair and nails are really extra long!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the Chinese word “特长,” which normally means “specialty” or “strong point,” but the child reinterprets it literally as “特别长” (“especially long”), so he uses it to describe long hair and fingernails.
interpretation_1: 指人的特殊长处、擅长的技能
interpretation_2: 指某物长度上特别长

surface_text: 有个教书先生名叫过江。一次，出个题目叫学生对对：隔河并马，学生把并字听成病字，脱口对道：过江瘟牛。先生听了哭笑不得。
interpretation_1_zh: 学生把上联中的“并”误听成“病”，所以下联对成“过江瘟牛”，字面意思是过江而来的瘟病之牛。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the teacher gives the antithetical phrase '隔河并马,' where '并马' means horses going side by side, and the student answers by matching it with '过江瘟牛.'
interpretation_2_zh: 原本应围绕“并马”来对仗，“并”指并列、成双的马；学生因同音误听，把“并”转成“病”，使语义从马匹并行偏到患病、瘟牛上，形成谐音双关。
interpretation_2_en: The humor comes from mishearing '并' as '病,' shifting the meaning from 'side-by-side horses' to 'sick horses/cattle,' so the reply turns into a ridiculous and insulting phrase that also plays against the teacher's name '过江.'
context: 先生名叫“过江”，出上联“隔河并马”，学生将“并”误听为“病”，据此误对出“过江瘟牛”。
literal_translation: A teacher named Guojiang asked students to match the phrase “across the river, line up horses,” but a student misheard it and blurted out “crossing the river, plague ox.”
functional_equivalence_translation: A teacher named Guojiang set a matching phrase, but a student misheard one word and answered with “Guojiang’s sick ox,” accidentally turning the teacher’s name into part of the joke.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on a mishearing in a couplet exercise: the expected matching phrase is closer to “crossing the river, steadying the ox,” but the student hears a similar-sounding word and says “crossing the river, plague ox.” Since “Guojiang” is also the teacher’s name, the mistaken answer sounds like it is mocking him.
interpretation_1: 按对对子规则，应与“隔河并马”对应，写成“过江稳牛”，表示过江时把牛稳住。
interpretation_2: 学生把“并”误听成“病”，说成“过江瘟牛”，意思变成过江的瘟病之牛，并且“过江”又恰好是先生名字，形成戏谑效果。

surface_text: 博物馆文创上新“盖章青年”系列，年轻人排队不是为了身份认证，是为了把一本空白册子盖成旅行履历。
hidden_form: 斜杠青年 / 盖章打卡
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指热衷于在博物馆、景点收集印章的年轻人群体。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to young people who love collecting stamps at museums and scenic spots.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义把“青年”标签化构词，仿照各种群体称呼，突出一种新的文化消费身份。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it turns 'youth' into a labeled identity, modeled after many social group tags, highlighting a new form of cultural consumption.
context: 适用于文博消费、社交媒体观察和青年文化描述。
literal_translation: The museum has launched a new 'stamp-collecting youth' series; young people line up not for identity verification, but to turn a blank booklet into a travel résumé.
functional_equivalence_translation: The museum's new merch is for 'stamp-collecting youth'—people line up to turn blank booklets into travel records.
explanatory_translation: The pun creates a social identity label by combining 'stamp collecting' with 'youth', turning a simple activity into a recognizable cultural persona.
interpretation_1: 爱收集印章的年轻人
interpretation_2: 新型文化身份标签

surface_text: 一到台上他刚张开嘴，紧张得舌头就像打了结，主持人说你这可真是张口结舌。
淘气的女儿总惹奶奶生气，奶奶实在忍不住了就说：你在不听话，奶奶的脾气一会儿就下来了！ 女儿把奶奶看了半天，奇怪的问：奶奶：你的脾气能下到哪儿去？
这家花店真会搭，花束搭得美，恋爱气氛也被它搭起来了。
interpretation_1_zh: 前一个“搭”指花店在颜色、品种和包装上搭配得巧妙，让花束整体非常协调美观。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, '搭' means to arrange or match things well: the flower shop is good at putting bouquets together beautifully.
interpretation_2_zh: 后一个“搭起来”指花束帮助营造浪漫氛围，把恋爱中的情绪和场景迅速烘托出来。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, '搭' extends to creating or building up a romantic mood, suggesting the shop not only matches flowers well but also helps spark romance.
context: 同一句中先说花束搭得美，再说恋爱气氛也被它搭起来了。
literal_translation: This flower shop is really good at matching: the bouquets are matched beautifully, and it has also matched up the romantic atmosphere.
functional_equivalence_translation: This flower shop really knows how to put things together—the bouquets are beautifully arranged, and they also set the mood for romance.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on 搭, which first means 'to match/arrange' flowers and then shifts to 'to build up/create' a romantic atmosphere.
interpretation_1: 指花束搭配、组合得好看。
interpretation_2: 指把恋爱氛围营造起来、带动起来。

surface_text: 我外甥女五岁，爱吃瓜果蔬菜，长得水灵可爱，就是说话有时候咬字不太清。一天，他从大门外跑进来喊：舅舅舅舅，外面一个卖王八的，你给我买，我要吃我要吃。说着就拉了我的手向外拽。我也好奇：真有来村里卖王八的，这倒要去看看。到了外面一看，原来是个买黄瓜的。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层文本实际所指是外面来了一个卖黄瓜的人，孩子想吃黄瓜。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the child seems to be saying that there is someone outside selling soft-shelled turtles, and she wants to buy some to eat.
interpretation_2_zh: 由于孩子咬字不清，把“黄瓜”说成了“王八”，从而让人误以为外面是在卖王八。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that because of her unclear pronunciation, "huanggua" (cucumber) was misheard as "wangba" (soft-shelled turtle / a term also associated with turtle), so the seller was actually selling cucumbers.
context: 孩子咬字不清；他爱吃瓜果蔬菜；大人出去一看发现其实是卖黄瓜的。
literal_translation: My five-year-old niece loves fruits and vegetables and looks fresh and lovely, but sometimes her pronunciation is unclear. One day she ran in from outside the gate shouting, “Uncle, uncle, there’s someone outside selling soft-shelled turtles. Buy me some, I want to eat them!” She pulled me outside. When I got there, it turned out he was selling cucumbers.
functional_equivalence_translation: My five-year-old niece sometimes muddles her words. One day she rushed in yelling, “Uncle, there’s a guy outside selling turtles—buy me one!” I went out in surprise, only to find it was just a cucumber seller. She had pronounced “cucumber” so badly it sounded like “turtle.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the child’s unclear pronunciation: she says “wangba” (“soft-shelled turtle,” also an insult in Chinese), but what she actually means is “huanggua” (“cucumber”). The humor comes from mistaking a vegetable seller for someone selling turtles.
interpretation_1: 孩子说成了“卖王八的”，表面理解为有人在卖甲鱼或乌龟一类东西。
interpretation_2: 实际所指是“卖黄瓜的”，因为孩子咬字不清把“黄瓜”说得像“王八”。

surface_text: 昨晚奇葩老婆忽然对我说：“皇上，臣妾有一事相求！” “但说无妨。” “恳请将臣妾打入冷宫，臣妾受不了了，这天太热了！” 我…
老师借着这道作文题顺势讲了半节课，同学小声说他又在借题发挥了。
我碰见了骑自行车的校长的秘书。
pun_word: 骑自行车的校长的秘书

surface_text: 经理：是啊！ 应聘者：你看我行吗？ 经理：对不起，我在电话里看不到你。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“看”理解为用眼睛看，应聘者问“你看我行吗”被经理按“你让我看看你”的意思来理解，所以经理回答电话里看不到人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the manager takes 'look' literally: since they are speaking on the phone, he cannot actually see the applicant.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上“你看我行吗”中的“看”是“觉得、认为”的意思，即应聘者真正想问的是经理是否认为自己胜任、是否可以被录用。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the applicant means 'Do you think I am suitable or capable?', but the manager deliberately shifts 'look' from judging suitability to physically seeing.
context: 电话面试场景中，应聘者说“你看我行吗”，经理利用“看”的字面义回应“在电话里看不到你”。
literal_translation: Manager: Yes. Applicant: Do you think I’m suitable? Manager: Sorry, I can’t see you on the phone.
functional_equivalence_translation: Manager: Right. Applicant: So, how do I look for the job? Manager: Sorry, over the phone, I literally can’t look at you.
explanatory_translation: The applicant uses “看我行吗” idiomatically to mean “Do you think I’m qualified?”, but the manager deliberately takes “看” literally as “to see with the eyes,” saying he cannot see the applicant over the phone.
interpretation_1: 应聘者想问自己是否合适、是否可以胜任。
interpretation_2: 经理把“看我行吗”理解成字面上的“看看我这个人”。

surface_text: 新出的收纳软件自称“文件减肥营”，不是让资料消失，而是让桌面终于不再虚胖。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把文件整理过程说成减肥训练，突出压缩和清理功能。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it frames file organization as a weight-loss camp, highlighting compression and cleanup functions.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上把“肥”借指冗余、杂乱和占空间，让数字文件像人一样需要瘦身。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, 'fat' refers to redundancy, clutter, and storage bulk, making digital files seem like they need slimming just like people do.
context: 适用于软件广告、数码产品宣传或办公效率场景。
literal_translation: The new organizer app calls itself a 'file weight-loss camp'; it doesn't make files disappear, it just makes the desktop stop looking bloated.
functional_equivalence_translation: It's a boot camp for bloated files and messy desktops.
explanatory_translation: The expression grafts the human idea of a 'weight-loss camp' onto file management. It therefore means both literal digital cleanup and metaphorical slimming of cluttered data.
interpretation_1: 文件整理压缩
interpretation_2: 桌面瘦身

surface_text: 那只平时安静的鹦鹉突然开口学人说话，把满屋人都吓了一跳，真是一鸣惊人。
有一天，小华到小明家玩，小华突然想上厕所就跟小明说：[小明厕所借我一下。] 小明回答：[不行你借走了我们家就没有厕所了。]
老师对吵闹不休的学生说：两个女人等于一千只鸭子。 正好师母来找他，一个女学生向他报告：老师，外面有五百只鸭子找你。
单位某领导口齿不清，说话漏风。 一次，单位晚上有文艺演出，该领导在广播中通知：各位鸡公（职工）请注意，今天晚上在灯光球场有好看的鸡母（节目），请鸡公们（职工们）晚饭后去看鸡母(节目）。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，领导把通知说成了让“鸡公”们去看“鸡母”，字面像是在召集公鸡去看母鸡，形成滑稽效果。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the leader is literally telling all the roosters to pay attention and go watch some hens at the stadium that evening.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是由于口齿不清把“职工”说成“鸡公”、把“节目”说成“鸡母”，实际要表达的是通知单位职工晚上去灯光球场观看文艺节目。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that because of his unclear pronunciation, 'employees' and 'programs/shows' are mispronounced as 'roosters' and 'hens'; he actually means to notify the staff to go watch the evening performance.
context: 单位领导口齿不清，在广播通知职工晚上去灯光球场看文艺演出时，把“职工”“节目”说成了“鸡公”“鸡母”。
literal_translation: A leader at the work unit had unclear pronunciation and spoke with air leaking. Once, there was an evening performance, and he announced on the radio: All rooster-workers, please note, tonight at the lighted ball court there will be good-looking hens-programs; rooster-workers, please go watch the hens-programs after dinner.
functional_equivalence_translation: A leader with slurred speech made an announcement: All staff, please note, tonight there will be a show at the lit court. But he mispronounced it so it sounded like: All roosters, come watch the hens tonight.
explanatory_translation: The humor comes from the leader's unclear pronunciation: he intended to say “zhigong” (employees) and “jiemu” (programs), but it came out sounding like “jigong” (roosters) and “jimu” (hens), creating a pun through mispronunciation.
interpretation_1: 表层上领导把通知说成了让大家去看公鸡和母鸡。
interpretation_2: 实际想表达的是通知职工们晚上去看文艺节目。

surface_text: 这款保温杯宣传自己有“续杯自由”，不是鼓励你无限喝，是让热水从早到晚都像刚续过。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是像餐饮里的续杯一样，随时都能喝到热饮的状态。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it suggests the convenience of endless refills, like being able to drink hot beverages at any time.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“自由”嫁接进“续杯”，强调保温能力带来的不受时间限制的饮水体验。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning grafts 'freedom' onto 'refill', highlighting the time-independent freedom made possible by heat retention.
context: 适用于保温杯广告、生活方式文案和电商详情页。
literal_translation: This thermos claims to offer 'refill freedom'; it is not encouraging you to drink endlessly, but making hot water feel freshly refilled from morning to night.
functional_equivalence_translation: This thermos gives you 'refill freedom'—your drink stays like it was just topped up all day.
explanatory_translation: The hybrid phrase combines the retail concept of 'refills' with 'freedom', turning heat retention into a lifestyle benefit rather than a literal refill service.
interpretation_1: 随时像能续杯
interpretation_2: 保温带来的自由感

surface_text: 项目群里最活跃的不是程序员，是一群“会开人”：白天开会，晚上还要被会议继续打开。
hidden_form: 会开 / 开会的人 / 会坑人
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义指总是在开会的人，被标签化成一种职场身份。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it refers to people who are constantly in meetings, turned into a workplace label.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义带出“被会议折腾到人都被打开了”的吐槽意味，也借近似结构激活其他网络标签词。
interpretation_2_en: It also implies that meetings wear people down and 'open them up,' while echoing internet-style label formations.
context: 适用于职场吐槽、群聊段子或短视频文案。
literal_translation: The most active ones in the project group are not programmers but a group of 'meeting-open people': they hold meetings by day and get further opened by meetings at night.
functional_equivalence_translation: The busiest people at work are basically full-time meeting creatures.
explanatory_translation: The pun creates an internet-style label by turning 'holding meetings' into a person category, while also implying that constant meetings mentally wear people out.
interpretation_1: 总在开会的人
interpretation_2: 被会议消耗的人

surface_text: 新来的同事是个“秒回避”，消息总能一秒已读，然后优雅失踪。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层看像是会立刻回复消息的人。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it looks like someone who replies instantly.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含其实是“秒回之后迅速回避”，指已读、简短回应后就消失。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it means someone who instantly responds only to immediately avoid further interaction.
context: 适用于社交吐槽、同事聊天、朋友之间调侃。
literal_translation: The new colleague is a 'second-reply-avoidance' type: every message gets read in one second, then he disappears gracefully.
functional_equivalence_translation: He's the type who replies instantly just to dodge the rest of the conversation.
explanatory_translation: The phrase recombines 'instant reply' and 'avoidance,' so it first suggests responsiveness but then reveals a hidden meaning of quick disengagement.
interpretation_1: 回复很快
interpretation_2: 快速回避交流

surface_text: 清洁工阿花只有小学三年级文化，经常写错字。 一天阿花用地拖将实验室地板拖干净，然后写了一张条贴在门口:请闲人勿进，我脱得很干净了。
interpretation_1_zh: 字面上写成“我脱得很干净了”，意思变成了“我把衣物脱得很干净”，带有把自己脱光之类的荒诞意味。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the note says: 'Please keep out, I have taken it off very cleanly already,' using the verb '脱' ('to take off/remove').
interpretation_2_zh: 实际想表达的是“我拖得很干净了”，意思是实验室地板已经被拖洗得很干净，闲人不要进入。
interpretation_2_en: The intended meaning is: 'Please do not enter, I have mopped the floor very clean,' where '脱' is a mistaken substitution for '拖' ('to mop/drag with a mop').
context: 清洁工拖完实验室地板后在门口贴通知，想表达“我拖得很干净了”，却把“拖”误写成“脱”。
literal_translation: Please keep idlers out; I stripped very cleanly already.
functional_equivalence_translation: Keep out, please—I’ve mopped it spotless, not stripped spotless.
explanatory_translation: The cleaner means to say “I’ve mopped it very clean,” but she mistakenly writes a homophone that means “I’ve taken it off very cleanly / stripped off,” creating the pun.
interpretation_1: 本意是说地板被拖得很干净。
interpretation_2: 字面上变成了把衣服脱得很干净，带有脱光之意。

surface_text: 一次，带着两岁的女儿去吃KFC。 女儿坐在我旁边，我拿起薯条，蘸了一下番茄酱； 然后对女儿说：“来宝贝，蘸着吃！” 只见女儿突然站起来，站着吃……
interpretation_1_zh: 表层中女儿把“蘸着吃”听成了“站着吃”，于是真的站起来吃东西。
interpretation_1_en: The child understood it literally as an instruction to eat while standing, so she stood up and ate.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是说话人原本想表达“把薯条蘸上番茄酱再吃”，即“蘸着吃”，并不是让她站起来吃。
interpretation_2_en: What the speaker actually meant was to dip the fries in ketchup before eating, i.e. eat it with the sauce.
context: 家长拿着薯条蘸番茄酱，对两岁女儿说“来宝贝，蘸着吃”，孩子因“蘸着/站着”近音而误解。
literal_translation: “Dip it and eat,” but the daughter stood up to eat.
functional_equivalence_translation: I said, “Eat it dipped,” and my daughter heard it like “eat it standing,” so she stood up.
explanatory_translation: The pun is between Chinese “蘸着吃” (eat it after dipping it) and “站着吃” (eat it standing up), which sound similar, so the child misunderstood the instruction.
interpretation_1: 把食物蘸上番茄酱再吃。
interpretation_2: 被孩子理解成站起来吃。

surface_text: 顾客刚开始吃饭，就连连抱怨：这饭怎么跟生的一样，太糟糕了！服务生麻木不仁地回答：你没看我们的招牌是野味餐厅嘛。
某日上数学课，A君感叹道：“真是度分如年啊，还有多久下课？” 旁边的班长看了看表，幽幽地说：“还有一年。” A君……
interpretation_1_zh: A君用“度分如年”夸张地说上数学课时每一分钟都像一年那么难熬；班长顺着“年”的字面义回答“还有一年下课”，表面上像是真的还要等一年。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'year' is taken literally as a unit of time, so the class monitor is jokingly saying there is still one whole year before class ends.
interpretation_2_zh: 这里的“年”触发了时间单位的双关，班长实际是把表上的“还有一分钟”故意说成“还有一年”，借用前句中的“年”来制造幽默。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that in math class, 'degree, minute, and second' are angle units; after hearing 'minutes feel like years,' the monitor shifts 'year' into the measurement context and plays on the idea that there is still 'one degree' left, sounding like 'one year.'
context: 数学课上，A君先说“度分如年啊”，其姓名含“念”字，班长随后答“还有一年”。
literal_translation: One day in math class, A sighed, “Time passes like years by the minute—how long until class ends?” The class monitor looked at the watch and said quietly, “One more year.”
functional_equivalence_translation: In math class, A groaned, “Every minute feels like a year. How long till class ends?” The monitor glanced at the clock and said, “Just one more year”—playing on “year” and A’s name-sound.
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on the monitor’s reply “还有一年” (still one year), where “年” sounds the same as “念” in A’s name. So the line can be heard both as “one more year” and as a name-based pun echoing A’s complaint that every minute feels like a year.
interpretation_1: 班长表面上回答离下课还有很久，像是“还有一年”。
interpretation_2: 借“A君”名字中的“念”与“年”同音，实际是在接“度分如年”，说“还有一念”。

surface_text: 小明是一个非常宅的宅男，都23岁了还没有成功的谈过一场恋爱，最近和一美女在网上聊了十多天，最终两人约好在公园里见个面。可是两人谈了没一会儿，美女便起身告辞。小伙子很喜欢那个美女，见她要走，心里特别着急，连忙追问原因。美女说：我觉得你虽然相貌堂堂，可是腹中空空。小伙说：谁说我腹中空空？来公园之前还吃了两包方便面。
interpretation_1_zh: 小伙把“腹中空空”按字面理解成肚子是空的、没吃东西，所以用自己来公园前吃了两包方便面来反驳。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, "empty in the belly" means his stomach is physically empty, so he answers that he did eat something before coming to the park.
interpretation_2_zh: 美女说“腹中空空”并不是指他没吃饭，而是借指他缺乏学识、谈吐空泛、没有内涵。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that he is intellectually empty or lacking knowledge and substance, which is why the woman loses interest.
context: 相亲式见面中，美女评价男方“腹中空空”，男方故意或误解为字面上的肚子空。
literal_translation: The woman said: although you look dignified, your belly is empty. The young man said: who says my belly is empty? Before coming to the park, I even ate two packs of instant noodles.
functional_equivalence_translation: The woman said, “You may look impressive, but there’s nothing inside.” He replied, “Nothing inside? I had two packs of noodles before I came!”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “腹中空空,” which normally means “empty-headed / lacking knowledge or substance,” but the man interprets it literally as “having an empty stomach,” so he answers by saying he had eaten instant noodles.
interpretation_1: 美女表面上说他没有学识、没有内涵。
interpretation_2: 小伙把这话理解成自己肚子里没有食物。

surface_text: 一个三岁小男孩拉着一个三岁小女孩的手说：我爱你。 小女孩说：你能为我的未来负责吗？ 小男孩说：当然能，我们都不是一两岁的人了！
修表台太滑，工具也没地方放，老师傅皱眉说这活我一时无从下手。
丈夫热衷于钓鱼，他把自己所钓到的大鱼、名贵鱼拍成相片，贴在床头墙壁上。并且一一注上它们的名称、重量以及垂钓地点，乐此不疲。 妻子见状，便将自己的玉照挂在丈夫床头，并在旁边注明：美人鱼，49.5Kg，钓于人民公园。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上妻子把自己的照片也按丈夫记录鱼获的格式来标注，称自己为“美人鱼”，像是在把自己归入丈夫钓到的“鱼”之列。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'mermaid' is being used as if the wife were one of the husband's fishing catches, labeled like a fish with its name, weight, and where it was 'caught.'
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是把“美人”与“鱼”并置，借“钓”字的常见引申义，表示丈夫像在公园把美女“钓”到手，暗指妻子就是他当年追到的美人。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the wife jokingly calls herself a 'beauty' while also implying that the husband 'caught' her at People's Park, treating their romantic relationship like a successful fishing catch.
context: 丈夫常把钓到的鱼照片挂在床头，并标注名称、重量和垂钓地点；妻子仿照这一格式挂上自己的照片并题注“美人鱼，49.5Kg，钓于人民公园”。
literal_translation: The husband is keen on fishing. He photographs the big and rare fish he catches and puts the photos on the wall by the bed, noting their names, weights, and fishing spots. Seeing this, the wife hangs up her own photo by his bedside and writes beside it: “mermaid, 49.5 kg, caught at People’s Park.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Seeing her husband label all his catches, the wife posted her own photo by the bed and captioned it: “Mermaid, 49.5 kg, hooked at People’s Park.”
explanatory_translation: The wife imitates her husband’s fish-labeling habit and calls herself a “mermaid.” The humor comes from treating a beautiful woman as if she were one of his fishing catches, blending “beauty” and “fish” into one label.
interpretation_1: 字面上指传说中的“美人鱼”这一鱼类形象，被当作丈夫钓到的一条鱼来标注。
interpretation_2: 实际上借“美人鱼”戏称妻子自己，既指她是美人，又讽刺丈夫把她也当成“钓获物”。

surface_text: 一天，孩子突然问妈妈小孩儿是怎么来的，妈妈便说小孩儿是老天爷给的。 不久，爸爸下班回家，刚走到门口，孩子便大叫：“妈妈！妈妈！老天爷回来啦！”
我们接待了北京来的专家的家属。
食堂今天做了好多种口味，还是有人挑剔，师傅叹气说真是众口难调。
小女孩：你知道天有多高地有多厚吗？ 小男孩：嗯......不知道。 小女孩：哼，你是一个不知天高地厚的家伙。
hidden_form: 不知道天有多高、地有多厚
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是说小男孩确实不知道天有多高、地有多厚，被按字面意思理解为不知道这个问题的答案。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the boy literally does not know how high the sky is or how thick the ground is when asked that question.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是借成语“不知天高地厚”批评对方无知、鲁莽，不明白事理和分寸。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, the girl is using the idiom to mean that the boy is ignorant, inexperienced, or does not know his place.
context: 前文先问“天有多高地有多厚”，后文用成语“不知天高地厚”回扣字面问句并激活其惯用义。
literal_translation: Little girl: Do you know how high the sky is and how thick the earth is? Little boy: Um... I don't know. Little girl: Hmph, you're a guy who doesn't know how high the sky is and how thick the earth is.
functional_equivalence_translation: Girl: Do you know how high the sky is and how thick the earth is? Boy: Um... no. Girl: Hmph, you're really out of your depth.
explanatory_translation: The girl first asks literally about the height of the sky and the thickness of the earth, then uses the idiom “not know heaven high and earth thick,” which idiomatically means someone is ignorant and overconfident.
interpretation_1: 字面上指不知道天空多高、地面多厚。
interpretation_2: 惯用义指人狂妄无知、没有分寸。

surface_text: 我把周末大扫除命名为“家班回收”，把散落一地的物件和上周的疲惫一起归位。
hidden_form: 加班回收 / 家务整理 / 把上班状态收回来
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是回到家中进行整理收纳，把家务做完。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means doing household cleanup and organizing things at home.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义借“加班”调侃周末仍在劳动，也带出把工作后的疲惫慢慢回收的意思。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it plays on 'overtime work,' joking that weekend chores feel like extra labor while also reclaiming oneself from work exhaustion.
context: 适用于生活方式分享、居家整理视频标题或周末吐槽。
literal_translation: I named my weekend deep cleaning 'home-shift recovery,' putting scattered items and last week's exhaustion back in place together.
functional_equivalence_translation: I call my weekend cleanup 'home overtime recovery'—tidying the house and recovering from work at once.
explanatory_translation: The pun remodels the near-sounding phrase 'overtime work' by replacing the first morpheme with 'home,' creating a hybrid expression that links housework, labor, and emotional recovery.
interpretation_1: 在家做整理
interpretation_2: 像周末加班般劳作

surface_text: 课间讨论考公务员的事，我说：海关方面的油水很多（油水，你懂的），结果宿舍那个奇葩冒出一句：啊，怎么办，我不会游泳诶！
今天花了一百五十块钱剪了一个很抽象的头。回寝室后遭到几个室友强力批判！ 这时候一旁沉默许久的一同学总结说：“这发型性价比很高！才花一百五，剪了个二百五的头。”
老妹处了个乡下男朋友，爸妈有点不乐意。 这天，这小伙子要登门拜访了，我妹妹千叮咛万嘱咐：“亲爱的，为了咱们将来的幸福，今天无论我爸妈说啥，你都一定要忍让，要懂得谦卑……” 小伙子连连点头。 一进门，我妈倒也算热情：“你是小王吧？欢迎欢迎！” 没想到小王一听竟然愣了，瞅瞅我妹妹，赶紧微笑着说：“阿姨您这么叫我真是抬高我了！我是小土鳖！”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上，妈妈是在确认并称呼他叫“小王吧”，其中“吧”是表示推测、确认语气的词，意思相当于“你是小王，对吧”。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the mother is simply asking politely, 'You are Xiao Wang, right?' using the common phrase '小王吧' to confirm his name.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上，“小王吧”与“小王八”近音，触发了带贬义的“王八”联想。小伙子误以为对方在借谐音骂自己，所以顺着“乡下”“谦卑”的语境，自嘲成“我是小土鳖”。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden joke is that '小王吧' sounds like '小王八' ('little bastard/turtle'), so the young man, having been told to stay humble, mishears it as an insult and jokingly replies by lowering himself even further as '小土鳖.'
context: 见家长语境中，男友被提醒要谦卑；母亲说“你是小王吧”，男友将其错听并触发自谦回应
literal_translation: My younger sister dated a rural boyfriend, and our parents were a bit unhappy. That day, the young man was coming to visit. My sister repeatedly told him, “Dear, for our future happiness, no matter what my parents say today, you must be patient and humble...” The young man kept nodding. As soon as he entered, my mom was rather warm: “You’re Xiao Wang, right? Welcome, welcome!” Unexpectedly, Xiao Wang froze, looked at my sister, and quickly smiled, saying, “Auntie, calling me that really flatters me! I’m just a little bumpkin!”
functional_equivalence_translation: When my mom greeted him with, “So you’re Xiao Wang,” he took “Wang” as sounding like “king,” and, trying to be humble, replied, “You’re giving me too much credit—I’m no little king, just a country bumpkin.”
explanatory_translation: The joke hinges on “小王” (Xiao Wang, a normal way to address someone surnamed Wang) being misheard as something like “little king,” an overly elevated label. Because he had been told to stay humble, he overreacts and self-deprecatingly says he is only a “little bumpkin” instead.
interpretation_1: 母亲按常见称呼把他叫作姓王的年轻人“小王”
interpretation_2: 他误把“小王”理解成与“小皇”对应的尊称，觉得对自己过于抬举，于是自谦为“小土鳖”

surface_text: 这款颈椎按摩仪主打“按部就松”，从肩到颈，哪里紧就先松哪里。
hidden_form: 按部就班 / 按摩 + 放松
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上指按摩仪按部位逐步进行放松。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it means the massager relaxes the body part by part in sequence.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上仿拟成语“按部就班”，把“班”替换成“松”，突出按摩后逐步放松的效果。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it reshapes the idiom 'step by step' by replacing the final morpheme with 'relax,' highlighting the gradual soothing effect.
context: 适用于按摩仪、理疗产品或健康类广告文案。
literal_translation: This neck massager promotes 'press-by-part then loosen'; from shoulders to neck, whichever part is tense gets relaxed first.
functional_equivalence_translation: This neck massager works 'step by step into relaxation'—loosening each tense spot from the shoulders up.
explanatory_translation: The pun is built by parodying a familiar idiom and replacing one component with 'relax,' forming a hybrid phrase that links orderly procedure with massage relief.
interpretation_1: 分部位放松
interpretation_2: 仿按部就班

surface_text: 大学有棵树，树下有座坟，叫微积分，里面埋了很多人。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上把“微积分”说成一座坟，借“分”字让人联想到坟墓，夸张地说里面埋了很多人，营造阴森搞笑的画面。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it says there is a grave under a tree at a university called 'calculus,' and many people are buried in it.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是微积分这门课很难，难倒了很多学生，像把很多人都“埋”进去一样；“分”借转出与成绩、课程相关的失败者，即很多人在这门课上挂科。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that calculus is so difficult that it metaphorically 'buries' or defeats many students, especially because of the concept of differentiation/division suggested by the word 'fen' in 'wei ji fen.'
context: 大学有棵树，树下有座坟，叫微积分，里面埋了很多人
literal_translation: There is a tree at the university, and under the tree there is a grave called calculus, with many people buried in it.
functional_equivalence_translation: At the university, there’s a tree, and under it a tomb called Calculus—it has claimed many lives.
explanatory_translation: There is a tree on campus, and under it a grave called calculus. This jokingly means calculus is so difficult that many students are metaphorically ‘buried’ by it, such as by failing the course.
interpretation_1: 指大学课程“微积分”
interpretation_2: 被说成像一座埋了很多人的坟墓，暗指课程极难、挂科者多

surface_text: 同事把工位绿植区命名为“班公室”，一边上班，一边靠办公桌上的植物补点生命值。
hidden_form: 办公室 / 上班 + 公室
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是对办公空间的改造命名，突出这是一个带有“上班气息”的小环境。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, it is a renamed office space that emphasizes its work-related atmosphere.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上拆改“办公室”，把“办”换成“班”，强化上班状态本身成了空间主题。
interpretation_2_en: Implicitly, it remodels the word for 'office' by replacing 'ban' with the character for 'work shift', making the state of working itself the theme of the space.
context: 适用于职场吐槽、办公室布置分享或社交媒体文案。
literal_translation: My colleague named the desk plant area the 'work-room', working while restoring life points with plants on the desk.
functional_equivalence_translation: They turned the office into a 'work-room' where plants keep your soul alive.
explanatory_translation: The pun alters the standard word for 'office' by swapping one near-sounding morpheme. This makes the space feel less like a neutral office and more like a place defined by the condition of being at work.
interpretation_1: 上班空间
interpretation_2: 办公室变体

surface_text: 社区通知业主和租客的家人登记。
下午最后一节自习课上，班主任查老师正抓紧时间给同学们补课上因式分解，可同学们那有心思，大家都在小声的议论着今晚的电视《西游记》。突然，查老师指着黑板上的代数式大叫一声：大家注意了！我要变了！ 哄堂大笑！
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是老师在讲因式分解，指着黑板上的代数式说自己要把式子进行变化、变形。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the teacher means he is about to transform the algebraic expression on the blackboard, that is, change its form during factorization.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是“我要变了”也可被学生听成“我要变化了、要变样了”，带有像《西游记》里人物施法变身的联想，因此引发哄堂大笑。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning echoes the transformation scenes in Journey to the West, making it sound as if the teacher himself is going to magically shapeshift, which is why the students burst into laughter.
context: 老师正在讲因式分解，学生却在议论《西游记》；“我要变了”既可指代数式变形，也会让人联想到西游记人物施展变化。
literal_translation: During the last self-study class in the afternoon, the homeroom teacher, Mr. Zha, was hurrying to make up a lesson on factorization for the students. But the students were in no mood for it and were all whispering about tonight's TV show Journey to the West. Suddenly, Mr. Zha pointed at the algebraic expression on the blackboard and shouted: “Everyone pay attention! I'm going to change!” The whole class burst into laughter.
functional_equivalence_translation: While teaching factorization, the teacher suddenly shouted, “Watch closely—I’m about to do a transformation!” Since the students had been chatting about Journey to the West, it sounded like he meant a magical transformation, not just an algebraic one.
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “变了” (“change/transform”). In math class it normally means transforming an algebraic expression, but because the students are talking about Journey to the West, it also suggests the magical transformations associated with characters like Sun Wukong.
interpretation_1: 老师说要对黑板上的代数式进行变形、变换。
interpretation_2: 结合同学们正在议论《西游记》，这句话像是在说自己要像孙悟空一样变化、变身。

surface_text: 前些天和邻居闲聊，说起孩子来。 他说：“现在我有孙子了。” 我说：“我家的孩子也是你孙子” 陈家的也是，那边的也是。 结果邻居来了句：是的，我们这都是孙子。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层上是顺着前文谈孩子辈分，意思是这一片的孩子按辈分说都属于孙子这一辈。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'grandson' means a male grandchild. The neighbor says he now has a grandson, and the speaker jokes that many children around here could be counted as his grandsons.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含上借用“孙子”的另一层俗语含义，带有自嘲或骂人色彩，意思像是在说我们这的人都是孙子、都是吃亏受气的小辈。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that '孙子' is also a colloquial insult meaning 'grandson' in the sense of 'brat' or 'subordinate,' so 'we are all 孙子 here' shifts to a self-mocking or joking rude meaning.
context: 谈论邻居有了孙子后，说话人把本家和周围人家的孩子都说成对方的“孙子”，触发“亲属称谓”与“泛指后辈/小辈”的双重理解。
literal_translation: A few days ago I was chatting with my neighbor and we talked about children. He said, “Now I have a grandson.” I said, “The child in my family is your grandson too.” The Chen family’s is too, and that one over there too. Then the neighbor said: “Yes, around here we are all grandsons.”
functional_equivalence_translation: My neighbor said, “I’ve got a grandson now.” I joked, “Mine’s your grandson too—so is the Chens’ kid, and theirs over there.” He replied, “Yep, around here they’re all my grandkids.”
explanatory_translation: The pun centers on “孙子,” which literally means “grandson,” but in colloquial Chinese can also be stretched to mean “junior/youngster” or be used jokingly to place others in a lower generation. The humor comes from shifting from the literal family term to a broader, teasing social meaning.
interpretation_1: 指祖辈的男孙，即邻居说自己有了孙辈。
interpretation_2: 口语中带贬义或自嘲地指晚辈、小辈，泛指这一片的孩子都是他的后辈。

surface_text: 一天，在给一男客户办理完取款业务后，我交待说：请您把卡收好。再看，发现客户手包拉链没拉好，又交待说：请您把拉链拉好。 客户立即低头查看，周围同事笑成一片。
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是工作人员看到客户手包的拉链没有拉上，提醒他把包上的拉链拉好。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the speaker is reminding the male customer to zip up the zipper on his bag because it was left open.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是这句话容易被理解成在提醒男客户把裤子上的拉链拉好，因此引发了尴尬和笑声。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the phrase can be misheard as telling the man to zip up his pants or check his trouser fly, which makes the situation embarrassing and funny.
context: 银行柜台办理业务后，柜员先提醒客户收好银行卡，随后看到客户手包拉链没拉好，说“请您把拉链拉好”，客户因此联想到自己衣裤上的拉链。
literal_translation: One day, after handling a withdrawal for a male customer, I said, “Please put your card away carefully.” Then I noticed the zipper of his handbag was open, so I added, “Please zip it up.” The customer immediately looked down, and my colleagues around burst into laughter.
functional_equivalence_translation: After serving a male customer at the bank, I told him, “Please keep your card safe.” Then I noticed his bag was unzipped and said, “Please zip it up.” He instantly looked down at his pants, and everyone nearby cracked up.
explanatory_translation: The humor comes from “zip it up”: the speaker meant the zipper on the customer’s bag, but the male customer understood it as a reminder to zip up his pants, so he looked down in embarrassment.
interpretation_1: 把手包的拉链拉严实。
interpretation_2: 被误听为提醒客户把自己裤子的拉链拉好。

surface_text: 女儿：“海都是蓝色的吗？” 妈妈：“不，还有红海、黄海和黑海。”
interpretation_1_zh: 表面上妈妈是在回答女儿：并不是所有海看起来都是蓝色的，还存在红海、黄海、黑海这些“不同颜色”的海。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, the mother is answering literally that not all seas are blue, because there are seas named the Red Sea, the Yellow Sea, and the Black Sea.
interpretation_2_zh: 实际隐含意思是“红海、黄海、黑海”是专有海名，并不表示海水真的分别是红色、黄色或黑色；这里利用海名中的颜色词造成了字面颜色理解与地名理解的双关。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that the daughter is asking about the actual color of seawater, while the mother shifts to interpreting color through proper names of seas, creating a semantic mismatch between real color and named color.
context: 根据表层文本可恢复的最小必要语境
negative_example: 不，还有大海、小海和深海。
literal_translation: Daughter: “Are all seas blue?” Mother: “No, there are also the Red Sea, the Yellow Sea, and the Black Sea.”
functional_equivalence_translation: Daughter: “Are all seas blue?” Mother: “No—there’s also the Red Sea, the Yellow Sea, and the Black Sea.”
explanatory_translation: The girl asks whether seas are blue in color, while the mother humorously shifts to sea names that contain color words, such as Red Sea, Yellow Sea, and Black Sea.
interpretation_1: 女儿把“海”理解为现实中海水通常呈蓝色。
interpretation_2: 妈妈把“蓝色”转到海的专名上，举出“红海、黄海、黑海”等带颜色的海名。

surface_text: 我们一个同事,他去考驾照时,对考官说了一句经典的话:报告仪表，考官正常
interpretation_1_zh: 字面上是在向考官汇报时说成了“考官正常”，意思变成了考官这个人状态正常。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, he is making a routine report during the driving test, saying that the dashboard instruments are normal and the examiner is normal as well.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含的常规说法应是“仪表正常”，本来是报告车辆仪表状态正常，却误把“仪表”替成了“考官”，形成语义转移的笑点。
interpretation_2_en: The joke is that he mistakenly uses the exam-style phrase on the examiner, making it sound like he is checking whether the examiner is mentally or physically normal, which creates an awkward and funny shift in meaning.
context: 考驾照场景中，考生需要检查车辆仪表是否正常，同时又用口头报告的格式向考官说话
literal_translation: One of our colleagues, when taking the driving test, said a classic line to the examiner: “Reporting dashboard, examiner normal.”
functional_equivalence_translation: During his driving test, a colleague joked to the examiner, “Reporting in: the gauges are fine—and so are you.”
explanatory_translation: A colleague taking a driving test told the examiner, “Reporting, dashboard; examiner normal.” The joke comes from mixing a formal reporting phrase with the car-check item “dashboard/instruments,” creating an awkward double reading.
interpretation_1: 把“仪表”理解为汽车上的仪表设备
interpretation_2: 借用“报告首长，一切正常”的口吻，把“仪表正常，考官正常”说成了“报告仪表，考官正常”

surface_text: 某人中了亿元大奖，记者采访问道：这么多钱你打算怎么花呢？ 中奖男说：我打算先把欠五家银行的钱还上。 记者追问道：那剩下的呢？ “剩下的？剩下的等几天再说吧……”
interpretation_1_zh: 表层义是记者在问：还完欠五家银行的钱之后，剩余的奖金打算怎么处理。
interpretation_1_en: On the surface, 'the rest' means the money left over after he pays back what he owes to the five banks.
interpretation_2_zh: 隐含义是中奖男理解成：还没还上的、剩余拖欠的债务怎么办，意思是这些欠款只能再等几天以后再说。
interpretation_2_en: The hidden meaning is that there may be no money left at all; the 'remaining' debts to the other banks will have to wait a few more days.
context: 中奖者先说要把欠五家银行的钱还上，记者再问“那剩下的呢”，触发“剩余奖金”与“剩余债务”的语义转移。
literal_translation: A man won a huge lottery prize. A reporter asked, “How are you going to spend so much money?” The man said, “I’ll first pay back what I owe to five banks.” The reporter asked, “What about the rest?” “The rest? I’ll talk about the rest in a few days.”
functional_equivalence_translation: After winning a huge jackpot, a man said he’d first repay five banks. The reporter asked, “And what will you do with the rest?” He replied, “The rest? I’ll repay that a few days later.”
explanatory_translation: The humor hinges on “the rest”: the reporter means the money left over after repaying debts, but the winner pretends to understand it as the debts still left unpaid.
interpretation_1: 记者表面上是在问还完银行欠款后还剩下多少钱、打算怎么花。
interpretation_2: 中奖男把“剩下的”理解成尚未归还的其他债务，意思是其余欠款过几天再还。

surface_text: 一哥们高中时和女同桌关系非常好，有一次他问她：“你一个月流量多少？” 女生一愣神，小声地坦白道：“100cc……左右吧……” 哥们大吼：“我问你手机包月！”
